headline: ‘Alliance is necessity, not choice’: Congress' Raj Kumar Verka targets BJP-SAD tie-up in Punjab | India News
content: Punjab Congress working President Raj Kumar Verka on Tuesday criticised the renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), calling it a political necessity rather than a choice and asserting that the two parties would not be able to challenge the Congress in Punjab.Speaking to ANI, Verka said, “I feel that this alliance is a necessity, not a choice. The Akali Dal had boycotted Parliament and withdrawn from its alliance with the BJP. This was followed by a prolonged farmers' movement, during which 700–800 farmers allegedly died, including those who died by suicide, and incidents of murder were also reported. Despite this, Sukhbir Badal supported the three farm laws from within.”Questioning the political understanding between the two parties, Verka said that people in Punjab considered both the BJP and the Akali Dal anti-Punjab and that their coming together would not translate into electoral gains. “I want people to understand that parties and leaders whom they consider anti-Punjab, including Sukhbir Badal, will not find public support. People in Punjab also consider the BJP their enemy and view it as anti-Punjab. Therefore, if these two parties come together, it will be like adding zero to zero; the result will remain zero. No matter how many smaller parties join hands, they will not be able to compete with the Congress,” he added. Also Read | ‘Natural alliance’: PM Modi says BJP-SAD reunion will ensure pro-people governance in PunjabVerka further alleged that the drug menace had grown during the period when the SAD and BJP were in alliance, claiming that the term 'Chitta' first came into prominence in Punjab under their government. He linked the issue to BJP leader Amit Shah and Sukhbir Badal.Meanwhile, former Punjab Congress president and Ludhiana MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring also accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and his wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal of misleading the people of Punjab by publicly denying an alliance with the BJP while allegedly supporting the party on key issues in Parliament.Reacting to the BJP-SAD tie-up ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, Warring said the alliance's announcement had come on a favourable day for Punjab and the Congress, adding that the two parties had maintained political proximity even after formally parting ways.Also Read | ‘Bada bhai becomes CM, Akali Dal is the elder brother’: Amit Shah after BJP, SAD announce alliance for Punjab polls"For the past few years, there has been a charade; the public was being misled by Sukhbir Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal. Whenever it came to voting, whether for the Presidential election or on the Uniform Civil Code in Parliament, they (SAD) would invariably stand with the BJP. Yet, back in Punjab, they would claim they had no alliance with the BJP. Why was the alliance supposedly broken? It happened after the 'black laws' (farm laws) were introduced... They also created a major stir regarding the 'Bandi Sikhs' (Sikh prisoners)... Yet, all these issues concerning Punjab remain exactly as they were... Now, realising they have lost their ground in Punjab, both parties have decided to join forces, hoping to salvage something. But for the second or third time, the people of Punjab have realised that Sukhbir Badal and the BJP are betraying them," he said.Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP President Nitin Nabin and Shiromani Akali Dal President Sukhbir Badal met on Tuesday in the capital to formally signal a tie-up between the two parties for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections and the strengthening of the National Democratic Alliance.The two parties have been one of the longest-standing allies in politics; however, they broke up in 2020 when the Akali Dal walked out over the Union Government's intention to introduce the three farm laws. The three laws were later withdrawn, but both parties contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately. (ANI)

headline: Opinion | BJP Seals Punjab Deal With Akalis. But What Explains Its Demand For More Seats?
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have finally announced their alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Neither party has found it easy to win without the other, and together they won three state elections in 1997, 2007, and 2012. The real question is no longer whether to reunite but on what terms. The BJP, long the junior partner, wants a bigger share of seats than it has ever had. Under the old understanding, SAD contested 94 of the 117 Assembly seats and the BJP, 23. For the Lok Sabha, SAD took 10 of the 13 seats and the BJP three: Gurdaspur, Hoshiarpur, and Amritsar. The logic was a natural division of the social base. The 2011 Census put Sikhs at 57.7% of Punjab's population and Hindus at 38.5%, so an alliance in which SAD gathered Sikh votes and the BJP gathered Hindu votes covered most of the electorate. The partnership ended in September 2020 in the aftermath of the farm bills. Since then, both parties have fought alone, with poor results. In the 2022 Vidhan Sabha elections, SAD won just three and the BJP two seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the BJP won no seats in Punjab, and the SAD won one. The BJP's argument rests on how the two parties fared in 2024. It polled about 18% of the votes in Punjab and led in 23 Assembly segments. SAD polled about 13% and led in nine. The BJP also finished second in seven segments against the SAD's six. The BJP's leads are spread across all three regions, while the SAD's are concentrated in Malwa, which accounts for eight of its nine. SAD has also been weakened by splits in the party and by the rise of Amritpal Singh's Waris Punjab De, which competes for the same Panthic vote. From the BJP's side, a party that outpolled its senior partner can no longer be expected to accept the old 23-seat quota. The BJP's second argument is demographic. Hindus are a majority in five districts: Pathankot, Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Fazilka, and Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar (Nawanshahr). Together, they hold 26 Assembly seats. In seven more districts, the Hindu population is above 40%: Mohali, Gurdaspur, Firozpur, Rupnagar, Ludhiana, Patiala, and Kapurthala. Those seven districts hold another 43 seats.

headline: Lured with money, medical & educational support: 10 arrested in Amethi over ‘conversion’ campaign
content: Ten persons, including four women, were arrested in Uttar Pradesh's Amethi district on charges of attempting to persuade people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds to convert to Christianity by luring them with financial assistance, medical care and educational support, police said. The accused, identified as three couples and a father-daughter duo from UP, Maharashtra and Odisha, particularly targeted members of the Dalit community, the police claimed. Those arrested are Rajkumar, alias Joel (50) and his wife Suryakala, alias Martha (47) of Amethi; Kanhaiya Bind, alias Samson (46) from UP’s Azamgarh; Srinivasan Daniel (58) and his daughter Divya Daniel (30), and Royal Rodrigues (53) and his wife Rita Rodrigues (50), all residents of Maharashtra; Mahipal Singh Bind, alias William (45) and his wife Elvina Williams (40), and Prakash Rao (42) of Odisha, those investigating the matter said. A case has been registered against them under Sections 3 and 5(1) of the Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, the police said, adding that four books related to religious conversion were recovered from their possession. Amethi Superintendent of Police (SP) Saravanan T said the group has been active for at least six years, having facilitated conversions in the past, and is linked with an organisation called the Revival Church which is registered in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The police are also examining the financial transactions of the accused to ascertain the source of funds. “We will write to the Income Tax Department seeking a scrutiny of the financial transactions of the Revival Church,” the SP said. According to the police, the accused travelled across the country to deliver religious sermons to propagate their beliefs, and have also been active in Uttarakhand, Punjab, Jharkhand, Odisha and Tamil Nadu. The investigators said they received information that a group was allegedly approaching members of the Scheduled Caste community at Amethi's Sindurva village and persuading them for mass conversions with promises of money and other incentives. Acting on the information, police on Monday conducted a search at a house where 20-25 people had gathered as part of a two-day programme before arresting the accused. The group had previously facilitated some religious conversions in Amethi through Rajkumar, alias Joel, one of the arrested accused, the police said.

headline: Dry weather to persist in Punjab; slowing winds likely to worsen pollution
content: There appears to be no respite from pollution, as dry weather is likely to prevail across the region over the coming days, with no possibility of rain. Day temperatures are expected to hover between 25°C and 29°C, while minimum temperatures are likely to remain between 8°C and 11°C, according to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) Meteorological Centre, Chandigarh.The continuation of dry weather, coupled with a slowdown in wind speed post Tuesday afternoon, is likely to aggravate pollution levels. Dense smog and hazy conditions are expected to persist, potentially worsening respiratory and allergy-related problems in the wake of farm fires in the region.Weather experts said reduced wind speed would hinder the dispersion of pollutants, leading to their accumulation in the atmosphere and further deteriorating air quality.The state has recorded 7,086 incidents of stubble burning so far, as compared to 5,088 incidents during the corresponding period last year.The Air Quality Index (AQI) continues to remain in the unhealthy category in many parts of the region. Ludhiana recorded an AQI of 183, Amritsar 167, Jalandhar 197, Mandi Gobindgarh 177 and Patiala 171. At one 139, the Chandigarh's AQI remained the cleanest.Meanwhile, the prevailing weather conditions are considered favourable for farmers engaged in wheat sowing. The dry spell and prevailing temperatures are conducive to wheat germination and early crop growth.

headline: Punjab : Farm fires see nearly 40% surge this season as paddy harvest ends | Hindustan Times
content: With the conclusion of the paddy harvest in Punjab, farm fire cases have climbed to 7,006 this season, marking a nearly 40% jump from the previous year’s 5,114 incidents. The sharp uptick breaks a six-year downward trend and has rattled state authorities and enforcement agencies.Farm fires have surged despite the government spending ₹576 crore on subsidised machinery for in-situ and ex-situ paddy straw management. Out of 24,817 subsidised machines supplied to farmers, 17,200 were super seeders and 1,100 were balers.This rise in incidents persists even with strict enforcement, which includes 11,000 monitoring groups and 1,200 round-the-clock parali (straw) protection teams led by deputy commissioners and sub-divisional magistrates.In 2024, 10,909 cases of farm fires were recorded in kharif (paddy) harvest and before that in 2023, 36,650 cases were reported. While the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has directed the state government to eliminate stubble burning entirely, this year’s spike makes that zero-incident target look increasingly difficult to achieve.Half of the cases (3,492) were reported in five hotspot districts: Ferozpur at the top with 906 cases, followed by Sangrur (793), Tarn Taran (711), Bathinda (638) and Patiala (444).Ludhiana-based state remote sensing centre started monitoring fire cases from September 15 and monitoring will continue until November 30. The centre fetches data from NASA satellites. For the past few days, fire cases have been steady, and according to officials in the state agriculture department, the harvest has completely finished.“Although the harvest season has practically ended, satellites continue to record scattered fire incidents,” said agriculture department additional director Jagdish Singh. He said while it is unclear if all of these are actual farm fires, they are still added to the department’s official tally.“Field reports indicate that the fires are occurring mostly in patches after baling and have reduced in overall intensity,” he said.According to him, the lesson for the upcoming season is “waste to wealth,” and it is better if farmers understand this sooner rather than later. “One trolley laden with 150 quintals of paddy straw sells for ₹60,000 and the price will increase in the future,” he said.A Punjab Pollution Control Board official, who serves as the state-level nodal officer for paddy straw management, expressed concern over the recent uptick in fire counts, especially after steady reductions over the past few years.“We see an increase in the number because of two spells of rainfall during the harvest, which delayed harvesting, and in the panic to prepare for upcoming rabi crops, farmers in some pockets resorted to burning of straw,” he said. ₹1.2cr penalties imposed on defaulting farmersThe Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) has imposed environmental cess penalties totaling ₹1.23 crore on defaulting farmers, of which ₹43.35 lakh has been recovered. Additionally, 2,144 FIRs were registered under Section 223 of the BNS, and 2,268 red entries were recorded in the farmers’ revenue records, which could result in an embargo on their crop loans. Furthermore, at least 41 nodal officers were prosecuted under CAQM provisions, and 2,193 show-cause notices were issued.

headline: Ludhiana: Input cost up, ₹4 hike in milk procurement price sought | Hindustan Times
content: The Progressive Dairy Farmers Association (PDFA), Punjab, has demanded an immediate increase in milk procurement prices by at least ₹4 per kg, citing a sharp rise in cattle feed costs and other input expenses. The association has warned the state government and milk plants that it will launch an agitation if its demands are not accepted by December 5.The association on Monday marched towards the mini secretariat and handed over a memorandum to the deputy commissioner regarding its demands. The association said prices of almost all major ingredients used in cattle feed had registered a steep increase in recent months. The price of maize had surged from ₹2,100 to ₹3,300 per quintal, soybean from ₹4,500 to ₹7,000, mustard oil cake from ₹3,000 to ₹4,200 and paddy straw from ₹350 to ₹1,300 per quintal.PDFA president Daljit Singh said the prices of other nutritional ingredients had also increased by nearly 50%, pushing cattle feed manufacturing costs up by ₹800 to ₹1,000 per quintal.He added that dairy farmers were facing mounting financial pressure. The association pointed out that milk plants had increased the selling price of milk by ₹4 to ₹6 per kg, but the benefit had not been passed on to farmers supplying milk.It said states such as Karnataka, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh had extended benefits to milk producers through subsidies of ₹7, ₹5 and ₹6 per kg, respectively. Punjab, however, had neither increased milk procurement prices nor provided financial assistance to dairy farmers, the association alleged.The PDFA demanded that the state government and milk plants ensure that the benefit of any increase in milk prices was directly passed on to milk producers. In view of the rising input costs, it sought an immediate hike of at least ₹4 per kg in the procurement price.Withdrawal of breeding policy soughtThe association has also demanded the withdrawal of Punjab’s breeding policy, alleging that its provisions were creating hurdles for dairy farmers and artificial insemination workers. The PDFA president claimed that the policy was adversely affecting efforts to improve the breeds of cows and buffaloes.It raised concerns over restrictions relating to manpower for artificial insemination, regulations governing semen storage, additional expenses, documentation and the implementation of embryo transfer technology. These provisions, it said, were making dairy operations more complicated and expensive.

headline: Councillor objects to NGO grants via direct cheques at F&CC meeting
content: Finance and Contracts Committee (F&CC) member and Congress councillor Gaurav Bhatti, by presenting an order of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, objected to the proposal to give grant of Rs 2.43 crore to NGOs and religious and social organisations under Rangla Punjab Vikas Scheme of the state government through direct cheques, during the committee meeting held on Monday at the Mayor’s camp office in Ludhiana.He said the Municipal Corporation should prepare an estimate and get works done through the tender process as per the rules, to maintain transparency. No payment should be made through cheque.Another agenda item of files relating to works worth over ?13 crore under the Municipal Development Funds (MDF) mentioned that payments would be made from the Municipal Corporation’s own funds. To this, Bhatti raised an objection saying if these works have been approved under the MDF, their payments should also be made from the respective MDF and not from corporation’s funds. Bhatti emphasised that the corporation’s own treasury should not be burdened with additional financial liabilities for works sanctioned under a separate funding source.In the previous F&CC meeting, certain resolutions had been kept pending with directions that the cases be thoroughly examined and presented again before the committee. However, the files were subsequently moved forward by officials.Gaurav Bhatti questioned the officials and asked them to explain the legal basis for forwarding files without first submitting the required report before the F&CC.Taking note of the matter, the MC Commissioner reprimanded the officials concerned, stating that such language should not be used in official files. He also questioned how the files had been processed further without reporting the matter to the committee.Bhatti raised serious concerns regarding the quality of development works being awarded at rates 35% to 40% below the estimated cost.Further, Bhatti pointed out that if a contractor takes up a project at 40% below the estimated rate and expenses such as 18% GST, the contractor’s profit and other costs are deducted and little money remains for the actual execution of the work.He questioned how the required quality of roads and other development works could be maintained under such circumstances.He demanded that appropriate standards be established and that a minimum five-year maintenance clause be included in future road construction tenders.During the meeting, a total of 125 resolutions were discussed and all works under the councillor quota were approved.

headline: Punjab dairy farmers warn of stir over milk price, new breeding policy
content: Dairy farmers in the state have warned of an agitation against the state government over milk procurement prices and the new breeding policy.Progressive Dairy Farmers Association (PDFA) leaders on Monday submitted a memorandum—addressed to Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann—to the Deputy Commissioner’s office, warning of an agitation if their demands are not met by December 5.In the memorandum, the association’s president, Daljit Singh Gill, raised serious concerns over the functioning of private milk procurement companies and Milkfed. The association alleged that while retail milk prices have been increased by Rs 4 to Rs 6 per litre in the market, dairy farmers have not received any share from the benefit.The farmers demanded that the complete increase in milk prices be passed on to producers, arguing that they are struggling to sustain their operations amid rising input costs. According to the association, dairy farmers are facing severe financial pressure due to the continuous increase in the prices of cattle feed, maize, soybean meal, mustard cake, fodder and veterinary medicines. As a result, the cost of milk production has risen significantly even as procurement prices remain inadequate.The association also criticised the state government’s breeding policy, claiming that it has created major obstacles for dairy farmers and artificial insemination workers. The association said the policy is adversely affecting breed improvement programmes and causing losses to the dairy sector.The dairy farmers alleged that stringent manpower requirements for artificial insemination services, strict semen storage norms, additional expenses, excessive paperwork and restrictions on embryo transfer technology have made dairy farming more difficult and costly.The association sought an increase of at least Rs 4 per litre in milk procurement prices and the immediate withdrawal of the new breeding policy.

headline: Money laundering probe: ED summons AAP’s Moga, Dharamkot MLAs, 8 others
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned two AAP MLAs, Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose from Dharamkot and Amandeep Kaur Arora from Moga, and eight others in connection with its probe into a money laundering case against her. Eight persons include some serving and retired Punjab government officials and Arora's family members. The ED summoned the Moga MLA and her husband Rakesh Arora to depose at its Chandigarh Zonal-1 Office for questioning on November 26 and 25, respectively. On November 4, the ED had searched seven properties of the Moga MLA in connection with fraudulent acquisition of government and institutionalised properties and misappropriation of public funds. In a statement issued subsequently, the ED alleged that she and her husband facilitated the siphoning of compensation funds the government gave to locals in Moga district whose land was acquired for constructing a highway. The ED probe stems from the alleged fraudulent mutation of government land acquired for National Highway No 754A acquired in Andraman village of Dharamkot and “wrongful” disbursement of compensation worth at least Rs 1.06 crore for which an FIR was also registered by Moga police at the Dharamkot police station on June 16, 2024. The ED, in a statement, had said that it was also probing “several other properties that were transferred to Moga MLA’s relatives by manipulating revenue records”. According ED sources, the Moga MLA is the principal beneficiary of alleged fraudulent acquisition and transfer of Government, Municipal Corporation, Market Committee and Church Trust properties through relatives and associates. Her husband has been summoned for his alleged involvement in fraudulent property transactions, handling of unaccounted funds and financial affairs of Aashirwaad Hospital. The Dharamkot MLA has been summoned on November 27 for his “beneficial interest” in approximately 2-3 acres at Baggipura, Ludhiana, and alleged involvement in irregularities concerning crematorium land compensation at Dharamkot. The Moga MLA’s father Jaspal Singh has been summoned on November 27 for allegedly holding seven marlas of the Punjab government land at Civil Lines in Moga on behalf of the MLA and her husband. Her brother Valjinder Singh has been summoned on November 30 for his alleged involvement in benami property transactions, handling of cash and acquisition of Market Committee land. Moga MLA’s maternal uncle Harminder Singh has been summoned on December 2 for allegedly acting as a benamidar in acquisition of Market Committee land and facilitating payments towards other properties. Lakhwinder Singh, Partner/Director, M/s Aashirwaad Hospital & De-addiction Centre, the private facility run by her husband, has also been summoned for his alleged involvement in the management of the hospital, unaccounted cash collections, financial transactions and procurement/dispensing of psychotropic medicines. The officials who have been summoned include Nirvair Singh, patwari, for his alleged involvement in manipulation of revenue records, fraudulent mutations, property transfers and withdrawal of compensation funds; Gurdev Singh Dham, former DRO, Moga, for alleged irregularities in assessment and disbursement of compensation under NH-754A, including compensation of approximately Rs 1 crore; and Lakhwinder Singh Gill, former tehsildar, Moga, for his alleged involvement in registration of sale deeds concerning Government, Municipal Corporation and Church Trust lands despite judicial orders and objections. Incidentally, the Moga MLA has been summoned on November 26, the day AAP will sound its poll bugle for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections at the “Khushaal Punjab” rally to be held at the border of Matwani and Nathuwal Jadid villages in Moga, with the party’s national convener Arvind Kejriwal in attendance. Speaking to The Indian Express, Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora said, “I will file an application before the ED for changing the date or the time, given I have to attend the party’s first election rally on November 26, which is being held in my constituency.” Responding to the ED summons, the AAP said, in a statement, “The Enforcement Directorate summoning the Moga MLA on November 26, the same day the Aam Aadmi Party is celebrating its Foundation Day with a historic Maharally for a Khushhaal Punjab in Moga, raises serious questions about the timing and intent of the action.” “This is a politically motivated attempt to target the Aam Aadmi Party and its leaders and disrupt the party’s historic rally. The BJP-led central government is misusing central agencies to target political opponents. AAP will not be intimidated by such tactics,” the ruling party said. Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora, who is also the president of the AAP Women's Wing in Punjab, has been renominated by the party from the Moga seat for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year. After the raids, the Moga MLA had accused the BJP of indulging in a political vendetta, alleging that the 42-hour-long ED raids at her residence included repeated pressure to join the BJP in exchange for a ministerial position. “Despite extensive searches at my residences and hospital, the ED could not recover a single penny and returned empty-handed,” she had said.

headline: Nearly 8k NDPS cases filed in HP in last 4 years: Sukhu | Hindustan Times
content: As many as 7,950 cases were registered, and 12,302 people were arrested under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act in Himachal Pradesh over the last four years, chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said in a statement on Tuesday.The chief minister stressed the need for cooperation from all sections of society to fight against drug abuse. He said police had seized 1,384 kg of charas and 59 kg of chitta.Since the implementation of the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PIT-NDPS) Act, 1988, a total of 225 drug traffickers have been detained, including 159 in 2026 alone. Himachal Pradesh ranks second in the country in terms of preventive detention under this Act, he said in the statement.“Over the past three-and-a-half years, the state government has seized assets worth ₹92 crore acquired through illicit drug trafficking. For the first time in the state, property worth ₹48 lakh, acquired through drug trafficking, has been transferred in the name of the government. Additionally, 86 properties involving encroachments and illegal constructions on government land by NDPS accused persons have been identified. Demolition and eviction proceedings have been completed against 22 of these properties. A dedicated revenue officer is being nominated to ensure the early disposal of the remaining cases,” the statement said.The chief minister said that the government is working with firm commitment to completely eradicate all forms of drugs, including chitta, from the state.“All concerned departments and central agencies have been directed to make the anti-drug campaign more effective through mutual coordination and accountability,” he said.The chief minister said that the fight against drugs is not limited to police action alone; rather, it is being transformed into a mass movement involving the public. “Walkathons are being organised in various districts, with enthusiastic participation from students, teachers, Mahila Mandals, Yuvak Mandals and citizens. The police and special task force have been directed to ensure that action is not restricted to small-scale drug peddlers. Instead, strict action must be taken against major kingpins, their associates, supply networks, financial sources and inter-state connections,” the statement added.Along with strict enforcement and punitive action against drug trafficking, the government is also focusing on the treatment and rehabilitation of people affected by drug abuse.“A police-operated de-addiction and rehabilitation centre for women has been established at Mashobra in Shimla district. Directions have also been issued to hand over the management and operation of the de-addiction centres at Tanda and Bilaspur to the police,” he said.A total of 246 highly drug-affected panchayats have been identified and placed under special monitoring. At the panchayat level, people affected by drug abuse and those involved in drug trafficking are being identified through red, yellow and green categories.“So far, approximately 12,000 individuals have been identified to ensure that those in need are connected with treatment and rehabilitation services, while strict action is taken against drug traffickers,” he said.The state government would soon launch a dedicated WhatsApp chatbot to facilitate the sharing of information related to drug trafficking. Through this platform, citizens will be able to provide information about drug trafficking while keeping their identities confidential. It will also provide information on treatment, counselling and rehabilitation to individuals affected by drug abuse and their family members.

headline: Delhi wakes to poor air as AQI stands at 242, NCR cities fare worse
content: Delhi woke up to another polluted morning on Tuesday, with the city's average Air Quality Index (AQI) at 242 at 7 am, compared with 248 at the same time on Monday, according to real-time data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). PM2.5 remained the prominent pollutant. According to CPCB data, of the 57 monitoring stations in the capital with valid readings, 46 recorded AQI levels above 200, placing them in the 'poor' category, while 10 reported readings above 300, in the 'very poor' category. Sirifort recorded the highest AQI at 336, followed by Ignou, Maidan Garhi, at 333 and North Campus, Delhi University, at 322. Talkatora Garden recorded 321, while NSUT Jaffarpur reported 314. CRRI Mathura Road registered 313, Burari Crossing 307 and ITO 306. Commonwealth Sports Complex and IIT Delhi recorded 304 and 302, respectively. At the other end, IMD Lodhi Road recorded the lowest AQI at 163, followed by Ghoga at 166, Jharoda Kalan at 175 and NSIT Dwarka at 178. These locations were in the 'moderate' category. NCR cities report mixed air quality Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained uneven, with several cities reporting readings in the poor category. Panchgaon in Haryana recorded the highest AQI at 310, followed by Dharuhera at 282 and Gurugram at 277. Bahadurgarh reported an AQI of 249, while Delhi stood at 242. Bhiwadi in Rajasthan recorded 223, while Meerut and Ghaziabad reported 214 each. Noida and Greater Noida both registered 211, followed by Bulandshahr at 205. Sonipat recorded an AQI of 199, while Baghpat reported 182. Faridabad was at 166 and Bharatpur at 156. Among the better-performing NCR cities, Rohtak recorded 125, Hapur 123, Panipat 121 and Palwal 90. Panchgaon records highest AQI nationally Among the 282 cities with valid readings in the CPCB's 7 am dataset, Panchgaon in Haryana recorded the highest AQI at 310. Ballabgarh, also in Haryana, followed at 304, while Sikar in Rajasthan reported 283. Dharuhera recorded an AQI of 282, followed by Gurugram and Khairthal at 277 each. Khanna in Punjab reported 268, while Kiul in Bihar recorded 255. Mandi Gobindgarh in Punjab and Bikaner in Rajasthan registered 254 each. Delhi's AQI of 242 placed it among the more polluted cities in the national list, alongside Baddi in Himachal Pradesh, which also recorded 242. At the other end, Aizawl in Mizoram recorded the lowest AQI at 17, followed by Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 26 and Sivasagar in Assam at 27. Eloor in Kerala and Gangtok in Sikkim reported 30 each, while Puducherry recorded 31. Under the CPCB's National Air Quality Index classification, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'. Transport dominates Delhi's PM2.5 mix, with biomass burning also contributing Biomass burning has featured in discussions around Delhi's PM2.5 pollution, but the latest source-apportionment estimates on the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's (IITM) Air Quality Early Warning System show a more nuanced picture. The system's source-apportionment display for November 23 puts stubble burning's contribution at 0.8 per cent of Delhi's daily mean PM2.5. The largest category was 'Others' at 32 per cent, followed by Delhi transport at 21.5 per cent. The estimates also attribute contributions to sources in neighbouring districts, including Jhajjar at 10.2 per cent and Rohtak at 6.1 per cent. CAQM retains Grap Stage II curbs The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) continues to list Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) as active across Delhi-NCR. Measures under this stage include enhanced mechanised road sweeping, dust suppression and water sprinkling, stricter enforcement of dust-control norms at construction sites, and steps to discourage the use of private vehicles. In a separate move, CAQM has asked Delhi and NCR states to prepare district-level action plans for 2027, with measures aimed at reducing air pollution by 15–20 per cent.

headline: Dense fog alert for 3 Himachal districts, dry spell to continue | Hindustan Times
content: The India Meteorological Department, Shimla, had issued an alert for dense fog at isolated places in Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Mandi districts over the next three days, even as dry weather is expected to prevail until November 28.The IMD said that in certain areas of Bilaspur, Mandi, and Hamirpur districts, visibility may drop to as low as 50 metres due to the fog.“The impact is expected to be most significant during late night and early morning hours. Dense fog is anticipated around the Bhakra Dam in Bilaspur, the Balh and Sundernagar areas of Mandi, and several parts of Hamirpur. In light of this, motorists are advised to exercise caution. Reduced visibility on the roads due to fog may disrupt traffic. Consequently, drivers are advised to maintain lower speeds and use their fog lights,” the MeT department said in a statement.Senior scientist Sandeep Kumar Sharma said the weather would remain dry across the state from November 23 to November 28, with no significant rainfall expected during the period.“The western disturbance that affected the region recently has moved away, and another weather system approaching the country is likely to bring high clouds to Himachal Pradesh but is not expected to cause rainfall in the state,” he said.Gradual dip in daytime tempsThe lowest minimum temperature in the state was recorded at around -3 degrees Celsius in the higher-altitude region of Kukumseri, while Keylong recorded -2 degrees Celsius. Tabo recorded a minimum temperature of around -1.3 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, temperatures in several other areas, including Solan, Bilaspur and Mandi, remained around normal levels.Sharma said daytime temperatures were likely to remain near normal in most parts of the state. “A gradual decline in daytime temperatures is expected after November 27, with the mercury likely to fall by around two to four degrees Celsius in several areas,” he said.75% less rainfall than normal in NovRainfall in November has been 74% below normal. In the districts of Bilaspur, Hamirpur, Sirmaur, and Una, not a single drop of rain has fallen so far this month.Rainfall deficits of 99% have been recorded in Kangra, followed by 98% in Mandi, 97% in Kullu, and 94% in Solan. Shimla has seen 88% less rainfall than normal.

headline: US planning to hike tariffs on India, 15 other countries: Report
content: The US is planning to hike tariffs on China, India and several other countries as early as this week, contending that they supported excess industrial production that hurt American companies, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer is expected to unveil the findings of an investigation his office opened on March 11 against 16 economies, including India, under Section 301 of the 1974 trade law, which allows the president to impose tariffs after finding unfair trade practices. Greer has said those subsidies and other governmental support have created excess industrial capacity in the targeted economies, allowing their firms to flood global markets with cheaper goods, undermining US producers, the WSJ reported. In July, the USTR completed an investigation into forced labour in foreign supply chains, which it said justified tariffs of between 10 and 12.5 per cent on dozens of trading partners, including all 16 of the economies covered by the excess manufacturing probe. The final tariff rates are still unclear, but will be over and above the existing tariff rates.India and the US are negotiating an interim bilateral trade agreement after the framework they had finalised in February went back to the discussion board, with the Supreme Court striking down the International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs imposed last year. India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitor nations such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia.

headline: 144 primary health centres across Mysuru district hit due to severe shortage of medicines, services disru
content: Mysuru: A seven-month shortage of medicines and medical supplies has severely disrupted services at 144 primary health centres (PHCs), including 25 in urban areas, across Mysuru district.Patients have been forced to buy basic medicines for diabetes and hypertension, besides disposable syringes, gloves and IV fluid bags. Supplies of bandages and catheters have also been affected. Patients suffering from diabetes, hypertension, fever and the common cold were severely affected by the shortage of medicines.Delays in state-level tender procurement have been cited as a major reason for the disruption of medical supplies. State govt has been supplying 450 types of medicines, tablets and injections to PHCs, 600 types to community health centres and 800 types to taluk-level govt general public hospitals.Until a few years ago, state govt also received Rs 1 lakh a month from Union govt under National Rural Health Mission for purchasing medicines for each PHC. The sudden stoppage of these grants has also affected patients.As the public hospital authorities prescribe that the patients buy from private pharmacies due to a shortage of medicines and other essentials in the hospital, people across the district depend upon public hospitals, cursing the elected representatives, health authorities and govt for their failure to ease the problem in govt hospitals.District family planning officer and in-charge district health officer Dr Gopinath said that this is a statewide issue; district health authorities had already brought this to the notice of the state health minister, and even state govt had also initiated measures to procure the medicines and essentials to ease the shortages in PHCs. Also, until the district health authorities received the medicines, directions were given to all PHCs to manage the hospitals utilising the locally available funds, drugs and medicines.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mysuru | Silver Rate in Mysuru | Bank Holidays in Mysuru | Public Holidays in MysuruStay updated with the latest Mysuru news. headline: Houthis won’t seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say
content: By Phil Stewart and Timour AzhariWASHINGTON/RIYADH, Nov 24 (Reuters) – Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have pushed as close as 60 km (37 miles) to Aden, the temporary capital of the country’s internationally recognised government, but they will not capture the city, Yemen’s military said on Tuesday. “I’ll speak to you frankly. The situation is not where we want it to be. But it’s not as dire as reported,” Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, spokesperson for Yemen’s armed forces, told a group of reporters via video link. Since fighting resumed in Yemen in July in parallel with the wider Iran war, the Houthis have rapidly advanced in Yemen, seizing territory from the internationally recognised government and its allies, who are backed by Saudi Arabia. The Saudis have carried out airstrikes on Yemen in support of their allies on the ground, while the Houthis have struck Saudi oil targets, airports and office towers. Aden, now the target of Houthi missile and drone strikes, had previously not seen major hostilities since street battles in 2015, soon after the internationally recognised government fled Houthi-run Sanaa and made the port city its base. Government forces inside the city, perched around an extinct volcano jutting into the Indian Ocean, have set up checkpoints, pulled in reinforcements, dug trenches and set up earth barricades on roads to the front line, residents and military officials say.

headline: Jai Ram calls HP government’s temporary job policy a ‘joke on’ youth | Hindustan Times
content: Leader of Opposition and former chief minister Jai Ram Thakur criticised the Himachal Pradesh government’s Engagement Policy 2026, saying it was designed to provide temporary employment to the youth ahead of elections rather than ensure long-term job security.Thakur said the government had failed to fulfil its poll promise of providing employment and was now coming up with these “stopgap” arrangements.Recently, the state government had notified the Engagement Policy-2026 to streamline the recruitment of temporary teachers in government technical educational institutions and address the shortage of teaching staff across the state. Under the new policy, recruitment for temporary teaching positions in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), polytechnics, engineering colleges and pharmacy institutions will be conducted through the Himachal Pradesh State Chayan Ayog on the basis of an open competitive examination. According to the notification, appointments will be made, as per institutional requirements, to the posts of assistant craft instructor, assistant lecturer and junior professor. The existing reservation roster will be followed during recruitment, although no new regular posts will be created under the policy.“Himachal Pradesh had effectively entered an election year. This new policy is a big joke on the youth. The government’s intention appears to be to recruit people in technical education institutions, polytechnic colleges and ITIs through temporary arrangements, keeping the elections in mind,” he said.“This is nothing more than a temporary arrangement. There is no policy for regularising them, no provision for bringing them under contractual employment and no clear framework for re-engagement on the basis of experience. The government is simply trying to buy time and mislead the youth,” he said.Welcoming the alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab, Thakur said both parties shared an emotional relationship that had existed for a long time.“The BJP and the Akali Dal have been alliance partners since 1996, and this relationship was strengthened by Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Lal Krishna Advani. The alliance had broken for some reason, but we are happy that it has now been revived,” he said.BOX BJP announces 12-member core committee for HimachalHimachal Pradesh BJP president Rajeev Bindal on Tuesday announced a 12-member state core committee with two special invitees.The announcement came in accordance with the directives of BJP national president Nitin Nabin. A notification has been issued in this regard, the party said in a statement.The state core committee includes former BJP national president and Union minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, the party’s state president Dr Rajeev Bindal, former chief minister and LoP Jai Ram Thakur, state general secretary (organisation) Siddharthan and Lok Sabha MP and former Union minister Anurag Thakur.The other members are former state president and Lok Sabha MP Suresh Kashyap, MLA and former state president Satpal Singh Satti, Lok Sabha MP Rajeev Bhardwaj, state vice-president and MLA Vipin Singh Parmar, Rajya Sabha MP and state general secretary Dr Sikander Kumar and state general secretaries Payal Vaidya and Sanjeev Katwal.Additionally, BJP state in-charge Shrikant Sharma and state co-in-charge Darshana Singh have been appointed special invitees to the core committee.

headline: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
content: The government is looking to part sale its equity shareholding in IIFCL along with a fresh issue of shares by the company in the initial public offering (IPO), which is likely by the end of the current fiscal year, an official said.The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval.Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO.Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI.As of March 31, 2026, IIFCL's gross sanctions stood at over Rs 3.64 lakh crore to about 890 projects under direct lending, takeout finance and refinance, credit enhancement, InVIT and bonds. Cumulative disbursements under these schemes stood at over Rs 1.89 lakh crore.The proceeds from the government stake sale in IIFCL will add to the government's disinvestment kitty. In the current fiscal year, the disinvestment proceeds stand at Rs 55,757 crore so far.

headline: ISRO aims to end the year with first operational launch of SSLV
content: THE INDIAN Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to end the year, which saw fewer missions following the back-to-back failures of its workhorse PSLV, with a key mission — the first operational launch of SSLV. “We are aiming to launch another SSLV mission in December,” confirmed a senior ISRO official. The space agency needs to carry out two successful development missions before a launcher is declared operational. It has already carried out three development flights of SSLV so far, with the first one, on August 7, 2022, falling short of placing the satellites in the intended orbit. The second and the third development flights, in February 2023 and August 2024, were declared successful. ISRO may also see another launch of its workhorse PSLV with a modified third stage soon, hinted ISRO chairman V Narayanan on the sidelines of the recently concluded India International Space Conclave. “We have already conducted one ground test and will be ready to launch the PSLV after another ground test,” he told The Indian Express. The space agency conducted the first ground test after making the requisite changes following the failures of PSLV C-61 in May 2025 and PSLV-C62 in January 2026. Both missions failed due to anomalies in the third and the uppermost stage of the rocket. According to ISRO, the reasons behind the failure of the two missions were different. After the failures, the third-stage configuration was revisited comprehensively and changes were made with respect to design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and quality checks that followed. The design was strengthened and essential improvements were also made to the nozzle configuration. The Indian Express on Monday reported that the launch of the privately built PSLV-N1 may have to wait until after the launch of ISRO’s own PSLV. Narayanan on Tuesday said the industry built PSLV will be launched in the first quarter of 2027. As against a planned 17 launches for FY 2026-27 — including at least four PSLV and five SSLV missions — as per ISRO’s annual report, the space agency was able to achieve only three launches this year, including the failed PSLV-C62. The space agency launched the earth observation satellite EOS-5 in September and much-awaited navigation satellite NVS-03 in October, bringing the country’s navigation system back online.

headline: J&K health minister reviews winter healthcare preps, stresses maternal care | Hindustan Times
content: Health minister Sakeena Itoo has asked officials to advance the survey of pregnant women living in remote and snowbound areas of Kashmir so that they can be shifted to safer locations closer to healthcare institutions in case of heavy snowfall.Reviewing the winter preparedness of government medical colleges (GMCs) across the Kashmir division on Monday, Itoo took stock of healthcare arrangements, emergency response mechanisms, availability of essential medicines, medical equipment, manpower and patient-care facilities to ensure uninterrupted healthcare delivery during the harsh winter months, an official spokesperson said.The meeting was attended by senior health officials, principals of GMCs and medical superintendents of all district and sub-district hospitals across the Kashmir division.The minister stressed the need for comprehensive planning, particularly for people residing in far-flung, remote and snowbound areas, where severe weather conditions and road closures often pose challenges in accessing timely medical attention.Giving special emphasis to maternal healthcare, Itoo directed the officials to conduct a comprehensive advance survey of expectant mothers residing in snowbound and inaccessible areas and maintain an updated, district-wise database of such cases.“Identify expectant mothers, particularly those nearing their delivery dates or requiring specialised medical attention, well before the onset of severe weather conditions,” the minister said.

headline: 23 injured in car bomb attack outside Colombian government offices amid rising armed violence | World News
content: A bomb exploded outside regional government offices in the Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring 23 people, authorities said Tuesday, as a wave of violence involving rebel groups and drug gangs spreads to urban areas.The explosion occurred Monday night in Villavicencio, a city with a population of half a million people. Authorities initially reported 19 injuries before raising the toll to 23. They said the attack remained under investigation.During the first three months of his term, President Abelardo de la Espriella has increased the use of air strikes against drug gangs and rebel groups in rural areas and acted on military intelligence to capture several mid-level commanders.Also read: New Colombian president announces anti-migrant crackdownRebel groups have responded with drone attacks on police stations and military bases around the country, and have also attacked their targets with rockets made from gas cylinders and by detonating roadside bombs.Villavicencio is a major agricultural and commercial hub on the edge of the Amazon rainforest, where rebel groups have long fought over control of drug trafficking routes, as well as legal businesses like cattle ranches and palm plantations.Alexander Baquero, the mayor of Villavicencio, told Colombian radio station Blu that he believed the attack could have been waged by a FARC holdout group that operates in Meta province and was seeking retaliation for strikes conducted against it by the military.Also read: Venezuela, Colombia to collaborate on border security following kidnappingsColombia this week is marking the 10th anniversary of a historic peace agreement between the government and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, or FARC, in which more than 14,000 fighters laid down their weapons.The peace deal initially brought relief to rural communities that had been caught in the fighting between the military and the rebels. But violence has once again increased in some rural areas, as smaller drug gangs and rebel groups attempt to take over territory that was once controlled by the FARC.On Tuesday, President de la Espriella vowed to intensify operations against rebel groups. In a post on X, the conservative leader said that the "narco-terrorists" behind the attack in Villavicencio will “pay for every drop of blood they have shed, and for every building they have destroyed.”

headline: J&K government approves land for fruit, vegetable markets in 3 districts | Hindustan Times
content: The Jammu and Kashmir government on Tuesday approved transferring 320 kanals (40 acres) of land to the agriculture production department to set up modern fruit and vegetable markets in Kulgam, Baramulla, and Pulwama districts.The initiative will strengthen market access for farmers, ensure transparent pricing, minimise post-harvest losses, promote value addition and generate local employment, providing a significant boost to J&K’s horticulture and agriculture sectors, the Chief Minister’s Office said in a post on X.The proposed sites include 50 kanals at Palhallan village in Tehsil Pattan of Baramulla district, 20 kanals and 4 marlas at Nowdal village in Tehsil Tral of Pulwama district, and 250 kanals at Kulgam village in Tehsil and district Kulgam.“The initiative will strengthen market access for farmers, ensure transparent pricing, minimise post-harvest losses, promote value addition and generate local employment, providing a significant boost to J&K’s horticulture and agriculture sectors,” the office of the chief minister said in a post on X.The proposed markets will provide farmers, including small and marginal growers and women farmers, improved access to organised marketing facilities and better opportunities to secure remunerative prices for their produce.“The facilities will also incorporate improved arrangements for grading, sorting, storage and transportation, helping reduce post-harvest losses, minimise marketing costs and ensure the availability of fresh produce to consumers,” an official spokesperson said.

headline: After 63 years of inception, first major overhaul for MCD-run hospital in East Delhi
content: After 63 years of operations, Swami Dayanand Hospital run by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) in East Delhi is set to get its first major infrastructure overhaul in two phases. An initial amount of Rs 40 crore has been approved in principle for the estimated Rs 190-crore project for the first phase of the new 250-bed modern integrated inpatient ward, ICU & Emergency Block, according to MCD sources. Dr Sunita Kujur, Medical Superintendent of the Hospital spoke to The Indian Express, about the need of the new overhaul. “The hospital has an influx of 3,000 patients daily. So, it has become more than necessary to replace the Old Ward block which was constructed during the hospital’s inception in 1963. The newly constructed block will come equipped with all the modern facilities. With the addition of new CT scan and MRI facilities under the PPP (public-private partnership) model, patients will not have to depend on other hospitals for those services, and we expect the ward block to be completed within two years. We expect the entire project to be completed within the next two years,” she said. Concern over safety The development comes after the hospital’s ward block was declared structurally unsafe following safety audits. As per MCD sources, the building, which has been in continuous use since 1963, developed severe water seepage, among other issues. These structural defects have made routine repairs both technically unsafe and economically unviable, prompting the hospital administration to propose demolishing the existing structure and replacing it with a modern healthcare facility. The project will be executed in two phases with the hospital administration seeking a capital grant-in-aid from the Trans Yamuna Area Development Board to fund the redevelopment. It is a non-statutory advisory body constituted by the Government of Delhi in 1994 to plan, coordinate, and recommend infrastructure development in the Trans-Yamuna (East Delhi) region. Officials said the two phases are intended to strengthen public healthcare infrastructure in East and North East Delhi, particularly for residents of Shahdara, Seemapuri, Nand Nagri and Dilshad Garden, who depend on the hospital for affordable treatment. Two-phased development The first phase, estimated to cost Rs 109.17 crore, will involve the construction of a basement-plus-six-storey integrated inpatient, emergency and intensive care block spread across 6,300 square metres. The second phase, estimated to cost around Rs 42 crore, will involve the construction of a ground-plus-three-storey integrated diagnostic centre on a 2,970-square-metre plot that will become available after the demolition of the Old Ward Block. The proposed centre will have a total super built-up area of 4,752 square metres and bring several diagnostic facilities under one roof. The addition of emergency, critical care, and diagnostic facilities is also expected to reduce the need for patients to seek investigations and specialised services at other hospitals. The proposed block will have 250 beds, with dedicated wards for different medical specialities. These will include a 50-bed orthopaedics ward, 60-bed surgical ward, 60-bed medicine ward, 60-bed paediatrics ward and a 32-bed ward for eye, ENT and dermatology patients, excluding gynecology wards. The ground floor will house the Emergency Department and intensive care facilities, including a covered ambulance drop-off area, separate triage zones, two modular emergency operation theatres, and a centrally monitored ICU with 24–30 beds.

headline: US prepares fresh tariff hikes on China and India over industrial subsidies; announcement expected this week
content: The Trump administration is preparing another round of tariff increases targeting China and several other major trading partners, with India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union among the economies that could be affected. Higher levies to target excess industrial capacity overseas are expected this week.The proposed move follows a US investigation into government subsidies that Washington DC believes give foreign manufacturers an unfair advantage over American businesses, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.Citing people familiar with the matter, the newspaper reported that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer mpcould announce the findings of the months-long investigation as early as this week. The probe covers China, the EU and 14 other economies, although the timing of the announcement remains subject to change.The fresh duties could affect a broad range of products entering the US, potentially reopening trade disputes with countries that had already negotiated agreements with President Donald Trump's administration.Why is Trump targeting China, India and other economies?At the centre of the investigation is the financial and policy support that governments provide to their domestic industries.The Trump administration argues that such support has encouraged manufacturers in several countries to produce more goods than their home markets can absorb. This surplus, it claims, is then sold overseas at lower prices, putting American manufacturers at a disadvantage.Greer has previously argued that these government-backed advantages have contributed to excess industrial capacity and disrupted global markets.The US Trade Representative's office declined to comment on the expected announcement, while the White House did not respond to requests for comment, the WSJ reported.How much could countries pay in fresh US tariffs?The final tariff rates have not yet been determined. However, US officials have indicated that they could be similar to the rates introduced by Trump in 2025, before the Supreme Court struck down his initial round of tariffs in February 2026.According to people familiar with the discussions cited by the WSJ, countries that had reached trade agreements with Washington could retain rates reflecting those arrangements.The EU, Japan and South Korea could face tariffs of 15% or less. India and Vietnam, however, may encounter higher rates depending on the terms of their respective trade agreements with the US.China is expected to face a comparatively higher rate because American officials consider its industrial subsidies particularly extensive.Which products could face the additional duties?The proposed tariffs are expected to cover most products exported by the economies under investigation.However, certain goods, including steel, aluminium and automobiles, could be excluded as they already face separate duties imposed under US national security provisions.The administration is also considering measures that would allow it to increase tariffs further if countries fail to address industrial overcapacity or introduce policy changes during future trade negotiations, the WSJ reported.Fresh tariffs could add to existing trade pressureThe proposed duties could come on top of another set of tariffs announced in July. That separate measure sought to penalise economies that fail to prevent the trade of goods produced using forced labour.The earlier action proposed additional duties ranging from 10% to 12.5% on products from around 60 economies. However, it is currently facing a legal challenge.The latest tariff plans also emerge amid growing scrutiny of Washington's China policy. The WSJ report noted that the expected announcement could come as the administration faces questions from lawmakers over its handling of China following allegations involving the smuggling of advanced Nvidia AI chips into the country.Neither the final tariff rates nor the precise timeline for their implementation has been confirmed.

headline: West Bengal pitches film policy, subsidies at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa
content: West Bengal made its debut at WAVES Film Bazaar, a major segment of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), in Goa. Minister of State for Information and Cultural Affairs and Tourism, Purnima Chakraborty, attended the event, accompanied by MLA Hiran Chatterjee. The West Bengal Pavilion attracted a steady stream of visitors. Producers, directors and filmmakers enquired about shooting in the state, facilities and government support, the minister said. At the pavilion, Chakraborty outlined the state's plans for the film sector. She said the government is working to simplify and speed up shooting permissions, so filmmakers do not face unnecessary delays while planning shoots. Chakraborty also highlighted proposed subsidies and other incentives for film production. She said these measures are intended to make West Bengal a more attractive destination for producers from across the country. During the event, she held discussions with representatives of other participating states. They exchanged views on their film policies, shooting infrastructure and initiatives to promote their film industries. She said the platform gave West Bengal an opportunity to present its cinematic heritage before a wider audience. The state has a long tradition in cinema, which continues to shape Indian filmmaking. The state also highlighted its film infrastructure and investment opportunities, with focus on positioning itself as a destination for film production and film tourism.

headline: After Akhilesh Yadav pens conciliatory note to Congress, SP springs a surprise
content: Hours after a contentious seat-sharing meeting between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP), triggered by the latter’s offer of just 26 seats, the Akhilesh Yadav-led party announced its first list of five candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections late on Tuesday. The list includes candidates for two seats in Saharanpur district in western UP that the Congress and its working president Imran Masood were eyeing. One of the SP's picks is a political rival of Masood. — Samajwadi Party (@samajwadiparty) November 24, 2026 Earlier in the day, the discussions began on a heated note over the SP responding to the Congress’s initial offer of 131 seats with just 26 constituencies, including just one from the Amethi-Rae Bareli belt that is considered the pocket borough of the Gandhi family. At the outset, Congress leaders at the meeting accused the SP of being “unserious” and leaking information to the media. “We will give a formal statement soon. But for now, we can say that this is infuriating. How can they offer us one seat in Amethi and Rae Bareli? How can they give us a list of 26 seats out of 403? We have contested 17 in the Lok Sabha out of 80,” said a senior Congress leader who participated in the talks. Hours later, Akhilesh Yadav took to X to pen a long message to the Congress, saying his party remains open to discussing seats and that winnability should be the main factor driving the negotiations. “We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our ‘alliance’ wins in most constituencies. Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose,” Akhilesh wrote, adding, “Therefore, in addition to the 26 seats from the priority list your team provided that we have discussed today, please identify and send us all other potential seats. Then we will sit down together and assess which seats, and which candidates for those seats, are in a winning position. Based on our assessment and the mathematical equation for victory, we may also be able to tell the Congress about many winnable seats it has not even considered for some reason.” The SP president said when the leaders meet, the discussion should be about the INDIA bloc’s candidates and not of the Congress or the SP. “We do not want candidates to be imposed on one another within the alliance; they should be decided by consensus. Only then will your votes and ours transfer to one another, ensuring our victory…,” he wrote. ‘Pact will be finalised soon’ The note from Akhilesh came against the backdrop of heated discussions held for the second straight day at the home of Congress MP Pramod Tiwari, who is the father of UP Congress president Aradhana Misra Mona. “There were some moments when discussions turned heated. Like when the Congress wanted us to concede seats we had given to the RLD (Rashtriya Lok Dal) and the SBSP (Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party) in 2022. These two are caste-based parties. Giving these seats to the Congress would mean a defeat for the alliance,” said an SP leader. SP sources accused the Congress of making “unreasonable” demands and struggling to base its demands on a formula. “Even during Monday’s meeting, we asked the Congress leaders to give us a formula on which they are asking for 131 seats. For around 30 seats, they said that it was those where the party led in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. But what about the other 90? These are crucial elections and they have to come up with a formula for asking us for seats,” said a leader. After the meeting, SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, who is heading the party’s negotiation team, said the discussions had been positive and expressed confidence that the talks would be finalised “in the next two meetings”. “We have offered two seats which the Congress won, four seats where it finished second in 2022, and 20 other seats where we (SP) had secured 60,000-70,000 votes, while the Congress had received only around 2,000 votes," he said. The AICC’s UP in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, said the dates for the next two meetings would be decided soon. Sources indicated that they could resume on November 27 following a break because of the engagement ceremony of Misra’s daughter on Wednesday. While the Congress was irked by the SP’s offer, by the end of the day it had revised its demand to 120 constituencies, dropping some seats currently held by the SP. SP's candidates In Saharanpur, the SP has fielded its sitting MLA Ashu Malik, a rival of Imran Masood, who wields influence in the region. Over the past few months, Masood has made remarks about Akhilesh Yadav that have not gone down well in the SP, party insiders said. The party has also nominated its sitting MLA from Behat in Saharanpur district, Umar Ali Khan. Masood, a former SP leader who left the party after being denied a ticket from Behat in 2012, was eyeing both the constituencies. The other seats where the SP has named candidates are: Kairana (Shamli district), where MP Iqra Choudhary’s brother and three-time sitting MLA Nahid Hasan has been renominated; sitting Amroha MLA Mehboob Ali; and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur in east UP. Sources, meanwhile, said the 26 seats offered by the SP had been chosen based on a distinct formula: Mathura, Kheragarh (Agra), Jagdishpur (Amethi), and Kidwai Nagar (Kanpur), where the Congress finished second in 2022, and the only two it had won last time. These two constituencies are Rampur Khas (Pratapgarh), which is Misra’s constituency, and Pharenda (Maharajganj). The 20 other seats the SP has offered are Baghpat, Modinagar (Ghaziabad), Hapur, Jewar (Gautam Budh Nagar), Syana (Bulandshahr), Khurja (Bulandshahr), Khair (Aligarh), Iglas (Hathras), Mant (Mathura), Agra North (Agra), Fatehpur Sikri (agra), Bilgram-Mallanwan (Hardoi), Govind Nagar (Kanpur), Nanpara (Bahraich), Gorakhpur City, Khajani (Sant Kabir Nagar), Padrauna (Kushinagar), Fazilnagar (Kushinagar), Pindra (Varanasi), and Varanasi Cantonment. Of these 20 constituencies, 11 are in west UP, where the SP is considered to be relatively weaker organisationally compared to the other regions in the state, two are in central UP, and seven are in east UP. The BJP won the 11 western UP seats in 2022. The Jayant Chaudhary-led RLD, then an SP ally, was the runner-up in seven. The BSP finished second in two seats, while the SP came second in two. Of the two central UP seats, the SP was the runner-up in Bilgram-Mallanwan, while in Govind Nagar, it lost by 80,896 votes. In the seven east UP seats, the SP finished second in all. All constituencies went to the NDA, with the BJP taking six and the Apna Dal (Soneylal) one (Nanpara). Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s Gorakhpur Urban constituency is among these seats.

headline: First DMK & now TVK: Tamil Nadu govt defies court-ordered lighting of Karthigai deepam at 'deepathoon'
content: Chennai: Karthigai Deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillayar Temple atop the Thiruparankundram hills in Madurai on Tuesday evening, as per the 150-year-old tradition, and not at the Deepathoon as per the orders of the Supreme Court. The ruling TVK government stood firm in its decision not to change the customs and light the Deepam at the Deepathoon (stone pillar) — which is very close to the Sikkander Badusha dargah in the hills — despite the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court reminding the administration on Tuesday evening to comply with the orders of the Supreme Court. The Madurai Bench intervened in the matter after several people pleaded before it against imposition of prohibitory orders in Madurai District. The Supreme Court had on November 20 stayed the Madras High Court allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam on the Deepathoon but asked the lamp to be lit atop the Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time measure. This is the second consecutive year that the Tamil Nadu government — the DMK last year and the TVK this year — has defied a court order to “preserve law and order” and to “prevent communal tensions. With this, the TVK government may face contempt proceedings before the Supreme Court since its orders were not implemented. .Karthigai Deepam row: Scuffle in Thirupparankundram as Hindu outfits stage protest as lamp not lit on 'Deepathoon'.The stand taken by TVK was not entirely surprising as the government contended before the Supreme Court that it cannot change the customs and traditions based on demands from individuals or organisations. The ruling party was also under intense pressure from alliance partners such as Congress, VCK, CPI(M), CPI, and IUML, whose support is crucial for the survival of the government, to defy the Supreme Court order. “The Karthigai Maha Deepam has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillayar Temple, which sits just above the main deity at Thiruparankundram (Lord Murugan),” Law Minister C T R Nirmal Kumar wrote on his X page. It was followed by a statement from the temple which said the decision to lit the Deepam at Uchipillayar Temple was taken by the trustees at a meeting held Tuesday afternoon. As the Deepam was not lit at the Deepathoon, a large number of right-wing protestors gathered outside Sri Subramaniya Swamy Temple in Thiruparankundram demanding that the Supreme Court orders be complied with. .Karthigai Deepam lamp lighting issue: Police detain BJP leader L Murugan.They clashed with the Madurai Police and tried to break barricades — almost all senior leaders of the BJP were taken into preventive detention and were released only after the Madurai Bench ordered their immediate release. While the allies welcomed the government’s decision not to follow the Supreme Court order, the BJP accused the TVK of “indulging in appeasement politics much like the DMK.” The DMK government under then Chief Minister M K Stalin had refused to allow the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam on the Deepathoon on December 3, 2025, as per the directions of Justice G R Swaminathan of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, citing law and order issues. Thiruparankundram hill has been a haven of religious coexistence and communal harmony for centuries, hosting the Subramaniya Swamy temple, Kasi Viswanathan temple, and Sikkander Badusha dargah. However, in February 2025, Hindu organisations launched a protest after Lok Sabha MP Nawaz Kani allegedly consumed meat at the hills – since then, the temple has been at the centre of a row though the residents of the village continue to live in harmony.
