headline: Chhattisgarh CM calls for mass movement against human trafficking, domestic violence
content: Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai has said social evils such as human trafficking and domestic violence have no place in a civilised society and called for collective efforts to turn the fight against them into a mass movement. The government has been working with sensitivity and commitment to ensure the safety of women and girls and safeguard their dignity and rights, the chief minister said on Monday while addressing the concluding session of a one-day state-level training-cum-workshop on human trafficking and domestic violence at Pandit Ravishankar Shukla University in Raipur. He said eliminating human trafficking and domestic violence is not possible through the efforts of the government or any single institution alone, and requires the entire society to work together. "Taking a collective pledge against human trafficking and domestic violence and turning it into a mass movement is the need of the hour," the Chief Minister said. Praising the Chhattisgarh State Commission for Women for organising the workshop, Sai said the ideas and suggestions would help make the existing system for women's safety more effective.

headline: 75-year-old man, 63-year-old woman find love at Bilaspur old age home
content: Apna Ghar, an old age home in Bilaspur, is witnessing celebrations like never before. Two of its residents, 75-year-old Kanhiya Lal and 63-year-old Sabina, have decided to tie the knot, with their fellow residents singing and dancing to celebrate the occasion.“We will have the wedding tomorrow at Apna Ghar with all the rituals. The haldi and mehendi ceremonies are currently underway, and everyone here is busy celebrating the occasion,” said Prakash Chand Bansal, chairman of the Manav Seva Trust, which runs the old age home.Like many residents of old age homes, Kanhiya Lal and Sabina came to the facility under difficult circumstances, with no one to look after them.Kanhiya Lal, who hails from Mandi district, became deeply distressed after losing his wife a few years ago and reportedly started living in the forest. Sabina, meanwhile, hails from Bengal. She somehow reached Shimla about four years ago. As she appeared somewhat disoriented, the police took her to Nari Niketan in Mashobra, near Shimla. She was later shifted to the old age home in Bilaspur.Distressed by the loss of their loved ones and other difficult circumstances, the two gradually found comfort in each other’s company.“Although they didn’t tell us anything, we observed that they were spending a lot of time in each other’s company and would do most activities together,” Bansal said.He further said the couple was initially reluctant and embarrassed to admit their feelings for each other but eventually opened up and expressed their desire to get married.“They had nothing to look forward to in life when they came here. So, it is really heartening that they have found love in each other and have decided to rebuild their broken lives,” Bansal said.There is more reason to celebrate, as both are now doing well, thanks to the care and support they have received at the old age home, along with the love and companionship they have found in each other.

headline: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ for M365 core service health following global Outlook outage, internal memos show | Hindustan Times
content: Microsoft has declared a “code red” for the health of its Microsoft 365 core services following an outage on November 12, Reuters reported, citing internal memos. The move signals increased attention to service reliability after the disruption.The company is now reviewing how its teams identify technical problems, manage major outages and restore services. The decision follows a 24-hour disruption that affected customers across several countries, including the United States, Australia and Japan. Trading firms faced delays, while airline communications were also disrupted.Microsoft traced the outage to a Windows scalability defect that had gone unnoticed after being introduced in July. The company clarified that the incident was not caused by a cyberattack or AI agents. CEO Satya Nadella also apologized publicly for the disruption.Also Read: Microsoft President warns global technology outage risks could persist for months amid security upgradesMicrosoft reviews its response to the outageThe incident affected several products, including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and its Copilot AI assistant. Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described it as the most damaging service incident in Exchange Online's history in a memo to employees on Friday.He highlighted how many customers had lost access to email for an extended period. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote.Another memo from Amanda Silver, Microsoft's corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, pointed to problems faced by engineers while trying to understand the situation. She described the response as working through a “fog of war”.According to Silver, engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats during the outage. However, information was spread across different internal tracking systems, making it difficult for teams to keep track of technical findings and decisions.Silver also referred to comments from Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform. During a review, he reportedly noted that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures”.Also Read: Satya Nadella says founders are 'not gods' following Jensen Huang's Nvidia exitNew targets for faster recoveryAs part of the Code Red effort, Microsoft has outlined five areas of work. These include managing heavy system loads, dividing traffic across different regions and improving the tools used to restore services.The company has also set a target of resolving future worldwide service disruptions within one hour. It plans to use AI agents to help engineers examine system data and identify problems more quickly.Henderson will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team to monitor progress, along with weekly reviews of the work.The company is also looking at how quickly urgent software fixes reach users worldwide. In an earlier memo reviewed by Reuters, Henderson raised concerns that some critical updates had taken too long to deploy. He cited one case in which an urgent production fix needed five to six days to reach users globally.He wrote that the goal for the most urgent security fixes should be to move from identifying a problem to safely deploying a solution worldwide within an hour.A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters that the company was working to apply lessons from the outage and improve its ability to prevent future disruptions.

headline: Breakaway Akali factions allege Dera hand in SAD-BJP reunion, warn of backlash
content: The renewed alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and BJP has triggered sharp reactions from opposition parties. Breakaway Akali factions have alleged that Dera Sacha Sauda played a role in bringing the two parties together.The Akali Dal-Waris Punjab De and SAD (Punar Surjit) have made Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh a key target in their attack on SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, reviving the controversy surrounding the Akali leadership’s handling of the Dera chief and the sacrilege incidents.Dakha MLA and Akali Dal-Waris Punjab De leader, Manpreet Singh Ayali, who parted ways with SAD, went a step further, alleging that Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh was instrumental in facilitating the alliance.“Till recently, the Akali Dal was blaming Waris Punjab De and Amritpal Singh, calling them BJP’s B-team. What has changed now? SAD has itself become the A-team of NDA. People are watching everything. The party stands to lose whatever remains of its vote bank,” Ayali said, adding that the alliance would fail to deliver electoral gains and the two parties would suffer a major defeat.Former Akal Takht jathedar and SAD (Punar Surjit) president, Giani Harpreet Singh, alleged that by entering into an alliance with the Badal-led Akali Dal, the BJP had become complicit in the latter’s alleged wrongdoings against the Sikh community — be it inaction in sacrilege cases, not holding election to SGPC for nearly 15 years, or not releasing the Sikh political prisoners, the Bandi Singhs.Meanwhile, sensing the possibility of SAD and BJP joining hands, the breakaway SAD (Punar Surjit), the Amritpal Singh-led Akali Dal-Waris Punjab De and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) have also been exploring an electoral understanding.The political realignment comes nearly 10 days after Giani Harpreet Singh, addressing a public meeting at Rehru Sahib Gurdwara in Sahnewal, launched an attack on Sukhbir Badal and ruled out any alliance with SAD. He had said his party would oppose any political outfit that joins hands with the Sukhbir-led Akali Dal.

headline: Borders can’t divide culture, affection: Hamza Sharif at Nankana Sahib calls for India-Pakistan peace
content: Calling for improved relations between India and Pakistan, Mian Muhammad Hamza Shehbaz Sharif, the former chief minister of the Punjab province in Pakistan, has urged both neighbouring countries to resolve differences through peace, tolerance and mutual respect.Hamza Sharif attended Guru Nanak Dev’s birth anniversary celebrations along with Sikh sangat that had poured in from all over the globe at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, in Pakistan. He conveyed greetings on behalf of Pakistan’s Prime Minister and his father, Shehbaz Sharif, emphasising that Guru Nanak’s timeless message of love, equality, service and humanity is relevant for the entire world.Recalling former Indian prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s visit to Pakistan and his message of goodwill, he appealed for renewed efforts to strengthen friendship between the neighbouring nations.He strongly advocated the continued opening of Kartarpur Corridor, assuring the Sikh community that Pakistan welcomes pilgrims with open arms. He encouraged Sikhs around the world to visit and help preserve their sacred shrines located in Pakistan.Referring to Guru Nanak’s teaching “Kirat Karo, Naam Japo, Vand Chhako” (earn an honest living, remember God and share with others), he described them as profound principles for a meaningful life. He added that Islam also promotes similar values of compassion and harmony.Reflecting on his 25-year political journey with the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) and service in various public offices, Hamza Sharif said the most important lesson he had learned was the spirit of sharing and helping others. True wealth, he said, lies not in accumulating but in distributing one’s blessings among those in need, a practice that brings peace in this world and rewards in the hereafter.During his address, he also recalled stories told by his grandfather, Mian Muhammad Sharif, about Amritsar and his ancestral village of Jati Umra. Looking at the gathering, he said he felt as though he was speaking to members of his own extended family.Speaking about global conflicts, he noted that while the world continues to face tensions and wars, lasting solutions can only emerge through dialogue. “Weapons cannot achieve what a few words of love and understanding can,” he remarked.Hamza Sharif asserted that minorities in Pakistan enjoy the same rights as all other citizens and said he did not believe in differentiating people on the basis of religion. He stressed that everyone is equal and urged people to follow Guru Nanak’s golden principles, saying such values could earn global respect and admiration.Referring again to Jati Umra, he said that while borders may divide land, they cannot divide culture, affection and human relationships. He recalled how fondly his grandfather remembered his roots and offered prayers for the prosperity and well-being of the Sikh community.He concluded by assuring the congregation that difficulties faced by pilgrims would be addressed and expressed hope that future generations would carry forward Guru Nanak’s message of love, peace and harmony, allowing stronger bonds of friendship to flourish on both sides of the border.

headline: German Chancellor dials PM Modi, holds talks on trade, defence
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Tuesday that he spoke to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and they discussed ways to “unlock new opportunities in trade and investment, defence and advanced technologies”. After the conversation, Modi said in a post on X, “Had a productive conversation with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. We reviewed the growing momentum in the India-Germany Strategic Partnership and discussed ways to unlock new opportunities in trade and investment, defence and advanced technologies.” “India and Germany will also continue to work closely together to address global challenges and promote peace, stability and a rules-based international order,” he said. According to a readout by the PMO, PM Modi received a telephone call on Tuesday from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “The two leaders reviewed progress in the India-Germany Strategic Partnership and expressed satisfaction at the sustained momentum in bilateral engagements,” it said. “As India and Germany celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across key sectors, including defence and advanced technologies. They noted that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement would unlock several new opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment,” it said. It said that the leaders exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest. They agreed to continue working closely together to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order. “They also emphasised the importance of continued cooperation at multilateral fora in addressing contemporary global challenges,” it said. They had last met in June this year on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Evian, France, and this was their first meeting after the Chancellor's visit to India in January this year. Chancellor Merz had invited the PM for the 8th India-Germany Inter-Governmental Consultations scheduled later this year in Germany, but that could not take place. Efforts are now underway to hold it next year.

headline: Jharkhand health minister urges PM Modi to regulate airfares
content: Ranchi: Amid the rising airfares hampering commoners’ travel plans ahead of the winter holiday season, Jharkhand health minister Irfan Ansari wrote a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking a policy to regulate airfares.The move comes after Ansari had to pay around Rs 31,000 for a flight from Ranchi to Delhi on Tuesday to attend Jharkhand Day celebrations at the trade fair being organised at the Bharat Mandapam.In his letter, Ansari highlighting the financial burden caused by exorbitant fare hike, asked that while his travel cost will be borne by the state govt, how would a middle class family arrange the money if they had to take a trip.Citing the case of a woman, whom he met at the airport and who needed to reach her ailing husband in Chandigarh, Ansari wrote, “The woman broke down on hearing the airfares on offer. I arranged her ticket so that she could reach her husband. Like her, many families are forced to undertake urgent journeys due to illness, accidents, or other emergencies. How will they afford such travel if airfares remain so high?”Urging the PM to direct the civil aviation ministry to set guidelines to regulate airfares, the minister said, “A ceiling should be imposed on airfares, and sudden and arbitrary fare hikes by airlines should be regulated. There should be special concessional fares for patients and their family members travelling during medical emergencies.”Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

headline: ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat – Hyderabad Walks’: Kishan Reddy urges Telangana govt to protect govt land parcels from indiscriminate sale and establish playgrounds in every village and locality to keep youngsters away from drugs and other addictions
content: Hyderabad: Union coal and mines minister G Kishan Reddy has urged Telangana govt to protect govt land parcels from indiscriminate sale and establish playgrounds in every village and locality to keep youngsters away from drugs and other addictions. Addressing a media conference during ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat – Hyderabad Walks’, he said providing sports facilities and encouraging physical activity were essential to safeguarding country’s youth, which he described as its biggest asset.Kishan Reddy said fight against drugs should become a mass movement involving parents, teachers, media organisations and citizens, rather than remain confined to police and govt agencies. He said the Centre was pursuing a target of making India drug-free by 2029, with manufacturers and suppliers being primary targets.Kishan Reddy urged Telangana govt to provide youngsters recovering from addiction opportunities to resume education and secure employment.While those involved in manufacturing and supplying drugs would face strict action, young people consuming drugs should be treated with sympathy and helped to overcome addiction rather than stigmatised, he said.Kishan Reddy said Centre planned to increase number of rehabilitation centres across country from 300 to 2,000 to provide treatment, particularly to youngsters from poor families. He also called for corporate organisations and voluntary agencies to support rehabilitation efforts.He said the Centre was strengthening intelligence and enforcement along borders to prevent drug smuggling and planned to reach 50 crore youngsters through awareness programmes. headline: With his majority at stake, Vijay sides with allies, risks contempt over Madurai lamp
content: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay faced a choice on Tuesday. Allow a lamp to be lit on a stone pillar in Madurai, as the Supreme Court had directed, and risk a rupture with the parties that keep him in office. Or stand with his allies and risk contempt proceedings. By 6 pm, his answer was visible from the foot of Thirupparankundram hill. The festival flame burned at its customary place near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple. The pillar remained dark. For Vijay, whose Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) fell short of a majority in its first Assembly election, the question was how much political risk he could afford for a ceremony the court had authorised for one evening. The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), the CPI, the CPI(M) and the Congress had taken a firm stand against lighting a second lamp at the disputed site. Their support is crucial to his government. The Left parties had urged him to preserve the existing practice. VCK minister Vanni Arasu had publicly taken much the same position. Karthigai Deepam is an evening when families across Tamil Nadu light rows of lamps outside their homes. At Thirupparankundram, the day began with a temple car procession. Later, a copper cauldron, a cotton wick and ghee went up the hill under police escort. About 6,000 police personnel had been deployed across Madurai and around the hill. Even the airspace was accounted for – police had banned drones. At the foot of the hill stands the Subramaniya Swamy Temple, one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan. Near the summit is the Sikandar Badusha Dargah, a Muslim shrine. The stone pillar stands about 50 metres from the dargah. Hindu organisations have long sought an additional flame there. That distinction matters in a town where, three decades ago, four temple priests put in writing what they understood the tradition to be. The annual lamp, they said, had been lit at Uchi Pillaiyar for as long as anyone could remember. #WATCH | Thiruparankundram, Tamil Nadu | Police deployment at the Deepathoon stone pillar, where the Supreme Court had given an interim order to light the lamp today at 6 pm. At a distance from it is located the Ucchi Pillayar Temple, where the Maha Deepam has been lit as part of the annual Karthigai Deepam festival. Visuals from Annamalai Hills in Thiruparankundram where both locations are. — ANI (@ANI) November 24, 2026 On November 20, Supreme Court Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi stayed the contested findings of a January 6 Madras High Court judgment, but directed the authorities to permit a small team authorised by the temple to light the pillar lamp this year. The public could not accompany it. The arrangement settled neither ownership of the site nor any customary right to worship there. The Madurai Collector was to report on compliance within three days of the festival. The state’s Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Commissioner sought a review on Sunday. The petition turned on a practical difficulty with a one-time ritual. Once performed, the state argued, it could never again be said that it had never taken place. The festival arrived before the state could secure a hearing and a stay. Vijay’s predecessor, M K Stalin, had faced much the same decision last December and personally instructed his administration to hold its position despite the risk of contempt. After officials failed to carry out Justice G R Swaminathan’s order to light the pillar lamp, the judge authorised petitioners to go up with a Central Industrial Security Force escort. Police blocked access. Protesters and police clashed, and the DMK government faced contempt proceedings. A division bench subsequently upheld the direction to light the lamp, setting the stage for the state’s appeal. On Tuesday, some of the policing took place a considerable distance from Madurai. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran had been on the road for 40 minutes when police detained him at Thatchanallur, on the outskirts of Tirunelveli, at 3:15 pm. Former Union minister L Murugan was stopped at Annur in Coimbatore district. He asked how a prohibitory order issued in Madurai had come to apply to him in Coimbatore. Shortly after 6 pm, CTR Nirmal Kumar, the state’s law minister and Thirupparankundram’s MLA, announced that the flame had been lit at the traditional spot. At the foothills, police removed devotees protesting over the unlit pillar. Vijay had given his allies their answer. The Collector still owed the Supreme Court his. Five days before the festival, the death of Kolathur MLA V S Babu left Vijay’s TVK with 108 seats in an Assembly with 228 sitting members, seven short of a majority on its own. The Congress holds five seats, while the IUML, the VCK, the CPI and the CPI(M) hold two MLAs each. Together, those 13 MLAs take the government’s tally to 121. The Left parties had urged Vijay to keep the flame at its customary site, VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan backed that position, and Congress MP Manickam Tagore defended the government’s stand on grounds of communal harmony. None of the five parties had publicly made the lamp a condition of continued support. But lighting a second flame near the dargah would have put Vijay at odds with partners whose votes give him his majority.

headline: Indians among 13 killed in UAE’s Ras Al Khaimah bus-truck collision
content: At least 13 people were killed and 14 others injured after a passenger bus collided with a truck in the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah, with Indian nationals among those who lost their lives, the Indian Consulate in Dubai said on Tuesday. The accident took place on Al Watan Road when a passenger bus carrying 41 people crashed into a truck that had reportedly stopped along the roadside following a mechanical failure. The UAE Ministry of Interior initially reported 11 fatalities. However, the death toll subsequently rose to 13 after two more injured passengers died in hospital, according to a report by Gulf News. Fourteen others sustained injuries in the collision, the report added. The Indian Consulate said it had contacted the families of those affected and was coordinating with local authorities to extend assistance. However, the exact number of Indian nationals killed or injured in the accident has not yet been confirmed. Deeply saddened by the tragic road accident in Ras Al Khamiah that claimed lives of several people, including Indian nationals. The Consulate has reached out to the bereaved families and is closely working with local authorities to provide all possible assistance and support. Our heartfelt condolences and prayers are with the grieving families during this difficult time. Further details are being ascertained. 24/7 Toll Free Helpline No: 800-46342 @MEAIndia @IndembAbuDhabi — India in Dubai (@cgidubai) November 24, 2026 In a post on X, the Indian mission expressed grief over the incident and offered condolences to the bereaved families. It said further information was being gathered and assured those affected of all possible support. The consulate has also activated a 24-hour toll-free helpline at 800-46342 for people seeking assistance or information regarding the accident. The latest tragedy comes less than two weeks after another major road accident in the UAE claimed 14 lives, including four Indian nationals. That collision took place in Fujairah in the early hours of November 13 and involved 23 vehicles, including trucks. Around 30 people were injured, among them seven Indian nationals. Citizens of the UAE, Jordan, Pakistan, Egypt, Oman and Brazil were also among the injured.

headline: Prohibitory orders, detentions as Vijay govt defies SC order. Karthigai Deepam not lit at Deepathoon
content: Chennai: The Vijay-led TVK government Tuesday defied the Supreme Court order permitting a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, as the ceremonial lamp was lit at the traditional location near the Uchi Pillayar Temple atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai. No lamp was lit on the disputed stone pillar even after the Madras High Court directed the Madurai district administration to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders. Expressing the TVK’s clear stance, Law Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar wrote on X, “The Karthigai Mahadeepam was lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram.” The decision triggered protests by Hindu activists and members of organisations including the Hindu Munnani, leading to scuffles with police near the Thiruparankundram temple. Nearly 50 protesters were detained after a confrontation in which two policemen sustained minor injuries. BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan criticised Kumar. “A law minister gleefully posts about violating the Supreme Court’s order. Who is the message you are posting now meant for? As law minister, opposing the Supreme Court’s interim action is condemnable. The Tamil Nadu law minister is losing the moral right to remain in office. This government must answer for its conduct in disregarding Hindu sentiments and the law…” she wrote on X. The Madras High Court’s Madurai bench had earlier directed the district administration to comply with the Supreme Court’s 20 November ruling. That order—passed by a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi—had stayed key findings of the High Court’s January judgment that treated the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon as an essential religious practice.

headline: ‘Education, Healthcare Are Free’: Indian Man In Norway Compares Tax Benefits With India; Divides Internet
content: Paying nearly half of one’s income in taxes may sound like a significant financial burden, but what if those taxes cover basic and important facilities like education, healthcare and financial support during unemployment? An Indian man who has spent 15 years in Norway sparked a discussion online after explaining the benefits residents receive in return for paying taxes of up to 47 per cent. In a post on X, Vinod compared Norway’s tax system and public services with the situation in India, questioning what Indian taxpayers receive in return for the taxes they pay. Listing the benefits of paying high taxes, he shared that education in Norway is free, including university studies up to the master’s level. He also said residents do not have to pay hospital bills, regardless of how expensive the treatment is and mentioned the financial support provided to families. “Spent 15 years in Norway. I pay up to 47% in taxes and this is what I get back," he wrote. “Education for child till Master’s: free. Hospital bill ₹1 lakh or ₹10 crore: you pay zero. Parents get ₹2.3 lakh a year from the government for every child until the age of 18. Tax free." He added, “Child birth: Mother gets 1 year of leave with paid salary. Father gets 4 months of leave with paid salary. You fall sick: full salary from day one until you recover. You lose Job: you are safe, you salary is paid by government until you get new job." Other perks of paying such high taxes are one-month paid summer vacation and pension benefits. Beyond the benefits of financial support, he mentioned, “Plus mountains, forests, ocean and fjords. Clean air, tap water, clean roads, all electric cars, no pollution and a healthy lifestyle."

headline: Union Minister Shivraj Chouhan urges Punjab to implement PM Fasal Bima Yojana
content: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday urged the Punjab Government to implement Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), saying crop insurance was essential to protect farmers against losses caused by floods and other natural calamities.Interacting with farmers at a Kisan Chaupal in Buh Havelian village of Tarn Taran district, he praised local farmers and panchayats for practising agriculture without burning paddy stubble for the past six years, describing their efforts as a model for the rest of the country.Highlighting Punjab’s contribution to the Green Revolution, Chouhan said farmers of the state had helped the country overcome food shortages and build its foodgrain reserves. However, excessive use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides, along with stubble burning, was now affecting soil health, he said.He warned that declining soil fertility and the loss of beneficial insects and earthworms could pose a serious challenge for future generations.Referring to Buh Havelian and neighbouring villages, he appreciated farmers for adopting happy seeder and direct-seeding techniques to manage crop residue without burning it.Commenting on the renewed political understanding between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and BJP, Chouhan called the two parties as “brothers who had reunited”.He said the people of Punjab had experienced governments led by both the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP ), and claimed that the BJP-SAD alliance would open a new path for the state’s progress and development.“The two brothers have come together again, and now Punjab’s progress and development will receive the people’s blessings,” he said.On machinery subsidies, Chouhan said the Centre had been providing substantial financial assistance to Punjab for crop residue management, including around Rs 286 crore this year. However, he said ensuring the quality of subsidised agricultural machinery and its timely repair was the responsibility of the state government.His remarks came after farmers raised concerns over the quality of subsidised machines, particularly balers, and difficulties in stubble management.Chouhan assured them that he would invite the farmers to Delhi for a detailed discussion on their suggestions.Expressing concern over Punjab not implementing PMFBY, Chouhan said he had written to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann during the recent floods as well, urging the state to introduce the scheme so that farmers could receive compensation for crop losses caused by natural disasters.During his interaction, the minister also reiterated the Centre’s commitment to procuring wheat and paddy at the minimum support price (MSP). He said the government had guaranteed procurement of 100 per cent of eligible quantities of tur, masur and urad under the relevant procurement arrangements, besides MSP-based procurement of cotton.Earlier, invoking the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev, Chouhan said public office should be viewed as an opportunity to serve people rather than a position of power.

headline: India and Cyprus discuss operationalising MoU on higher education and research
content: Nicosia [Cyprus], November 24 (ANI): India and Cyprus have held discussions on implementing the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Higher Education and Research, signed during Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides' State Visit to India in May, the High Commission of India in Cyprus said.The meeting took place on Monday between India's High Commissioner to Cyprus, Manish, and Marios Panayiades, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth of the Republic of Cyprus, according to a post by the High Commission on X."Discussions focused on operationalising the MoU on Higher Education and Research signed during the State Visit of President Nikos Christodoulides to India in May 2026, translating the commitments of the leadership into concrete institutional partnerships," the High Commission said.The discussions covered academic cooperation, student mobility and issues concerning Indian students pursuing higher education in Cyprus, the High Commission noted."The High Commissioner discussed opportunities for joint research, academic collaborations, faculty and student mobility, and strengthening engagement between Indian institutions and leading Cypriot academic and research institutions. Discussions also covered matters concerning the situation around Indian international students pursuing higher education in Cyprus and opportunities for Indian researchers working with Cypriot institutions," it stated.The two countries also agreed to continue discussions through another meeting early next year, the High Commission said."Both sides agreed to take forward the discussions through a follow-up meeting proposed for January 2027, with a view to developing actionable initiatives under the MoU. Education, research and knowledge partnerships are emerging as important pillars of the India-Cyprus Strategic Partnership, creating new opportunities for the next generation of students, academics and researchers in both countries," it added.Earlier, on November 12, India's High Commissioner to Cyprus, Manish, met Cyprus' Minister of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Michael Damianos, in Nicosia to discuss the minister's proposed visit to India for the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit.During his visit to India in May, Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides oversaw the elevation of bilateral ties between the two countries to a Strategic Partnership.According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the discussions resulted in several key outcomes, including the proposed establishment of a Joint Working Group (JWG) on Counter-Terrorism, cooperation between the Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service and Cyprus' Diplomatic Academy, and collaboration in higher education and research. (ANI) (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: Explainer-What are the disputes between Iraq’s federal government and Kurdistan region?
content: Nov 24 (Reuters) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on Tuesday ordered federal authorities to take over border crossings in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region and directed the oil ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in four provinces, following an oil smuggling investigation at the state-run North Oil Company. The orders are part of a broader crackdown by Zaidi against oil smuggling. They also reopen long-running disputes between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) over control of oil, money, territory and trade. Though Baghdad says state oil marketer SOMO has sole authority to export Iraq’s crude, for years the KRG exported independently through a pipeline to Turkey’s Ceyhan port. In 2014, Iraq took Turkey to arbitration at the Paris-based International Chamber of Commerce, which in 2023 ordered Ankara to pay Iraq about $1.5 billion for unauthorised exports between 2014 and 2018. Turkey shut the pipeline, halting about 450,000 barrels per day for two and a half years. Flows resumed in September 2025 under an interim deal between Baghdad, the KRG and most foreign producers operating in the region. Under the deal, the KRG delivers crude to SOMO. In August, Turkey and Iraq signed a one-year agreement maintaining use of the pipeline after the previous bilateral agreement expired. The arrangement covers capacity of 750,000 bpd while the two governments negotiate a longer-term deal.

headline: Puneeth Rajkumar Hrudaya Jyothi Scheme to be extended to all district, taluk hospitals: State health minister
content: Mangaluru: The Puneeth Rajkumar Hrudaya Jyothi Scheme, which provides emergency cardiac care during the critical 'golden hour' following the onset of heart attack symptoms, will be extended to all district and taluk hospitals across Karnataka, Minister for Health and Family Welfare U T Khader said. Speaking to mediapersons, Khader said the scheme, introduced to save patients suffering from sudden and severe heart attacks, had so far been implemented in 80 district and taluk hospitals. According to the Health Department, 14,94,578 ECG tests have been conducted under the programme since its launch in March 2023, resulting in the identification of 22,579 cases of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), a serious form of heart attack requiring immediate medical intervention. .Shops, commercial establishments allowed to remain open till 11:45 pm in Mangaluru.With the expansion, patients experiencing chest pain or symptoms of cardiac problems, including those in rural areas, can visit the nearest taluk hospital for an immediate ECG examination. Even if minor abnormalities are detected, patients will be administered an injection free of cost and referred to district hospitals for further treatment, including angiograms or angioplasty, wherever necessary. The government has decided to introduce single-use dialysers in all government-run dialysis centres to minimise the risk of cross-infections associated with the reuse of dialysers and tubing, Khader said. Earlier, used dialysers and tubes were cleaned after every dialysis session and reused. The new system will discontinue this practice in the interest of patient safety. .AI-based equipment The Health Department will introduce AI-based equipment to screen women for breast cancer in rural areas. The department has submitted a proposal to the Cabinet for procuring one machine for each district. Each compact unit is expected to cost around Rs 30 lakh. Before the screening programme begins, ASHA workers and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) will conduct awareness campaigns in villages and encourage women to undergo screening. Those identified during preliminary examinations as requiring further investigation will be referred for additional tests, with free treatment provided to eligible patients, Khader said. The government will establish chemotherapy day-care centres in all district hospitals within the next three months. He also announced that under the Kusuma Sanjeevini scheme, patients with haemophilia will be given an injection once a month as a preventive measure, to check the recurrence of bleeding. .Mangaluru: 54-year-old woman duped of Rs 8.5 lakh in UK gift parcel scam.Responding to a question on the proposal to extend business hours until 11.45 pm within Mangaluru Police Commissionerate limits, Khader said matters relating to law and order came under the jurisdiction of the police department. Register online The Minister urged job aspirants to register online for the mega job fair scheduled to be held on November 30. Around 3,000 candidates have already registered. Those registering online will be allotted time slots in advance, helping avoid confusion and delays on the day of the event, he said. Rangamandira Minister UT Khader said the tender process has been initiated for the long-pending district Rangamandira project at Bondel. The project will be taken up at an estimated cost of Rs 8.17 crore, and the foundation stone will be laid shortly, he said.

headline: Telangana to unveil five-month El Niño preparedness programme worth Rs 10,000 crore at climate conclave
content: Hyderabad: Irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy on Tuesday directed officials to ensure that the climate conclave, to be held as part of the three-day Global Summit beginning Dec 7 at Bharat Future City, focuses on practical and scientifically proven solutions to climate change, with particular emphasis on drought resilience, water security, sustainable agriculture and preparedness to tackle the impact of El Niño conditions.Reviewing preparations for the conclave, Uttam stressed the need to incorporate globally recognised climate-resilience models, including best practices identified by ICRISAT, into presentations and audio-visual content. Discussions covered programme design, expert participation, investor engagement and presentation plans. “A major highlight of the conclave will be the govt’s proposed five-month El Niño preparedness programme worth Rs 10,000 crore, conceptualised by chief minister A Revanth Reddy. The programme envisages taking up works worth nearly Rs 2,000 crore every month after Sankranti in Jan,” the minister said.To be implemented jointly by the irrigation and panchayat raj departments, the initiative aims to rejuvenate tanks, streams and canals, improve groundwater recharge, expand rainwater harvesting and strengthen water conservation across rural Telangana. It is also expected to generate employment during the agricultural lean season.The presentations will explain the govt’s measures to safeguard drinking water availability and food security in the event of drought. Farmers are being encouraged to shift from water-intensive paddy cultivation to alternative crops to conserve reservoir reserves until the next monsoon.Uttam said Telangana currently has sufficient rice stocks to meet nearly one year’s requirements under the public distribution system, providing a cushion against possible crop losses caused by drought. The conclave will also highlight sustainability initiatives, including renewable energy expansion, industrial reuse of treated wastewater and measures to achieve Telangana’s net-zero objectives. Officials noted that data centres in the state are already required to source at least 51% of their energy from renewable sources.Around 125 rural representatives, including sarpanches and grassroots stakeholders, are expected to participate in discussions on water security, climate resilience, biodiversity, urban heat management, agriculture and clean energy. The event is also expected to bring together environmental experts, scientists, water conservation specialists, community representatives and investors. An investor engagement platform is being planned to explore opportunities in renewable energy, green credits, eco-tourism and the circular economy. headline: Deepam Lit Away From Approved Spot As Vijay Government Defies Supreme Court Order
content: The Tamil Nadu government today lit the Karthigai Deepam at the traditional location near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple on the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai, but not at the hilltop stone pillar next to a Dargah, as permitted by the Supreme Court as a one-time event in an interim order. The decision comes despite the Madurai district administration, headed by a Collector whom the Supreme Court had designated as the nodal officer for implementing its order, earlier informing the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court that all steps were being taken to comply with the directions. Neither the ruling TVK nor the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department has so far explained why the lamp was not lit at the hilltop pillar. The decision could expose the government and the officials responsible for defying the Supreme Court's order to further legal scrutiny, particularly against the backdrop of an existing contempt petition over the earlier non-compliance with the Madras High Court's directions. The temple administration, in a statement, said the Karthigai Maha Deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple, located on the hill directly above the presiding deity's sanctum. It maintained that the practice was rooted in age-old customs, established rituals and Agama rules, and that the temple's traditional religious practices and distinct customs must be protected.

headline: Karnataka health department considers drug take-back programme for unused & expired antibiotics at homes
content: Bengaluru: Soon, unused or expired antibiotics in households may have to be segregated and disposed of separately, much like sanitary waste or e-waste, as the state health department considers a drug take-back programme to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR).AMR occurs when microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites evolve and develop the ability to survive medicines designed to kill them or stop their growth, making infections difficult to treat.A five-year state action plan to tackle AMR, launched recently, tasks the health department, medical education department, Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) and Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) with establishing and updating standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the disposal of expired or unused drugs in hospitals, homes, farms and garbage collection centres. It also recommends that these departments work towards establishing drug or antibiotic take-back programmes.“Expired or unused drugs are generally thrown away or dumped randomly by consumers. They get absorbed into the soil or, when it rains, seep into groundwater. When vegetables and fruits are grown in such soil or using such water, it contributes to AMR. This is why we need to dispose of them scientifically at common biomedical waste treatment facilities,” said Dr Chandramohan KN, deputy director and state nodal officer (AMR).He said most hospitals have tie-ups with agencies that scientifically dispose of such drugs. Pharmaceutical companies are also required, through tender conditions, to take back unused medicines before their expiry. However, these regulations are not being followed stringently. “Through the plan, we are reiterating this and making it compulsory for them to follow these steps,” Chandramohan said.He added the proposal to collect unused and expired medicines from households and farms is still in the pipeline and would be taken forward after discussions with other concerned departments and agencies.The action plan also recommends introducing a state-level digital system to monitor antibiotic use across human healthcare, animal husbandry, agriculture and food sectors. The proposed software will track antibiotics from production and procurement to distribution and sale, with a quality management system for the supply chain. It also proposes making aggregated data collected through the system publicly accessible.Adviser calls action plan a diluted versionSwetavalli Raghavan, adviser to the state’s AMR programme, who conducted a field study across 11 districts, has criticised the new plan as a copy of the national policy that has lost its regional relevance.She said the original action plan was developed following field research across 11 districts, evidence-based recommendations and citizen consultations, and was reviewed by experts before being approved by the authorities. She alleged that the current administration has diluted the Karnataka-specific strategy by turning it largely into a copy of the national plan.Citing her study, she estimated that Karnataka records around 5.5 lakh AMR cases and 1.1 lakh associated deaths annually. Criticising the new plan for lacking measurable targets, accountability and meaningful interventions, she called it “merely an administrative formality.”She warned that the consequences would ultimately be borne by patients and their families, rather than the system responsible for protecting them.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. headline: 8th Pay Commission: BPMS demands 6% annual increment, five career upgrades and higher insurance cover for employees
content: The 8th Central Pay Commission is set to examine a wide range of demands from central government employee organisations, covering salary hikes, pension benefits, insurance, leave entitlements and career progression. Among the latest submissions is a memorandum by the Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh (BPMS), which has put forward 73 proposals seeking improvements in employees' financial and service benefits. In its memorandum dated 18 November 2026, the federation has sought an increase in the annual increment from 3% to 6%, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), 45 days of paternity leave and at least five financial upgradations during a 30-year career. The proposals also include higher insurance coverage, improved medical benefits, menstrual leave for women employees and changes to the promotion system. While several demands concern civilian defence employees, others seek broader changes in the service conditions of central government employees and pensioners. What BPMS wants for salaries and pensions One of the key proposals is to double the annual increment for central government employees from the existing 3% to 6% of basic pay. BPMS has argued that a higher increment would help employees improve their earnings over their service period and deal with rising living costs. The federation has also sought the merger of 50% of existing dearness allowance (DA) with basic pay and pension before the revised salary and pension structures are determined. On minimum pay, it has recommended using actual family consumption requirements, Indian Labour Conference norms and the Aykroyd formula, while factoring in prevailing market prices of essential commodities. Another important demand concerns the fitment factor, which determines how existing basic pay is revised under a new pay commission. BPMS has called for an appropriate fitment factor to offset inflation and ensure that the difference between the highest and lowest salaries does not exceed a ratio of 1:10. The federation has also sought the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), calling for the discontinuation of the National Pension System (NPS) and Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for central government employees. Higher bonus, insurance and provident fund benefits The memorandum proposes changes to bonus and insurance benefits, which could influence employees' take-home benefits and financial security. BPMS wants ad-hoc bonus and Productivity Linked Bonus (PLB) to be extended to all central government employees without exclusions. It has proposed calculating the bonus using the minimum pay of the respective pay level, with a minimum entitlement equivalent to 30 days' pay plus DA. For employee insurance, the federation has sought an increase in coverage under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS) from ₹30,000 to at least ₹15 lakh. It has separately proposed increasing the Deposit Linked Insurance benefit to ₹10 lakh to provide greater financial protection to the family of a deceased employee. The federation has also demanded that the interest rate on the General Provident Fund (GPF) should not be lower than the rate applicable to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF). Longer paternity leave, menstrual leave and medical benefits Several proposals concern work-life balance and employee welfare. BPMS has sought an increase in paternity leave to 45 days, with the benefit also extended to cases of child adoption. It has proposed child care leave of up to two years with full wages, subject to prescribed conditions. Other leave-related demands include increasing casual leave to 12 days a year and providing one day of menstrual leave every month to female employees. The federation has also sought leave encashment of 20 days on every eligible Leave Travel Concession (LTC) occasion and the reintroduction of the LTC Special Cash Package introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. Another proposal seeks to extend Children Education Allowance (CEA) up to the postgraduate level. On healthcare, BPMS has sought an increase in fixed medical allowance for serving employees and pensioners who do not have access to equivalent government healthcare facilities. It also wants the government to fully fund the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), removing subscription payments by employees and pensioners. For employees working in hazardous conditions, the federation has proposed increasing risk allowance to up to ₹10,000 per month. It has also sought an increase in ex-gratia compensation to ₹1 crore for families of employees who die in accidents while performing official duties. Five financial upgradations and changes to promotion rules Career progression is another major area covered in the memorandum. BPMS has proposed a Dynamic Promotion Scheme to replace the existing vacancy-based promotion system, linking career advancement to an employee's length of service, merit, competence and experience. It has also demanded at least five financial upgradations over a 30-year service period under the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme. This is aimed at addressing career stagnation among employees who may not get regular promotions because of limited vacancies. The federation has further proposed capping the waiting period between a feeder post and its promotional post at five years. For Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), it has sought reservation of 50% of promotional vacancies in Lower Division Clerk, store staff, stenographer and Rajbhasha cadres for eligible employees. The memorandum also includes defence-specific proposals, including better pay scales for technical workshop staff, pharmacists and medical support personnel, along with improved career progression for fire-engine drivers and security staff. Will these demands be implemented? The 8th Pay Commission will have to examine representations from employee organisations and other stakeholders before finalising its recommendations. The Commission's mandate covers salaries, allowances, pensions and other service conditions of central government employees, including defence personnel. It must also consider the country's economic conditions, fiscal prudence and the financial implications of its recommendations. Any changes to salaries, pensions, allowances or service benefits will require subsequent government approval. For employees and pensioners, the BPMS memorandum therefore provides an indication of the benefits being sought from the 8th Pay Commission. However, the 73 proposals remain demands, not confirmed changes to their existing entitlements.

headline: Telangana high court stresses parental duty in divorce cases involving children with special needs
content: Hyderabad: Telangana high court has ruled that both parents have a responsibility to ensure that matrimonial disputes and personal differences do not affect their children. The court, dealing with a doctor couple’s divorce case, said this responsibility becomes even more important when the child has a neurodevelopmental condition such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), where parental love, affection, constant care and emotional security are even more essential.A division bench of Justice K Lakshman and Justice K Sujana made these observations recently while setting aside a one-month civil detention sentence imposed on the man by a family court for alleged violation of an interim order.High court has directed the family court to hear the other petitions filed by the wife afresh in accordance with law and dispose of them as early as possible, keeping Supreme Court guidelines in view. Married in 2018, the couple has a six-year-old son suffering from speech and behaviour-related issues.Disputes arose between them after about three years. The man filed a divorce petition before a court in the UAE, while the wife approached the family court in Hyderabad. She filed cases seeking action under IPC Section 498-A (Cruelty by husband), monthly maintenance and divorce. She also sought an order restraining the husband from continuing the divorce proceedings before the foreign court.Despite the order, the Abu Dhabi court granted divorce on Aug 19, 2025. The wife then filed a contempt petition before the family court, seeking disclosure of the husband’s assets, bank accounts, salary and income details, attachment of properties and civil imprisonment.On April 29, the family court sentenced the husband to one month in jail, which he challenged before high court.High court said punishment in such matters could be imposed only when “wilful and deliberate violation of a court order is proved. A mere allegation is not enough.” It also said courts must act with caution while issuing orders that might interfere with proceedings before foreign courts.The bench observed that family courts and lawyers should adopt a constructive approach in matrimonial disputes and should not worsen differences between spouses through their words or conduct. “Reconciliation must remain an important objective, especially when children are involved,” it said.The court further noted that parental responsibility does not end even if the marriage ends. Every child deserves a dignified and happy childhood. “Children with ASD need routine, patience, understanding and emotional support, along with medical care and special education. Personal disputes between parents should not disturb a child’s emotional well-being,” the court added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Telangana former CM KCR’s long-time attendant, another youth killed as truck rams bike in Sircilla
content: Hyderabad: A road accident in Rajanna Sircilla district claimed the lives of two young men, including a long-time attendant of BRS chief and former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao, on Monday night. The death of Kasturi Mahender Reddy, alias Manikumar Reddy, who had been working at KCR’s Erravelli residence for several years, left the BRS chief and his family deeply distressed.According to police, the accident occurred near Venkaiahkunta, close to the Hanuman Nagar crossroads near Bandankal village in Mustabad mandal. A truck coming from behind rammed into the motorcycle carrying Manikumar Reddy and another youth, Bharat. Both sustained serious injuries in the collision.Manikumar Reddy died on the spot due to the impact of the crash. Bharat, who was critically injured, was shifted to a hospital by locals. However, he succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment around 2 am, taking the death toll to two.Upon learning about Manikumar Reddy’s death, KCR expressed shock and spoke to former Mustabad mandal parishad president Janagama Sharath Rao on the phone to enquire about the accident. He conveyed his condolences to the bereaved family and assured them of all possible support.Mustabad police registered a case and took up an investigation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Ensure Global Summit showcases Telangana’s industrial ecosystem: IT minister Sridhar Babu tells officials
content: Hyderabad: ‘Invest Telangana Global Summit-2026’ will serve as a platform to showcase Telangana’s industrial strengths, investment opportunities and future growth plans to national and international investors, IT and industries minister Duddilla Sridhar Babu said on Tuesday.The minister inspected the arrangements at Young India Skills University campus at Bharat Future City and directed officials to ensure that the summit effectively showcases the state’s industrial ecosystem and its potential across key sectors.At a review meeting with officials following the inspection, Sridhar Babu said the summit was aimed at strengthening Telangana’s brand image on the international stage, attracting large-scale investments and creating employment opportunities for the state’s youth.He said delegates should be given a comprehensive understanding of the advantages of investing in Telangana, the progress achieved in the industrial sector, the objectives of ‘Telangana Rising-2047’ vision and the state’s future development plans. The minister directed officials to complete all pending works within the stipulated timeframe and prepare a clear action plan for the successful conduct of the summit. He said coordinated arrangements were needed for security, parking, hospitality, connectivity, transportation, traffic management, uninterrupted power supply, high-speed internet and emergency medical services.Expo zones, he said, should meet international standards to highlight the state’s industrial strengths, talent pool and skill development capabilities. Key sectors, including information technology, pharmaceuticals, defence and aerospace, should receive particular attention. headline: SCCL to provide free education up to Class X for children of 30,000 contract and outsourced workers
content: Hyderabad: The Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) has decided to provide free education up to Class X in its schools to children of nearly 30,000 contract and outsourced workers across its 12 operational areas.More than 400 children currently studying in the nine schools run by the Singareni Collieries Educational Society will benefit immediately, officials said. From the next academic year, the facility will also be extended to newly enrolling children of contract and outsourced workers.The decision was among the welfare measures taken at a recent meeting of public representatives from the coal belt region.Following the decision, the general manager of the Singareni Collieries Educational Society has issued orders to all areas. Children of contract and outsourced workers employed in Singareni areas will be eligible for free admission and education up to Class X in Singareni schools in their respective areas.The move is expected to boost enrolment of contract workers’ children in Singareni educational institutions from the next academic year.It is also expected to provide financial relief to thousands of contract and outsourced workers who would otherwise have to bear the cost of private schooling. headline: Rebel TMC MPs submit replies to Speaker, claim they followed all norms
content: THE 20 Trinamool Congress MPs who rebelled after the party's defeat in the West Bengal elections earlier this year, and subsequently joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), have furnished their respective replies defending their decision to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. According to one of the rebel MPs, Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, who is currently the NCPI parliamentary chairperson, they asserted that they had followed all parliamentary and constitutional norms. The replies came on the last day of the deadline set by the Lok Sabha Secretariat for the MPs to respond to notices issued by Speaker Birla on petitions seeking their disqualification under the anti-defection law. “We have submitted our replies to the Lok Sabha Speaker and have defended our decision to join the NCPI. We have joined the NCPI following all parliamentary and constitutional norms,” she told PTI. She said each rebel MP sent a 17-18 page reply to the respective notices issued to them following petitions seeking action against them for quitting the TMC and joining the NCPI. The rebel MPs have maintained that their move does not attract disqualification under the anti-defection provisions. Since the last week of August, the MPs had sought time more than once to respond to the Speaker's notices, citing the need to collate documents and prepare a comprehensive reply with their legal team's assistance.

headline: IIT Bhubaneswar-developed TB vaccine eyes human trials by mid-2027
content: A next-generation tuberculosis (TB) vaccine candidate that could help address a major gap in the prevention of pulmonary TB among adolescents and adults is expected to enter human clinical trials by mid-2027. Jointly developed by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bhubaneswar and the Institute of Life Sciences (ILS), Bhubaneswar, the vaccine candidate is being evaluated as a potential booster to the century-old Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine, which offers limited protection against pulmonary TB in these age groups. Mumbai-based TechInvention Lifecare Ltd, which has licensed the technology for development and commercialisation, has optimised the production process and is generating additional data on the vaccine candidate, which was granted a patent on November 16. Syed S Ahmed, director and chief executive officer of TechInvention Lifecare, said the commercialisation plan was progressing as scheduled. The company is also working on novel adjuvants to improve vaccine efficacy. “We recently consulted a group of experts and based on those interactions, we are generating more and more data. We will go for human trials by mid-2027,” he told Business Standard. The vaccine candidate, Hsp16.3ΔC4, has been developed from a heat shock protein antigen derived from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for TB. The innovation assumes significance because the world continues to rely on the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine, developed more than a century ago, which provides good protection against severe forms of TB in young children but has limited effectiveness in preventing pulmonary TB among adolescents and adults. Unlike BCG, which is a live attenuated vaccine, Hsp16.3ΔC4 is a protein-based vaccine candidate designed to stimulate both cellular and antibody-mediated immune responses. Ashis Biswas, a professor at IIT Bhubaneswar, said TechInvention had initiated preparations for GLP (good laboratory practice) and GMP (good manufacturing practice)-compliant production. The technology was transferred to the company after the National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) evaluated it and facilitated the licensing process. Biswas said this was India’s first indigenously engineered TB vaccine candidate, developed through a joint research effort, with the protein developed at IIT Bhubaneswar and its preclinical evaluation carried out at ILS. “This is a protein subunit vaccine developed as part of a joint collaboration. The protein was first developed at the IIT lab and then underwent pre-clinical trials on mice models at ILS, which tested its efficacy levels,” Biswas said. Preclinical studies in mice showed that administering the vaccine candidate in combination with BCG generated stronger immune responses than either approach alone. The combination also generated stronger memory T-cell and B-cell responses. Scientists said the preclinical safety assessment did not identify significant toxicity signals in the vaccinated animal models. "While the findings of preclinical studies are encouraging, safety and efficacy in humans will have to be established through successive clinical trials. The vaccine has the ability to target an antigen specific to Mycobacterium tuberculosis that is not present in the BCG strain. This could be used both as a stand-alone immunisation and as a booster or co-administration strategy alongside BCG in infants, adolescents and adults," said Sunil Raghav, a senior scientist at ILS. Biswas said the vaccine candidate would undergo independent evaluation in animal models in the UK. The additional preclinical studies are expected to generate further evidence on its safety and efficacy ahead of regulatory submissions for human clinical trials. According to the World Health Organisation’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025, while 1.13 million died from the disease. An estimated 370,000 people developed rifampicin-resistant TB during the year. India accounts for a substantial share of the global TB burden. The emergence and spread of drug-resistant strains, coupled with the limitations of existing preventive measures, underline the need for more effective vaccines.

headline: On crutches, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani attends Gurpurab celebrations
content: In a gesture that resonated spiritually with New York’s Sikh community, Zohran Mamdani, the city’s first Muslim Mayor, attended Gurpurab celebrations marking the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak despite recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon and relying on crutches for mobility.Mamdani joined devotees at Baba Makhan Shah Lobana Sikh Centre Gurdwara, located in South Richmond Hill, Queens, where community members observed the occasion through Gurbani kirtan, seva, and langar.The visit carried added significance as it was his first Gurpurab celebration since assuming office as Mayor of New York City earlier this year. His attendance on the occasion went viral on social media.The Mayor’s presence was particularly noteworthy because it came just days after he suffered an Achilles tendon rupture while playing in a friendly soccer match against members of the City Hall press corps.Wearing a medical walking boot and using crutches, Mamdani chose to attend the event, underlining his commitment to engaging with the city’s diverse communities and honouring a promise to stand with the Sikh community during one of its most important religious observances.Community members welcomed the Mayor’s participation, viewing it as a powerful symbol of inclusivity and mutual respect in one of the world’s most multicultural cities.Reports also indicated that he planned to continue Gurpurab observances with members of the Sikh community at Gracie Mansion, the official residence of the Mayor of New York City.

headline: Meghalaya: 44 health facilities secure NQAS certification; hospitals, labs honoured
content: Shillong, Nov 24: Meghalaya has awarded national quality certifications to 44 public healthcare facilities, including 37 Primary Health Centres (PHCs), six district hospitals and one Community Health Centre (CHC), in recognition of improvements in healthcare standards and service delivery. The achievements were recognised at the second National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) award ceremony organised by the Health and Family Welfare Department in Shillong on Tuesday. Three district hospitals also received LaQshya certification, which focuses on improving the quality of care during childbirth, while one district hospital secured MusQan certification for child-friendly healthcare services. In another milestone, the Molecular Laboratory at the Pasteur Institute in Shillong received NABL accreditation under ISO 15189:2022. The institute’s Regional Blood Centre was also awarded accreditation by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH). Health Minister Wailadmiki Shylla, who attended the ceremony, said the achievements reflected the state’s efforts to improve the quality, safety and reliability of public healthcare services. He acknowledged the contributions of the three health directorates and the Joint Directorate Committee and Joint Directorate Quality Committee in coordinating quality improvement initiatives across healthcare institutions.

headline: ACS (health) orders rectification of new 500-bed Dumka hospital flaws in 30 days
content: Dumka: Additional chief secretary (ACS) of the health department-cum-development commissioner, Dr Ajoy Kumar Singh, on Tuesday checked the infrastructure, construction quality, and facilities available at the newly built 500-bed hospital at the Phulo Jhano Medical College and Hospital (PJMCH), Dumka.The inspection revealed several technical and structural shortcomings. A lecture hall, meant for 120 students, had only 112 seats.He ordered an examination of the role of the consultant associated with the hospital’s construction and design and directed the construction agency to ensure rectification of the deficiencies within a month.“The new 500-bed facility would be integrated with the existing 300-bed Sadar Hospital and operated through the medical college, raising the combined capacity to 800 beds. The health department would appoint the required doctors, lecturers and faculty members,” Singh said.A special team, led by the deputy development commissioner, would inspect every building structure, facility, room, and submit a detailed report, the ACS added.The medical college campus, spread over around 25 acres, would be expanded to more than 100 acres in accordance with the chief minister’s directions. The district administration has provided the required land. The govt also plans to increase MBBS seats from 100 to 200 over the next three years and introduce postgraduate courses from next year, with a target of 150 PG seats, said Singh.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

headline: Students assault English lecturer over alleged obscene messages on WhatsApp to classmate in Sangareddy; Cops book Pocso case
content: Hyderabad: An English lecturer at a private polytechnic college in Patelguda, Sangareddy district, was allegedly assaulted by students after they found WhatsApp messages in which he reportedly sent obscene texts to a first-year diploma student and pressured her to chat with him daily.According to police, the 47-year-old lecturer had been sending inappropriate messages to the student and repeatedly insisting that she communicate with him every day. The messages allegedly made the student uncomfortable, and screenshots of their conversation were later shared with fellow students.Angered by the contents of the messages, the students confronted the lecturer and assaulted him on the college premises. The incident triggered tension at the institution, prompting Ameenpur police to rush to the spot and bring the situation under control.Ameenpur inspector M Praveen Reddy said police had registered a case against lecturer under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act based on the allegations. Police are examining the WhatsApp conversations and other details to verify the allegations and establish the circumstances of the incident.
