headline: Villagers opposed to coal project called firm officials to Gram Sabha. A hostage crisis followed
content: A coal exploration company's general manager held hostage, a dozen policemen injured, and a rescue operation. In the Badalpara-Kalyanpur area of Jharkhand’s Dumka, anger over a proposed coal mining project has taken a violent turn. According to officials, Haryana Power Corporation Limited, which has been allocated a coal block in the area, had hired Synergy Geotech to undertake exploratory drilling to assess the quality and quantity of coal underground. But villagers have been protesting against the proposed project for the past three months, alleging that the company has not obtained the Gram Sabha's consent. On Saturday, the villagers decided to convene a Gram Sabha the following day and asked the company officials to attend. Shikaripara police station in-charge Amit Lakra told The Indian Express that the company's staff, along with government officials, arrived in the village on Sunday. However, the company's general manager, Sagar Singh Meena, was allegedly held hostage by villagers for several hours, beaten and thrown in the water while the other officials escaped. Villagers, speaking to The Indian Express on condition of anonymity, claimed that the company had brought heavy machinery to conduct the survey without obtaining the Gram Sabha's consent. "This is our land, and this is not the first time we are fighting against a coal block,” claimed one villager. “We asked them to remove the machines and not conduct any survey. But they refused and brought the police to suppress our protest. This angered the villagers and led to the clash, in which several villagers were injured.” Meena, the general manager of Synergy Geotech, said the Gram Sabha meeting was scheduled for Sunday after the village head agreed to the date fixed by the Circle Officer. “While the Circle Officer and other officials were allowed to leave after their vehicles were checked, my vehicle was stopped around 4 pm and detained until 11 pm,” he said. He alleged that villagers demanded that the company remove its machines from Jharkhand and threatened to kill him if that did not happen by midnight. He also claimed that villagers attacked police personnel who reached the spot, and that he was assaulted during the confrontation. Meena is currently undergoing treatment at AIIMS Deoghar. Meena said that the coal block area was expanded up to 1,700 acres and around 70 to 80 per cent of the exploratory work had been completed, with only one or two tasks remaining. The project was still in its initial stage, and the company would have to prepare a geological report and mining plan before it could seek forest and environmental clearances for actual mining, he said. Dumka Deputy Development Commissioner Aniket Sachan told The Indian Express that at least 12 police personnel were injured when they went to rescue the GM. “Some were discharged immediately, three were treated at the Dumka district hospital and three others were referred to AIIMS,” he said. He said police had registered an FIR and were identifying those involved, including people suspected to have come from outside the area. “The company's general manager was rescued the following evening after his whereabouts were established,” he said. “When the police went to rescue the GM with its force of around 70-80 police personnel, they were surrounded and attacked using traditional weapons, stones and sticks.”

headline: Uttarakhand's Baini-Bhuli Yojana: 5.23 lakh women to get ₹20,000 aid in 2 instalments—check who will benefit
content: The Uttarakhand government is set to launch the Baini-Bhuli Yojana next month, offering financial assistance of ₹20,000 to 5.23 lakh eligible rural women associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs). The initiative aims to strengthen women's economic independence and improve livelihood opportunities in rural areas.Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced that the financial assistance would be provided in two instalments. Under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries will receive the first instalment of ₹10,000 directly into their bank accounts in December. The remaining ₹10,000 will be transferred in the second instalment.The state government has set a target of covering 5.23 lakh women under the initiative. According to the government, ₹523 crore will be transferred from the state treasury towards the first instalment. Baini-Bhuli Yojana aims to promote women's financial independenceChief Minister Dhami said women's dignity, security and self-reliance remained key priorities of his government. He emphasised that the administration was committed to ensuring equal opportunities for education, development and economic progress for every woman in Uttarakhand.The scheme is expected to provide additional financial support to rural women engaged in various income-generating activities, helping them strengthen their livelihoods and become financially independent.State Rural Development Minister Bharat Singh Chaudhary said the initiative would benefit women associated with Self-Help Groups, the Rural Livelihood Mission and different self-employment programmes.He highlighted the contribution of rural women to the state's economy through agriculture, animal husbandry, handicrafts and the production of locally made goods. The government intends to support these activities through financial assistance and improved livelihood opportunities.Government measures aim to promote women entrepreneursChaudhary said the state government had introduced several measures to promote women's welfare and empowerment across different sectors, including education, employment, entrepreneurship, healthcare and sports. He also referred to the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in Uttarakhand.The Rural Development Department is also implementing programmes aimed at helping women become 'Lakhpati Didis', while encouraging the branding, promotion and marketing of locally manufactured products.These initiatives are intended to increase women's participation in economic activities, improve household incomes and create sustainable employment opportunities in rural communities.The minister said the Baini-Bhuli Yojana would complement existing government programmes and further strengthen efforts towards women's economic empowerment.Will urban women also receive benefits?Responding to a question about extending the scheme to women living in urban areas, Chaudhary said the government was planning to introduce a separate initiative for them soon.This indicates that the Baini-Bhuli Yojana will initially focus on eligible rural women, while a separate framework may be introduced for urban beneficiaries. Documents that may be required for Baini-Bhuli YojanaThe government is yet to issue the detailed official application and verification guidelines. However, beneficiaries may be required to keep the following documents ready:Aadhaar cardUttarakhand permanent residence certificateBank account passbook linked with AadhaarRegistered mobile numberRecent passport-size photographSelf-Help Group (SHG) membership details or certificateThe final list of documents, eligibility conditions and application procedures will depend on the official guidelines issued by the state government.

headline: AAP MP Sanjay Singh acquitted in panchayat poll violation case, 5 years on
content: A Sultanpur court in Uttar Pradesh acquitted Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh and the other accused in a case over an alleged violation of the model code of conduct and COVID-19 protocols during the 2021 panchayat elections, citing "lack of evidence" on Tuesday. Singh's counsel, advocate Madan Singh, said the court reached its decision after going through the evidence and hearing both sides. The case dates to 13 April 2021, when an FIR was filed on the complaint of Praveen Kumar Singh, then Station House Officer of Bandhuakala police station. Police alleged that a public meeting was held in Hasanpur village in support of Salma Begum, an AAP-backed candidate for district panchayat member, without administrative permission. Around 50 to 60 people attended, which police treated as a breach of poll and pandemic rules. Besides Sanjay Singh, the accused included Maqsood Ansari, Salim Ansari, Jagdish Yadav, Sukai, Dharmraj, Zeeshan, Sahban, Sikandar, Jalil and Ajay. Police filed a chargesheet after their investigation. One accused died during the trial, which continued against the rest. Reacting to the verdict, Singh said the case had been lodged against him and his associates five years ago and after a long legal fight, the court had cleared everyone on the basis of "facts and evidence". He also thanked the court for its decision. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: PM Modi’s Jobs Push: Why Rahul Gandhi Calls It ‘Jobless Growth’ | Express Newsroom
content: Why is Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking corporate India to invest more and create jobs after 12 years in power? And why has the Opposition called his remarks an admission of India's jobless growth? In this episode of Express Newsroom, Neeta Sharma is joined by Sandeep Singh, Ishaan, Manoj and Liz Mathew to decode the Prime Minister's remarks, the slowdown in private investment, concerns over employment and the political implications ahead of crucial Assembly elections. Production: Tista Roy Chowdhury Edit: Meetesh Dixit Camera: Madhur & Vikas

headline: Video of woman dancing inside Pilibhit Tiger Reserve goes viral, probe launched
content: The forest department has launched an investigation after a video purportedly showing a woman dancing inside the Pilibhit Tiger Reserve went viral on social media, raising questions over security arrangements and monitoring in the restricted forest area.The video was posted on Tuesday morning on Instagram, showing a woman dancing inside the forest.Pilibhit Tiger Reserve Deputy Director Manish Singh said the department was investigating the video to ascertain where it was shot and whether the woman entered a restricted area."Necessary action will be taken once the facts emerge from the investigation," he said.According to forest department officials, the video came to their notice after it was uploaded to social media.Similar instances of people making social media reels inside the tiger reserve have been reported earlier as well.

headline: ‘World could know about cockroach movement’: Saurav Das on UK visit that didn’t happen
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das said on Tuesday that he had planned to speak about Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and B R Ambedkar at a lecture at the University of Oxford where he was invited by the students’ union. However, he claimed, immigration officials stopped him on Monday night at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport from boarding his flight to London. Das said he wanted to talk about the “cockroach movement” in India — for which he was invited — and how it had grown so large without violence. “The world would have seen how such a big movement happened without any violence,” he said at a press briefing, adding that people in other countries are also curious about it. A show-cause notice, he claimed, was emailed to him about five hours before his flight. He did not see it because he was on his way to the airport, he added. When he reached immigration, officials told him to check his email. There was no response from the government on his claims. According to Das, the notice said that the authorities had received inputs about discrepancies regarding his place of birth. Das said he had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union at Oxford University, as well as at the London School of Economics (LSE), Cambridge University and Queen Mary University. “Getting invited to the Oxford Union is a big honour,” he said. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had also been invited to the Oxford Union earlier but could not go for personal reasons. Das questioned the timing of the notice. His passport was issued in 2019 after police verification, and he said he had since travelled abroad twice — to Norway for a conference, and to one other country. "It's your government only. Why did you give me a passport? Why did you let me go then?" he asked, alleging that he was stopped only because he was associated with CJP. Das said he would respond to the notice. "I will comply with any lawful inquiry. But if you do CAA-NRC in the garb of an inquiry, I will not allow that," he said, referring to the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the proposed National Register of Citizens. He added, "If I was Nirav Modi, Mehul Choksi or Vijay Mallya, I would've gotten the red carpet," he said. He also said some ministers in the government had never been to university. Referring to CJP not being allowed to protest at Jantar Mantar, he said, "The youth is being stopped from speaking everywhere,” he said. No young person should think we are going to back down because of this.”

headline: Haryana links civil servants’ appraisals to school inspections amid CJP’s ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign
content: Chandigarh: Haryana’s bureaucrats will now be judged, in part, on how often they visit a government school. Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi on Monday directed that school adoption, inspection visits and follow-up reports will be part of the Annual Confidential Reports (ACRs) of Class I and Class II officers. This is the second major step Haryana has taken regarding government schools since the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) launched its ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign. Presiding over a meeting on the school adoption initiative and monthly school visits via video conferencing with senior officers and Deputy Commissioners, Rastogi asked for a dedicated column to be added to the ACR forms for the current reporting year. It will record the name of the school an officer has adopted, the number of visits made and the details of inspections carried out. Officers will also have to attach their inspection reports to their annual self-appraisals. He also asked that communication be sent to all administrative secretaries and departments so the ACR format could be changed accordingly. Rastogi said officers visiting schools should go beyond routine inspections by interacting with students and teachers, checking whether the available facilities were being utilised and identifying areas that needed improvement. “The ultimate idea is that all the schools function to the best of their ability and capability,” he said. He added that inspections must follow the prescribed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and observations should be properly documented if any action is needed.

headline: NABARD Goa Organises State Rural Development Conference in Goa; Estimates Credit Potential at ₹17,343 Crore
content: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) organised a State Rural Development Conference in Goa today 24 Nov to develop a framework for promoting rural livelihoods and sustainable development. The conference, chaired by Chief Secretary Dr. V. Candavelou, brought together officials from the State Government, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), ICAR-CCARI, various banks and development organisations. Based on the Potential Linked Credit Plans (PLPs) for North Goa, South Goa and the Kushavati region, NABARD has estimated Goa’s total credit potential at ₹17,343 crore for the financial year 2027–28. Addressing the participants, Dr. Kandavelu urged all stakeholders to align their efforts with the vision of ‘Viksit Goa 2037’ and leverage institutional financial expertise to achieve measurable development outcomes. The one-day conference featured detailed discussions on developing comprehensive value chains in key sectors, including cashew rejuvenation, horticulture, dairy, inland and marine fisheries, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), GI-tagged products and rural tourism. Stakeholders highlighted the need to strengthen essential infrastructure, including the restoration of traditional Khazan embankments, establishment of small-scale processing units, packhouses and cold chain facilities, as well as reliable rural energy systems. The need to develop more robust and bankable schemes was also emphasised. Special attention was given to marginalised and remote communities, with participants stressing the importance of integrating traditional knowledge, local crafts and the unique strengths of these communities into a comprehensive rural development framework. Participants also highlighted the importance of strengthening Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and cooperatives through improved governance, access to working capital and stronger market linkages.

headline: Tamil Nadu District Collector files formal complaint against TVK MLA Vignesh, alleging sexual harassment
content: TVK had earlier taken the position that no formal case existed and that the allegations were politically motivated. However, at an alliance meeting Monday, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay told alliance MLAs that the party is looking into the issue. Police have registered a case against the MLA under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. The development came hours after the Tamil Nadu government told the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any complaint or representation from the Collector in the matter. State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan made the submission before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, while the court heard a criminal writ petition filed by advocate R. Thrishuli seeking directions for the registration of an FIR against the MLA. The petitioner alleged that Vignesh trespassed into the Collector’s bungalow in an inebriated state, threatened officials, and sent obscene messages. The judge directed the prosecutor to contact the Collector and report back. The Collector in her complaint stated that the MLA commented on her attire, behaved inappropriately, and attempted to invade her personal space at public events. The allegations first gained public attention in early November after opposition leader and DMK MP K. Kanimozhi asked for an inquiry. The DMK MP has welcomed the Collector’s action and said, “What will those who questioned me, other political leaders and the DMK that day, and accused even those who spoke about women’s safety of playing politics, say today? I wholeheartedly commend the District Collector, who courageously filed a police complaint against a ruling-party MLA and is setting an example for all women enduring harassment in their workplaces.”

headline: Women giving new direction to rural economy: J-K LG
content: Jammu, Nov 24 (PTI) Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Tuesday said women are playing a significant role in transforming the Union Territory’s rural economy, with self-help groups, women farmers and rural entrepreneurs promoting economic self-reliance through local products, handicrafts, food processing and small enterprises. Sinha said the contribution of women had been instrumental in the progress made by Jammu and Kashmir over the past six to seven years. He said efforts under the Holistic Agriculture Development Programme (HADP) focused on giving rural women due recognition as farmers and providing them access to training and modern technology. “I am pleased that this vision has largely been realised. Women associated with several self-help groups, working alongside women farmers, are giving a new direction to the rural economy,” he said while addressing the gathering at the annual Jhiri Mela on the outskirts of Jammu city. The Lieutenant Governor said women in Jammu and Kashmir are setting new examples of economic self-reliance through local products, handicrafts, food processing and small enterprises, while young women are establishing new benchmarks of innovation in agriculture and allied sectors. Highlighting the achievements of women in education, Sinha said that during a recent university convocation, 25 out of 26 gold medals were awarded to women.

headline: Punjab Roadways, PRTC contractual workers defer 3-day strike after talks with Transport Department
content: Contractual employees of Punjab Roadways and the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) have postponed their three-day statewide strike, scheduled to begin on November 25, following fresh assurances from the state Transport Department.The decision was taken by the Punjab Roadways, Punbus and PRTC Contract Workers Union after telephonic discussions between its representatives and senior Transport Department officials on Tuesday evening.Shamsher Dhillon, general secretary of the union, said, “We have decided to wait until Wednesday afternoon for the government to fulfil its commitments before deciding our next course of action.”He said the Secretary and the Director, State Transport, had assured the union that contract numbers would be allotted to outsourced employees of Punbus and PRTC on Wednesday and their agreements issued immediately.The union said a meeting with the Transport Minister had been scheduled for November 27 to discuss and resolve its remaining demands.The strike had been announced over delays in implementing assurances given by the state government during previous meetings. The employees had been demanding regularisation, with appointment letters distributed only to employees at the Chandigarh depot, while those posted at other depots were still awaiting completion of the process.In an earlier video statement, Resham Gill, state president of the union, had said employees had met Transport Minister Harpal Cheema in Chandigarh on Monday, following which appointment letters were issued to Punbus and PRTC employees at the Chandigarh depot. However, the department had yet to complete the process for employees at other depots, prompting the union to announce the strike.The employees are seeking regularisation of thousands of contractual and outsourced workers employed as drivers, conductors and workshop staff, many of whom have been working for more than a decade. Their other demands include an end to recruitment through third-party contractors and the withdrawal of FIRs registered against employees during previous protests.

headline: Himachal Pradesh Government
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta today said that India has witnessing a remarkable cultural renaissance alongside rapid modern development under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the country's rich spiritual and civilisational heritage gaining renewed recognition on the global stage. The Governor was accompanied with the Lady Governor Bindu Gupta. Addressing the closing ceremony of the International Shree Renuka Ji Fair in Sirmaur district, the Governor said the Prime Minister's mantra of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’ had provided a new direction to the country's development journey by integrating modern progress with the preservation of its ancient cultural and spiritual heritage. Referring to the Shree Ram Temple in Ayodhya, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Shree Mahakal Lok in Ujjain, Kavinder Gupta said these initiatives reflected India's renewed cultural consciousness. He observed that religious and cultural gatherings like the Shree Renuka Ji Fair were instrumental in strengthening India's civilisational identity, preserving traditional values and promoting social harmony. Highlighting the significance of the divine reunion of Mata Renuka Ji and Bhagwan Parshuram Ji, the Governor said the fair symbolised maternal affection, sacrifice, devotion and the enduring strength of Indian family values. Emphasising the prominent position accorded to women in Sanatan Dharma, Kavinder Gupta said the traditions of invoking Sita-Ram, Radhe-Krishna and Lakshmi-Narayan reflected the profound reverence for womanhood in Indian culture. “Respect for women must not remain confined to religious beliefs but should be reflected in our conduct and social practices,” he said, adding that in consonance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of women-led development, society must create greater opportunities for women to assume leadership roles in education, science, entrepreneurship, politics and public administration.

headline: Bisleri says FSSAI scrutiny limited to one Goa batch, now out of circulation
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) Packaged drinking water maker Bisleri International on Tuesday said the FSSAI scrutiny related to just one batch manufactured at its Goa plant in September 2025, which is no longer in circulation, adding that subsequent testing found bromate levels in the sample within permissible limits. The company said all its 143 manufacturing plants remain operational and compliant with FSSAI regulations, with the Goa facility also continuing operations without any suspension order from the regulator. “Bisleri produces more than 50,000 batches annually. FSSAI’s sale prohibition applies only to one Batch GO 270, manufactured in Goa on 27 September 2025. There are no stocks of this batch in the market currently,” it said. “The FSSAI has categorically and conclusively clarified on 23rd November 2026 that bromates were found below the permissible limit on re-testing of the above batch sample.” Responding to an FSSAI clarification issued on November 23, Bisleri said the regulatory action related exclusively to batch GO 270, manufactured on September 27, 2025, and that no stocks from the batch were currently available in the market. The company said FSSAI had clarified that bromate levels detected on retesting the batch sample were below the permissible limit. Separately, it acknowledged that one of six samples tested in a subsequent round had reported polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch had cleared all parameters. On Sunday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had said it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International, whose one sample of packaged drinking water failed in lab tests following the detection of bromate beyond permissible limits and, on subsequent testing, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

headline: NIC's fragmented IT architecture raises questions over cyber resilience
content: There is an application on the Indian government's IT platform to ensure the secrecy of state Cabinet papers. The application is named Gopan, or secret, the name almost equivalent to keeping the lock open for hackers to rifle through the files stored there.

headline: Sikh votes to panthic hot buttons: Why BJP-SAD alliance faces an uphill task
content: The BJP chose the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the first Sikh Guru, on Tuesday to join hands with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the Punjab Assembly elections slated for February 2027. This announcement was made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah at a joint press conference with SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the BJP headquarters in Delhi. On paper, the reunion of the two old NDA allies, and its symbolism, appear to be formidable. However, going by various factors and past instances, both the BJP and the SAD have reasons to tread cautiously over their poll campaign. Following the year-long agitation by farmers on the Delhi borders, in November 2021, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the three central farm laws, it was also the occasion of Guru Nanak Dev's birth anniversary. However, three months later, in February 2022, when the BJP contested the Assembly polls on its own, with the SAD then having broken up with the party in September 2020 over these legislation, the move did not yield any electoral dividends. While the AAP swept the polls, winning 92 of the state's 117 seats as against the Congress's 18, the BJP and the SAD could win just two and three seats respectively. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP could not win any seat in Punjab, but its vote share rose to 18%. On the other hand, the Akali Dal won only one out of 13 seats, but its vote share plunged to 13%. Observers say despite the two parties' move to renew their alliance now, there is no guarantee that their old equations, with the BJP aiming to garner Hindu votes and the SAD Sikh votes, would again deliver results for them. In the wake of the backlash from farmers among other people across Punjab, the Akali Dal was forced to leave the NDA. The SAD had then also accused the BJP of interfering in Sikh institutions, including the Akal Takht, with Badals even alleging that the BJP had tried to destabilise their party. Both sides have now chosen to put their bitter conflict behind them. Panthic challenge The Akalis' biggest task now would be to win back the Sikh vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, radical preacher and Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) chief Amritpal Singh, wh has been incarcerated in a Dibrugarh jail in Assam since April 2023, won the Khadoor Sahib seat, while Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa, ex-PM Indira Gandhi’s assassin Beant Singh’s son, won from Faridkot. In the 2017 Assembly polls, which saw the return of the Congress to power by defeating the incumbent SAD-BJP, a large section of Sikh voters seeking justice in the sacrilege cases had backed the party, which then shifted its support to the AAP in 2022. While the alleged failings of the AAP and the Congress to ensure justice in the sacrilege cases give an opening to the SAD in the 2027 polls, the BJP has also drawn fire for its Haryana government's repeated moves to grant parole to Gurmeet Ram Rahim, an accused in the sacrilege cases. His Dera Sacha Sauda is believed to have backed the BJP since 2024. Whether the Akalis would let the BJP court the Dera may be a friction point in their relationship ahead. While Amit Shah has flagged the eradication of the drug menace as a key plank of the BJP-SAD alliance, Amritpal Singh had also run a campaign against drugs earlier. The previous SAD-led government had been in the dock for its alleged failures to curb drugs. It has also been alleged that the ruling BJP has not been able to check drug smuggling through various routes – from the Pakistan border to various states in the country including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi. Seat-sharing, turncoats The BJP and the SAD have yet to announce their seat sharing formula. A larger share of seats for the BJP may cause resentment within the SAD, sources said. Several former Congress and AAP leaders, who have switched to the BJP over the months, have been opposed to the Akalis. They include leaders like former IG Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh and H S Phoolka. Now, BJP leader and ex-Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu will also have to share stage with the SAD leaders seeking the release of Balwant Singh Rajoana, who had been sentenced to death for the assassination of former Congress CM and Bittu's grandfather, Beant Singh. Sikh prisoners, 1984 riots The BJP dispensation in Delhi had not allowed Jagtar Singh Hawara, also a convict sentenced to life in the Beant Singh murder case, parole to meet his ailing mother, even as the Sikh bodies' pleas for commuting Rajoana's death sentence remain pending. The Kartarpur Corridor has also remained closed since the terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam in April 2025, even though the SAD, SGPC and Akal Takht have repeatedly sought its reopening. The Akali Dal has long kept its guns trained on the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, but it has not worked in several elections in the past. The Congress has also been going all out to woo Sikh voters. Its decision to appoint former Indian hockey captain Pargat Singh, who had started his political stint in the SAD, is said to be driven by the Sikh vote. He could be a significant hurdle for the Akali Dal in its bid to regain its traditional base.

headline: Anaemia incidence lower, finds ICMR survey, but over half of India’s women still affected
content: New Delhi: The burden of anaemia in India is lower than that reported in previous national surveys, with severe cases accounting for less than 2 percent of most population groups, a new survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) has found. The bad news is that anaemia continues to affect more than half of women of reproductive age and nearly half of adolescent girls, pointing to a substantial public health burden despite decades of government efforts to tackle it. Anaemia is a condition in which the level of haemoglobin, a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body, is lower than normal. It can cause fatigue, weakness, dizziness and breathlessness, and affect people’s health and ability to carry out daily activities Conducted between 2023 and 2025, the survey found anaemia in 55.9 percent of women of reproductive age, 46.3 percent of adolescent girls aged 10–19 years and 41.8 percent of children aged 12–59 months. Among pregnant women, 43.6 per cent were anaemic, while the figure was 58.1 percent among lactating women. The prevalence was lower among adolescent boys, at 22.8 percent, and men aged 20–59 years, at 22 percent. Called the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), the exercise covered more than 2 lakh people across over 81,000 households in 183 districts and 35 states and Union Territories. Researchers analysed more than 1.7 lakh blood samples to estimate haemoglobin levels. Released on Monday, the findings come against the backdrop of India’s decades-long effort to reduce anaemia through iron and folic acid supplementation, screening and treatment under programmes such as Anaemia Mukt Bharat. They also provide fresh national estimates, as the recently released NFHS-6 fact sheets did not include figures on anaemia. The government had said that a separate ICMR survey would provide these figures. The survey has also found considerable variations in anaemia across states. State-wise estimates show that among women aged 15–49, West Bengal recorded the highest prevalence among states at 72.4 percent, followed by Assam (71.9 percent), Chhattisgarh (71.5 percent), Punjab (70.5 percent) and Tripura (70 percent). Gujarat reported 66.2 percent, above the national average of 55.9 per cent. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands recorded the highest estimate overall, at 81.2 percent.

headline: From Kanpur to Ropar: 42 years on, 1984 anti-Sikh riots survivor’s fight for compensation continues
content: Forty-two years after the anti-Sikh riots of 1984 devastated his home and disrupted his life, 80-year-old Harnam Singh, a resident of Giani Zail Singh Nagar in Ropar town, continues to wait for justice. What began as a fight to recover compensation for his belongings, which were looted and burnt by rioters in Kanpur, has turned into a decades-long struggle against official apathy, with the elderly survivor still awaiting his rightful dues.Now settled in Ropar, Harnam Singh has spent a major part of his life seeking compensation for the losses he suffered during the horrific events of November 1984. His long-pending case has now been taken up by Ropar-based advocate Abhimanyu Singh Rana, who has approached the Home Department of the Uttar Pradesh Government, seeking details of the current status of Harnam Singh’s compensation claim.Harnam Singh said he was employed as a fitter with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, when anti-Sikh violence erupted in November 1984 following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.On November 2, 1984, when violence against members of the Sikh community had engulfed several parts of the country, rioters allegedly targeted his house in Kanpur. His belongings were looted and whatever remained was set on fire. Within hours, the home he had built through years of hard work was reduced to ashes, leaving the family to cope with the financial and emotional consequences of the violence.A police report was subsequently registered at Chakeri police station in Kanpur, documenting the value of the looted belongings at Rs 48,118. However, despite the registration of the report and official documentation of his losses, he has received only Rs 2,000 in relief to date.The family eventually left Kanpur in 1985 and shifted to Ropar, hoping to rebuild its life away from the memories of the violence. However, relocation did not bring an end to Harnam Singh’s struggle. For years, he continued visiting government offices, submitting representations and approaching political leaders in the hope that the authorities would acknowledge his losses and release the remaining compensation.His efforts, however, failed to yield any results. On March 20, 2010, the Uttar Pradesh Government rejected his compensation claim. Refusing to give up, he subsequently approached the National Commission for Minorities, which also wrote to the Uttar Pradesh Government, seeking appropriate action.Despite the commission’s intervention, the matter remained unresolved. More than four decades after the riots, Baba Harnam Singh is still fighting for compensation for the property and belongings destroyed in the violence.Today, he lives with his wife and only son, who works in a private company. He hopes to receive compensation for his life’s earnings, lost in the 1984 riots, during his lifetime.Advocate Abhimanyu Singh Rana has urged the Uttar Pradesh Government to take into account the survivor’s advanced age and ensure that his claim is settled without further delay.“In case the claim is not settled, we shall fight the case legally in the courts,” he said.For Baba Harnam Singh, the compensation is no longer merely a question of money. It is also about recognition of the suffering endured by his family and the hope that the injustice of 1984 will finally receive official acknowledgment.

headline: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
content: COLOMBO Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan warns he may not 'return alive', seeks medical treatment for himself, wife Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan warns he may not 'return alive', seeks medical treatment for himself, wife Khan, the former cricketer-turned-politician and founder of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, has been incarcerated since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan warns he may not 'return alive', seeks medical treatment for himself, wife storyline 1 Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game. Pakistan govt. denying rights to Imran Khan and his wife; his party unit alleges Pakistan govt. denying rights to Imran Khan and his wife; his party unit alleges Shafi Jan, a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party Minister in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province alleged that the jailed former PM and his wife are denied of legal rights and healthcare Pakistan govt. denying rights to Imran Khan and his wife; his party unit alleges storyline 1 Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

headline: Rahul Gandhi didn’t use the ‘genocide’ word now. But Congress has many times in the past
content: Rahul Gandhi’s comments in Chicago on India-Israel relations have generated vocal criticism from the Left. But context matters, and it’s not usually visible in short social media clips. Gandhi was not outlining his stance on the Israel-Palestine question or on Israel’s war in Gaza. He was responding to a specific question about whether Prime Minister Narendra Modi was too close to Israel, and if this was hampering India’s relations with other countries. Gandhi gave a measured reply, saying that India and Israel have longstanding ties but India is larger than Israel and “our foreign policy should be based on what’s good for us and not based on what’s good for someone else.” This statement speaks directly to debates in the US over the influence of pro-Israel lobbies like AIPAC. In an April 2026 Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos poll, 52 per cent of Americans said that Israel had “too much” influence on the US decision to go to war with Iran. In the Indian context, Gandhi’s statement was a thinly veiled criticism of Modi’s kowtowing to Israel, including his poorly timed visit to Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in February, only two days before the US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Israeli human rights lawyer Eitay Mack wrote at the time that Modi “acted and spoke like the leader of a minor state visiting a global power, desperate to curry favour.” Gandhi went on to condemn both the 7 October 2023 attack by Hamas and Israel’s brutal military campaign in Gaza, without using the word ‘genocide’. But a brief, pointed answer to a specific question does not represent the sum and substance of a leader or his party’s position. Consider the Congress party’s statements since the war began in 2023. Sonia Gandhi has repeatedly criticised Israel’s conduct, most recently writing that “in the two-and-a-half years since the dastardly, horrific, and absolutely unacceptable attack by Hamas on Israel, it has become clear that the retaliation of the Israeli armed forces and political leadership has been characterised by wanton cruelty and barbarity”. She also said that some Israeli leaders have displayed “clear genocidal intent”. Her statements were amplified and reposted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra has on several occasions used the word genocide to describe Israel’s actions in Gaza. Jairam Ramesh, the party’s communications head, has described Israeli actions in Gaza as an “ongoing genocide”.

headline: T.N. Minister inaugurates infrastructure projects in Marakkanam
content: VILLUPURAM Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu on Tuesday inaugurated various infrastructure works taken up under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMSSY) scheme at Mandavai Pudhukuppam in Marakkanam in Villupuram district. The works were taken up at an estimate of ₹1.4 crore. According to a press note, the works included the construction of 190 artificial reef modules and the construction of a net-mending shed and a fish-drying platform. The artificial reefs, comprising 80 triangular modules, 55 grouper modules and 55 well-ring modules, were installed on the seabed to provide habitat for marine organisms and help improve local fishery resources. Mr. Vanni Arasu also inaugurated fish landing centres at Vasavankuppam, Kaipanikuppam and Alagankuppam, each built at a cost of ₹80 lakh. Collector Sheik Abdul Rahman participated. EOM

headline: Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister
content: KALABURAGI The State government is examining a series of measures to address the growing problem of human-elephant conflict in Hassan district, including the installation of steel-rope barricades and fitting GPS collars on elephants to monitor their movements, Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy said on Tuesday. The Minister said residents of Belur, Sakleshpur and other parts of Hassan district have been facing difficulties owing to elephant movement, and the State government was taking their concerns seriously. The Minister was speaking to presspersons after inaugurating the new main entrance gate and various development works at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district. The works were taken up at a cost of ₹18 crore with assistance from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation and other sources. He also laid the foundation stone for additional works estimated to cost ₹3 crore. Pointing to the fragmented nature of forest areas in the region, he said nearly 13,000 acres of forest in Belur taluk were spread across nine separate patches, and the nearly one lakh acres of forest area in Sakleshpur were similarly divided into more than 80 patches. “This fragmentation made it difficult to regulate elephant movement and prevent human-elephant conflict,” he said. The proposal to relocate elephants to the Bhadra forest area had been under discussion for some time, and the government would also take into consideration the concerns expressed by local elected representatives, Mr. Reddy said. “The feasibility of installing steel-rope barricades to prevent elephants from straying out of forests is being examined, subject to financial constraints. A plan to fit GPS collars on elephants and continuously monitor their movements was also being implemented,” he said. Kamalapur zoo development Speaking on the development initiatives taken at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district, Mr. Reddy said that several facilities have been developed at the zoo with funding from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation, the Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation and contributions from mining companies. “Hampi is an important historical destination that attracts a large number of tourists. The government is committed to developing the zoo as an additional attraction,” he said. The Minister said that arrangements had been made to ensure an uninterrupted supply of water, fodder and food for the animals and birds. Solar-powered borewells had been installed to ensure a regular water supply and to meet emergency requirements. Shade had also been provided for the animals, while a sprinkler system had been introduced to maintain the plants. The zoo would be provided with additional animal species, with priority given to their health and conservation, he said. New open and closed jeeps and buses had also been arranged to facilitate safari tours. K.S. Basavanthappa, Vijayanagara district in-charge Minister; H.R. Gaviyappa, Hosapete MLA; E. Tukaram, Ballari MP; M.P. Latha Mallikarjun, Harapanahalli MLA; K. Rangaswamy, Karnataka Zoo Authority chairman; Kavita Mannikeri, Deputy Commissioner; S. Jahnavi, Superintendent of Police; and senior forest department officials were present.

headline: SCCL to provide free education to contract workers’ children
content: PEDDAPALLI Children of contract and outsourced workers of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) will get free education up to Class X in Singareni-run schools from the 2026-27 academic year, extending a key welfare benefit to thousands of workers’ families. The decision is expected to benefit children of nearly 30,000 contract workers employed across the company’s 12 areas. More than 400 children already studying in the nine schools run by the Singareni Collieries Educational Society (SCES) will be among the immediate beneficiaries, according to a press release. Under the initiative, children of contract and outsourced workers will be eligible for free admission to Singareni schools in their respective areas and will not have to pay tuition fees up to Class X. The decision is part of a series of welfare measures announced at a recent meeting of public representatives from the coal belt region, chaired by Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka. In another measure, SCCL recently extended a profit-sharing bonus of ₹5,500 to contract workers for the first time, bringing them under a benefit previously not available to them.

headline: YSRCP and government trade charges over temple demolition in Tirupati
content: TIRUPATI A controversy erupted over the demolition of a roadside Anjaneya Swamy temple at Anjaneyapuram in Renigunta mandal of Tirupati district on Monday, with the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) accusing the State government of hurting Hindu sentiments through what it termed ‘rampant destruction’. The State government, however, clarified that the demolition was part of the widening exercise undertaken to develop the Renigunta-Kadapa stretch of National Highway 716 into a four-lane road. While former YSRCP MLA and former TTD trust board chairman Bhumana Karunakar Reddy staged a sit-in at the demolition site on Monday in protest, Minister for Endowments Anam Ramanarayana Reddy dismissed it as ‘political drama’ on Tuesday. The Minister said revenue and panchayat records showed that the temple was built 70 years ago and not 1,000 years ago, as claimed by the YSRCP. He also rejected Mr. Karunakar Reddy’s claim that it was a self-manifested (Swayambhu) shrine, stating that local villagers had built it seven decades ago. The Minister pointed out that the land acquisition award for the road-widening project was issued by the erstwhile YSRCP government in October 2023, paving the way for the demolition. “Either out of ignorance or wilful defiance, the YSRCP leader has tried to portray the government in a poor light,” he charged. The government had deposited ₹59.30 lakh into the temple Executive Officer’s account as compensation for the 10 cents of land acquired. The amount was intended to be used for constructing a bigger temple on an adjoining 50 cents of land. Mr. Ramanarayana Reddy said the deities had been carefully dismantled in accordance with the Agama Shastra and kept safe for re-consecration before the structure was pulled down. He appealed to political parties not to seek political mileage by playing with religious sentiments.

headline: Guidelines sought to define local bodies’ role in health services
content: PALAKKAD The government has taken seriously a complaint by a medical officer seeking fresh guidelines to prevent local bodies from sidelining Health Department officials in the implementation of health programmes. The complaint, submitted by medical officer K. Prathibha, follows an incident in which polio drops were administered to children at a veterinary hospital at Changaliri near Mannarkkad. Dr. Prathibha wrote to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan seeking action to avoid further embarrassment to Health Department officials. Chief Minister’s office forwarded the complaint to the Director of Health Services for examination and appropriate action. The vaccination was conducted at the veterinary hospital despite the presence of a sub-centre of the family health centre in the area. The sub-centre, however, remains non-functional even after its inauguration. Following protests from local residents, the vaccination centre was shifted to an anganwadi at Parambulli. In her complaint, Dr. Prathibha said local self-government institutions should consult Health Department officials before making decisions on health programmes. She pointed out that the involvement of local bodies in managing health institutions was intended to improve public services and transparency, not to sideline department officials. She also alleged that some local representatives were acting as though they had sole authority over health institutions, leaving Health Department employees with little role in decisions about their work. Dr. Prathibha has sought clear government guidelines defining the roles of local bodies and Health Department officials and preventing interference in the duties assigned to department employees.

headline: Expanded NCD survey in Andhra Pradesh to cover four additional health conditions
content: VIJAYAWADA The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare has announced that health screenings being conducted in the State under the Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) survey will be expanded to cover four additional health conditions — obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders. Until now, screening has been conducted for people aged 18 and above for five major health conditions — hypertension, diabetes, oral cancer, breast cancer and cervical cancer. The health screenings will be conducted every financial year, and the survey for the financial year 2026–27 is expected to begin soon. “The programme is being expanded, considering changing lifestyles, rising obesity levels and growing risk of other chronic diseases,” a release from the department said on Tuesday. Participating in a virtual review meeting on the upcoming NCD programme, Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav briefed officials on the proposed changes and the precautions to be taken. “The focus is on identifying these diseases at an early stage before the problem becomes a serious one,” he said. Under the new survey, individuals who are overweight will be identified at an early stage, and their risk of developing other health complications will be assessed. They will also receive guidance on dietary habits, physical activity and weight management. People with obesity, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disorders will also be assessed for their risk of developing fatty liver disease. The survey will also identify those with chronic respiratory conditions at an early stage. Those with symptoms will be examined by medical officers at the Primary Health Centres (PHCs). Patients requiring further investigations will be referred to the regional and district hospitals, where spirometers will be made available to assess lung function. To assess the mental health condition of an individual, a questionnaire will be prepared, which will include questions to identify symptoms of depression, anxiety, memory-related problems and psychotic disorders. Individuals identified as being at risk will undergo preliminary telephonic assessments through Tele-MANAS. Those requiring further medical evaluation will be referred to the appropriate healthcare facilities through the District Mental Health Programme. The Minister directed the officials to adopt a Facial Recognition System (FRS)-based identification mechanism during the upcoming survey, which means biometric details would be collected during the survey for verification. An Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID would be generated for individuals, and their medical records linked to it. Details of screenings, disease diagnosis, treatment and follow-up consultations would be digitally recorded.

headline: Karnataka HC declines to quash case against government doctor for attesting documents of 14 illegal Bangladeshi immigrants to secure Aadhaar card
content: Bengaluru The High Court of Karnataka refused to quash a criminal proceedings against a government doctor for allegedly attesting the forged documents related to residential addresses of several illegal Bangladeshi immigrants enabling them to secure Aadhaar card in Bengaluru. Justice H.P. Sandesh passed the order while rejecting a petition filed by Lokesh, a government doctor who is a gazetted officer authorised to attest documents. The criminal proceeding was initiated after the Bellandur police in 2017 filed a chargesheet against the petitioner after investigating the complaint lodged by the Deputy Director of Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Bengaluru, and a metropolitan magistrate court had in 2020 taken cognisance of offence against him and others. The chargesheet alleged that Dr. Lokesh attested address and identity proofs for 14 Bangladeshi nationals without documentary verification, facilitating their acquisition of Aadhaar cards. Rejecting arguments on behalf Dr. Lokesh’s that cognisance was taken against him sans prior sanction for prosecution under Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court said that the necessity of prior sanction depends on whether the act complained of is directly connected to the official duties. Attesting documents without verifying documentary proof in favour of a series of foreign nationals who had allegedly entered the country illegally is not a public duty, the court noted while pointing out that report of the Forensic Sciences Laboratory had confirmed the signatures on the attested documents as his signatures.

headline: LDF weaponises RSP’s ‘mutiny’ to put Keralam UDF government on the defensive
content: Thiruvananthapuram The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) in Keralam on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) weaponised the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP)’s unusually vocal break with the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) leadership to portray the ruling alliance as riven by disarray, dissent and lack of consensus. The RSP on Monday publicly expressed annoyance at the lack of regular UDF meetings, delays in political appointments to various corporations and boards, and the conferral of Cabinet-rank positions without consultation. The UDF constituent also flagged the lack of regular alliance meetings to thrash out key issues before they become government policy. The RSP also demanded that party veteran A.A. Aziz be accommodated in a Cabinet-equivalent position, given the yardstick set by the Congress leadership. ‘Widening divide’ LDF convener T.P. Ramakrishnan said the RSP’s pushback exposed a widening divide within the UDF. He said the RSP had obliquely criticised Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan for granting Cabinet-level ranking to Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission chairperson and Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader M.K. Muneer; Forward Bloc leader and Keralam government’s Special Representative in New Delhi G. Devarajan; and Kerala Congress leader and Chief Whip Apu John Joseph without consultations in the UDF. Mr. Ramakrishnan said the RSP’s “mutiny”, led by Forest Minister Shibu Baby John and N.K. Premachandran, MP, has come on the heels of a sparring between Ministers and Mr. Satheesan in last week’s Cabinet meeting. Collective responsibility He said the Ministers had accused Mr. Satheesan of pursuing policy in other departments whimsically, thereby risking the constitutionally mandated collective responsibility in the Cabinet. Mr. Ramakrishnan said Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph’s grievance that he learned of key decisions in his department through newspapers indicated growing fissures in the Cabinet. He said the RSP’s grouse with Mr. Satheesan dovetailed with UDF convener Adoor Prakash’s complaint to Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge that the Chief Minister’s Office was rendering the alliance leadership redundant through unilateral decision-making. Mr. Ramakrishnan accused the UDF of fooling the electorate, which gave the ruling alliance the mandate to govern.
