headline: 'Comply with SC order, release detainees': Madras HC directs Tamil Nadu government ahead of deepam lighti
content: NEW DELHI: The Madras HC's Madurai Bench on Tuesday directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court's order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill. It also directed the officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under Thiruparankundram prohibitory orders.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid heightened security and restrictions ahead of the ceremony.The court's intervention came amid a dispute over the implementation of the apex court's November 20 order, which permitted a one-time lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.The state informed the HC that 258 persons have detained apprehending disorder based on intelligence and past conduct.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran, who was placed under house arrest while attempting to visit Thiruparankundram, accused the police of preventing him from exercising his fundamental rights."In the absence of any legally valid prohibitory order, the police are preventing me from visiting the temple to offer prayers. Preventing us from leaving our homes in the name of arrest amounts to a violation of an individual's fundamental rights," he said.Citing Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution, Nagenthran said citizens had the right to worship according to their faith and freely practise religious activities."However, these fundamental rights are being denied in Tamil Nadu. Despite the Supreme Court's directions, how can restrictions on lighting the ceremonial lamp and offering prayers at sacred places such as Thiruparankundram be justified?" he said.He also alleged that around 200 police personnel had been deployed outside his residence since morning and that police vehicles followed him even when he attempted to drop his children at school."Such acts of oppression are taking place only in Tamil Nadu and are not witnessed in any other state," he said.Nagenthran further accused the state government of using the restrictions to divert public attention from other issues, including sexual harassment allegations against ruling party members and MLAs and the Kallakurichi incident.The dispute centres on a demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The issue has been contested for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government-facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.The Supreme Court, in its November 20 interim order, permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah. It directed that the ceremony be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.The Tamil Nadu government moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its interim order.The Madurai district administration had imposed prohibitory orders from November 23 night until November 25 morning, banning public gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of the hill. Security was also tightened, with more than 5,600 police personnel deployed across the hill and surrounding areas.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Bengal announces ₹2,000 monthly allowance for unemployed youth: Who is eligible? Know key details
content: The West Bengal government has announced that graduates as well as diploma holders from vocational institutions attached to the government who are still unemployed will be eligible for a monthly allowance of ₹2,000 under the 'Bhorsha Karmasuchi' scheme. The announcement was made by the state's chief minister, Suvendu Adhikari, on Monday.Non-graduates who are unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of ₹1,500, CM Adhikari also announced.Adhikari added that, as promised in the BJP's election manifesto, the allowances will be increased to ₹3,000 and ₹2,000, respectively, from the 2028-29 financial year.Eligible candidates have to be between the ages of 21 and 45.Bhorsha Karmasuchi, the new scheme launched by the BJP government under Adhikari, has replaced the earlier Yuvasathi scheme, which was launched by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee's administration."We urge our youngsters to be patient for some time, as we have initiated many new schemes, cleared arrears and taken on huge financial responsibilities. We will keep our commitment," Adhikari told reporters after a cabinet meeting, as per a report by PTI.Adhikari also said that verification of the 54 lakh existing beneficiaries under the previous government's scheme will be completed by 31 December.Those who have not yet applied for the same will be able to submit their applications through the 'Apnar Sarkar Apnar Pashe' programme.Adhikari added that the applications will be forwarded to the Youth Welfare Department.By the second week of every month, the allowance will be transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts. The formal launch of the scheme will be done at an event in February.A family can have a maximum of two beneficiaries, and those receiving the ₹3,000 monthly allowance under the Annapurna Yojana will not be eligible.No application fees for Bengal govt job exams: Suvendu AdhikariAdhikari also announced on Monday that his government will do away with the application fees charged for applying for government jobs, and instead, his administration would be cutting down expenses on administrative meetings and official programmes to fund the relief for aspirants."Charging unemployed youths fees to apply for government job exams is a crime. It reflects extreme narrow-mindedness," he said while announcing the decision after a Cabinet meeting in Kolkata."As far as administrative meetings are concerned, we are completing programmes in just one day that earlier took five days. We have substantially cut the grandeur of government events. As a result, we are generating considerable savings," Adhikari was quoted as saying by PTI.The CM also drew a comparison on spending with the Mamata government, saying that the previous dispensation had spent ₹611 crore in organising 67 administrative review meetings."We do not spend anywhere near that amount on our meetings. You can assume that our expenditure is not even 20 per cent of what the previous government used to incur," he said."From today onwards, no application fee will be charged for government job exams," he announced.Adhikari also announced the Cabinet's decision to undertake fresh recruitments, stating that a total of 10,146 appointments would be made across various state government departments. "Of these, 1,000 posts have been earmarked for the Eastern Frontier Rifles."With PTI inputs

headline: Beyond sun, sand and tourism: How Goa is emerging as a national hub for higher education
content: With ₹3,400 crore allocated to education, new universities, national institutes, digital learning and industry-linked skill programmes, Goa is positioning itself as a major centre for higher education and research. !Image 1: By blending foundational reforms with forward-looking investments in technology and higher learning, the State administration is steadily laying the groundwork for a future where Goa is celebrated not only as a haven for travellers, but as a premier intellectual and educational powerhouse on the national and global map. By blending foundational reforms with forward-looking investments in technology and higher learning, the State administration is steadily laying the groundwork for a future where Goa is celebrated not only as a haven for travellers, but as a premier intellectual and educational powerhouse on the national and global map. For decades, Goa’s global identity was anchored in its sun-drenched coastline, vibrant hospitality sector, and relaxed pace of life. Today, a quiet yet transformative revolution is reshaping the state’s economic and intellectual landscape. Backed by policy reforms, this smallest state in the Country is rapidly evolving into a hub for higher learning, research, and skill development. With a high literacy rate, Goa has long possessed strong academic fundamentals. However, for years, ambitious local students were forced to migrate to other states for specialized degrees. Now, with the State actively positioning itself as a world-class education hub, it will help in retaining local talent while attracting candidates from outside the State.

headline: India's informal economy grows at record pace in Jul-Sep, but paid job creation lags
content: New Delhi: India's unincorporated non-farm economy expanded at its fastest quarterly pace on record in July-September, but the surge was driven largely by owner-operated businesses rather than paid employment, pointing to an expansion in self-employment even as the creation of hired jobs remained relatively weak. .The number of establishments rose 18.81 per cent from a year earlier to 9.47 crore, while employment increased 16.86 per cent to 15.03 crore, the National Statistics Office (NSO) said in its latest Quarterly Bulletin of the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. Both growth rates were the highest in the quarterly series. .The composition of employment, however, presents a more mixed picture. The number of hired workers increased by only about five per cent to 3.49 crore, while working owners accounted for nearly 62 per cent of the workforce, up from 59.98 per cent a year earlier. .India’s economy is growing, but are jobs growing with it?.The figures suggest that the expansion of India's vast small-business economy is translating more rapidly into self-employment and owner-operated enterprises than into conventional wage-paying jobs. .Growth was broad-based across rural and urban areas, although urban establishments expanded faster. The number of urban enterprises increased 22.05 per cent year-on-year, compared with 16.05 per cent in rural areas. Employment growth, however, was marginally stronger in rural areas at 17.52 per cent, against 16.30 per cent in urban centres. .Services recorded the strongest expansion among the three broad sectors covered by the survey. Establishments in the 'other services' category grew 29 per cent, while employment increased by more than 33 per cent. .Trade establishments rose 11.70 per cent, with employment increasing 8.36 per cent. Manufacturing establishments expanded 10.55 per cent, but employment growth was more modest at 3.52 per cent. .Retail trade, repair and maintenance, land transport, personal services and apparel manufacturing were among the fastest-growing activities. .The share of hired workers in total employment declined to 23.22 per cent, while working owners' share increased to 61.99 per cent from 59.98 per cent a year earlier. The number of working owners rose by roughly 21 per cent, based on the published employment shares. .The average number of workers per establishment also declined to 1.59 from 1.61, suggesting that the increase in enterprise numbers has not been accompanied by a corresponding rise in average establishment size. .Women accounted for slightly more than 31 per cent of the workforce, compared with 28.70 per cent a year earlier, indicating an increase in their participation in the unincorporated non-farm sector. .The survey also pointed to greater formalisation and digital adoption among unincorporated enterprises. .The share of establishments registered with at least one government or other authority increased to 43.28 per cent from 37.20 per cent a year earlier. Around 80 per cent of establishments reported using cashless payment methods, while nearly 84 per cent used the internet for business purposes. .Government not bothered about health of economy but about Rahul Gandhi speaking about it: Congress.The NSO, however, noted that questions relating to technology adoption had been redesigned in the latest round, including the introduction of a separate question on online banking and payment gateways, which could affect comparability with previous estimates. .The latest estimates come from a quarterly sample of 1,80,025 establishments spread across 6,002 survey units, substantially smaller than the sample used for the annual survey. .The survey covers unincorporated manufacturing, trade and services enterprises but excludes construction. Its estimates therefore provide a picture of a specific segment of the economy and should not be interpreted as a direct measure of overall GDP or economy-wide employment growth. .Launched in 2021-22, the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises has become an important source of information on businesses operating outside the corporate sector. Quarterly bulletins have been published since 2025. .The latest annual survey, covering calendar 2025, estimated 7.92 crore establishments and 12.81 crore workers, broadly in line with the July-September 2025 quarterly estimates of 7.97 crore establishments and 12.86 crore workers.

headline: Before the next peg, a blood test: MP stations doctors outside liquor shops after spate of deaths
content: A liquor shop is probably the last place where customers expect to be greeted by a doctor, asking questions about their health. But in Madhya Pradesh's Bundelkhand region, medical teams have been stationed outside liquor outlets, screening customers, collecting blood samples and advising them to cut down on drinking. In Sagar district, the administration has gone a step further, asking liquor-shop operators to prepare lists of their most regular customers — including those who turn up before the shops even open — so that doctors can identify and examine chronic drinkers. The exercise follows a spate of deaths in the district, including 20 in a suspected spurious-liquor tragedy in September. Speaking to The Indian Express, Collector Dilip Kumar Yadav said the campaign aimed to identify people at risk due to prolonged and excessive alcohol consumption, often combined with existing medical conditions and poor nutrition. “The concern is excessive consumption, particularly among those who drink throughout the day - from morning to evening. There are also people who have other diseases or comorbidities. Because of these factors, they are at greater risk. You can look at this as an awareness exercise,” he said. Yadav said the administration had specifically sought the help of liquor-shop operators because they were familiar with customers who drank regularly. “There are some people who come to the liquor shops every day. The shops open at 8 am, and there are people who arrive and sit there even before that. The shop operators know them. We got them to prepare lists of who these people are. There are some who do not even eat properly. They become chronic drinkers over time and can develop health problems later,” he said. The lists were then used to identify people who could be brought in for medical examinations. Teams were then stationed outside liquor shops to conduct check-ups, collect blood samples, and provide medicines where required. “We are doing all of this so that people and their families become aware. The idea is to protect them from any major health risks,” Yadav said. The exercise kicked off on Sunday. Over two days, medical teams screened 147 people; blood samples were collected from 144 of them for liver and kidney function tests, according to some reports. On the first day, around 50 people were examined in Banda and Sagar, followed by 97 on Monday across Sagar, Deori, Rahli, Khurai and Bina. People showing signs of deteriorating health are being advised to undergo further medical examination and treatment, district health department officials said. Doctors are also recording the mobile numbers of those screened so that they can be contacted once their test reports arrive. Chief Medical and Health Officer (CMHO) Dr Devesh Pateria said the screening exercise had brought to light several cases of chronic alcoholism, including people showing signs of damage to liver function. He said the exercise would help the Health Department identify such patients earlier and intervene before their condition deteriorates further. He said medical teams were also providing medicines to address nutritional deficiencies commonly associated with prolonged alcohol consumption. “We are providing medicines that can help address Vitamin B1 deficiency, along with multivitamin supplements. The idea is to provide immediate medical support wherever required and identify those who need further treatment,” he said. Dr Pateria said the Health Department had known about several chronic alcoholics in the district because they would frequently end up in hospitals with health complications. However, the current exercise was helping officials build a consolidated database of such people. “The numbers have now gone up considerably compared with the figures that the Excise Department had earlier provided to us. We are collating this information, and this first-of-its-kind data will help us develop strategies for further intervention,” he said. The Collector said the campaign was not restricted to customers identified by liquor-shop operators. Health teams were also working through primary and community health centres and visiting villages to identify habitual drinkers who might not appear on the lists.

headline: Scaling India’s Blue Economy: FIFI Takes Indian Seafood to Global Buyers
content: PNNKochi (Kerala) [India], November 24: The Forum of Indian Food Importers (FIFI), in close collaboration with GEFA, Fischverband, the German Embassy in India, and MPEDA, has concluded a high-impact bilateral engagement programme aimed at strengthening India’s position in the global seafood value chain. Held across Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, and Kochi, Kerala, the programme brought together international buyers, German industry representatives, Indian exporters, processors, and sector stakeholders for more than 120 targeted business interactions, curated site visits, and commercial discussions now advancing toward contracts and partnerships. Attributing to the facts, India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly 8% of global fish output. Its seafood sector is also a major contributor to the country’s agri-food economy. Statistically, India exported 16,98,170 metric tonnes of seafood worth ₹62,408.45 crore (US$7.45 billion) in FY 2024–25. For India, seafood is more than a trade category. Behind every consignment are millions of livelihoods—coastal communities, fisherfolk, aquaculture farmers, processors, packers, exporters, and logistics teams—who take immense pride in delivering India’s finest to the world.FIFI’s programme was designed to convert India’s seafood strengths into actionable trade outcomes. More than US$2 million in trade discussions were initiated, while multiple contracts and commercial partnerships are under active negotiation and moving toward signature. Amit Lohani, Founder and Director of FIFI, was quoted as saying,“FIFI took it upon itself to change the perception of Indian shrimps amongst German buyers, who otherwise heavily rely on Ecuadorian and Thai-origin products. As India welcomes imported products, it must also work collectively to create meaningful opportunities for Indian food products, ingredients, and packaged goods in overseas markets.” He further said, “The programme was made possible through collaboration with FIFI’s associates—partners who share FIFI’s belief that global trade must create value on both sides. FIFI will continue to work with government bodies, industry associations, international delegations, and Indian exporters to promote balanced bilateral trade and position India as a trusted, competitive, and future-ready global food partner.” A key highlight of the engagement was a bilateral industry deliberation convened at the office of Shri P. Jawahar, IAS, Chairman, MPEDA, the statutory body under India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry that promotes and regulates seafood and marine-product exports. MPEDA welcomed Shri Amit Lohani, Founder Director, FIFI; Mr Volker Klima, Head of the Agriculture and Food Division, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in India; Mr Fabian Schäfer, Policy and Communication Officer, Federal Association of German Fish Wholesalers (Fischverband); Mr Rakesh Banga, Founder Director, FIFI; and representatives of fisheries associations and FIFI. The discussions focused on India’s strengths across the seafood value chain, opportunities for deeper industry collaboration, and the upcoming Seafood Expo Bharat, scheduled for 1–3 July 2027 in Chennai. The Expo is hosted by MPEDA and is designed to bring together the seafood value chain, international buyers, technology providers, and exporters.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by PNN. headline: Saurav Das’s passport flagged over birthplace discrepancy; gets notice
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das was stopped from travelling to London from Delhi late Monday night after immigration authorities flagged his passport over an alleged discrepancy in his place of birth, according to a notice issued by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai. The office initiated proceedings that could result in the impounding of Das’s passport and issued him a show-cause notice on November 23, asking him to respond within seven days. The notice also advises him not to use the passport for any travel until he submits his explanation. The Regional Passport Office, Chennai, issued Das's passport on August 21, 2019. Under Section 10(3) of the Passports Act, 1967, passport authorities may impound or revoke a passport if it was obtained on the basis of suppressed material information or incorrect information, among other specified grounds. 'Anti-intellectual government' He later shared a video on social media in which he said that a student organisation in the United Kingdom had invited him to speak at an event, but he was prevented from travelling. In the video, Das said that when he reached the immigration counter, officials informed him that his passport had been flagged and he would not be allowed to travel. In a series of posts on X, he lashed out at the "anti-intellectual" government for his detention and alleged that it was afraid of him speaking at these institutions. 🚨This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement. Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions! @Cockroachisback — Saurav Das (@SauravDassss) November 23, 2026 Das accused the government of preventing him from attending the event, alleging that his participation in discussions on the Cockroach movement at British academic institutions had been blocked. “This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement. Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!” However, the reported invitation was from the Oxford Union, a debating society independent of the University of Oxford, rather than the university itself. Das also shared a photo showing several copies of the Constitution. "The gifts I was carrying for my friends in the UK. But a coward who fears this book did not let me travel. Guess who?" he wrote. This is the second time Das has been stopped at an airport in less than two months. On October 10, he and fellow CJP leaders Abhineet Dipke and Ashutosh Ranka were detained after arriving in Delhi on a flight from Mumbai. The three had travelled to the national capital to participate in a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Tamil Nadu BJP chief detained on way to lamp ceremony near Muslim shrine
content: Police detained Nainar Nagenthran, the Tamil Nadu BJP president, at a checkpoint outside Tirunelveli on Tuesday as he headed to Thirupparankundram, where a ceremonial lamp was due to be lit at 6 pm on a stone pillar near a Muslim shrine under a one-time arrangement ordered by the Supreme Court. Nagenthran had left his home at 2.35 pm with a group of party functionaries. Police stopped them 40 minutes later at Thatchanallur and took them to a nearby marriage hall. L Murugan, a former Union minister travelling to Thirupparankundram from Mettupalayam, was stopped at Annur in Coimbatore district. இன்றைய தினம், திருக்கார்த்திகை தீபத் திருநாளை முன்னிட்டு, திருப்பரங்குன்றம் முருகப் பெருமானை தரிசிப்பதற்காகவும், மாண்புமிகு உச்சநீதிமன்றத்தின் தீர்ப்பின்படி திருப்பரங்குன்றம் மலையில் தீபம் ஏற்றப்படுவதைக் கண்ணாரக் காண்பதற்காகவும் திருநெல்வேலியில் இருந்து புறப்பட்டுச் சென்றோம். ஆனால், இந்த ஜனநாயக நாட்டில், நீதிமன்றத் தீர்ப்பை மதித்து, அதன்படி நடைபெறும் நிகழ்வைக் காணச் சென்ற எங்களை, இந்து மக்கள் விரோத தமிழக வெற்றிக் கழக அரசின் காவல்துறையினர் கைது செய்துள்ளனர். நீதிமன்றத் தீர்ப்பை மதிப்பதும், மக்களின் வழிபாட்டு உரிமையைப் பாதுகாப்பதும் ஓர் அரசின் கடமை. ஜனநாயக நாட்டில் மக்களின் உரிமைகளுக்காகக் குரல் கொடுப்பவர்களைக் கைது செய்வது எந்த வகையில் நியாயம்? (1/3) — Nainar Nagenthran (@NainarBJP) November 24, 2026 The dispute is about where on the Madurai hill the Karthigai Deepam flame should burn. The Subramaniya Swamy Temple, dedicated to Murugan, stands at the foot of the hill. Thirty years ago, four temple priests told authorities that the festival lamp had long been lit at the Uchipillaiyar temple. Hindu groups have sought a second flame at the deepathoon, a stone pillar about 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. On Friday, Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi directed that a small team authorised by the temple administration be allowed to light the lamp at the pillar on Tuesday. The bench left open the question of whether worshippers had a customary right to light it there in future years. Tamil Nadu’s Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department has sought a review of the order. On Tuesday, police restricted access to the hill to people cleared by the administration, closing the ascent even to devotees headed for the Kasi Viswanathar temple or the dargah. About 6,000 police personnel were deployed across Madurai and around Thirupparankundram. At the hill, where the district collector and city police commissioner inspected the arrangements, police also banned drone flights. The age-old legal row near the dargah of Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha atop the hill ignited a political debate after a single-judge bench of the High Court allowed a writ petition on December 1, 2025, and held that the “deepathoon” stood on temple land and asked the temple management to light the lamp there.
