headline: Two poll setbacks later, why Chandigarh matters more than ever to BJP
content: The upcoming Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections are shaping up to be much more than a battle for control of the civic body for the BJP. Coming after a series of electoral and political setbacks since 2021, the elections will test whether the party has managed to rebuild its credibility, overcome internal differences and regain the confidence of voters in Chandigarh. From being stunned in the 2021 civic polls, where its seats in civic polls were reduced to 12 while the AAP emerged with 14 seats, to the party losing the Lok Sabha seat of Chandigarh in 2024, the BJP has to try hard this time to reflect that the results were not signs of a deeper shift in the city’s political landscape. The stakes for the party are particularly high this time as the civic polls come not just ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, but the party has suffered political setbacks since 2021. Chandigarh’s political outcomes are being closely watched in the neighbouring state, and the result could be an important indication of the changing political mood in the region. Here’s a look at why these polls are high-stakes ones: A setback in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections The BJP’s defeat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was a major blow to the party in Chandigarh. A BJP councillor told The Indian Express, “After winning the parliamentary seat in 2014 and 2019, the party lost it to Congress candidate Manish Tewari, who defeated BJP’s Sanjay Tandon by a narrow margin of 2,504 votes. The result ended the BJP’s decade-long hold over the constituency and exposed its vulnerability even in a city where it has traditionally enjoyed considerable organisational strength- something which was quite a big dent." The decision to replace sitting MP Kirron Kher with Sanjay Tandon so as to check anti-incumbency had failed to deliver the desired result. The councillor also said, “The MC elections will now test whether the party has addressed the reasons behind that defeat… A poor performance would reinforce the perception that the 2024 result was not an isolated setback but part of a larger erosion of its support base. If this time again, the BJP does not perform well here, it will be a third consecutive loss.” BJP leader Sanjay Tandon said, “Every election is important for us, whether it is a parliamentary, Assembly or Municipal election. We approach every election with the same seriousness and commitment. Chandigarh is important for us, and our focus is on strengthening the organisation, reaching out to people and winning their trust.” Political signal ahead of Punjab Assembly polls The timing of the Chandigarh civic polls makes them particularly significant. In the 2021 MC elections, the AAP made a spectacular debut, emerging as the single largest party with 14 seats, while the BJP was reduced to 12 and the Congress won eight. Just months later, the AAP swept the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections and formed the government. Although Chandigarh’s electorate is not a direct reflection of Punjab’s, with Punjab scheduled to go to the polls in 2027, the Chandigarh MC results will be closely scrutinised. A strong performance would allow the BJP to project itself as an emerging political force in the region, while another setback could strengthen the Opposition’s argument that the party is losing ground even in urban areas where it traditionally enjoyed influence. Anil Masih controversy The January 2024 mayoral election controversy remains one of the biggest political liabilities for the BJP in Chandigarh. The presiding officer, Anil Masih, was caught on camera marking ballot papers during the counting process. BJP’s Manoj Sonkar was initially declared elected mayor with 16 votes against 12 secured by the AAP-Congress alliance candidate Kuldeep Kumar, with eight votes declared invalid. The matter reached the Supreme Court, which examined the video footage and ballot papers and found that all eight votes declared invalid had actually been cast in favour of Kuldeep Kumar. The court set aside the result and declared AAP’s Kuldeep Kumar the validly elected mayor. The episode became a national political flashpoint, with the opposition accusing the BJP of attempting to manipulate the electoral process to retain control of the mayor's office. The BJP is likely to face repeated reminders of the episode during the campaign, making it difficult to keep the focus exclusively on development and civic governance. The 2021 electoral mandate The 2021 MC election result remains another challenge for the BJP. The party, which won with a comfortable majority in the 2016 corporation polls, was reduced to just 12 of the 35 seats, while the AAP emerged as the largest party with 14. Although the BJP subsequently managed to retain control of the mayor’s office through political realignments and defections, the original electoral verdict cannot be erased. The president of the Chandigarh Congress committee, HS Lucky, said, “There is a difference between securing control of a corporation through shifting numbers in the House and winning the confidence of voters through an electoral mandate. The BJP’s subsequent political manoeuvring cannot substitute for the question it must answer: why did voters reject so many of its candidates in 2021 and make it lose the Lok Sabha polls also in 2024.” A battle to reclaim its urban stronghold Chandigarh has traditionally been an important urban base for the BJP. However, the 2021 MC elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha defeat have demonstrated that its support base cannot be taken for granted. A former BJP councillor told The Indian Express, “The party’s challenge will now remain to convince residents that it remains the most credible option for running the city, while countering the opposition’s narrative on governance, the mayoral election controversy and political defections. Ultimately, the MC elections will test whether we can turn the tide after successive setbacks.” He said, “Retaining political control of the corporation through shifting numbers is one thing; winning back the electorate is quite another. And moreover, with Punjab heading into an Assembly election year in 2027, the Chandigarh verdict will carry significance beyond the city’s 35 wards. For us, winning the civic elections would mean an opportunity to reclaim our political narrative.”

headline: India’s informal economy grows at record pace in Jul-Sep, but paid job creation lags
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) India’s unincorporated non-farm economy expanded at its fastest quarterly pace on record in July-September, but the surge was driven largely by owner-operated businesses rather than paid employment, pointing to an expansion in self-employment even as the creation of hired jobs remained relatively weak. The number of establishments rose 18.81 per cent from a year earlier to 9.47 crore, while employment increased 16.86 per cent to 15.03 crore, the National Statistics Office (NSO) said in its latest Quarterly Bulletin of the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. Both growth rates were the highest in the quarterly series. The composition of employment, however, presents a more mixed picture. The number of hired workers increased by only about 5 per cent to 3.49 crore, while working owners accounted for nearly 62 per cent of the workforce, up from 59.98 per cent a year earlier. The figures suggest that the expansion of India’s vast small-business economy is translating more rapidly into self-employment and owner-operated enterprises than into conventional wage-paying jobs. Growth was broad-based across rural and urban areas, although urban establishments expanded faster. The number of urban enterprises increased 22.05 per cent year-on-year, compared with 16.05 per cent in rural areas. Employment growth, however, was marginally stronger in rural areas at 17.52 per cent, against 16.30 per cent in urban centres. Services recorded the strongest expansion among the three broad sectors covered by the survey. Establishments in the ‘other services’ category grew 29 per cent, while employment increased by more than 33 per cent.

headline: Why an Ayushmann Khurrana movie has sparked a language row in Bengal
content: A Kolkata-based cinema chain’s decision to pull Bengali movie Sadhak Bamakhyapa from movie halls to screen more shows for Sooraj Barjatya’s Yeh Prem Mol Liya has sparked a row, underlining regional cinema’s unequal fight against big-budget Bollywood releases. Sadhak Bamakhyapa, which released on November 20, is based on the life of 19th-century Tantric saint Bamakhyapa. Directed by Sayantan Ghosal and starring Sabyasachi Chowdhury, Payel De and Saheb Chatterjee, the movie postponed its release from November 6 to 20 to avoid a clash with Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana. Now, with Yeh Prem Mol Liya, starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari Wagh, set to release this Friday, SVF Cinemas, which operates 67 cinema screens in Bengal, has announced its decision to discontinue shows of Sadhak Bamakhyapa. “The decision to discontinue the theatrical run of Sadhak Bamakhyapa from this Friday is an extremely disheartening one for us, especially when the film has been receiving such overwhelming love and appreciation from audiences. Since its release on November 20, the film has witnessed an encouraging response, with audiences turning up in significant numbers and several shows recording houseful occupancy, even on weekdays. The appreciation, word-of-mouth and audience connect that the film has garnered have been truly heartening,” a statement from SVF Cinemas said. “However, with the upcoming release of Yeh Prem Mol Liya, produced by Rajshri Productions and distributed by YRF, we have been informed by exhibitors about the challenges of accommodating adequate shows for Sadhak Bamakhyapa from this Friday. We have absolutely no objection to another film releasing or finding its audience. Every film deserves its rightful opportunity. However, we strongly believe that this should not come at the cost of another film that is already performing well and receiving genuine audience appreciation. There should be a fair and equitable allocation of screens and shows, allowing both films to coexist and audiences to exercise their choice,” the statement added. “It is unfortunate that despite the audience response, including houseful shows on weekdays, Sadhak Bamakhyapa may have to discontinue its theatrical journey from this Friday due to the lack of adequate show allocations. We sincerely hope that the exhibitors will reconsider the situation and that a fair solution can be reached. A film that is finding its audience deserves the opportunity to continue its journey,” it said. How actors reacted Actor Sabyasachi Chowdhury, who has played the titular role in Sadhak Bamakhyapa, said he was “shocked”. “If people did not like the film, we would have no problem if it was removed. But people have appreciated the film. We appeal for equal treatment for Bengali and Hindi films,” he told media persons. “Could they have dared to do this in South India? But they are doing it here. We lodge our strong protest. People are appreciating the film; the shows are houseful. Then why remove it. Let the people decide. This will hit the Bengali film industry badly,” said actor Saheb Chatterjee. State Cabinet Minister Dilip Ghosh, however, said there is no Bengali versus Hindi conflict here. “Cinema is amusement. The people will decide. People have seen Sadhak Bamakhyapa. If businessmen think another film will work, they will show it. If the government thinks it will give subsidies, it will.” Chief Minister calls meeting At the meeting, Chief Minister Adhikari made it clear that every cinema hall in the state must screen at least one Bengali film during prime time. He sent a clear message that while there is no restriction on screening films in other languages, prime-time shows for Bengali films must be guaranteed. “If someone fails to do this, legal action will be taken. The Chief Minister said the state government will set up 51 new cinema halls. The infrastructure of auditoriums and halls will be developed so that cinemas can be screened there,” Rudranil Ghosh, actor and BJP MLA from Shibpur, told the media after the meeting. According to sources, speaking on the ongoing controversy, the Chief Minister told cinema hall owners he does not want to know what happened under the previous government, but the current administration won’t tolerate such an approach. In fact, the previous Mamata Banerjee government had issued a directive in 2025, asking cinema hall owners and multiplexes in the state to screen at least one Bangla film every day in prime time slots. Sources from a section of the film fraternity said that this policy was not properly enforced.

headline: Bend it like Heema: Meet the Jhabua teen who won David Beckham’s praise
content: When her family began discussing her marriage while she was still in school, 17-year-old Heema Ninama decided she would not let it interrupt her education. Undeterred by mounting pressure from her family, Heema sought help from her teachers at the government Sandipani Vidyalaya in Kalyanpura, Madhya Pradesh's Jhabua district. Her principal, Gyanendra Prasad Ojha, intervened and eventually persuaded her family to let her continue studying. Today, the Class 12 student from Barkheda village is continuing her studies, competing in athletics, and working to become a teacher. Her determination to resist child marriage has now brought her international recognition, with former England football captain David Beckham sharing her story on social media on November 20, marking World Children's Day. “To mark this World Children's Day, I am sharing the story of 17-year-old Hima, from Madhya Pradesh, India, who bravely stopped her own child marriage, with the help of her school teachers. She now dreams of following in their footsteps to help other girls shape their own futures. Stories like this wouldn't be possible without the work of UNICEF and its partners on the ground,” Beckham wrote. Speaking to The Indian Express, Heema said, “My family was talking about getting me married, but I did not want to. I wanted to study further, so I went and spoke to my principal.” “My principal spoke to my family members and explained to them that child marriage is prohibited. After that, my family agreed and is allowing me to continue my studies,” she said. Principal Gyanendra Prasad Ojha told The Indian Express that Heema approached him shortly before her Class 10 examinations, saying that her father had fixed her marriage. He called her father to the school and counselled him against going ahead with it. “He understood what I told him and agreed,” Ojha said. By the time the matter came to the principal's attention, some of the traditional rituals associated with the proposed marriage had already begun. Heema, however, refused to go along with the arrangements. Heema said she was not aware of other girls in her village currently facing a similar situation, although Ojha said child marriage remained a concern in the wider area. For Heema, the opportunity to continue studying has also strengthened an ambition she had held for years. “I want to become a teacher. Children belonging to the Adivasi community usually struggle with education, so I want to help in this field,” she said. Heema is enrolled in the Arts stream in Class 12 and says she wants to return to her community and help children who struggle to access quality education. Before joining Sandipani School, she studied from Class I to V at a government school with only two teachers. The shortage, she said, affected the education children received and their academic performance. “Because there were so few teachers, the students' results were affected. Since then, I decided that I would study hard and become a teacher who could provide good education to tribal children,” she said in an earlier account of her journey. Heema, who belongs to the Bhil tribal community, comes from a family with limited means. Her parents are both illiterate and work as daily-wage labourers. The family owns only a small amount of agricultural land. Ojha said that despite these circumstances, she had consistently performed well in her studies and secured a first division in Class 11. Her ambitions extend beyond the classroom. Heema participates in running and shot put and has won awards at the district level. She also takes part in essay-writing, drawing and speech competitions. Her participation in sports is particularly significant because a physical disability affecting her ability to walk had initially made her reluctant to take part in athletics. “I was interested in sports, but because I cannot walk properly, I used to stay away from participating. My teacher encouraged me and told me that I could participate too,” she said. Ojha said, “She has won district-level awards in shot put and sprint events. She also participates in essay competitions, drawing competitions and speech competitions.” The international attention has encouraged Heema, who is happy her story reached people worldwide. “When the UNICEF people came to know about my situation, they helped me a lot. I am very happy that David Beckham shared a post about me on Instagram and Facebook,” she said. Asked whether she knew who Beckham was before he shared her story, Heema said she had only recently learnt about him.

headline: India's health bill: Who really pays?
content: In October 2026, a 27-year-old woman from Mathura who had lost the ability to walk underwent two complex spinal operations in Lucknow. At a private hospital, doctors estimated, the treatment could have cost Rs 6–7 lakh. Under Ayushman Bharat, she received it free, TOI reported.That same month, in Odisha's Bargarh district, a daily-wage worker was borrowing money to buy medicines for his family. His son's chemotherapy was covered under Ayushman Bharat, but as TOI reported, the family's monthly medicine requirements alone amounted to Rs 20,000.Both stories point to the same reality, albeit with different outcomes. The government is now picking up a larger share of the country's health bill, yet on the ground, massive medical costs can still push individual households into financial distress.Imagine India's entire healthcare bill as Rs 100. In 2013–14, families paid Rs 64.20 directly from their pockets, the government spent Rs 28.60, and other sources financed the remaining Rs 7.20.By 2023–24, the government's share had risen to Rs 43.50, while direct household payments accounted for Rs 42.70. Other financing arrangements, including private insurance, accounted for the remaining Rs 13.80. In absolute terms, government health expenditure rose from Rs 1.30 lakh crore in 2013–14 to Rs 4.14 lakh crore in 2023–24. Direct household payments increased much more slowly, from Rs 2.91 lakh crore to Rs 4.06 lakh crore. Government spending thus exceeded direct household payments by around Rs 8,000 crore.Government expenditure first overtook direct household payments in the National Health Accounts series in 2021–22, when pandemic-related spending pushed its share to 48%. A closer look at the latest National Health Accounts reveals what lies behind these numbers.The hospital-building spendOf the Rs 4.14 lakh crore spent by the government in 2023–24, approximately Rs 1.13 lakh crore was capital expenditure on healthcare infrastructure, equipment and other long-term investments. Excluding that, government spending on current healthcare, which is the money used to provide services and goods during the year, stood at about Rs 3.01 lakh crore. Households, meanwhile, paid Rs 4.06 lakh crore directly.For every Rs 100 spent on current healthcare services and goods, the government accounted for Rs 36, while households paid Rs 48.50 directly. Other sources financed the remaining Rs 15.50.However, government spending on current healthcare also more than tripled, from about Rs 98,000 crore in 2013–14 to Rs 3.01 lakh crore in 2023–24. The government's share of current healthcare expenditure rose from 23.2% to 36%.Nearly half the decade-long decline in the household share of total healthcare spending occurred in a single year, when it fell from 58.7% to 48.8% in 2017–18. This coincided with a change in the survey used to estimate household health expenditure and preceded the September 2018 launch of PM-JAY. How much of the decline was attributable to the change in estimation remains unclear.What changed over the decade?Government health expenditure increased by approximately 219% over the decade, without adjusting for inflation. Direct household payments grew by about 40%. For every Rs 100 the government spent on health in 2013–14, it was spending about Rs 319 a decade later. For households, Rs 100 became about Rs 140.Ayushman Bharat, launched in 2018, has been a prominent initiative in this expansion. Its hospital insurance component, the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), provides eligible families with annual health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh for specified hospital treatments. In October 2024, eligibility was extended to all senior citizens aged 70 and above, irrespective of their economic status. But India's increased public spending goes well beyond hospital insurance.Government-financed health insurance schemes, including PM-JAY and state-specific schemes, accounted for Rs 33,385 crore in 2023–24, or about 8% of government health expenditure. A much larger part of public spending supports the healthcare system itself. Government spending on primary healthcare, the first point of contact for many patients, increased from about Rs 50,000 crore in 2013–14 to Rs 1.53 lakh crore in 2023–24. It accounted for roughly half of the government's current health expenditure in 2023–24.Through the National Health Mission and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the government has sought to expand basic consultations, maternal and childcare services, access to essential medicines and diagnostic tests. State and local governments accounted for nearly 68% of government health expenditure in 2023–24, underscoring their role in this expansion.One country, very different health billsIn 2023–24, government expenditure exceeded direct household payments in 13 of the 21 states and UTs for which the National Health Accounts provided comparable estimates. In the other eight, families still paid more directly. In Uttarakhand, the government accounted for 66% of total healthcare expenditure, whereas households paid 26.7% directly. The government's share stood at 57.9% in Odisha and 59.5% in Assam.Kerala shows the opposite pattern. For every Rs 100 spent on healthcare in the state, households contributed Rs 65.20 directly, against Rs 25 from the government. In West Bengal, the figures were Rs 63 and Rs 30. State-level government expenditure figures include spending by the Union government and local bodies, not merely the state government's own health budget. The estimates for household spending are based on survey data from 2017–18, updated for subsequent years.What happens when you walk into a hospital?The 2025 National Sample Survey indicated that health insurance or healthcare financing coverage has risen from fewer than one in five Indians in 2017–18 to nearly half, largely through government-sponsored schemes.At least half of outpatient treatment episodes at public facilities involved no direct medical expenditure. Average out-of-pocket medical expenditure per hospitalisation, excluding childbirth, was Rs 6,631 at public facilities against Rs 50,508 at private hospitals. While the types of treatment may differ, private hospitals, including those empanelled under government schemes, accounted for 60.3% of hospitalisations excluding childbirth.Medicines remain a major financial burden, with households spending Rs 1.71 lakh crore on separately purchased medicines in 2023–24, accounting for roughly 42% of their direct healthcare expenditure. While PM-JAY primarily covers hospitalisation, initiatives such as government free-drug programmes and Jan Aushadhi seek to reduce everyday medical costs. The number of Jan Aushadhi outlets rose from around 80 in 2014 to around 11,000 by March 2024.Who ultimately pays?Families also finance healthcare through insurance premiums. Expenditure through private health insurance, which includes employer-based group cover and individual policies, rose from 3.4% of total health expenditure in 2013–14 to 10.2% in 2023–24. When we look at where healthcare funds originate, including household insurance contributions, the picture changes. Households supplied Rs 55.70 of every Rs 100 spent on current healthcare in 2023–24, down from Rs 72.90 in 2013–14. The contribution from government budgets and grants rose from Rs 21.10 to Rs 34 over the same period.There is also a cost that the National Health Accounts cannot capture: the treatment someone needed but could not afford. A patient treated free at a government hospital and someone who forgoes treatment because it is unaffordable can both record zero direct medical expenditure. Their experiences could hardly be more different. The real measure of India's healthcare progress is whether an Indian can afford to fall ill without becoming poor.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Delhi govt plans app to help EWS patients check bed availability
content: New Delhi, The Delhi government is planning a mobile app to help EWS patients check vacant beds, including ICU beds, at identified private hospitals, as over 3,000 EWS patients were treated free of cost daily between April 2025 and October 2026.The proposed Android and iOS application is expected to allow people to check the availability of vacant and occupied beds, as well as ICU beds, before visiting a hospital, saving them time and travel expenses.According to an official, an online portal displaying live bed availability at identified private hospitals is already operational. It provides details of the hospitals, the total number of EWS beds, vacant beds, and the names and contact details of government liaison officers posted there.Hospitals and liaison officers update the portal three times a day, at 9 am, 2 pm and 6 pm.An analysis of official data showed that 18,73,238 EWS patients received free treatment between April 2025 and October 2026. Of these, 17,78,938 were outpatients and 94,300 were inpatients. This translates into an average of around 3,235 patients treated free of cost every day during the period.In 2024-25, a total of 7,65,422 patients received free treatment under the EWS category, including 7,23,522 outpatients and 41,900 inpatients.Under the EWS scheme, eligible patients can avail free treatment at identified private hospitals that were allotted land at concessional rates.The annual income eligibility limit for the scheme was increased from ₹2.2 lakh to ₹5 lakh following a Delhi High Court order in January this year.The court directed that the revised income criteria be applicable to all government hospitals in Delhi and identified private hospitals built on land allotted at concessional rates.Hospitals were also directed to publicise the revised eligibility criteria so that more people could avail the benefit.The government published a newspaper advertisement on April 12 to inform the public about the scheme and the revised income limit, the official added.The number of identified private hospitals providing treatment under the scheme has increased to 58, with Amerix Hospital and Sant Nirankari Health City among the two latest additions. The number of government liaison officers has also been increased from 22 to 39. They are currently posted in 56 identified hospitals.In another healthcare initiative, around 85,000 newborns have been screened and nearly 1,000 babies have received treatment under the Delhi government's ANMOL scheme as of November 10, officials shared.ANMOL, or Advanced Newborn Monitoring and Optimal Life Care, aims to screen newborns for congenital, genetic and metabolic disorders to enable early detection and treatment.The annual screening target under the programme has been increased from 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh newborns, while the number of conditions covered has been expanded from 56 to 63.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Labour survey: Some segments might not be captured—that could have policy implications
content: India’s labour-market debate is increasingly being shaped by the level of confidence in official numbers. The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025 reports that self-employment accounts for 56.2% of the workforce, regular wage and salaried employment 23.6%, and casual labour 20.2%. But a question precedes their interpretation—how much of India’s labour market does its statistical system capture?

headline: Inventure Academy Named Among World’s Top 3 Schools for Community Collaboration at World’s Best School Prizes 2026
content: Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], November 24: Inventure Academy has been named among the world’s Top 3 schools for Community Collaboration at T4 Education’s World’s Best School Prizes 2026. The Community Collaboration prize recognises schools that build meaningful partnerships with their wider communities to support children’s learning and development, with equity and inclusion at the centre. In 2026, T4 Education shortlisted 50 schools from thousands of applications worldwide. Ten schools were shortlisted in each of five categories following expert review, due diligence and interviews. An international Judging Academy selects one winner in each category against published criteria. The Community Choice Award is decided by a separate public vote across all 50 shortlisted schools. Community collaboration: Learning and creating change together Since its founding in 2005, Inventure Academy has been guided by its Core Purpose. Empower learners to realise their full potential, ignite change, and create positive impact. At Inventure, this purpose comes to life through the work school leaders and educators undertake with students, families and community partners. Students have a voice in issues that affect their lives and are trusted to act on it, learning alongside educators whose own involvement demonstrates what it means to contribute. Together with researchers, civic authorities and community organisations, they investigate shared challenges, listen to the people affected and develop and test ideas in pursuit of a purpose beyond themselves. Through Our Mobility, Our Voice, students studied their daily commutes, gathered data on travel times and traffic congestion, and presented their findings and recommendations to Bengaluru’s civic authorities. Through Our Safety, Our Voice, students helped develop a charter on school safety that informed Karnataka’s Child Protection Policy. In 2019, Our Future, Our Voice brought together students and teachers from across Karnataka to share their recommendations with the government during consultations on the draft National Education Policy. Students have also engaged with civic stakeholders on lake rejuvenation through Our Lakes, Our Voice.

headline: After spurious liquor claimed 20 lives, MP launches health check-up drives at liquor shops to urge drinkers to quit
content: Sagar, MP: Months after spurious liquor claimed over 20 lives in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar district, authorities are taking healthcare straight to the liquor shop door with on-the-spot health check-up camps to urge habitual drinkers to quit, officials said on Tuesday. .The move follows investigations into the September incident in Banda, which revealed that while the victims had consumed alcohol, they were already suffering from serious liver and kidney ailments, they said. .Keeping this in mind, District Magistrate Dilip Kumar Yadav launched the drive through a joint team of the Health and Excise departments to screen regular drinkers and advise them to abstain from alcohol, an official said. .GIFT city in 'dry Gujarat' records surge in liquor sales, earns over Rs 87 lakh in 2 years.On Monday, the joint team conducted health check-ups of 97 individuals across Sagar city, Deori, Rahli, Bina and Khurai, providing medical counselling and advice, he said, adding that the campaign would continue across the district. .Chief Medical and Health Officer (CMHO) Devesh Pateriya said the drive was aimed at raising awareness among drinkers about the direct impact of alcohol on their health. ."In recent times, there have been several cases of alcohol-related deaths. In light of this, the District Magistrate issued an order, and in compliance, we are visiting liquor shops and testing people's blood," he said. .Pateriya said individuals were being specifically screened for liver and kidney function, informed of their health status and advised to undergo periodic check-ups and quit alcohol. .Even those who reported no immediate symptoms were cautioned that health complications could surface later, he added. .Excise Inspector Shailendra Singh said probes into several recent alcohol-linked deaths in the district showed that pre-existing liver and kidney illnesses were the primary cause of death. ."On the instructions of senior officials and with the support of the Health Department, we are visiting liquor shops to identify regular drinkers, check their health and raise awareness," Singh said. .Work from home with AI? MP spurious liquor case accused used technology to make alcohol.In September, more than 20 people had died after consuming spurious liquor in Banda, following which police arrested around 20 accused. .Meanwhile, local social worker Kapil Swami said it would have been more effective if the administration had organised health camps in slum areas instead, noting that many buyers purchase liquor from shops to consume at home. .Speaking to PTI, Swami alleged that the drive was an attempt by officials to cover up their lapses.

headline: Keralam escalates ethanol war with Centre, asks for pure petrol samples
content: The Congress government in Keralam has stepped up its confrontation with the NDA government at the Centre over ethanol in petrol. The state’s Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Anoop Jacob, has written to Union Minister for Petroleum Hardeep Singh Puri seeking a directive to oil marketing firms to supply 100 per cent pure petrol samples so ethanol levels in the fuel distributed in the state can be checked. Early this month, the state civil supplies department collected petrol samples from outlets of various public sector firms to ascertain whether petrol is being sold in the state with ethanol blended in excess. The samples had been despatched to regional chemical laboratories. Keralam had joined the issue after the Congress-led Karnataka government alleged that petrol containing ethanol in excess of the prescribed limit was being sold in the state. While the results of the samples tested are yet to come out, the Keralam minister, in his letter to Puri, said the civil supplies department had collected samples as per protocol and entrusted them to the government's Chemical Examiner’s Lab. “It was informed that cross-matching of the samples collected would require 100 per cent pure petrol samples, which are only available with oil firms such as IOC and BPCL. Though oil companies had initially agreed to supply pure samples, they later desisted from handing over the model samples to the civil supplies department. Persistent efforts made by senior government officials to procure pure samples from oil firms were turned down,” he said. The minister said checking samples supplied in the state is not intended to tarnish the credibility of oil companies, but focuses on addressing apprehensions raised by the general public about the impact of blending ethanol in petrol distributed in the state. Earlier, the minister had stated that if the fuel supplied in the state is found adulterated, strict action will be taken. As per a state notification issued in 2014, in accordance with the Central Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, officials ranging from the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs to Taluk Supply Officers are empowered to conduct inspections and initiate legal action, he had stated, while ordering examination of the petrol samples in the state. The Karnataka government had claimed that it had conducted laboratory tests and found petrol samples containing substantially more than the prescribed 20 per cent ethanol. However, the Union government and the public sector OMCs rejected the finding and questioned sample collection and testing procedure adopted by the Karnataka Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology department. Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad had stated that independent studies of fuel samples at a private laboratory had revealed “31.2% ethanol blending in IOCL and 30.5% in HPCL, exceeding 20%.” Last week, Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi had dismissed concerns over E20 fuel. Questioning the testing of samples being conducted by the state governments, Gopi told the media in Thrissur that those who make such claims are idiots who do not know science. He said India moved to E20 after extensive research and approval from the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI). “Several political claims were being made about ethanol blending, particularly allegations that the permitted limit had been exceeded. I will not call such persons any bad names. All I would say is that none of these idiots has any knowledge about science," he said.

headline: India’s First Quantum-AI University Inaugurated In Andhra Pradesh; Classes To Begin In December
content: India’s first dedicated university campus focused on Quantum Computing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been inaugurated in Andhra Pradesh. The temporary campus has been set up at Acharya Nagarjuna University (ANU) in Guntur, with classes and training programmes scheduled to begin in December 2026. The campus has been established by the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), a deemed-to-be university under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). It will operate from the ANU premises until the permanent campus in Amaravati is ready. The initiative is aimed at developing skilled professionals in emerging technology fields, including Quantum Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and semiconductor technologies. Four specialised laboratories are being planned at the temporary campus, covering Quantum Computing, Quantum Communication, Chip Design and Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI), and AI and Computing. The facilities are expected to provide students with practical exposure to these emerging fields. The permanent campus is planned at Nidamarru in Amaravati. The project is expected to strengthen the state’s efforts to develop a hub for quantum technology and artificial intelligence. The campus aims to train around 8,250 people over five years. This includes students enrolled in degree programmes as well as participants in skill development and certification courses. According to the official press released, the proposed campus will focus on cutting-edge domains including: – Quantum Computing and Quantum Algorithms – Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning – Quantum Communication and Cybersecurity – Quantum Hardware and Systems Engineering – High-Performance Computing – AI–Quantum Convergence Research “While anchored within NIELIT’s Deemed-to-be University ecosystem, the Amaravati campus will represent India’s first institutionally dedicated academic hub focused solely on Quantum and Artificial Intelligence,” the released, issued in February, had stated. The initiative is expected to provide opportunities for students to gain specialised knowledge and practical skills in advanced technologies, preparing them for emerging roles in the technology sector.

headline: In MP, health check-ups come to liquor shops to persuade drinkers to quit
content: Sagar , Months after spurious liquor claimed over 20 lives in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar district, authorities are taking healthcare straight to the liquor shop door with on-the-spot health check-up camps to urge habitual drinkers to quit, officials said on Tuesday.The move follows investigations into the September incident in Banda, which revealed that while the victims had consumed alcohol, they were already suffering from serious liver and kidney ailments, they said.Keeping this in mind, District Magistrate Dilip Kumar Yadav launched the drive through a joint team of the Health and Excise departments to screen regular drinkers and advise them to abstain from alcohol, an official said.On Monday, the joint team conducted health check-ups of 97 individuals across Sagar city, Deori, Rahli, Bina and Khurai, providing medical counselling and advice, he said, adding that the campaign would continue across the district.Chief Medical and Health Officer Devesh Pateriya said the drive was aimed at raising awareness among drinkers about the direct impact of alcohol on their health."In recent times, there have been several cases of alcohol-related deaths. In light of this, the District Magistrate issued an order, and in compliance, we are visiting liquor shops and testing people's blood," he said.Pateriya said individuals were being specifically screened for liver and kidney function, informed of their health status and advised to undergo periodic check-ups and quit alcohol.Even those who reported no immediate symptoms were cautioned that health complications could surface later, he added.Excise Inspector Shailendra Singh said probes into several recent alcohol-linked deaths in the district showed that pre-existing liver and kidney illnesses were the primary cause of death."On the instructions of senior officials and with the support of the Health Department, we are visiting liquor shops to identify regular drinkers, check their health and raise awareness," Singh said.In September, more than 20 people had died after consuming spurious liquor in Banda, following which police arrested around 20 accused.Meanwhile, local social worker Kapil Swami said it would have been more effective if the administration had organised health camps in slum areas instead, noting that many buyers purchase liquor from shops to consume at home.Speaking to PTI, Swami alleged that the drive was an attempt by officials to cover up their lapses.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Rs 80 lakh as legal fees in Gokul case? Congress questions Fadnavis government
content: Maharashtra’s largest dairy cooperative is once again at the centre of a political storm, with the Congress questioning the state government’s decision to approve Rs 80 lakh in legal fees for senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi in the ordinance dispute involving the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union (Gokul). Congress MLC Satej Patil on Tuesday questioned the government’s expenditure priorities amid drought and other financial challenges and alleged that public money was being spent to defend an ordinance brought to secure control over the cooperative. “The government hastily introduced an ordinance to bypass the farmers’ mandate and secure power at Gokul. Now, to sustain that ordinance in court, it is spending Rs 80 lakh on advocates. This expenditure is an attempt to wash away the sins committed at Gokul,” Patil alleged. The Gokul controversy The row stems from the Gokul board election held on October 19. A panel led by Patil won 13 of the 25 director seats, with the Mahayuti-backed panel winning the remaining 12. However, the 12 from the Mahayuti stayed away from a board meeting on the chairman’s election, denying Patil’s panel the 14 members allegedly required for a quorum under Gokul’s existing bylaws. Even as the Opposition moved the Bombay High Court over the stalemate, the state government on November 6, 2026, issued an ordinance amending a section of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, which is linked to the appointment of four government-nominated directors to Gokul’s board. The ordinance was challenged before the Bombay High Court’s Kolhapur circuit bench through a writ petition filed by Shashikant Anandrao Patil Chuyekar and others. According to a government order shared by Patil on X, the state government appointed Rohatgi, a former Attorney General for India, through a government letter dated November 9 to represent its position. Rohatgi appeared before the High Court on the same day. He subsequently submitted an invoice of Rs 80 lakh for his professional services. The finance department approved the disbursement. The government order stated that a 10 per cent tax deduction under the Income Tax Act would be applicable, bringing the net payment to Rs 72 lakh. ‘Reflects government’s priorities’ Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, Patil questioned the decision to engage a senior advocate at such a cost to defend the ordinance. He also questioned why the government was willing to spend such a substantial amount on the Gokul case while, according to him, several other important legal and public issues remained unresolved. “Have we seen these advocates being engaged to fight the Maharashtra-Karnataka border dispute, sustain Maratha reservation, present teachers’ issues in the TET [Teacher Eligibility Test] case before the Supreme Court or argue the triple-test requirement in the OBC reservation matter? This reflects the government’s priorities and its interest in Gokul,” he said. Drawing attention to the state’s drought situation, Patil said the government should have provided greater financial assistance to affected farmers instead of spending such a large amount on legal representation. He also referred to the pending Ladki Bahin scheme payments for 94 lakh women, rising unemployment and delays in recruitment through the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC). “If the government had been sensitive towards drought-hit farmers, it would not have limited the assistance to Rs 5,000. It should have provided Rs 25,000 or Rs 50,000 during Diwali. At a time when farmers are struggling, development funds are under pressure, and several other issues remain unresolved, is it justifiable to spend Rs 80 lakh to defend the appointment of four government-nominated directors to Gokul?” Patil asked. He further questioned why the government had not relied on its existing legal machinery if it was confident about the strength of the ordinance. “If the ordinance was so strong, why did the government not engage the assistant government pleader or advocates from the Law and Judiciary Department?” he said. BJP questions Patil’s legal expenses However, the BJP hit back at Patil, with party spokesperson Navnath Ban accusing the Congress leader of having incurred substantial legal expenses in the Gokul dispute. Ban alleged that Patil had spent Rs 80 lakh on advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi to represent his side in the case and another Rs 1 crore on a special chartered flight for Singhvi from Delhi to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. “Patil should clarify where the Rs 1.80 crore spent on a single hearing came from. Was it paid from Gokul’s funds or from some other source?” Ban said. Defending the government’s decision to appoint Rohatgi, Ban said senior advocates were engaged as per established government norms and that the fees were not an additional expenditure arising exclusively from the Gokul dispute. “Government advocates are on the panel and are paid proportionately. It is not that the government is paying higher legal fees only because of the Gokul matter. The Rs 80 lakh fee paid to Mukul Rohatgi is as per government norms,” he said. Ban also countered Patil’s criticism over drought relief, citing the assistance announced by the Karnataka government. “The Congress government in neighbouring Karnataka gave only Rs 2,500 to farmers as drought relief, whereas Maharashtra has provided Rs 5,000, that too as initial assistance, along with a loan waiver for drought-hit farmers,” he said. Recover money from ministers: Sanjay Raut Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut also questioned the government’s decision to bear the legal expenses, saying the amount should instead be recovered from state ministers Hasan Mushrif and Chandrakant Patil, whom he held responsible for the developments at Gokul. “The Rs 80 lakh legal fee should be paid through the bank accounts of Hasan Mushrif and Chandrakant Patil. All this has happened at Gokul because of them,” Raut said. Responding to Raut, Mushrif defended the government’s decision. “If the government’s side is being represented, as it is the government’s ordinance, the government will pay the legal fees. If our side is represented, we will pay ourselves. Also, if the public prosecutor is not available, it is routine practice to hire a senior counsel,” Mushrif said.

headline: Will Health Minister Nadda survive release of 'damning report' on anaemia prevalence: Congress
content: New Delhi: The Congress on Tuesday cited an official report that showed Gujarat fairing poorly in terms of anaemia prevalence in 2023-25, and asked whether Union Health Minister J P Nadda would survive the release of this "damning report". .Congress general secretary in-charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh, pointed out that the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has just put out a report titled "Anaemia and Micronutrient Deficiencies Across the Life Course in India". .In Gujarat, 61.4 per cent of adolescent girls (10-19 years), 63.8 per cent of adult women (20-59 years) and 66.2 per cent of women in reproductive age (15-49 years) were found to be suffering from anaemia during 2023-25, Ramesh said on X. ."Only Chhattisgarh fared worse. The corresponding figures for the best performing state Kerala were 21.4 per cent, 28 per cent and 29.1 per cent, no doubt high but nowhere near the levels prevailing in Gujarat, which for some years has been propagated as a model state by the prime minister and his cheerleaders," Ramesh said. .Low birth weight babies to be added to Anaemia Mukt Bharat as Centre prepares to revamp guidelines.In fact, for children in the age group of 12-59 months, Gujarat had the highest anaemia prevalence (56.5 per cent) while Kerala had the lowest (14.5 per cent), he said. ."Will the genial Union Health Minister survive the release of this damning report?" Ramesh asked. .Prevalence of anaemia in India is lower than reported in previous national surveys, with severe anaemia accounting for less than 2 per cent of cases across most age groups, according to findings of the Indian Council of Medical Research's SAMPADA survey released on Monday. .SAMPADA -- or the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry -- conducted during 2023-25, covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 states and Union Territories. .More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex and physiological groups. .The findings also showed that most cases of anaemia were mild, indicating an opportunity for early intervention, the Department of Health Research said.

headline: ‘How can they offer 1 seat in Amethi, Rae Bareli?’: SP leaves Congress fuming
content: A day after the Congress asked for 131 seats in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party (SP) led by Akhilesh Yadav countered with an offer of just 26 seats for the grand old party, offering just one seat to its ally in Rae Bareli and Amethi, the Congress strongholds and the pocket boroughs of the Nehru-Gandhis, where the party is looking to contest all Assembly seats. The discussions concluded on Tuesday with the Congress revising its offer to 120 constituencies. SP sources said the Congress was making “unreasonable” demands for seats and struggling to come up with a formula for demanding seats. “Even during Monday’s meeting, we asked the leaders of the Congress to give us a formula on which they are asking for 131 seats. For around 30 seats, they said that it was those where the party led in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. But what about the other 90 seats? These are crucial elections and they have to come up with a formula for asking us for seats,” said the source. Sources said the 26 seats they had offered were chosen based on a distinct formula: four are those where Congress finished second in 2022 Assembly elections, while two are those it won in 2022. “We are offering the party another 20 seats,” said the source. Of the 26 seats, the Congress won Rampur Khas and Farenda in 2022 — the only two it won — and finished second in Mathura, Kheragarh (Agra), Jagdishpur (Amethi), and Kidwai Nagar (Kanpur). The other 20 seats are Baghpat, Modinagar (Ghaziabad), Hapur, Jewar (Gautam Budh Nagar), Syana (Bulandshahr), Khurja (Bulandshahr), Khair (Aligarh), Iglas (Hathras), Mant (Mathura), Agra North (Agra), Fatehpur Sikri (agra), Bilgram-Mallanwan (Hardoi), Govind Nagar (Kanpur), Nanpara (Bahraich), Gorakhpur City, Khajani (Sant Kabir Nagar), Padrauna (Kushinagar), Fazilnagar (Kushinagar), Pindra (Varanasi) and Varanasi Cantonment. A closer look at these 20 seats shows that 11 seats are in West UP, where the SP is considered to be relatively weaker organisationally, two are in central UP, and seven in East UP. Congress leaders reacted furiously to the list shared by the SP. “We will give a formal statement soon. But for now, we can say that this is infuriating. How can they offer us one seat in Amethi and Rae Bareli? How can they give us a list of 26 seats out of 403? We have contested 17 in the Lok Sabha out of 80. We will speak on this after the meeting,” said a senior Congress leader who is part of the seat-sharing talks. Sources in the All India Congress Committee said Tuesday’s meeting, which was held at MP Pramod Tiwari’s residence, saw some heated exchanges between the two sides. The 2022 results The 11 West UP seats the SP has offered were won by the BJP in 2022. The Jayant Chaudhary-led RLD, then an ally of the Akhilesh Yadav-led party, was the runner-up in seven. The BSP was the runner-up in two seats, while the SP finished second in two. Of the two central UP seats, the SP was the runner-up in Bilgram-Mallanwan, while in Govind Nagar, it lost by a massive 80,896-vote margin. In the seven East UP seats, the SP finished second in all. All constituencies went to the NDA, with the BJP taking six and the Apna Dal (Soneylal) one (Nanpara). Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s Gorakhpur Urban constituency is among these seats.

headline: Miranda House, DU Launches 15 Professional Certificate Courses In AI, Animation, VFX, Creator Economy
content: Miranda House, University of Delhi, has launched 15 professional certificate courses in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Eros AIVidya, aimed at equipping students with skills in artificial intelligence (AI), filmmaking, animation, virtual reality and the creator economy. The six-month programmes will offer industry-oriented training in emerging creative and digital fields. Admissions will be open to eligible University of Delhi students on the basis of merit. According to the institute, the courses will be open to students of both genders. The programme portfolio includes AI filmmaking, influencer and creator business, avatar and digital human creation, animation, video blogging, AR/VR production, visual effects (VFX), script writing, acting, music production, music composition and direction, sound editing, editing and art direction. The certificates will be co-certified by NSDC and Eros AIVidya. The programmes aim to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements in fields being transformed by AI, immersive media and digital content creation. The AI filmmaking course will introduce students to AI-enabled content creation, while the influencer and creator business programme will focus on commercial and professional aspects of the creator economy. Avatar and digital human creation will cover emerging forms of virtual identity and digital media. Other courses will focus on creative disciplines such as animation, acting, script writing, music, sound, editing and visual effects. Under the collaboration, 15 high-performing students will receive support to start their own businesses. The opportunity will be offered to students who demonstrate outstanding performance during the courses. The initiative aims to provide students with opportunities beyond certification by connecting skill development with creative projects, career opportunities and entrepreneurship. Eligibility, Fees And Admission The courses will be open to students currently enrolled at the University of Delhi who have a valid Class 12 pass certificate or marksheet. Admissions will be based strictly on merit. The duration of each programme is six months, while the indicative fee ranges from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1.5 lakh, depending on the course. The launch comes amid the government’s growing focus on India’s animation, visual effects, gaming and comics (AVGC) sector and the creator economy. The Union Budget 2026-27 announced support for the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) to establish AVGC Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges. Miranda House Principal Dr Bijayalaxmi Nanda said the collaboration would help bridge traditional academic learning and the demands of the evolving digital workforce, while equipping students with specialised skills and career opportunities. Eros AIVidya CEO Prashant Pandit said the programmes would enable students to apply their learning, create projects and develop capabilities that could translate into careers, entrepreneurship and new forms of creative work.

headline: India, China set for record Russian oil imports in 2026 amid Iran war
content: India and China are on track for record Russian oil imports this year, plugging a supply gap caused by the Iran war, as US sanctions waivers eased purchases and Ukrainian drone attacks knocked ​out Russian refining, according to tanker data and industry sources.But traders and analysts expect shipments ​to Russia's two biggest customers to wane in 2027 as Middle Eastern supplies recover and reclaim market share.Seaborne Russian oil supplies ‌to the world's two most populous countries averaged 3.4 million barrels per day this year through mid-November, up about 530,000 bpd from a year earlier, according to Vortexa Analytics.With Brent crude up nearly one third since the start of the war, the increased volumes, which include Kazakhstan oil transited via Russian ports, have bolstered Moscow's oil revenue even as repeated drone attacks by Kiev have hit nearly half of Russian refining capacity, prompting more crude exports.Russia's oil exports are expected to rise 6 per cent in 2026 to 244.7 million metric tons, or about 4.9 million bpd, according to a forecast by its Ministry of Economic Development.Temporary US waivers on Russian oil sanctions, aimed at keeping markets supplied amid the Middle East crisis, widened the pool of vessels and suppliers available to India and China, allowing them to increase purchases.Together, the two bought more than 80 per cent of Russia's crude exports, according to estimates by two industry sources familiar with ‌Russian oil flows.Russia supplies a quarter of China's importsRussian oil exports to top overall buyer China rose 17 per cent to 2.34 million bpd during January-October, worth $59.6 billion, accounting for about a quarter of Beijing's oil imports, according to Chinese customs data, despite a 15 per cent fall in its crude imports as Middle Eastern supplies plunged."Lower shipping risks and greater supply reliability have been the main reasons behind the increase in China's Russian crude imports since the war broke out," said Muyu Xu, analyst with tanker tracker Kpler.However, Michal Meidan, head of China Energy Research at the Oxford Institute of Energy Studies, predicted China's appetite will wane in 2027 as Russia's surging import share exceeds Beijing's comfort zone with a single ​supplier."More importantly, they are no longer at a discount and are trading at higher premiums to Brent than Gulf crudes. The teapots can no ‌longer afford them," said Meidan, referring to smaller independent Chinese refiners that rely on discounted crude."As Gulf flows stabilise, Chinese refiners will revert back to those crudes and are already favouring Brazilian grades," she added.Strong demand for Russian barrels, spurred also by dwindling ​Iranian oil flows due ‌to the US naval blockade, lifted spot premiums of ESPO to as high as nearly $30 a barrel over ICE Brent for deliveries into east China.India's record Russian purchasesIndia, the top buyer of seaborne Russian crude, averaged imports of 1.99 million bpd through early November, up 250,000 bpd annually, Kpler data showed, despite cutting purchases earlier this year after a threatened hike in US tariffs.During January to October, India's Russian ‌oil imports ​rose about 10 per cent ​to 1.87 million bpd, about 38 per cent of overall volumes, according to data from trade sources.India's Russian oil imports are likely to average 1.9 million bpd in 2026, sources at Indian refiners said.India's purchases are likely to return to pre-Iran war levels ‌in 2027 if supplies from ​the Middle East normalise, with imports expected to be driven by prices, the sources said.

headline: Rajasthan Industrial Park Promotion Policy 2026: Building Industrial Ecosystems
source: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute
content: Rajasthan Industrial Park Promotion Policy 2026 supports private sector involvement in developing industry. It promotes 4 distinct development approaches; shared infrastructure support, green benefits and staged payments – all aiming to overcome issues related to industrial development funding and delivery. Thereafter there should be a regular review of data relating to industrial park development including ideas, permissions, land allocation, funds pledged and used, infrastructure provision, operating industrial space, utilisation levels and jobs created. Information should also be analysed by district, development approach and industry type. An ad-hoc joint working group comprising RIICO, Industries and Commerce, power, water, Public Works Department and pollution control bodies could be set up. Specific service delivery targets for electricity, transport, water and environmental services can then be established. This can assist in overcoming challenges associated with external infrastructure provision and further enhance development delivery. Industrial park developments should be based upon analyses of market need, infrastructure provision, water and power access, labour supply and environmental capacity. Parks should also be designed to meet the needs of specific industries and to encourage local procurement especially for MSMEs. Particular industrial park space (or pre-constructed ‘plug and play’ industrial space) could even be reserved for MSMEs and local supporting businesses, thus further enhancing cost-efficiency and enabling MSMEs to become more effectively embedded within industry networks. Infrastructure, environmental and industrial performance should all be independently reviewed alongside the payment of benefits. Developers must also reveal information regarding land costs, rental agreements and general maintenance fees. Stage-wise independent reviews can highlight where there are development delays and ensure that public sector funds are delivering extra economic benefit. Whilst much will hinge upon how effectively Rajasthan is able to utilise its pro-investment policy to establish efficient industrial environments, the recent decision to provide land for 3 industrial parks is a good early move. Long-term policy success will rely upon continuing industrial and job creation together with local networking and sustainable natural resource management. By integrating industrial development with sustainability, regional planning, accountability and MSME involvement, Rajasthan can further bolster its role in achieving Viksit Rajasthan@2047 and India’s wider industrial and economic development aspirations.

headline: The Spanish paradox: Booming economy, angry young voters
content: A giant banner featuring Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s smiling face hangs over the main entrance to Madrid’s central Sol station. A few weeks earlier, it was the epicenter of some of the biggest protests the country has seen in a generation. Above ground, demonstrators railed against politicians and their failure to deal with a housing crisis, which has become a symbol for broader anger about the cost of living and inequality. Below, many commuters shared the frustration, enduring delays on trains taking them to jobs that barely pay enough to cover rent. The protest camp is gone now, removed by police. But the outrage that drove people there in the first place remains. And Spanish voters will have their say this Sunday after Sánchez called a snap election. The mood among large swathes of the population is at odds with the image of Spain on paper. It looks like a model economy, expanding more than twice as fast as the eurozone, cutting its budget deficit and reducing unemployment. Just this month, ING called it the “comeback kid.” The numbers, however stellar, don’t capture reality for many Spaniards, especially the younger generation, whose life is dominated by worries about money, job security and what the future holds. Housing looms large. Property prices have risen about twice as fast as wages for young workers. Two thirds of adults under the age of 34 still live with their parents. As if the daily grind wasn’t enough, the country has been traumatized by a series of catastrophes, from tragic rail crashes that killed more than 100 people to summer wildfires, climate-fueled storms and flash floods that destroyed homes and businesses.

headline: Delhi HC refuses bail to man accused of robbing Rapido driver
content: New Delhi, The Delhi High Court has denied bail to a man accused of robbing his Rapido driver, observing that he breached the trust of a cab driver who was engaged to facilitate his travel.In July, the accused, along with two other men, allegedly robbed the cab driver of ₹3,000, a mobile phone, and his vehicle, a Maruti Dzire car, while pointing a knife at his neck.The three accused had booked the cab ride through the Rapido app for travel from Ghitorni village to Lal Quila.Rejecting the bail application by Zunaid Ali, Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav observed that the accused persons seemed to be mentally prepared to commit the crime, as no normal person moves around with a knife, and it was appropriate to await the framing of charges and examination of public witnesses before releasing the accused. "Having considered the submissions made by the contesting sides, especially the fact that the act of the applicant reflects that he has breached the trust of a cab driver, who was engaged by them to facilitate their own travel. He was merely a service provider to them, but instead of availing the services, it seems that they were mentally prepared to commit this crime, inasmuch as the availability of the knife is indicative of this fact. A normal man does not go and move around with a knife," the court said in the order passed on November 19.Noting that the cab driver's vehicle, mobile phone, driving license, and the knife were recovered from the accused persons during investigation, the court said, "Recoveries effected from the applicant and the co-accused cement the case further against the present applicant and co-accused."The court concluded that granting bail at this stage would prejudice the prosecution's case and could be detrimental to the victim."The application is declined as the applicant does not deserve to be considered for bail at this stage," it held.The prosecution opposed granting bail to the accused, stating there was cogent evidence, including CCTV footage and recovery of the victim's belongings, to prove his complicity in the offence.It was stated that a knife was used to commit the robbery on a highway between the sunset and sunrise and the accused did not deserve to be released on bail.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited Reports Double-Digit Growth In H1 Fy27, Despite Headwinds From Middle East Conflict On The Experience Economy
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 24: Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited today announced its consolidated results for the half year ended September 30 2026. The company delivered strong growth even though the global experience economy was affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.H1 FY27 HIGHLIGHTS (CONSOLIDATED, UNAUDITED):- Revenue from operations: ₹116.41 crore, up 13.1% from ₹102.91 crore in H1 FY26;- Profit before tax: ₹27.85 crore, up 12.8% from ₹24.69 crore;- Profit after tax: ₹24.60 crore, up 10.6% from ₹22.25 crore;- PBT Margin: 24.0%, unchanged year on year;- Basic EPS: ₹16.07, up 6.6% from ₹15.07;- Sequential Growth: PBT up 19.4% and PAT up 19.8% over H2 FY26, making H1 FY27 the strongest half-year for both among the periods reportedSTRONGER BALANCE SHEETTotal equity rose 45.6% to ₹250.40 crore from ₹171.94 crore at 31 March 2026. Total assets grew 27.3% to ₹299.36 crore. The company received ₹53.00 crore against shares and warrants during the half. Cash and cash equivalents rose 28.4% to ₹33.84 crore, with other bank balances of ₹25.90 crore.Management commentary"The conflict in the Middle East has weighed on the global experience economy, with events, travel and exhibitions all affected. We will keep investing in exhibition infrastructure, venues and event solutions." - M Q Syed, Chairman & Managing Director, Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL.
