headline: Tibetan representative raises concerns over Chinas cultural assimilation policy during Japan visit
content: Tokyo [Japan], November 24 (ANI): Representative of the Dalai Lama and the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) to Japan and East Asia, Lobsang Choedak, has highlighted concerns over China's policies in Tibet, calling for greater international support to protect the region's cultural, religious and linguistic identity during an interaction with Japanese supporters in Hokkaido.According to a report by the Central Tibetan Administration, Choedak addressed an event organised by the Hokkaido Friends of Tibet in Sapporo on November 21, where he spoke about Tibet's historical status as an independent nation before its occupation by the People's Republic of China in 1950.He expressed concern over China's so-called Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, which came into force on July 1, 2026, describing it as an attempt by the Chinese Communist government to institutionalise policies aimed at weakening Tibet's distinct cultural, religious, linguistic and national identity.Emphasising Tibet's rich heritage as one of the world's ancient civilisations, Choedak said that protecting Tibetan culture and traditions was not merely the responsibility of the Tibetan people but a shared responsibility of the international community.According to the report, he also outlined the Central Tibetan Administration's efforts to counter the impact of the legislation by strengthening Tibetan monastic institutions, educational centres, schools and communities in exile.These initiatives, he said, are aimed at preserving the Tibetan language, religious practices and cultural traditions for future generations.The report said that, on the diplomatic front, Choedak stated that the CTA was working to expand international support by engaging governments and people across the world to raise concerns over China's policies in Tibet.He also appreciated the Japanese Parliamentary Support Group for Tibet for its strong position against the Chinese legislation. The group had issued a statement condemning the law, warning that it threatened the distinct identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs and Southern Mongolians. (ANI) (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: DDA announces online booking policy for 17 parks, amphitheatres for festivals, exhibitions
content: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on Tuesday announced a policy for booking parks and recreational green spaces for literary festivals, exhibitions, food festivals, cultural performances, heritage walks, yoga sessions and community gatherings. It said 17 parks, including Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Asita (Yamuna River Front), Hauz Khas Park and Baansera, and amphitheaters at places like Sanjay Lake, Coronation Park and Vasant Udyan will be covered under the policy.A DDA spokesperson said a centralised, single-window online booking portal will be linked to the DDA website, bringing the entire process onto a common digital platform, enabling applicants to explore available locations, check designated areas and capacities, understand applicable charges and submit applications and payments online. “LG [Lieutenant Governor] Taranjit Singh Sandhu has issued directions for rationalising services offered by the DDA parks, after which the authority has introduced a new policy for booking these spaces for public, educational, cultural, recreational and community activities in designated green spaces,” the spokesperson said.The DDA said the permitted activities will include meditation and fitness programmes, poetry readings, book launches and discussions, guided nature and heritage walks, workshops, awareness programmes, art and craft exhibitions, cultural performances, theatre, book fairs, craft bazaars, food festivals, educational activities and institutional events, subject to approval of the proposed event plan.The designated open park spaces have been classified under Category A, with three sub-categories based on the anticipated peak gathering. Category A1 will be for gatherings of up to 200 people, A2 for 200 to 500 people, and A3 for large gatherings of over 500 people. “The classification will enable DDA to regulate activities according to the scale of participation and the requirement of individual locations,” an official said.Facilities such as amphitheatres will be available under Category B. There are separate provisions for half-day and full-day bookings and for ticketed and non-ticketed events.The sites include large parks, places of archaeological importance, spaces near waterbodies, and amphitheaters, including Swarna Jayanti Park (Rohini), District Parks in Dwarka, Indraprastha Park (Millennium Park), Astha Kunj, Hauz Khas Park and Mehrauli Archaeological Park.The amphitheatres at Indraprastha Park, Astha Kunj, Utsav Ground, Vasant Udyan, and Tughlaqabad Recreational Park are proposed to be made available, subject to notified capacities.The DDA policy provides for schools to book designated park spaces for ₹1 for educational and recreational activities. “These may include school picnics, painting and photography activities, debates, competitions and similar educational engagements,” the official said.The initiative is intended to take learning beyond classroom boundaries and provide children with opportunities to connect with nature, observe biodiversity, appreciate the environment and participate in creative and collaborative activities in open green spaces.Schools booking parks for other purposes will be eligible for a 50% concession on applicable booking charges, subject to the policy provisions. Recognised higher educational institutions, government departments, public sector undertakings and autonomous bodies can get a 50% concession on applicable booking charges.The DDA said that special safeguards have been incorporated for ecologically sensitive locations, including Asita and Mehrauli Archaeological Park. “Activities in notified ridge areas and protected forest areas will be subject to applicable conservation guidelines and restricted to sunrise-to-sunset timings,” says the policy.“The booking agency will be responsible for crowd management, safety arrangements, waste segregation and disposal, cleaning and restoration of the allotted area. GPS-tagged photographs before and after the event will help ensure accountability and proper monitoring of the condition of the site.”

headline: Private project announcements jump 58.5% to ₹26.6 trillion in H1 FY27: CII
content: Private sector project announcements surged 58.5% year-on-year to ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), signalling a sharp expansion in India's investment pipeline, with manufacturing, electricity and technology-related infrastructure emerging as key drivers, according to industry body Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).According to the second edition of CII's Private Investment Barometer, project announcements in H1 FY27 were 4.4 times the average recorded in the same period between FY17 and FY25.The private sector's share of total project announcements also rose to 86.2% during April-September 2026 from 74.2% a year earlier. The increase comes amid sustained policy reforms, infrastructure development and improvements in the regulatory framework, which have strengthened the foundation for private investment, the industry body said on Tuesday. It urged companies to step up capital expenditure, innovation and project execution to support the government's Viksit Bharat agenda. The improvement is also reflected in actual capital formation. Gross capital formation by around 1,800 listed private companies touched ₹12.4 trillion in FY26, equivalent to 3.6% of nominal gross domestic product (GDP), compared with an average of 2.2% during FY17-FY21. On a comparable-company basis, investment increased 8.7% in FY26. Further, 54% of companies increased their fixed investment rates, while approximately three out of four added net productive capacity. Private-sector project completions during April-September 2026 stood at ₹1.8 trillion, the highest for the corresponding period since FY17. "The government deserves considerable credit for creating a strong enabling environment for private investment through sustained policy reforms, infrastructure development and improvements in the regulatory framework," CII president R. Mukundan said, adding that Indian industry had been responding to these opportunities. The investment pipeline also reflects a shift towards manufacturing, infrastructure and emerging technology-related sectors. Manufacturing project announcements stood at ₹8.1 trillion in H1 FY27, 3.2 times their historical average, while electricity-sector announcements reached ₹7.7 trillion, 5.1 times their historical average. Information technology project announcements, largely comprising data centres and artificial intelligence-related infrastructure, reached approximately ₹9.5 trillion during the period, against ₹70,000 crore in the corresponding period last year. Mukundan said private enterprises were investing in manufacturing, infrastructure, energy and digital technologies, supported by stronger balance sheets and greater confidence in India's economic prospects. CII also highlighted the government's efforts to modernize financial markets and strengthen the regulatory framework. It said the consultative approach adopted by regulators, including the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), had contributed to deeper and more resilient capital markets. The industry body said investor protection, market integrity, regulatory predictability and proportionate compliance requirements would remain important to mobilising long-term domestic and international capital.Teaming upLooking ahead, CII said achieving the Viksit Bharat vision would require closer collaboration between industry and the government, with a focus on accelerating investment and project execution, creating quality employment, improving productivity and strengthening domestic manufacturing and supply chains.It identified research and innovation, skill development, export expansion and deeper integration into global value chains as key priorities. The transition to clean energy, adoption of emerging technologies, development of globally competitive Indian enterprises and greater participation of micro, small and medium enterprises would also be important to sustaining growth.While acknowledging progress in improving the ease of doing business, Mukundan said the next phase of reforms should focus on the speed of doing business, particularly faster decisions, approvals and project execution."The government has demonstrated its commitment through sustained reforms and substantial investments in building India's economic foundations. It is now incumbent upon industry to match this commitment with greater investment, innovation, risk-taking and long-term capacity building," he said.CII said better access to long-term finance and faster project implementation would be critical to translating investment intentions into productive capacity and employment. It added that it and its members were committed to working with the government to improve investment, employment, competitiveness, sustainability and inclusive growth.

headline: Maharashtra FDA warns gyms against unauthorised sale of health supplements
content: Maharashtra Food and Drugs Administration Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has warned of strict action against unauthorised sale of health supplements in gyms and manufacturers printing health claims on the labels of nutraceutical products.Talking to reporters on Monday, Mundhe asserted that wholesalers, retailers and gym operators cannot shift the blame onto manufacturers and are individually responsible for verifying that the products they sell are legitimate, free from false claims and backed by a Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) licence.He clarified that no health supplement or nutraceutical company, manufacturer or producer is permitted to claim specific health benefits or print such claims on product labels.If gym owners wished to sell supplements on their premises, they would have to obtain a proper FSSAI licence, he said, warning of strict action against those selling such products without authorisation."Nutraceuticals and health supplements are being consumed improperly, and misleading advertising claims are being made about them. People in gyms often claim that eating protein powder will automatically build muscles. These misconceptions and false practices have no legal basis and must stop," the senior official said.He further stressed that simply holding an FSSAI licence does not give shopkeepers or sellers the right to sell substandard or adulterated products."Sellers cannot shift the blame onto manufacturers; wholesalers, retailers, sellers, and manufacturers are each individually responsible for verifying that the products they buy and sell are legitimate and free from false claims," Mundhe added.Last week, the FDA issued a statewide compliance order imposing stricter regulations on health supplements, nutraceuticals and special dietary foods.The order, specifically targeting sports nutrition, weight loss, sexual wellness and herbal products, covers the entire supply chain, including manufacturers, importers, distributors, warehouses, retailers, pharmacies, gyms and e-commerce websites.

headline: Delhi government plans separate detention facility for female foreign nationals in Narela
content: New Delhi: Delhi government is working to establish a dedicated detention facility for female foreign nationals in Narela, along with a centre to accommodate families and a proposed open jail, officials said on Tuesday. .The proposed facility is part of an expansion of the existing detention infrastructure at Lampur — close to the Delhi-Haryana border. The move aims to address the shortage of appropriate accommodation for women held pending deportation or other immigration-related proceedings. .There are five blocks at the Lampur detention centre and it was decided to lodge male detainees in two blocks and female detainees in one block. .No bulletproof van for jailed Bishnoi gang lawyer: Delhi court says separate him from rivals in Tihar, transit.The fourth block is to be used as an open jail for female prisoners, while the remaining one is to be used as an administrative block, a senior Home Department officer said, adding that work is to be started on it. .Currently, female foreign nationals requiring detention are kept in temporary arrangements, including community centres and shelter homes. One such facility at Nirmal Chhaya has a limited capacity of around 30 inmates, they said. .However, the number of women requiring such accommodation sometimes rises to 70-80, putting pressure on the available infrastructure and highlighting the need for a separate facility. .The Lampur detention centre, spread across 18.5 acres in the Sewa Sadan complex, primarily accommodates male foreign nationals. The premises include an old building that is around five decades old and are managed with the involvement of the Delhi government, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office and the Central Reserve Police Force. .The proposal envisages additional infrastructure at the Lampur premises, including accommodation for women. An adjoining plot may also be utilised to develop a family detention facility and an open jail, they said. .Currently, over 280 male foreign nationals are lodged at the centre. They include undocumented migrants, asylum seekers and refugees who are awaiting deportation following visa violations or completion of their prison terms. .A substantial number of foreign nationals detained in Delhi are from Bangladesh, while Nigerians constitute another significant group. .Separately, the Delhi government has sought 27 acres of land from the Delhi Development Authority in Narela for developing another prison near an upcoming high-security jail. The proposed facility is expected to help reduce the pressure on the overcrowded Tihar prison complex. .An earlier plan to construct a multi-storeyed prison in the area was reconsidered over security-related concerns, an officer said. .The proposals are at the planning stage, and further details are awaited.

headline: Rajib seeks Centre's intervention over soaring Airfares, Flags connectivity concerns for Tripura & Northeast
content: Amid growing concern over steep increases in airfares on routes connecting Tripura and other Northeastern states with major cities, MP Rajib Bhattacharjee has sought the intervention of the Union Civil Aviation Minister, calling for measures to curb excessive fare escalation, particularly during festivals, holidays and periods of high passenger demand. In a letter sent to the Union Minister, Bhattacharjee drew attention to the particular dependence of the Northeast on air connectivity and urged the Centre to consider a combination of fare regulation, closer monitoring of dynamic pricing and increased flight capacity to protect passengers from sudden and excessive price increases. The MP highlighted air routes linking the Northeast with Delhi, Kolkata and Guwahati, arguing that affordable connectivity on these sectors is essential for large sections of the population. He pointed out that passengers frequently encounter sharp fare increases during the festive season, holidays and other periods when travel demand rises significantly. According to Bhattacharjee, such escalation places a disproportionate financial burden on ordinary travellers, including students, patients travelling for medical treatment, government employees, businesspeople and families who depend upon air services for essential journeys. The geographical location of Tripura and other Northeastern states, he argued, makes the issue particularly important. With many alternative modes of transport involving considerably longer journeys, air travel often becomes a necessity rather than a matter of convenience for residents travelling to major cities for education, employment, healthcare and other urgent requirements. Bhattacharjee maintained that exceptionally high fares could therefore have consequences extending beyond travel expenses, potentially making essential journeys more difficult for people who have limited practical alternatives.

headline: The Nepal Lesson | Why patience works in foreign policy
content: Like many upstart politicians, Balendra Shah shoots from the hip. Provocative? No problem. For Nepal's youth, this unapologetic, direct, even controversial approach only makes the country's rapper-turned-prime minister more appealing. For three years now, as Shah first assumed the mayorship of Kathmandu and then rode the Gen Z anger that overthrew then Prime Minister K P Sharma Oli's government, winning national elections earlier this year, India has often been the target of his criticism. Over maps and Bollywood depictions. Over territorial claims and India's 'big brother' status in South Asia. And through diplomatic slights — soon after he came to power, Shah refused to meet the Indian foreign secretary.

headline: Mehbooba heads to Sheshnag lake after excavator row, stopped mid-way
content: Former Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti was stopped at Chandanwari as she was heading to Sheshnag lake on the Pahalgam-Amarnath cave route on Tuesday. Mufti was accompanied by two PDP legislators: Waheed Para and Aga Muntazir Mehdi. As they reached Chandanwari, the police stopped them citing “security reasons”. Sheshnag lake, a glacial lake that sits at an altitude of 3,950 meters on the route to Amarnath cave, is around 12 kilometres from Chandanwari. A controversy has erupted in the Valley after a video showing excavators moving mounds of earth near the Sheshnag alpine lake and dumping soil on its shores. The lake is also considered sacred in Hinduism. ALSO READ | Mehbooba Mufti’s history lesson for National Conference on Centre-J&K ‘mistrust’ The political and religious leaders of the valley as well as environment activists have called for an immediate halt of the use of excavators in the ecologically fragile region citing damage to Himalayan ecosystem and sacredness of the lake. “This is a disaster. How such heavy machines reach our glaciers of Kashmir,” asked climate activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat in a post on X. “What is all this? Can anyone update?” PDP leader and spokesperson Mohit Bhan called it a “crime against Hindu faith”. “Sheshnag is not just another lake in the mountains of Kashmir. In Hinduism, it is the sacred landscape where Lord Shiva is believed to have left behind the serpents before proceeding towards the Amarnath Cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati,” Bhan said. Valley’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq called the visuals “very disturbing”. He said, “With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm.” Former MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said that the mountains of Kashmir are “not BJP’s real estate”. “A party that wins votes in the name of faith is now taking JCBs to a holy lake,” he said. Communist leader M Y Tarigami said the government must “immediately stop any work that threatens the lake and its surroundings”. He said, “Sheshnag is surrounded by loose moraine and steep slopes. Disturbing this fragile terrain with heavy machinery is an invitation to disaster.” The Border Roads Organisation (BRO, however, has said that it is carrying out work on Amarnath yatra track stabilisation and that all measures to ensure safe disposal of excavated material, protect natural drainage and minimise disturbance to surrounding terrain have been taken. “The recently circulating video on social media, claiming about new works, is incorrect. Based on experience of previous Yatra and requirement highlighted for wider road for Shri Amarnath ji yatra, BRO has started widening of tracks focusing on stabilising vulnerable stretches as prescribed to ease congestion and allow safer passage,” it said in a statement. In a video originally shared by an Instagram account, ‘Neeraj_excavator_lover’, a heavy earth excavator could be seen being used to create a road near the Sheshnag lake that falls on the trekking route from Pahalgam to the Amarnath cave shrine. By the time the Instagram user deleted the video, it had triggered a controversy and sparked concern over the possible ecological impact of such activities.

headline: India needs greater private investment to realise USD 45 billion space economy potential: Jitendra Singh
content: New Delhi [India], November 24 (ANI): Union Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences Jitendra Singh on Tuesday called on domestic businesses to increase investments in India's space sector and help attract overseas capital, as the country looks to expand its space economy from nearly USD 9 billion to USD 40-45 billion in less than a decade.Addressing the fifth India International Space Conclave (IISC 2026) in New Delhi, Singh said domestic private investment had taken time to gather momentum and needed to be scaled up. He added that industry leaders could use their business networks to facilitate greater overseas investment."Investments from domestic private players have taken some time to pick up initially. So we need to scale them up," he said, urging industry participants to take a more active role in bringing capital into the sector.He noted that India had moved from having only a handful of space startups to around 400-500 following the opening up of the sector to private participation. The space economy, which was earlier negligible, is now close to USD 9 billion and could reach USD 40-45 billion in less than a decade, he said.The government approved space sector reforms in June 2020 to enable private companies to participate across the space value chain, while establishing IN-SPACe as a single-window interface to facilitate their entry and participation. Building on these reforms, it liberalised foreign investment rules in 2024, allowing up to 74 per cent FDI through the automatic route in satellite manufacturing and operations.Singh called for greater corporate participation in scientific research, urging businesses to make better use of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding and develop a stronger culture of philanthropy for science."What you spend on research is also a worship," he said, stressing that scientific research should receive greater support from private businesses.He highlighted the role of space technology beyond rocket launches, saying its applications in infrastructure projects, housing and other government programmes were helping reduce delays, wastage and costs. Citing the Gati Shakti programme, he said space technology was helping improve project timelines and prevent leakages.The Minister also pointed to the growth in defence production, which rose from Rs 46,429 crore in 2014 to Rs 1.7 lakh crore in the last financial year. Defence exports stood at around Rs 23,000 crore in the preceding year, of which nearly Rs 15,000 crore came from the private sector, he said.He further said biotechnology, quantum technology and artificial intelligence would be among India's other major growth areas, alongside space, in the coming years. headline: Inside the return of Akali Dal-BJP alliance: Why the two parties reconciled
content: Reuniting after six years in the countdown to the Punjab Assembly elections, the BJP and the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) Tuesday announced an alliance for the state polls due early next year. This also marked the return of the SAD, one of the founding members of the NDA, to the ruling alliance at the Centre. In 2020, the SAD had walked out of the NDA, protesting against the farm laws later repealed by the Centre. Announcing the alliance in the presence of Badal and BJP president Nitin Nabin at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the SAD’s return to the NDA was a matter of “great joy”. “Akali Dal will remain in the role of bada bhai (elder brother). Akali Dal and BJP will fight together. Both the parties will contest together on all 117 seats. But Akali Dal will take the role of bada bhai,” Shah said. Asked who will get the Chief Minister’s post should the alliance win, he said, “Bada bhai is the one who becomes Chief Minister.” Sources in both parties said seat-sharing discussions will take place over the coming days and they could “settle for a combination of around 70-plus seats for the Akalis and around 45 for the BJP”. Welcoming the announcement, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a post on X, said, “Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji.” “Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress. Nurtured by Atal Ji, Advani Ji and Sardar Parkash Singh Badal Ji, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. I am confident that our Alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab,” Modi said. Shah said Modi spoke to Badal Monday. “The BJP and SAD have had historic ties… This alliance will be a symbol of Hindu-Sikh unity… While we will come out with a detailed manifesto later, uprooting the drug menace and corruption will be core concerns.” “I have full confidence that the people of Punjab will bless this alliance which is under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi… We will surely make an NDA government in the state and bring the state back to its glory,” he said. Calling it a natural alliance, Nabin said, “We will discuss seat sharing later. Today, the message which we want to give is that we have come together to fulfil the commitment of a Viksit Punjab.” Badal said the alliance was not just political. He called it an “emotional one” which had produced successive governments rooted in communal harmony and prosperity for Punjab. “Today I am happy that this relationship, which was forged in 1996 by my father and Atal Bihari Vajpayee ji, is surfacing again… It was like a family,” he said, adding that only an “NDA double engine sarkar” with a strong and stable Centre could pull Punjab out of its drug menace, corruption and dire financial condition. “I want to thank Modi Saab, Amit Shah Ji and Nitin Nabin Ji… They have assured me that we will bring back a glorious Punjab and I can assure you that I will work round the clock… for a drug-free and development-oriented Punjab… and bring back the atmosphere of communal harmony and brotherhood which used to exist,” he said. According to Badal, Modi was likely to be part of a “big event” being organised on the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal on December 8. “This is because there was a strong bond of love between him (his father) and Modi Ji,” he said. Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said the two parties, in the coming days, will sit for a seat-by-seat assessment with the main criterion being “winnability”. “We will sit down together and do a seat-by-seat analysis; which one the Akalis or BJP can take on the basis of winnability. We will work together as proper partners… winnability is the sole criterion,” Dhillon said. How the alliance came together Senior BJP leaders had earlier rejected the likelihood of the former allies coming together. But BJP insiders said an initiative was undertaken recently following a push from Modi who told his party colleagues that they should contest the Assembly elections with the Akalis. Shah then stepped in to iron out the differences and dropped the tough conditions that had held up discussions, making the reunion possible. Buoyed by the increase in vote share – from 9.63% in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls to 18.56% in 2024 – the state BJP was of the view that the party should have a claim to the CM post. But Shah intervened to put forward a more feasible proposal, according to a BJP leader familiar with the developments. Sources said the idea of an alliance came up after the BJP’s internal surveys indicated that individually both the BJP and the Akalis could win around a dozen seats each, but if they came together it could be an electoral combination that would give people the confidence to trust it as an alternative. The BJP team led by Satish Poonia, party national general secretary in charge of Punjab, had conducted several rounds of surveys and explored various combinations before finalising the BJP’s strategy, sources said. At the very top, Modi “made an earnest attempt to change the BJP’s approach”. Since the party had failed to establish itself as a choice for voters, it began to consider an alliance with the Akalis who had been affected by breakaway groups, the Akal Takht’s edicts, and the rise of Panthic movements in the state. Leaders working on the ground credited Shah’s multiple meetings with Badal for the rebirth of the alliance. “Over a month ago, a survey showed surprising findings. If an election was held then, most votes would have been polled by the AAP. However, it was clear from the poll that if the Akalis and the BJP came together, people would see them as a winning combination, and it could gather anti-incumbency votes. Neither was a viable option individually and the anti-incumbency votes could go back to the AAP. An alliance creates a winning alternative in the minds of voters,”a BJP leader said. “The question of who will lead the government was a stumbling block. The Home Minister’s intervention eased it out. The BJP leadership was clear that Punjab should not go back to the AAP and the anti-incumbency votes should not go to the Congress,” the leader said. Sources said at least two breakaway groups of the SAD were willing to join the alliance if the BJP and Akalis were to fight the elections together.

headline: Riddhima Kapoor Sahni thanks Upasana Konidela for introducing her to ragi: ‘Feel more fitter’
content: Riddhima Kapoor Sahni recently thanked Upasana Konidela for introducing her to ragi, or finger millet. "Thank you, Upasana, for introducing me to ragi, and I am eating ragi every day after that. Very healthy. I feel stronger, more energetic, and fitter," Kapoor said during a conversation with Curly Tales. Her mother and actor Neetu Kapoor added, "Ragi is one of the best". Ragi, also known as finger millet or nachni, is one of India's traditional millets and is gaining popularity as a nutritious alternative to refined cereal-based foods. "Its versatility makes it easy to incorporate into everyday meals through preparations such as chillas, dosas, rotis, porridges and pancakes," shared consultant dietitian Garima Goyal. DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. From a nutritional perspective, one of the biggest advantages of ragi is its calcium content. "It is naturally rich in calcium compared with most other commonly consumed cereals, making it a useful addition to diets that support bone health. Calcium is essential for maintaining bone mineral density, muscle contraction and nerve function. However, ragi alone cannot fulfil calcium requirements, and its calcium bioavailability can be influenced by antinutritional compounds such as phytates and oxalates," said Goyal. Ragi also provides dietary fibre, which supports digestive health, promotes satiety and can help regulate post-meal blood glucose responses. "Its fibre content makes it a useful ingredient for individuals looking to improve overall dietary quality and manage hunger. However, the glycaemic response of a ragi-based preparation depends on the quantity consumed, processing method and other ingredients used in the meal. Ragi is still a carbohydrate-rich food, so portion control remains important, particularly for people with diabetes," mentioned Goyal. Another nutritional advantage is its polyphenol content. "These naturally occurring plant compounds have antioxidant properties and may help protect cells against oxidative stress. Ragi also provides iron, magnesium and some B-group vitamins, although its protein content and amino acid profile mean it should ideally be combined with other protein sources," Goyal said. A ragi chilla can be made more nutritionally balanced by adding vegetables such as spinach, carrots, onions and capsicum. "Incorporating curd, paneer, besan or moong dal can further improve its protein content and make it a more complete meal. Adding seeds such as sesame can also contribute healthy fats and minerals," said Goyal. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kahaniyaan RasoiSe (@kahaniyaanrasoise.official) At the same time, Goyal remarked that it is important to remember that millets are not automatically superior to all other grains. "Wheat, rice, oats and other cereals can also form part of a healthy diet. The key is dietary variety, appropriate portions and minimal dependence on refined and highly processed foods," said Goyal. headline: Iffco Tokio readies new health product as it widens bets beyond motor insurance
content: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd plans to launch a new health product early next year as the company widens its bets beyond motor insurance under Tatsuya Fujimoto, its first Japanese managing director and chief executive officer. “We see opportunities across multiple health segments, with retail health being an important focus," Fujimoto said. Fujimoto said the product is almost ready. He described it as a comprehensive plan for individuals and families that will offer wider protection and more flexibility than a basic cover. “It is, however, not intended to be a disease-specific or standalone OPD product," Fujimoto said, referring to policies that cover only one illness or only outpatient expenses such as doctor visits and tests. "We are not putting out a premium target at this stage." He said health is a key growth area for the insurer, and it will focus on building new products rather than reworking its older health policies.

headline: As BJP, Akali Dal reunite for Punjab elections, a look at their past battles
content: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are back into an alliance in Punjab at a time when both parties, struggling in state politics for years, need each other’s support to revive their fortunes in the Assembly polls due in February 2027. The two allies drifted apart in 2020, when the SAD left the NDA in protest against the three central farm laws, which were repealed by the Narendra Modi government later following a year-long agitation by farmers on the Delhi border. The two parties complemented each other till they were allies from 1997 to 2020, with the SAD enjoying a rural base among Sikhs, centred on the support of the dominant Jat Sikh community, and the BJP having influence among urban Hindus, particularly traders. Their alliance also played a significant social role in the 1990s – it was seen as a bridge between Sikhs and Hindus after the Khalistan militancy period, which had made the Hindu minority in Punjab insecure. Past performances In the 1997 Punjab Assembly elections, when the SAD and the BJP came together for the first time, their alliance reaped rich dividends. Out of the state's 117 seats, the SAD bagged 75 of the 92 seats it contested, with 37.64% vote share, and the BJP won 18 of the 22 seats it fought with 8.33% votes. The then SAD head Parkash Singh Badal became the chief minister, with his party backing the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led central government that came to power in 1998. In the 2002 elections, the Congress wrested Punjab from the NDA, winning 62 of the 105 seats it contested. The SAD won 41 of the 92 seats it fought, securing 31% votes, with the BJP getting three of the 23 seats it contested, with a vote share of 5.67%. The alliance stayed intact despite the loss. In 2007, the NDA bounced back. While the SAD bagged 49 of the 93 seats it contested with 37% vote share, the BJP won 19 of the 23 seats it fought, with 8.28% votes. The NDA returned to power in 2012, with the SAD winning 56 of its 94 seats, garnering 34.73% vote share, and the BJP getting 12 of its 23 seats with 7.18% votes. In 2017, the decade-long “anti-incumbency” led to the NDA's loss to the Congress. The SAD could then win just 15 of its 94 seats with a 25.42% vote share, and the BJP got three of its 23, with 5.4% vote share. The 2015 sacrilege cases dealt a blow to the incumbent SAD-BJP, as the Congress, then led by Captain Amarinder Singh, managed to create a perception that the government did not do enough to assuage Sikhs' hurt sentiments. The sacrilege incidents, particularly the Bargari case, followed by police firing at Kotkapura and Behbal Kalan, damaged the Akali Dal’s credibility. The issue has continued to haunt the party. In the 2017 polls, the Congress won 77 seats with 38.77% votes. The elections also saw the rise of a new player, the Arvind Kejriwal-led AAP, which won 20 seats with 23.88% votes to emerge as the principal Opposition party. In September 2020, the SAD-BJP alliance collapsed amid the farmers' stir against the controversial farm laws. Days after Harmimrat Kaur Badal, wife of SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, resigned from the Modi ministry in protest against these laws, the SAD pulled out of the NDA. Farm laws As Punjab's farmers launched their movement against the farm laws, the SAD took the brunt despite breaking up with the NDA as it was seen as a long-standing ally of the BJP. PM Modi's announcement about the farm laws' withdrawal in November 2021 did not help the party, whose past association with the BJP, along with the sacrilege cases, led to a severe erosion in its support base. In 2022, the AAP won 92 seats against the Congress's 18. The SAD was reduced to just three seats and 18.38% votes. The BJP got two seats with 6.6% votes, even though the party contested 73 seats this time. The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also highlighted the challenges facing the two parties. Although there was a buzz about their tie-up, any formal negotiations between them failed to materialise. The then farmers' protests on the Punjab-Haryana borders and seat-sharing differences reportedly proved to be obstacles. The results were disappointing for both parties. The SAD managed to win only the Bathinda seat with Harsimrat Kaur Badal retaining her constituency. Ten of its 13 candidates forfeited their security deposits. Its vote share fell to 13.42% from 27.45% in 2019. The BJP, which had won two seats in the 2019 parliamentary polls as the SAD's partner and had secured 9.63% votes while contesting three seats, failed to win any seat in 2024 despite contesting all 13 seats. Its vote share, however, increased to 18.56%, although five of its candidates forfeited their security deposits. 2027 roadmap The 2027 poll situation seems to be substantially different from the past elections. After snapping its ties with the BJP in 2020, the Akali Dal's political troubles further weakened its standing. Of its three MLAs elected in 2022, only one currently remains with the party, with one each having defected to the AAP and the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) led by jailed MP and radical preacher Amritpal Singh. Their alliance this time could however help both parties and improve their performance, even as their seat-sharing deal has yet to be worked out. The BJP is looking to get a significantly higher number of seats from its senior ally than in their previous pacts, even as both parties brace for a formidable challenge in what would be a multi-cornered battle.

headline: Bid 'responsibly': RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain to Gsec market makers
content: Primary dealers need to step up efforts to deepen liquidity in the secondary market for government bonds where a few securities dominate trading volumes, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Rohit Jain said on Tuesday, adding that dealers must price their bids “responsibly” and in line with prevailing market conditions while underwriting government bond auctions. Trading in the top five government securities (G-Secs) accounted for 72 per cent of volumes over the past 12 months, with select maturities seeing the most trading, particularly the 10-year benchmark bond, Jain noted, emphasising that this poses challenges for the Centre and States’ borrowing programmes. “The borrowing requirements of the Centre and states have steadily increased, making even a small rise in yields significant for the government’s interest burden,” Jain noted. Flagging the implications of recent geopolitical developments on the cost and stability of government borrowing, Jain also stressed that the institutional capacity to absorb longer-tenor issuances remains “relatively limited” and there is a structural reduction in the demand for government securities. Commercial banks accounted for 35 per cent of total government securities holdings at the end of March 2026, making them the largest holders, followed by insurance companies and provident funds. While insurers and pension funds have historically been the most consistent buyers of longer-dated government securities, demand from them as well as banks for long-term sovereign debt has marginally declined, with the former shifting towards greater equity exposure. “Asset managers and other investors are also becoming more selective about duration, liquidity and mark-to-market risks. In an uncertain interest-rate environment, this could make it more challenging to issue longer-dated government securities at attractive yields,” Jain remarked. A resilient G-sec market would require credible fiscal and debt-management policies, a transparent and predictable auction calendar, deeper secondary market liquidity and broader participation from long-term institutional investors, he stressed in an address to the Primary Dealers’ Association of India (PDAI) in Mumbai. Jain said underwriting auction prices had, on a few occasions, been volatile and not in line with market-relevant levels, even when market conditions improved and were orderly. He urged primary dealers (PDs) to bid responsibly and make greater efforts to ensure the success of both underwriting and main auctions. “PDs are urged to place bids in underwriting auctions responsibly, having regard to prevailing market conditions,” he said. For context, PDs account for around 60 per cent of turnover in dated central government securities, 45 per cent in treasury bills and about 50 per cent in state government securities – in the secondary market. They have exclusive access to underwriting auctions for dated central government securities. Such auctions involve them bidding for the right to underwrite a portion of the government bond issue before the main auction – so that borrowing plans go through even when investor demand is weak. A failed auction can disrupt the market or elevate borrowing costs, and the underwriters act as a backstop for such scenarios. In return, PDs quote a commission or underwriting fees — a charge for taking on this risk — and those quotes are generally viewed by the market as an indication of prevailing conditions that may influence the government’s borrowing costs. Jain noted that there had been no devolvement of such auctions, in the recent past. PDs’ subscription in primary auctions of central government securities, as a share of notified amounts, declined from 65 per cent in FY25 to 54 per cent in FY26, before rising to 58 per cent in the first half of FY27. Their average participation in state government securities auctions also fell to 41 per cent from 45 per cent over the previous two years. Participation in treasury bill auctions remained between 73 per cent and 76 per cent. There are 21 primary dealers in the country, comprising seven standalone PDs and 14 bank-owned PDs. On secondary market liquidity, the Deputy Governor said securities with maturities of up to five years and those above 15 years accounted for only around 7 per cent each of trading in the first half of 2026-27 (FY27). State government securities accounted for just 5 per cent of secondary market turnover during the period, despite an increase in state borrowing and the introduction of the Benchmark Issuance Strategy. While reducing the frequency of benchmark issuances and increasing the volume of each auction have helped improve liquidity, trading activity remains low compared with other countries. Jain said PDs could help deepen the market by stepping up market-making activities, particularly by providing two-way quotes in off-the-run securities. Jain also called for greater retail participation in the government securities market. Since the launch of the Retail Direct Market Making Scheme in November 2021, PDs have executed trades worth Rs 8,438 crore with Retail Direct gilt account holders up to October 2026, a figure he described as modest. He urged PDs to conduct awareness campaigns to educate retail investors about government securities and develop products suited to their needs, including shorter-tenor STRIPs, which are relatively less complex. On the foreign exchange market, Jain said standalone primary dealers (SPDs) were permitted to offer all foreign exchange market-making facilities available to Category-I authorised dealers, subject to prudential guidelines. However, initial uptake had been slow, and SPDs needed to accelerate the development of the required infrastructure, risk management systems and skills to participate actively in the market. A narrow market 72% of secondary-market trading over the past year was concentrated in the top 5 traded Gsecs, led by 10-year bondsState Gsecs’ share in trading in H1FY27 was 5%, despite a rise in state’s borrowings

headline: Parag Milk Foods opens 53,837 sq ft distribution hub in Bhiwandi to support expansion
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) Parag Milk Foods Ltd on Tuesday said it has set up a new distribution hub in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, to support its growing business and product range. The facility spans 53,837 square feet and can store 2,700 pallets, equivalent to about 1,100 tonnes or 110,000 cases. It can handle up to 240 tonnes, or 24,000 cases, a day, the company said in a statement. Bhiwandi is one of Maharashtra’s main warehousing and logistics centres. The hub will serve Mumbai city and its suburbs, Navi Mumbai, the wider Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Vasai-Virar, Palghar, Alibaug, Jawhar, Raigad and Panvel. It will distribute the company’s Gowardhan, Go and Avvatar brands. The company said distribution of its ‘Pride of Cows’ brand through the facility was subject to confirmation. “As our business continues to evolve, building the right infrastructure and capabilities becomes as important as building our brands and product portfolio,” said Anirban Roy, general manager for supply chain and procurement.

headline: Jagan accuses Andhra government of bulldozing centuries-old Anjaneya temple | India News
content: YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the N Chandrababu Naidu-led Andhra Pradesh government of bulldozing a centuries-old Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple at Anjaneyapuram in Tirupati district, wondering if this is how the coalition government is protecting the 'Santana Dharma'.Calling it an assault on the faith of crores of devotees, the former CM alleged that the TDP-led NDA government is bulldozing the heritage site."Hey Ram! Save Temples! Save Andhra Pradesh! The Saga continues in Chandrababu Naidu garu's regime! Bulldozers tearing down the centuries-old Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple at Anjaneyapuram, an assault on the faith of crores of devotees, are truly disturbing," said Jagan in a post on X late on Monday. Also Read | Lord Hanuman idol at historic temple in Hyderabad vandalised, incident sparks outrageAccording to the opposition leader, sacred structures continue to be allegedly destroyed without exploring any alternative in the southern state, "From Tirumala's historic thousand-pillared mandapam to demolishing 40 temples in Vijayawada during the Krishna Pushkaralu (during erstwhile TDP govt) and the demolition at Kasinayana Jyothi Kshetram in Badvel."While the previous YSRCP government established the SRIVANI Trust to build and restore temples across the country, Chandrababu garu administration is bulldozing heritage sites, he claimed.Is this how your government defines protecting 'Sanatana Dharma', asked Jagan, sharing a video in which the temple was being bulldozed.Former TTD chairman and senior YSRCP leader B Karunakar Reddy visited the temple and strongly condemned the demolition of the ancient Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple at Anjaneyapuram in Renigunta mandal for the expansion of National Highway 716, questioning the Naidu government's commitment to protecting the religion.Also Read | No consensus between Andhra, Telangana over distribution of water in Krishna riverIn a video statement, Karunakar Reddy claimed that the coalition government deliberately demolished the centuries-old temple despite having the "option to modify the highway alignment," said a YSRCP press release.He questioned whether this was Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan's idea of protecting the Hindu religion.Highlighting the temple's spiritual significance, he said the deity was believed to be "Swayambhu" and associated with Lopamudra, wife of sage Agastya.He recalled that Annamacharya praised the deity in his compositions and that Pallava rulers constructed the temple's gopuram and sacred tank around 1,400 years ago.Karunakar Reddy described the demolition using JCBs, allegedly without Vedic priests supervising the process, as an act of "sacrilege".He recalled that colonial British authorities had established Anjaneyapuram railway station near Mamandur in recognition of the temple's significance.The YSRCP leader further alleged that the highway alignment was altered to protect the properties of wealthy investors near Karakambadi, while the historic temple was "sacrificed.""Months-long talks were held over shifting the temple for national highway construction. A decision was made with everybody's consent to construct another temple at a different place with the same idols," a government source told PTI.Also Read | Andhra Pradesh: 17.1% of ASDD electors get enumeration forms for re-enrolmentWith the agreement of the locals, villagers, devotees, priests, and Endowments Department officials, it was decided to install the idols at a different place, it said.Two days ago, priests and officials temporarily shifted the main idol after conducting the necessary rituals to a nearby plot given by the government.The government acquired 10 cents of the temple land for the construction of the highway and deposited ₹59 lakh in return for a new temple and land, said the source.On August 1, ₹59.3 lakh was deposited into the temple executive officer's account, and 50 cents of land was allocated nearby for the construction of the new temple, it said.

headline: 4G camera traps help nab two with loaded guns in Himachal reserve forest
content: 4G-enabled camera traps installed in the Paonta Sahib reserve forest area in Sirmaur district helped forest officials apprehend two persons, including a juvenile, allegedly carrying loaded guns and equipment used for laying traps inside the forest on Sunday night, officials said on Monday. The 4G cameras were installed in Paonta Sahib forest when a tigress was spotted in June this year. The two suspects, Dinesh Kumar, 36, a resident of Sarah village, and his juvenile nephew, were apprehended following an alert generated by images transmitted in real time by the camera trap. The forest department subsequently registered an FIR against them under various provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The suspect, Dinesh Kumar, works as a security guard with Indian Institute of Management (IIM) at Dhaula Kuan in Sirmaur. The 4G-enabled camera traps are equipped with cellular connectivity, allowing them to transmit photographs directly to the designated forest officials’ mobile devices as soon as any movement is detected. Unlike conventional camera traps, which store images for subsequent retrieval, the 4G technology enables officials to receive live photographic alerts remotely, helping them monitor sensitive forest areas and respond promptly to suspicious activities. Additional Conservator of Forests (ACF), Paonta Sahib, Aditya Sharma, told The Indian Express that the 4G cameras were installed in Paonta Sahib forest when a tigress was spotted in June this year. “Yesterday, we received two pictures from one camera trap installed in Sarah forest beat in the reserve forest. First picture was received around 4.19 pm showing two men carrying guns and bags passed nearby the camera. Around 5.27 pm, again a picture was received showing the same people passing the same location. An alert was sounded and three teams were constituted. Two suspects were apprehended with guns, which were found to be single-barrel muzzle-loading guns, and bags around 10.15 pm near the forest,” Sharma added. The operation was conducted by three teams constituted following the receipt of the photographs. The teams were formed under the supervision of Range Officer Surinder Singh and comprised nine forest department personnel, including Forest Guards Vijay Kumar, Ranbir Singh and Kailash, among others. Sources said that the bags, which were found in the possession of suspects, were full of gunpowder and clutch wires (used for lying traps). The forest department personnel also seized the cell phone of Dinesh Kumar as certain pictures showed the suspect with the carcasses of wild boars were found stored in the phone. The phone will be sent for forensic examination. The photographs stored in the mobile phone are likely to form a key part of the investigation, as the forest department intends to ascertain whether the suspects were involved in illegal hunting of wild animals or laying traps in the reserve forest area. “The juvenile has been handed over to his parents after completing the legal formalities while suspect Dinesh Kumar was produced in a local court at Paonta Sahib on Monday. He was released on bail,” a senior forest department officer said. As the firearms were seized from the suspects, a separate complaint was to be lodged with the local police, the officer added. Meanwhile, the apprehension of the two suspects reportedly triggered objections from some local villagers and their family members, who questioned the forest department’s action. Sources said the family members claimed that the single-barrel guns were licensed and were being carried for crop protection. However, the relevant licence documents had not been produced before the forest officials at the time of the apprehension. An FIR has been registered under Sections 9, 52, 2(16) and 2(35) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The forest department is also preparing to lodge a separate complaint with the local police in connection with the recovery of the firearms. The 4G-enabled camera traps, initially installed following the reported sighting of a tigress, believed to have come from the nearby Rajaji National Park in Uttarakhand in June.

headline: Lung health beyond smoking: The everyday risks we often overlook
content: Ask most people what damages the lungs, and smoking is the answer almost every time. Fair enough. It's the biggest single cause, and nobody should stop saying so. But it's also the only cause most people can name, which is where the trouble starts. A lot of lung damage builds up quietly, from things nobody thinks to mention at a check-up, because they don't come in a packet with a warning label on it.(Author: Bilal Thangal T M, Medical Lead, NURA - AI Health Screening Center)Most Indian cities sit well above what the World Health Organization considers a safe level of particulate matter in the air, and this isn't some rare, localised problem. Most of the world's population lives with air that fails that same benchmark. You don't choose to breathe city air the way you choose to light a cigarette. It's simply there every time you step outside, and it adds up whether you notice it or not.Somebody who spends two hours a day stuck in traffic is taking in a fair amount of this without realising it. The effects tend to show up a decade or more later, by which point nobody thinks to connect a cough to a daily commute from years ago.Occupational exposure gets far less attention than air pollution does, even though it can be just as damaging. Someone spraying pesticide on a farm, working a textile mill floor, or welding in a poorly ventilated workshop is not a smoker by any definition, yet may end up with lungs that look a lot like a smoker's. Part of the reason this goes unnoticed is that a routine consultation rarely asks what a patient actually does for a living. Smoking history gets asked about as a matter of habit. Occupational history mostly doesn't, even though it deserves the same weight.A poorly ventilated kitchen with a wood or coal stove can expose whoever is cooking, usually a woman, to smoke levels that rival standing on a busy street. Damp walls, mould, and a family member who smokes indoors only make this worse. It's entirely possible for the air inside a home to be dirtier than the air outside it.Second-hand smoke is easy to dismiss because the person affected never lit a cigarette themselves. A child who grows up in a house where someone smokes still carries years of that exposure in their lungs, even though they never made the choice to smoke at all.Pneumonia in childhood or a treated case of tuberculosis rarely just disappears once the acute illness is over. Lungs that have already been through an infection tend to be a little less resilient afterward, more prone to complications down the line. This matters more in places where healthcare access is uneven and the air was already working against people to begin with, though it's a connection that rarely comes up outside a specialist's office.None of this is an argument against taking smoking seriously. It remains the single most preventable cause of lung disease, full stop. But more people who have never touched a cigarette are showing up with conditions that catch them off guard, and that alone says something about how narrow the smoking-only story has become.Treating lung health as something shaped by an entire environment, rather than one habit, is simply more useful. That means paying attention on bad pollution days, using proper protection at work where the job calls for it, keeping homes ventilated, and getting checked rather than waiting out a cough that refuses to go away. Periodic lung screening, regardless of smoking history, remains one of the few tools that can catch trouble early. Tobacco has anchored this conversation for a long time, understandably so, but it's overdue for a wider lens.

headline: AI infrastructure spending set to jump 53% to $2.4 trn in 2027: Gartner
content: Global spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is expected to rise 53 per cent to $2.4 trillion in 2027, accounting for nearly 59 per cent of total worldwide AI spending, according to a forecast by the technology research and advisory firm Gartner. Total global spending on AI is projected to reach $4.05 trillion in 2027, up 47.5 per cent from $2.75 trillion in 2026, according to Gartner's estimates. Infrastructure spending is expected to remain the largest component of this expenditure. Where will the spending be done? Gartner's forecast puts spending on AI infrastructure at $2.397 trillion in 2027, compared with $1.563 trillion in 2026. According to the forecast, infrastructure alone will account for more than half of the anticipated increase in global AI spending over the period. The biggest contributor within infrastructure will be AI-optimised servers, with spending on these systems expected to increase about 81 per cent from $527.6 billion in 2026 to $957.2 billion in 2027. The increase is being driven by continued infrastructure expansion by hyperscalers, or large cloud computing providers, and newer specialised cloud infrastructure companies known as neocloud providers. Gartner also pointed to rising prices of AI-optimised servers, partly reflecting what it described as 'memflation', or inflation in memory component prices. "Faster than anticipated expansion of user requirements into scaling up inference workloads, coupled with increasingly compute-intensive training workloads, continues to increase spending on AI infrastructure globally," said John-David Lovelock, distinguished vice-president analyst and chief of research at Gartner. Inference refers to the process of running a trained AI model to generate responses, predictions or other outputs. As businesses deploy AI applications at scale, these workloads require computing capacity on an ongoing basis, adding to demand beyond the resources needed to train models. Gartner also expects worldwide spending on AI software to grow 42 per cent to $649 billion in 2027, from $458 billion in 2026. Spending on AI services is expected to increase 29.5 per cent to $746 billion from $576 billion. According to Gartner, organisations were increasing software expenditure as vendors incorporated AI capabilities into existing products and developed platforms to manage and govern AI across businesses. AI cybersecurity spending is forecast to increase 69 per cent to $86 billion in 2027, from $51 billion in 2026. Spending on AI agents and assistants is expected to more than double to $67 billion from $30 billion. Foundation models retain dominance Gartner expects the generative AI model market to grow 82 per cent to $51 billion in 2027, from $28 billion in 2026. Foundation models are forecast to account for 81 per cent of this spending, despite faster growth in specialised and domain-specific models. Spending on the latter is projected to increase 99 per cent in 2027, according to Gartner. Foundation models are large AI models trained on extensive datasets that can be adapted for a range of tasks. Domain-specific models, by contrast, are designed or adapted for particular industries or applications, where specialised knowledge and accuracy are important. Lovelock said foundation models would continue to provide the core intelligence for a growing ecosystem of AI agents, industry-specific models and enterprise applications.

headline: 80 passengers escape unhurt as bus plunges into trench on UP’s Ganga Expressway
content: Around 80 passengers travelling from Haryana’s Panipat to Bihar had a close shave on Tuesday morning after their bus fell into a trench between the two carriageways of the Ganga Expressway here, police said.The accident occurred near Hadha-Malikpur village when the speeding bus apparently went out of control, broke through a roadside railing and plunged into the trench, police said.“All passengers were safe, and no one sustained serious injuries,” Shahabad Circle Officer Santosh Singh said.The police said around 80 passengers were on board the bus, which also has a sleeper facility, even as some eyewitnesses estimated the number to be higher.Singh said that following information about the accident, Dial 112 police personnel reached the spot, along with a team of the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA).The UPEIDA team used a crane to pull the damaged bus out of the trench. It was subsequently taken to the toll plaza control room, the officer said.

headline: Person filled with hatred towards country won't be accepted by people: BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi
content: New Delhi: The BJP on Tuesday slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks against the Indian economy and electoral system during foreign visits, saying he may try to relaunch his political career from foreign soil but would never be accepted by the people of the country. .As several BJP leaders offered prayers at gurudwaras and performed community service on the occasion of Parkash Purab, they also pledged to work towards making the country, particularly Punjab, drug-free and hit out at opposition parties for allegedly failing to do enough to tackle the menace. .The birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev is being observed on Tuesday. .After offering prayers along with other BJP leaders at a gurudwara, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari told reporters that this pious occasion should also be used to pledge to make Punjab and the entire country free of drugs. .He further said the Lowy Institute's Asia Power Index had stated that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership, India had emerged as one of Asia's leading powers. ."Goldman Sachs and the IMF have also described India as the fastest-growing major economy," he said. .Taking a swipe at Gandhi, Bhandari said, "He may make every effort to relaunch his political career from foreign soil, but a person whose every fibre is filled with hatred towards the country will never be accepted by its people." .'You advocate for votes of infiltrators': BJP chief Nabin slams Rahul Gandhi over SIR allegations."That is why the people of India will not accept Rahul Gandhi," he added. .India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China's, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric. .The report said India has consolidated its position as the third-most powerful country and a "major powerhouse" in Asia, with Prime Minister Modi rated as the second-most effective regional leader. .According to the Index, the US and China are "superpowers in Asia for 2026", with the US' score being the highest, at 78.9. .Gandhi had triggered a political row with his remarks on India's economy during an address at Columbia University in the US. .India is sitting on an "economic disaster" with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in its education system, Gandhi said, warning that the country risks getting into serious trouble if it continues on the current economic path. .Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University last week, Gandhi said India's economic model "stopped giving results almost a decade ago" and criticised the government's initiatives such as 'Make in India' and 'Start-up India', claiming they had failed to revive the country's "broken" economic
