headline: E20 Petrol Row: Karnataka Seeks Transparency in Ethanol Blending
content: Ethanol Blending Controversy The ongoing tussle between the Karnataka government and oil marketing companies (OMCs) over the exact quantum of ethanol being blended in petrol is the latest chapter in the crucial debate over E20 fuel (a blended fuel containing 80 per cent petrol and 20 per cent ethanol). https://frontline.thehindu.com/news/ethanol-blending-e20-petrol-karnataka-oil-companies-controversy/article71689181.ece A controversy erupted on November 6, when Karnataka’s Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad claimed that 11 of the 14 samples tested at a lab certified by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) and the International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO) exceeded the stipulated 20 per cent ethanol level, with one sample even containing as much as 31.2 per cent ethanol. https://frontline.thehindu.com/interviews/karnataka-probe-ethanol-e20-interview-minister-rizwan-arshad/article71697406.ece In response, Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) brushed off the claims, saying they were “not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures”. The OMCs alleged that the testing had been conducted at a third-party laboratory, and not one specified under the Control Order. They also claimed that the certificates did not provide the complete technical details necessary to independently verify the reported ethanol content. In a strong rebuttal on November 9, Arshad said that the State government had followed the IS 17021:2018 standard cited by the OMCs for testing ethanol content. He noted that the State government had provided 63 samples to the OMCs’ own laboratories and sought the percentage of ethanol blend in each sample. In an exclusive interview with Frontline, published on November 13, Arshad said that the OMCs did not give a “clear answer” on the issue of the percentage of ethanol blended for any of the 63 samples. He said: “That made us suspicious. What options were left with us? We had to collect more samples as per the law, [samples that were] also jointly collected by all three parties, duly signed in the proforma. The testing was conducted by an NABL-accredited third-party lab. The result was that ethanol up to 31.2 per cent was being blended.” While Congress leader Rahul Gandhi picked up the issue and questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi about the quantity of ethanol in petrol, the Congress-led UDF government in Keralam followed in Karnataka’s footsteps, ordering a similar investigation to ascertain the quantity of ethanol in petrol. Minister’s demands from Centre In his latest move, Arshad wrote to Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri on November 18, recollecting the recent developments, and placed five demands before him. They include displaying the actual percentage of ethanol blend in every petrol pump and bill, providing an option to choose between pure petrol, E10, and E20 until vehicles are fully compatible with higher blends, establishing a third-party mechanism to randomly test fuel quantity, and creating a dedicated fund to compensate consumers whose vehicles undergo damage due to usage of petrol with ethanol levels above the prescribed limits. Speaking to Frontline, Bhamy Shenoy, a petroleum industry veteran and founding-working president of Mysuru Grahakara Parishat, said that the ethanol level depended on the part of the tank from which the fuel was drawn. He said: “Since water and ethanol are heavier than petrol, they sink to the bottom. So, ethanol quantity at the top will be much lower, while it will have to be higher at the bottom. Since the nozzle goes to the bottom of the tank, samples need to be taken from the top, middle, and bottom to test ethanol content.” He added that the issue could be resolved only through neutral, third-party testing by reputed institutes such as the Indian Institute of Science or the Indian Institute of Technology. While allegations of over-blending act as the tipping point, the larger controversy revolves around whether E20 petrol is needed in its current form. The controversy began in 2025 itself, when widespread blending of 20 per cent ethanol in fuel began. The government faced outrage for having advanced its earlier plan of implementing E20 by 2030 by five years. Since vehicles compatible with E20 petrol were being produced only from 2023 onwards, concerns grew that earlier vehicles may face trouble, including mileage issues and increasing frequency of vehicular repair. (Vehicles produced from 2008 are E10 compliant, while those produced before 2008 are built for pure petrol.) In a press release on August 12, 2025, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas defended the 20 per cent blending of ethanol, saying it benefited the rural economy, eliminating sugar cane arrears and improving the viability of maize cultivation. “More income to farmers has not only contributed to furthering their well-being but has also helped decisively tackle the challenge of suicides by farmers. It may be recalled that in areas like Vidarbha, farmer’ suicides were widespread a few years ago,” the release said. In June 2026 there were complaints over a drop in vehicle efficiency that raised suspicions over the usage of E20 fuel. On July 28, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) wrote to the Union Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, raising concerns over E20 fuel. SIAM letter and retraction In a letter, which Frontline accessed, SIAM said: “SIAM members are observing huge increases in the issues in customer vehicle parts and replacement (like fuel injectors, duel pump, EGR valve, exhaust and parts that are in direct contact with fuel or engine emission gases). Investigations of field failure vehicle parts reveal the failure is due to corrosion or wear caused by high chloride presence which is traced to the fuel used. Deposits in failed parts also have shown presence of chlorides (sic).” Pointing out that chloride is “highly detrimental” to engine parts, SIAM explained that including chloride limits in fuel specifications and implementing quality control was imperative to avoid chloride-related failures in customer vehicles. However, SIAM retracted this move within a week and withdrew its earlier communication on August 4. In a public clarification, SIAM said: “The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has also instituted 3 ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into the petrol supply chain. All of these steps fully meet the needs of the automobile industry. Further, we understand from OMCs that checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets and after each instance of rain near petrol pumps.” It added: “There is no cause for concern arising from the matter reported as these issues have been routinely addressed over the past several decades between the auto industry and OMCs.” Critics accused the Central government of pressuring SIAM into withdrawing its earlier objections. On Instagram, the political analyst Tehseen Poonawalla accused the Central government of trying to “hide this letter” and attempting to take down everything from the Internet, including news reports about this letter. A major concern about the entire controversy of implementing the E20 policy five years ahead of schedule has been the lack of discussions, either in Parliament or in public forums. Industry opinion An oil industry veteran, who spoke to Frontline on the condition of anonymity, said that a major push for ethanol could result in a clash between the sugar, alcohol, and automobile industries. He said: “In principle, ethanol blending in petrol has been accepted, and Brazil is the global leader in this. While E20 has been mandated in India, there are allegations of extra mixing, resulting in the consumer getting a raw deal. We need a discussion between the affected parties on the pros and cons of this policy decision. If any side stands to suffer, they must be informed about it in advance.” Stating that there are concerns on side effects, potential engine issues, and extra wear and tear, the veteran sought a white paper on the entire issue. It is widely considered that biofuels are necessary at a time when oil is becoming more expensive and there are geopolitical risks in gaining access to it. The practice is also expected to lower emissions and support the agricultural sector. In fact, the ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme that was initiated in 2002-2003 by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led NDA government was subsequently expanded by the UPA government that succeeded it. The latest controversy revolves around the incompatibility of a majority of existing vehicles with E20 petrol and the need to develop physical infrastructure in petrol pumps to ensure proper supply of E20 fuel. “We are not against blending ethanol with petrol. However, engines should be able to digest ethanol-inclusive petrol. Petrol pumps must possess the required infrastructure to disburse such fuel,” Rizwan told Frontline. Shenoy argued that cellulosic ethanol, which is prepared from cornstalks, grasses, miscanthus, bamboo, or woodchips should be prioritised over corn ethanol. Gadkari under scanner Within the ruling NDA government, Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari of the BJP has arguably been the biggest ambassador of the current E20 policy. During the 14th Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Bioenergy Summit held on November 17, Gadkari batted for ethanol blending in fuel. In a post on X, the Minister said: “Addressed the 14th CII #Bioenergy Summit, highlighting how scaling bioenergy can drive cleaner energy, reduce fossil fuel dependence, boost farmer incomes, create rural jobs, and unlock value from agricultural waste.” During the KPMG ENRich 2026 Conference at New Delhi in November, the Minister announced the commercial launch of the 100 per cent ethanol powered Toyota Innova Hycross and urged major automobile manufacturers to adopt flex-fuel engines. However, critics have slammed Gadkari’s push for ethanol from a seat of power as a “conflict of interest”, pointing out that his children are top executives and major shareholders in companies producing ethanol. While his elder son Nikhil Gadkari is managing director of CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure Ltd, his younger son Sarang Gadkari is a director of Manas Agro Industries and Infrastructure Ltd. “Nitin Gadkariji was promoting ethanol and speaks more about ethanol than the Petroleum Minister himself. Let him propagate ethanol and its advantages. However, his own children are running ethanol-producing factories, and he as a Minister is promoting it. There is some sort of a conflict of interest here,” Rizwan told Frontline. Speaking to Frontline, Poonawalla said that ethanol is the “biggest scam” in India, adding that the huge number of ethanol distilleries in Karnataka and Maharashtra had contributed to the ongoing drought situation in both States. On the Centre’s claim that sugarcane farmers benefit from increased ethanol blending, Poonawalla said: “Sugarcane farmers didn’t get any money from ethanol. In fact, Karnataka’s sugarcane farmers are on the streets. By growing water-intensive sugarcane, they have harmed India’s food security. We are now importing more oil and pulses and even sugar, a commodity which India used to export. So, we are not saving foreign reserves.” Global ethanol blending trends Across the world, ethanol blending has been in vogue for decades. As many as 19 European Union countries, including France, Germany, Belgium, Denmark, Poland, the Czech Republic, and Estonia, and non-EU countries like the United Kingdom and Norway, have rolled out the E10 policy. However, the leading global practitioner of blending ethanol with fuel is Brazil. It began ethanol blending in 1931, mandating a minimum of 5 per cent blending, extendable up to 10 per cent. Following the oil crisis in 1973 that exposed Brazil’s vulnerability in the energy sector, the Proalcool policy was rolled out in 1975, ramping up the ethanol blending percentage to 20-22 per cent. Currently, Brazil uses E32 petrol (blending 32 per cent anhydrous ethanol with 68 per cent petrol). Alongside, it also supplies E100 (95 per cent ethanol and 5 per cent water) fuel. The policy has been successful as Brazil uses flex-fuel vehicles that can run on different types of fuel, which consumers decide based on a number of factors. In his letter to Puri, Rizwan also highlighted the concerns surrounding the quantity of petrol being dispensed at fuel stations. Of the 5,946 retail outlets in Karnataka, 805 were inspected, and 768 required recalibration. Of the 3,071 nozzles tested, 2,618 showed deviation from their rated accuracy. A total of 101 outlets were found dispensing beyond the maximum permissible error and were booked, and fines totalling Rs.6.66 lakh were collected. The Minister also took severe exception to Notification GSR 905(E) dated December 18, 2025, which doubles the mandatory verification interval for petrol and diesel dispensers from 12 months to 24 months, meaning that a faulty meter may now go unchecked for up to two full years. He said that the existing annual cycle itself was “barely adequate”. India’s ethanol drive is creating a new food security crisis India’s ethanol drive is creating a new food security crisis The E20 campaign is pushing farmers towards maize, which is more profitable for distilleries, taking land away from pulses and oilseeds. If the trend continues, it could worsen India’s food security challenges and increase dependence on imports. Policy Analysis India’s ethanol drive is creating a new food security crisis storyline 1 Ethanol blending: Who gains and who pays? Ethanol blending: Who gains and who pays? The new E20 policy transfers costs onto consumers by way of lower mileage and higher maintenance, while offering limited gains to farmers and strong incentives to ethanol distillers. headline: UGC, AICTE, NCTE Merger: Higher Education Bill Stuck As Parliamentary Panel Delays Report
content: The Centre’s proposed overhaul of India’s higher education regulatory system is facing uncertainty, with the parliamentary panel yet to finalise its report on the proposed Bill. The delay has raised questions over when the Bill will be taken up in Parliament and whether changes will be made to address concerns raised by state governments, political parties and educational institutions. The proposed legislation, called the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, seeks to replace three existing regulators — the University Grants Commission (UGC), the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) — with a single umbrella body. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for examination. The committee is chaired by BJP MP Daggubati Purandeswari. A meeting scheduled for July 20 to consider and adopt the draft report was cancelled, reported The New Indian Express. The panel has not met since September 30, leaving the legislation’s timeline uncertain ahead of Parliament’s Winter Session. What Are The Major Concerns? One of the major concerns surrounding the Bill is the extent of powers it proposes to give the Centre over the new regulator. According to the report, the proposed framework provides for a central commission supported by three councils dealing with regulation, academic standards and accreditation. However, provisions allowing the Centre to issue policy directions to the proposed bodies and dissolve or supersede the commission have raised questions about the regulator’s independence. The proposed legislation has also faced objections from some states, including Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Meghalaya. Concerns have also been raised about the division of powers between the Centre and states, as education falls under the Concurrent List of the Constitution. The Bill also brings Institutions of National Importance, including the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), National Institutes of Technology (NITs) and Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research (IISERs), within the proposed regulatory framework. The JPC’s draft recommendations include consulting such institutions before framing rules that could affect their autonomy. The Bill was listed for consideration during the Monsoon Session but did not move forward as expected. With the committee’s report still pending, it remains uncertain whether the legislation will be taken up during the Winter Session.

headline: Central government pensioners must submit Annual Life Certificate by 30 November: Know six ways to complete process
content: Central Government pensioners must submit their Annual Life Certificate (ALC) by 30 November every year to ensure the continued disbursement of their pension, with the certificate serving as proof of their continued eligibility.In an Office Memorandum dated 26 October, the Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare, under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, outlined six modes of submission to streamline the process for pensioners.Central Government pensioners are required to submit their Annual Life Certificate every November to ensure the continued disbursement of their pension. However, pensioners aged 80 and above can submit their certificates starting 1 October each year, rather than waiting until November.How can pensioners submit their Annual Life Certificate?The government has listed six options by which pensioners can submit their life certificates, either manually or digitally, at their convenience.Physical submission at the bankPensioners can submit their life certificates in person by visiting their Pension Disbursing Authority (PDA), such as their bank branch, where the certificate will be recorded.Certificate signed by designated officialsPensioners do not need to appear in person before the Pension Disbursing Authority (PDA) if a designated official signs their Life Certificate form. In such cases, another person can submit the signed certificate on the pensioner's behalf.The authorized officials include magistrates, registrars and sub-registrars, gazetted government servants, police officers of at least Sub-Inspector rank, postmasters, eligible RBI and SBI officers, Justices of Peace, Block Development Officers, tehsildars, village panchayat heads, MPs, state legislators and Treasury Officers.Online submission through Jeevan Pramaan portalPensioners can generate and submit a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) through the Jeevan Pramaan portal using fingerprint authentication. They need to provide their Aadhaar number and pension-related details, including PPO number and bank account details, and authenticate their identity using a compatible, UIDAI-approved biometric device.Once authentication is successful, a unique acknowledgement number, called the Pramaan ID, is generated. The certificate is stored digitally and can be accessed by the pension-disbursing authority.Face authentication through smartphonePensioners can also submit their Digital Life Certificate via Aadhaar-based face authentication in the Jeevan Pramaan mobile application, without the need for a separate biometric device.To use this facility, they must first download the Aadhaar Face RD application by UIDAI from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store, followed by the Jeevan Pramaan application. They then need to enter their Aadhaar and pension details, verify their identity through OTP, and select the face scan option.The application captures their live photograph using the smartphone camera for Aadhaar-based authentication. Once verification is successful, the Digital Life Certificate is submitted online.Doorstep service through India Post Payments Bank (IPPB)Pensioners can request that a postman or Gramin Dak Sevak visit their homes to generate a Digital Life Certificate. IPPB uses its network of over 1.41 lakh access points and over 1.80 lakh postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks to provide this service.Pensioners can seek assistance or information about the service by emailing ‘contact@ippbonline.in’.Doorstep banking through PSB AllianceDoorstep Banking is also available through PSB Alliance, a network of public-sector banks that offer doorstep services to customers in major cities. Pensioners can use this facility to get their Life Certificates collected at home through a Doorstep Banking agent.They can book the service through the Doorstep Banking mobile app, the PSB Alliance website, or the toll-free number 9152220220.Disclaimer: This information is for informational purposes only. Please contact your bank for more updates.

headline: BJP and Akali Dal announce return of Punjab alliance after six years
content: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) announced the revival of their alliance in Punjab at a joint press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Tuesday, coinciding with the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the first Sikh Guru. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the alliance with Sukhbir Singh Badal's party, saying the NDA was complete after Akali joining the fold. BJP national president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal were also present at the press briefing. "Till December 31, I want to repeat, we will make Punjab drug-free…after three days of detailed discussions between BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal ji, a detailed roadmap has been made in this direction," Shah said at the briefing. "I have full confidence that the people of Punjab will bless this alliance which is under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi… We will surely make an NDA government in the state and bring the state back to its glory," he added. Sukhbir Singh Badal, while addressing the press conference, said the alliance was "not just a political but emotional alliance". He said the alliance has brought governments which brought communal peace and prosperity to Punjab. Sources in both parties indicated that an alliance announcement is likely to be made on the occasion. The two parties were alliance partners from November 1996 until September 2020, with the BJP as the junior partner contesting 23 of the 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD contested 94. However, on September 27, 2020, the SAD walked out of the alliance over the now-repealed three farm laws. Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal had also resigned from the Union Cabinet in protest against the laws. In the alliance, both had formed government in 1997, 2007 and 2012 in Punjab. Seat-sharing equation While most of the BJP's state leadership maintained that the party would contest the 2027 Assembly elections on its own, the SAD leadership had repeatedly hinted at an alliance, describing it as an emotional connect with the masses. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has indicated the possibility of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) returning to power in Punjab in 2027, first at a function in Delhi on October 27 and subsequently in Chandigarh on November 1. The SAD, led by Sukhbir Singh Badal, was part of the NDA during its earlier alliance with the BJP. The key question now is the seat-sharing arrangement between the two parties and how many constituencies each will contest. Interestingly, the parties have chosen Guru Nanak Dev's birth anniversary for the joint announcement, a move that could also convey a message of communal harmony and brotherhood. Earlier, on November 19, 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had chosen Guru Nanak Dev's birth anniversary to announce the repeal of the three farm laws, over which the SAD had walked out of the NDA.

headline: Why MBA education matters more than ever: IIM Bangalore professor makes the case for business schools | Hindustan Times
content: Every once in a while, someone comes along to announce the demise of MBA (or more broadly business school) education. The latest such salvo was fired by Chris Marquis, a professor at the University of Cambridge Judge Business School, where he makes a provocative case for abolishing traditional business schools.His central argument is that business school education provides students with a limited understanding of real-world mechanics, thereby privileging shareholders and corporate executives often at the expense of employees, communities and society. These are certainly important concerns. Business schools should reflect on the values they promote, the quality of their teaching, and the impact their graduates have on society. But the response to a perceived lacuna in today’s business leadership is not to shut business schools; on the contrary, I would argue that this makes the case for MBA education even stronger.Why global business education is becoming essential for future leaders?Growing up, I used to think engineering was hard and management was fluff. Engineering appeared to demand intellectual rigour, mathematical precision, and an understanding of the laws of physics, while management seemed to involve little more than common sense dressed up in fashionable terminology. Over time, I have come to appreciate how deeply flawed is this perception. The physical world operates within three spatial dimensions and is governed by well-established laws of physics. Engineering problems can be extraordinarily complex, but they are generally approached through scientific principles, mathematical models, and established processes. While there is considerable scope for innovation, the underlying physical laws remain intact.Business, on the other hand, operates in a far more unpredictable environment. It exists in a hyper-dimensional space involving products, processes, markets, capital, technology and, most importantly, people. Unlike physical systems, markets or human behaviour is neither predictable nor governed by immutable laws. Markets change, consumer preferences evolve, competitors respond, employees behave differently, and external events can fundamentally alter the business landscape overnight. Far from being fluff, management is an intellectually demanding discipline precisely because it continuously and simultaneously judged by both consumers and financial markets.‘Analytical thinking and adaptability are key’: BIT Mesra Registrar shares insights on changing education, future skills and career opportunitiesWhile professional degrees such as engineering, medicine, and law produce highly specialised individuals who develop considerable depth in their respective disciplines, business education plays a rather distinctive role. By teaching subjects spanning analytics, finance, marketing, operations, strategy, organisational design and human resources, business schools help students develop a 360-degree view of a business. The MBA is arguably the only professional degree specifically designed to equip students with the unique ability to look at a business from multiple perspectives, thereby elevating their capabilities and judgement to a plane that is inaccessible in a core discipline.As a professor of decision sciences, I work with students to develop a rigorous, data-driven approach to decision-making. I teach them to use analytical models, statistical reasoning, and optimisation techniques to make better decisions under uncertainty. Similarly, a strategy professor would introduce frameworks that enable students to understand a firm’s competitive positioning and identify opportunities for sustained advantage; or an organisational design faculty would explore the complexities of managing people, teams, and institutions. Every professor in an MBA classroom brings a particular lens or perspective through which students learn to examine distinct facets of a business problem.Breaking Subject Barriers: How NEP 2020 is giving students more academic choicesNone of these perspectives, in isolation, provides a complete picture. It is their combination that makes business education powerful. The objective is not to create specialists in every discipline but rather to develop individuals who can understand enough about each discipline to ask the right questions, appreciate competing viewpoints and make informed decisions. One of the most intriguing aspects of teaching at a business school is watching students gradually develop this ability to connect dots pertaining to seemingly unrelated contexts within a business.At the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, training an elite group of MBA students to become the next generation of business leaders and CEOs is an enormously rewarding experience. I see little difference in the importance of this responsibility compared with that of a medical school training the next generation of cardiac surgeons. Both institutions are entrusted with developing professionals who will eventually make decisions that have a profound impact on other people's lives. The consequences of poor leadership can be just as far-reaching as those of medical malpractice.The answer to the shortcomings of business leadership, therefore, cannot be to abandon the institutions that train business leaders. It must be to make those institutions better at preparing students for the responsibilities they will eventually shoulder. Marquis, in his New York Times article, is only partially right: Questioning whether business schools adequately emphasise the broader interests of all stakeholders in a business is a legitimate concern but this is an argument for a broader curriculum and not for dismantling business education!We are living through a period of extraordinary geopolitical uncertainty, with conflicts and tensions across geographical regions, economic inequality, technological disruption, climate challenges and profound shifts in the global balance of supply chains. Problems of this magnitude cannot be understood through a single disciplinary lens and education in silos is simply not the answer. We need graduates who can appreciate the different dimensions of a problem, understand the trade-offs involved, and develop nuanced responses. Business schools, with their inherently multidisciplinary approach, are uniquely positioned to nurture this capability.The argument for business school education becomes particularly relevant in the Indian context. India is at an important inflection point in its economic journey. With an economy expected to expand significantly over the next two decades, our country needs capable leaders to build and manage enterprises across manufacturing, technology, infrastructure, healthcare, financial services, and entrepreneurship. If anything, India and the world need more high-calibre managers who can think across disciplines, be nuanced in their approach to business, and lead complex organisational transformations. The case for furthering an MBA and business school education has indeed never been stronger; the Marquis article will soon be lost in the shadows with scant effect on the enduring allure of an MBA education!(The author Jitamitra Desai is a Professor of Operations Research in the Decision Sciences (DS) group at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore)

headline: Days before daughter’s wedding, farmer, son killed in cylinder blast at Greater Noida home
content: Just a week before his daughter’s wedding, a man and his son died in a gas cylinder blast at their home in Jewar village of Greater Noida on Monday. Two other family members were injured in the incident. According to ADCP Greater Noida Santosh Kumar, around 6:30 pm, a fire broke out at the house in Dayanatpur village under the jurisdiction of Jewar Police Station due to the gas leaking from a cylinder. "Veerpal (56) and his son Abhishek (24) died in the incident,” he added. While Veerpal was a farmer, his son worked as a graduate in D. Pharma and was working in a private company. Abhishek’s wife, Kajal, 22, and their two-year-old son, Aditya, are currently admitted in the hospital for treatment after sustaining burn injuries. However, police said that their condition is stable. Preparations were going on in the home as Veerpal’s daughter was set to get married December 2. “In the evening, Veerpal’s wife and their daughter were out in the market to shop for the marriage. A cooking gas cylinder was kept in a room of the house, Veerpal switched on the lights after he entered and it is suspected that he lit an incense stick which caught fire to the cylinder,” the officer said. In order to save his father, the man ran inside the room but he also got killed. While Kajal and her son were inside another room, they also ran after the sound of an explosion. “The fire spread like a wildfire and the blast generated huge pressure and the curtains of the house also caught fire which injured the mother and son while they tried to move,” the police officer said. Jewar MLA Dhirendra Singh visited the house later in the day. In a post on X, he wrote, “The untimely deaths of Shri Veerpal Singh, a resident of Dayanatpur village in my legislative assembly constituency and his son Abhishek Singh in a tragic accident caused by a gas cylinder leak are deeply heartbreaking. I immediately visited the scene, met with the grieving family, expressed my condolences and offered them comfort. May God grant the departed souls a place at His divine feet and give their family members the strength to bear this immense grief.”

headline: How Nvidia Became So Big And Critical To The US Economy That Trump Stepped In To Bring Jensen Huang Back
content: In a stunning turn of events, Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following reported pressure from President Donald Trump. Huang had resigned on November 12 after revelations of his extramarital affair involving a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who was alleged to have spied for China. Nvidia said in a statement on November 23 that, based on input from the US government, the board was confident that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk” — a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

headline: CM Vijay’s popularity is intact, but his government in Tamil Nadu is facing a political storm
content: C Joseph Vijay, as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has entered the sixth month of a non-Dravidian government in the state. The six-month-old Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government is caught in a series of controversies, with political volcanoes erupting around it. On crucial issues, Vijay often goes into a dim mode. One such controversy involves allegations that TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh, who represents Kallakurichi, sent obscene WhatsApp messages to district collector JE Padmaja and visiting her residence while intoxicated. The MLA has denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. Vijay is gifted with a cool, quiet personality. Even when provoked, his reactions are rarely provocative. His first crisis was establishing a majority in the Assembly. He managed it through a live telecast of the Assembly proceedings, a bold decision. However, he continues to head a minority government, and allegations of horse-trading remain a constant challenge. Vijay faced this crisis with considerable courage. Yet, he has also committed several political missteps in his first six months in office.

headline: Sheikh Hasina fixes Dec 16 for return home, Dhaka says arrest awaits her
content: More than three months after she declared that she planned to return to her home country, ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced Tuesday a date for her return: December 16. Observed as Victory Day, it marks the end of the 1971 Liberation War when Pakistani Armed Forces in then-East Pakistan surrendered to the joint command of Indian Armed Forces and the Mukti Bahini. She asked the Bangladesh government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to send an aircraft to Delhi for her return to Dhaka. She faces a death sentence in Bangladesh. Hasina’s spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali, in a statement, said, “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka.” “Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th,” he said. Responding to this, Bangladesh Minister of State for Foreign Affairs-1 Humaiun Kobir said, “She (Hasina) can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.” “A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen,” Kobir was quoted saying by the state-run BSS news agency. Shama Obaed Islam, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs-2, said the government will treat Hasina in accordance with the same laws applicable to any other convicted fugitive staying abroad, the BSS reported. “The position of the Bangladesh government regarding Sheikh Hasina is the same as its position, under Bangladeshi law, regarding any other convicted person who has fled abroad,” she said, adding that Hasina will be arrested wherever she enters Bangladeshi territory. Zahed Ur Rahman, Information and Broadcasting Advisor to the Prime Minister, said, “Whether Sheikh Hasina will come or not is not a matter to be discussed with her. The discussion will be with India.” “A serious criminal is in India along with her associates. She has been convicted. So, whether she will come or not, whether she will travel on Biman Bangladesh Airlines or their aircraft, or come on foot, and how she will be handed over – these matters will be discussed with India,” he said, according to the Prothom Alo newspaper. Earlier this month, on November 9, Hasina had requested a new passport to facilitate her return. Living in India ever since her ouster on August 5, 2024 following protests in Bangladesh, Hasina, on the second anniversary of the collapse of her government, declared her intention to return home. Earlier this month, in a letter to Preeti Rahman, Bangladesh Acting High Commissioner to India, Hasina’s lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers wrote, “In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client.” The letter asked for the applications to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of her Bangladeshi nationality ‌ and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments”. Responding to questions about this letter, Bangladesh High Commission spokesperson Md Saidur Rahman had told The Indian Express, “Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who was ousted following the student-people uprising, has not applied for a new passport or National Identity Card (NID).” “We have received an email from a law firm named Matrix Chambers requesting the issuance of a new passport and NID in the name of Sheikh Hasina. However, we are not sure whether the request is genuine. There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said. “However, we have forwarded the email to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for necessary consideration,” the spokesperson had said. Later, Bangladesh authorities said that Hasina’s signature did not match with her signature on the database maintained by the country’s government. Dhaka has been seeking Hasina’s extradition. The Indian government has said the extradition request is “being examined” and that it is a “legal matter” and will be dealt with accordingly. – With agency reports

headline: Indian diaspora brings more visitors than foreign tourism. The homecoming economy is undermeasured
content: New Delhi: Every December, the arrival halls of airports in Delhi, Mumbai and Kochi fill with Indian nationals coming home from overseas. India receives more visitors from its own diaspora than from foreign tourists. Yet much of the money these homecomings bring into the country remains invisible in official tourism statistics. In 2025, 110.7 lakh Indian nationals, most of them living overseas, visited India, outnumbering the 91.5 lakh foreign tourists who came to the country. Arrivals of Indians living abroad have nearly doubled from 54.3 lakh in 2014, while foreign tourist arrivals have grown by only about 19 percent over the same period. Since 2024, returning Indians have consistently outnumbered foreign tourists. Even among foreign tourists, a significant proportion were people of Indian origin. Of the 91.5 lakh foreign tourists in 2025, approximately 30.1 lakh, or one-third, were people of Indian origin visiting family and friends. These visitors came predominantly from a handful of countries. The US accounted for approximately 10.6 lakh such visitors, representing 58 percent of all US travellers to India. Britain, Australia and Canada followed, with more than half of their respective tourists to India constituting those who came to see family and friends. Together, six countries accounted for 24.4 lakh such visitors. Visitors coming to see family and friends also tend to stay longer. In 2025, they spent an average of about 25 days in India, compared with 15.5 days for those visiting on holiday. The undercounting of travel to visit friends and relatives is not unique to India. In 1990, tourism researcher R.T. Jackson questioned whether this category of travel was being systematically underestimated and concluded that it was.

headline: India Inc responds to PM Modi's call, seeks greater regulatory transparency
content: Days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised Indian industry for falling short on job creation and other fronts, senior officials of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on Monday outlined steps the government could take to boost private investment, including strengthening market integrity, improving regulatory transparency and easing the flow of cross-border capital. “The key strategy of the government must be to create a business environment characterised by robust investor protection and regulatory ease coupled by market integrity. Towards this objective, regulatory authorities would play a key role by ensuring that their compliances do not stand as an obstacle for the free flow of cross border capital,” said CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee, in a post on X. He said Modi’s call for industry to invest more, foster innovation and improve competitiveness was a strong reminder of the need to raise productivity and secure long-term economic growth. “India’s ability to attract long-term capital will be determined by the strength of its markets and the competitiveness of our industries. Increased transparency, along with ease of doing business, will strengthen India’s standing as a global investment destination,” he added. Addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry’s (Ficci’s) annual general meeting last week, Modi criticised Indian companies for their continued reliance on imports in critical sectors and for treating the country’s vast domestic market as a “comfort zone”, rather than improving product quality and building capabilities to compete globally. Rajiv Memani, CII’s immediate past president, said global investors sought clear, predictable and proportionate rules. “India’s regulatory framework must deliver on all three. India will need both domestic savings and foreign capital to finance its investment requirements. Long-term global investors weigh regulatory clarity, predictability and compliance costs alongside returns,” he said. He further said openness to global capital and market integrity are complementary objectives. “A transparent, predictable and proportionate regulatory framework is essential to achieving both and sustaining India's attractiveness to long-term investors,” he added. Memani said SEBI's use of public consultation allows market participants to provide feedback and enables regulatory requirements to be reviewed in the light of changing market conditions, emerging risks, and benchmarked with international standards and practices. “SEBI has taken several steps to make India's capital markets more accessible to foreign investors, including risk-based regulatory requirements, simplified operating processes and initiatives such as SWAGAT-FI. These efforts are important, alongside effective safeguards for investor protection and market integrity,” he added. Sanjiv Puri, former CII president and chairman and managing director of ITC, said for Indian enterprises seeking to attract long-term domestic and global capital, strong governance and predictable regulation are essential. “Transparency, investor confidence and ease of investment reinforce one another. Vibrant markets can give a significant impetus to robust economic growth and competitiveness,” he added. Puri said capital markets have played a vital role in channelising savings into productive investments contributing to nation-building and enabling growth with inclusiveness. “Undoubtedly, market integrity is built on transparency and good governance. India has made considerable progress on both,” he said. Puri said over the years, Sebi has steadily strengthened corporate governance and disclosure standards for listed companies apart from a sharp focus on enabling ease of doing business. “Laudable steps include the strengthening of board oversight, related-party transaction norms and comprehensive Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRR). These measures have helped improve corporate accountability and the quality of information available to investors. Good regulation must also evolve with changing market conditions. SEBI's consultative approach to reviewing and refining its regulations provides an important opportunity to balance compliance requirements with emerging opportunities risks, while keeping transparency and investor protection central,” he added. R Dinesh, another former CII president and executive chairman of TVS Supply Chain Solutions, said access to long-term capital and confidence in market regulation were crucial for an economy investing heavily in infrastructure and logistics. “Clear rules, strong governance and proportionate regulation can help deliver both,” he suggested. Dinesh said India’s infrastructure needs patient, long-term capital, and the right market frameworks help bring it in transparently. “SEBI's frameworks for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) have created regulated avenues for domestic and global investors to participate in infrastructure and real estate assets, including roads, power transmission, warehousing and commercial properties. Strong disclosure and governance requirements have been central to these frameworks. Equally important is the willingness to review and refine regulations as markets develop. SEBI's consultative approach provides an opportunity to calibrate requirements to evolving risks and investor needs, without compromising transparency or investor protection,” he added. CII President R Mukundan, who is also managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Chemicals, said the next priority was to move beyond ease of doing business to the “speed of doing business”. CII’s Private Investment Barometer showed that private project announcements reached a record ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of FY27, 4.4 times the long-run average, he said. As the prime minster Modi has said, “the task now is for industry to make ‘India First’ the basis of every long-term decision. CIl and its members are committed to this agenda,” he added.

headline: AAP’s Chandigarh picks: A 2012 loyalist, businessmen and a comeback
content: The AAP government on Monday (November 23, 2026) released its second list of eight candidates for the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections scheduled for December 23, and fielded a mix of old party loyalists, businessmen and grassroots workers, including a postgraduate and candidates with local business connections. The list, announced by AAP’s Chandigarh in-charge and Delhi MLA Jarnail Singh, takes the party’s tally of declared candidates to 17. The party had announced its first list of nine candidates earlier. One of the notable names in the second list is Lalit Mohan, who has been associated with the AAP since 2012 and is among the party’s oldest workers in Chandigarh. Sources said the party decided to accommodate an old organisational face who has been associated with it since its early days. AAP president Vijay Pal said, “The candidates have been selected based on an internal survey and their clean background. We have given tickets to people who enjoy public support, are loyal to the party and have worked hard to strengthen the organisation.” He also said the party would contest the elections with full strength and unity, to provide better civic amenities, transparent administration and people-centric governance. The list also features Bindu Bala Garg from Ward 17. A postgraduate, she comes from a business background. Her husband, Bajrang Garg, runs a shop in Shastri Market. Her candidature brings a business-family face into the party’s candidate list. Another candidate with a business background is Ram Jaiswal, who has been fielded from Ward 14. He runs a marble shop in Dhanas and has local connections in the area. For Talwinder Singh, who has been fielded from Ward 6, the second list brings another opportunity to contest the civic elections. Sources said he had missed out on a ticket in the previous election cycle after being dropped from the list but has now found a place among the eight nominees. The party has also fielded Sukhwant Kaur from Ward 8, Anju Sethi from Ward 13, Satvinder Kaur from Ward 26 and Narender Bhatia from Ward 34. Announcing the candidates, Jarnail Singh said the people of Chandigarh would extend their support to the party’s politics and commitment to public welfare. He said the AAP would work towards transforming Chandigarh into a better, cleaner and more developed city. The party’s candidate selection comes as it seeks to build on its performance in the previous municipal corporation elections. In the 2021 civic polls, AAP had won 14 of the 35 wards and emerged as the single largest party in the council. With two lists covering 17 wards, the party is gradually firming up its candidate line-up for the December 23 contest.

headline: CISCE Teachers Undergo Training To Strengthen Competency-Based Assessment
content: The Australian Council for Educational Research (ACER) India has conducted a faculty development programme in Hyderabad for around 300 teachers affiliated with the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE). The five-day training sessions focused on strengthening teachers’ understanding of competency-based assessment and improving their assessment design skills. The programme was conducted across nine batches and covered five subject areas: languages, mathematics, sciences and humanities. It was aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasises competency-based education and learning outcomes. According to ACER India, each batch participated in a hands-on learning programme centred on the question, “What can we do with what we know?” Teachers explored the principles of competency-based assessment and practised designing, reviewing and refining multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and constructed-response questions, according to the official press release by CISCE. The sessions focused on using real-world contexts, relevant assessment material and plausible answer options to evaluate students’ understanding. Teachers also examined how assessment tasks can test students’ ability to apply concepts, analyse information, evaluate evidence and solve problems in unfamiliar situations. The programme encouraged teachers to shift their focus from making questions more difficult to making them more meaningful. It also highlighted the importance of designing assessments that measure what students can do with their knowledge, rather than testing only their ability to recall information. ACER India said more than 90% of participants found the programme extremely useful for their day-to-day work. Over 90% also reported acquiring a new skill of aligning competencies with learning goals before framing assessment questions. Commenting on the initiative, Dr Joseph Emmanuel, Chief Executive and Secretary of CISCE, said the transformation envisioned under NEP 2020 requires a corresponding change in assessment practices. He said the programme reflected CISCE’s commitment to developing assessment-literate teachers who can promote deeper understanding, critical thinking and the practical application of knowledge. Dr Priyanka Sharma, CEO of ACER India, said the programme helped teachers shift their focus from the difficulty of a question to the evidence of learning it can generate. She described this change in approach as important for developing students’ reasoning, critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. The programme also discussed the growing importance of transferable skills such as collaboration, analysis and problem-solving as artificial intelligence and machine learning reshape the world. It highlighted how competency-based assessment can help schools move beyond marks and rote learning towards deeper understanding and practical application of knowledge.

headline: ‘Prioritised profits over lives’: No bail for PG operator in Delhi building collapse case
content: A Delhi court on Monday dismissed the regular bail application of Shubham Tyagi, an advocate and co-operator of the Hostel Daze paying guest facility that collapsed at Delhi’s Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people, holding that he was in occupation and control of the premises and had “prioritised his financial benefits” over the lives and safety of students and labourers. In his order, Additional Sessions Judge (Patiala House Courts) Dhirendra Rana said the allegations against the applicant were serious and that granting bail was a discretion to be exercised by balancing the accused’s personal liberty against society's larger interest. “The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled for the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand. The court cannot turn blind eyes towards the fact that seven valuable lives have been lost and the impact of their death would be everlasting on their families,” the judge observed. Alteration work without permission: Order According to the prosecution, the South Campus police station received a police control room call at around 1.34 pm on September 6 about the collapse of a building at 14, Satya Niketan, which was being run as a hostel-cum-paying guest accommodation for male students. Twelve men were pulled from the debris. Seven were declared brought dead and five injured were hospitalised, of whom two remained hospitalised. The victims included five students and two labourers. “A preliminary inspection found that an old building had been subjected to additional construction and structural changes in the basement and upper floors without taking permission from competent authorities, allegedly increasing the load on the existing structure and affecting its load-bearing capacity. Later, an FIR [First Information Report] was registered,” the order said. “The basement and ground floor were in the exclusive control and possession of the owner, the upper ground floor and first floor were leased to one Sudhanshu [Lovenish Kumar] to run a boys’ PG, and the second and third floors were leased to Tyagi to run a boys’ PG, under a rent agreement dated September 6 last year,” it added. Construction work began days before collapse The investigation found that accused Urmila Gupta owned the building. The electricity and Jal Board connections were in the name of accused Hari Ram Gupta. “Urmila Gupta, Hari Ram Gupta and their son Mahesh Gupta were arrested on September 7. Accused Sanoj, an unqualified rajmistri/contractor, and Sudhanshu Lovenish Kumar, the other PG operator, were arrested on September 9. Tyagi later surrendered before the Patiala House Courts on September 11, after his anticipatory bail plea was dismissed on 10 September, and has been in judicial custody since,” the order said. The police submitted in their report that 10-12 days before the building collapse, Urmila, Hari Ram and Mahesh had jointly begun construction, structural alteration and repair work on the building without approval, engaging Sanoj, who in turn employed two unqualified labourers. “Neither the contractor nor the property owner, the prosecution said, obtained the opinion of a qualified architect or structural expert. The prosecution further alleged that both PG operators took the premises on rent without verifying its structural safety or design, failed to take precautions despite ongoing construction, and failed to warn or guide residents of the danger,” Rana said in his order. “It relied on the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, who said construction had been underway in the basement for about 10-12 days. When he complained about the noise, both Sudhanshu and Tyagi told him renovation work was going on. Iron rods were being cut on the ground floor, and when he and other students objected, they were threatened with eviction, after which the work continued,” the order said. ‘Knew rules, should have asked students to vacate’ Judge Rana rejected the argument that Tyagi had no role in the construction. “The fact remains the same that he was in occupation and control of the property after executing rent agreement with co-accused persons,” the order stated. “If construction work was not under his control and not on his instructions then he was duty bound to get the property vacated from occupants till the time construction was going on. He was duty bound to take care of the safety of the innocent students by informing about the threat in the said property on account of such illegal construction,” it added. The court further noted that Tyagi is a qualified legal professional who was well aware of the rules governing the running of a PG. “He could have easily foresee the danger on account of illegal construction activities but he prioritised his financial benefits above the life and safety of innocent students/labours,” the order said, adding that judicial notice could be taken of the recurring loss of life in building collapses caused by illegal construction.

headline: 4 children killed, 32 injured as truck rams stationary school bus in UP’s Kannauj
content: At least four children were killed and 32 others, including 24 students, injured after a speeding truck rammed into a stationary school bus on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway in Uttar Pradesh's Kannauj on Tuesday morning, police said.The accident took place around 6 am near the Thathia area when the bus belonging to Kaushambi-based Oriental Public School was parked on the shoulder of the expressway to allow the children to use the toilet. The injured included eight school staff members, police said.The bus was carrying 50 people, including students returning from an excursion to the Taj Mahal in Agra, Superintendent of Police (SP) Vinod Kumar said. The truck hit the bus from behind, damaging its rear portion, he added.“Police personnel, Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) staff and commuters passing by rushed to the spot and rescued the children from the damaged bus,” Kumar said.“They were subsequently taken to a medical college in ambulances, where doctors declared four of them dead,” he said.The deceased were identified as Aryan Chaurasia, 14, son of Prem Kumar Chaurasia; Raziullah, 16, son of Shamiullah; and Armaan, 17, and Zaid Mirza, 17, both sons of Riaz Ahmad, according to police.School manager Salman and one child, whose condition was stated to be critical, were referred to Kanpur for further treatment, Kumar said.The remaining injured students and staff members are undergoing treatment at the medical college.District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and SP Kumar reached the medical college and enquired about the condition of the injured.Students who escaped unhurt were being sent back to their homes in another bus, police said.आज दिनांक 24.11.2026 को #Digrknr यमुना प्रसाद द्वारा जनपद कन्नौज में लखनऊ-आगरा एक्सप्रेसवे पर स्कूली बच्चों से भरी बस एवं ट्रक के मध्य हुई सड़क दुर्घटना के घटनास्थल का स्थलीय निरीक्षण किया गया।इस दौरान महोदय द्वारा घटनास्थल का बारीकी से निरीक्षण कर दुर्घटना के संबंध में विस्तृत जानकारी प्राप्त की गई। साथ ही संबंधित अधिकारियों को प्रकरण की गहनता एवं निष्पक्षता से जांच करते हुए दुर्घटना के कारणों का पता लगाने तथा शीघ्र प्रभावी विधिक कार्रवाई सुनिश्चित करने हेतु आवश्यक दिशा-निर्देश दिए गए।#UPPolice #Digrknr #KannaujPolice @Uppolice @adgzonekanpur @kannaujpolice— IG RANGE KANPUR (@igrangekanpur) November 24, 2026

headline: Last legal hurdle gone, Jaipur Polo Ground’s takeover by Centre will now move ahead
content: In what removes the last legal hurdle for the Centre’s takeover the Jaipur Polo Ground in the heart of Lutyens’ Delhi, the Indian Polo Association (IPA) last week withdrew its appeal against the takeover proceedings from a district court in Delhi. Principal District and Sessions Judge Dr Vijay Kumar Dahiya dismissed the appeal by IPA after the association opted to withdraw it, with liberty to pursue alternate appropriate remedies. Earlier in August, IPA, which was operating the 15.20-acre Jaipur Polo Ground, had also withdrawn a plea from before the Delhi HC where it was seeking appointment of an arbitrator to adjudicate over alleged breach of lease terms, as was earlier claimed by the government. No alternate land and out of Polo Ground According to sources in IPA, the body was urged by the government to withdraw its litigations against the government and instead urged to conduct deliberations with the Land and Development Office (L&DO), which comes under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), off-court for requesting alternate land. Earlier in August, IPA’s Vice-President and BJP MP Naveen Jindal, in a representation addressed to L&DO, had requested the “allotment of alternate land admeasuring at least 500 acres in the National Capital Territory of Delhi, in lieu of the Jaipur Polo Ground.for the establishment of a world-class polo and equestrian facility to promote the sports of polo in India.” As per the IPA, no headway has been made with respect to this representation till date. Jindal, in his representation, had, however, outlined that IPA is “committed to finding an amicable and pragmatic resolution in the larger public interest”, and that IPA is “willing to cooperate” and give up the premises, provided an alternative site within NCT of Delhi is provided to them. The latest development, however, leaves IPA without any alternate land at present and out of the Jaipur Polo Ground, closing the last remaining potential hurdle for the government. Had IPA succeeded in its appeal before the district court, the government may have had to contest before courts its takeover of the land parcel. Why Indian Polo Association went to court Over decades, the Jaipur Polo ground has been a centre of national and international events and tournaments such as the Asian Games equestrian events, IPA National Polo Championship, Indian Masters Trophy, among others. The land parcel, gifted by the erstwhile Maharaja of Jaipur to the Delhi Polo Club in around 1930, was formally leased to the club on February 24, 1951, by the Central Public Works Department for a period of 20 years. The land parcel, gifted by the erstwhile Maharaja of Jaipur to the Delhi Polo Club in around 1930, was formally leased to the club on February 24, 1951, by the Central Public Works Department for a period of 20 years. According to the IPA, the lease was extended in 1971 through 1982, with further extensions continuing thereafter. Following the dissolution of the Delhi Polo Club in 1983, the premises were transferred and allotted in favor of the IPA. On March 12, this year, the government issued an eviction notice following which IPA moved the Delhi HC and then invoked arbitration clause from its lease deed. However, while arbitration proceedings were underway, the government again issued a show-cause notice on April 17, terming IPA as unauthorised occupant. On May 20, an eviction order was passed by the L&DO’s Estate Officer, which IPA has claimed, was issued without affording them a fair opportunity of hearing. IPA had moved the district court in June, challenging a May 20 eviction order by the Estate Officer. It had also sought a stay on the eviction as an interim measure, which the district court refused. In June, before the HC, the Centre’s Standing Counsel, Ashish Dixit, had outlined that the government plans to take over the Jaipur Polo Club, Race Club and Delhi Gymkhana as “the entire area is being redeveloped for public purpose”, which includes “defence requirements”.

headline: Sale of fake cosmetics lacking approval will not be permitted in Keralam: Health Minister | India News
content: Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan on Tuesday said that the government will take stringent action against anyone selling fake cosmetics andsale of any such product lacking the requisite approvals will not be permitted in the state.Muraleedharan told reporters that while there will be no compromise in the government action against those selling fake cosmetics, "the public should avoid experimenting with such creams".The minister made it clear that any such product that does not have government approval or clearance will not be allowed to be sold in the state, and anyone found doing so will face strict action."Directions have been issued to the state Drugs Controller to carry out more inspections," he said.He said that several aspects, including the source of such creams and what is being mixed in them, have to be examined, and that is why he has asked the State Home Minister to order a vigilance probe into the issue.The issue came to light after a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram district allegedly developed a serious kidney disease after using a fairness cream bought online following promotions by Instagram influencers.Doctors treating the girl found dangerously high levels of mercury in her body.The police have registered a case following a complaint over the product.The issue has also drawn attention to singer Saleem Kodathoor, who recently said he had been diagnosed with membranous nephropathy after using a fairness cream about 10 years ago.He said he had undergone several months of treatment and hospitalisation.Following the complaints, the health minister had directed the State Drugs Controller to conduct inspections across the state to check the sale and online promotion of illegal cosmetics and other unapproved products.He has also sought strict action against social media influencers promoting fake and substandard cosmetic products.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: India looking to scale space infrastructure “beyond first success” through international collaboration: L&T senior VP Ramchandani
content: New Delhi [India], November 24 (ANI): India is looking to scale its space infrastructure "beyond the first success" through international collaborations and partnerships with global players, L&T Precision Engineering Senior Vice President and Head Arun T Ramchandani said on Monday.Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the fifth edition of the India International Space Conclave (IISC 2026), Ramchandani said India is working with partners from countries including France, Japan and the United States to develop different aspects of its space infrastructure and expand the country's capabilities in the sector."We are looking at building India's space infrastructure in a global context. We have partners from France, Japan, the US, and other parts of the world, and we are looking at building the various aspects of the Indian space ecosystem and scaling it beyond the first success," he said.He also highlighted the role of partnerships between private companies and academic institutions in strengthening India's space ecosystem, pointing to several Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) facilitated by the Indian Space Association (ISpA)."There are various MOUs between ISpA (Indian Space Association) and academic institutions, and private-to-private partnerships, and these MOUs are building partnerships within the space ecosystem to strengthen the space ecosystem," Ramchandani added.French Ambassador to India Thierry Mathou also emphasised the importance of strengthening the longstanding India-France partnership in the space sector, calling for renewed cooperation to address emerging challenges and opportunities.Mathou said the two countries needed to reinvent their partnership, which has spanned six decades, while highlighting strategic autonomy and India's push for domestic manufacturing as key areas of cooperation."The French approach has always been, whenever suitable, to offer as much indigenous production in India as possible. As a matter of fact, Make in India has been the reality for French industry for decades and is being continuously boosted. And it's exactly what we plan to do in the space sector," Mathou said.The fifth edition of the India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association, was held in New Delhi on November 23 and 24. The event brought together policymakers, representatives of space agencies, defence officials, industry leaders and startups to deliberate on India's growing role in the global space sector and opportunities for collaboration. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: Government Warns Against Leaving Accounts Logged In On Shared Computers
content: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has issued a high-priority cybersecurity advisory on the ‘Safe Use of WhatsApp Web,’ urging citizens and officials to avoid using browser-based messaging for sensitive or official work. Dated November 18 and highlighted across national advisories on November 23, the directive warns that an active, authenticated WhatsApp Web session can be hijacked to silently infiltrate a user's account without triggering immediate suspicion. headline: How a Bihar Farmer Built an 18-Acre Aquaculture Enterprise | Indian Council of Agricultural Research
content: The Inspiring Journey of Shri Mithilesh Kumar Singh: From No Pond Ownership to a Crore-Plus Fisheries Enterprise Shri Mithilesh Kumar Singh, a progressive fish farmer from Rohtas district of Bihar, exemplifies the transformative potential of scientific knowledge and institutional support in promoting rural entrepreneurship. From having no prior experience in fisheries and no ponds of his own, he has developed an 18-acre commercial aquaculture enterprise, generating an annual turnover of over ₹1 crore with a net profit margin of 20–25%. His remarkable journey demonstrates how technical training, systematic investment and the adoption of scientific practices can create sustainable livelihood opportunities and strengthen the rural economy. Scientific Training: The Foundation of Entrepreneurial Success Recognising the growing potential of inland fisheries as a viable business opportunity, Shri Singh participated in a seven-day training programme on Inland Fisheries Management organised by ICAR-Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute, Barrackpore, with sponsorship from the Department of Fisheries, Government of Bihar. The programme provided him with practical knowledge and essential technical skills in pond preparation and management, water quality monitoring, fish species selection, stocking density, scientific feeding practices and fish health management. More importantly, the training equipped him with the confidence and technical understanding required to venture into commercial aquaculture. Applying the knowledge acquired through the training, Shri Singh gradually established and expanded his fish farming activities through systematic investment, scientific management and sustained entrepreneurial efforts.

headline: ‘I added one serving of pulses to my diet for a week: How much fibre did I get?’
content: Including a serving of pulses in your daily meals can significantly increase your fibre intake, particularly if your diet is otherwise low in dietary fibre. Pulses such as lentils, chickpeas, kidney beans, black gram and green gram are excellent sources of both soluble and insoluble fibre, supporting overall digestive health. Dr Abhishek Deepak, Director (Hepatologist & Therapeutic Endoscopist), Institute of Gastro Sciences, ShardaCare - Healthcity says, "Depending on the type and preparation, one cooked serving of pulses (approximately 150–180 grams) can provide around 7–15 grams of fibre." DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. How much fibre intake can pulses provide? Dr Deepak says, "For an adult, the recommended daily fibre intake is generally around 25–30 grams, although individual requirements may vary. So, adding one serving of pulses each day can provide a substantial share of your daily fibre requirement. Over a week, this dietary change can improve overall fibre consumption and support better digestive health." "Soluble fibre absorbs water and forms a gel-like substance in the digestive tract, helping regulate bowel movements and slow digestion. It can also support healthy cholesterol levels. Insoluble fibre adds bulk to stools and helps food move through the digestive tract more efficiently, reducing the likelihood of constipation. Pulses also contain resistant starch, which benefits gut bacteria. These bacteria ferment certain fibres and produce short-chain fatty acids that help maintain the health of the intestinal lining," he adds. What if you suddenly add large quantities of pulses to your diet The digestive system may need time to adjust to an increased fibre intake. As per Dr Deepak, "People who suddenly introduce large quantities of pulses may experience bloating, gas or abdominal discomfort, particularly if their previous fibre intake was low. This is why it is advisable to increase fibre gradually, drink adequate water and ensure pulses are properly soaked and cooked." While adding pulses for a week is a positive dietary step, the benefits are more sustainable when they become part of a consistent, balanced eating pattern. "Combining pulses with vegetables, whole grains, fruits and adequate hydration can further improve fibre intake and support long-term gut health," he adds.
