headline: Forus Health, Eyebetes Foundation work on AI-based diabetes screening - Mint
content: Mumbai’s Ganpati celebrations are synonymous with faith, community and public gatherings. This year, two of the city’s festival destinations became the setting for an initiative that brought an important conversation into the celebrations: preventive healthcare.Eyebetes Foundation, in collaboration with Forus Health, conducted a pilot retinal screening initiative at Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal, exploring how retinal imaging and artificial intelligence could potentially support diabetes risk screening and generate insights associated with HbA1c levels.The initiative offered free screening activities to devotees and was designed to reach more than 15,000 people, bringing health awareness and preliminary screening closer to communities in an accessible environment.When the eye becomes a window to metabolic healthThe retina offers a distinctive view of the body’s microvascular system. Since diabetes can affect small blood vessels and cause changes in retinal structures, retinal imaging has attracted attention as a potential tool for identifying indicators associated with systemic health.At the Mumbai pilot, Forus Health explored this potential through AI-enabled retinal analysis, including its FH-POISE AI solutions. The technology uses retinal images to explore associations with diabetes risk and estimate HbA1c levels, offering a non-invasive screening pathway that does not initially require a blood sample or laboratory processing.“With FH-POISE AI solutions, we were exploring how a simple retinal image could provide insights that traditionally required a blood test. Our AI models could estimate HbA1c levels and flag diabetes risk from a single retinal image, without the need for a blood draw or laboratory processing. The retina gave us a unique, non-invasive view of the body’s microvascular health, and AI could help translate these insights into meaningful screening support,” said Srinivasan Venkatakrishnan, Chief Technology Officer and Head of Research & Development, Forus Health.The pilot demonstrated how technology can potentially bring preliminary health screening into settings beyond conventional hospitals and diagnostic centres.Taking screening where communities gatherOne of the takeaways from the initiative was the importance of accessibility. Diabetes screening often depends on an individual actively visiting a healthcare facility, undergoing testing and following up with a medical professional. Community-based initiatives can create an additional touchpoint by taking awareness and preliminary screening directly to people.Ganpati celebrations provided a significant setting for this approach. With thousands of devotees visiting the pandals, the initiative integrated health awareness into an existing community experience rather than requiring people to make a separate healthcare visit.Such models could have relevance for community health camps, workplaces, primary healthcare settings and mobile screening programmes, particularly where awareness or access to diagnostic facilities remains a challenge.Moving from screening to timely actionThe potential of AI-powered screening lies not simply in generating a digital insight, but in encouraging people to take the next step towards appropriate healthcare.An AI-generated estimate or risk indicator cannot replace conventional diagnostic testing. For individuals identified as potentially at risk, appropriate follow-up, including conventional HbA1c testing and consultation with a qualified healthcare professional, remains essential.“Diabetes was no longer only a metabolic concern; it was a major public health challenge with consequences that could affect the eyes, kidneys, heart, nerves and overall quality of life. What made AI-powered retinal screening particularly promising was its potential to make diabetes risk assessment quicker, non-invasive and more accessible, especially in communities where regular laboratory testing might not always be easy to access,” said Dr. Nishant Kumar, Consultant Ophthalmologist, Retina Surgeon and Uveitis Specialist, and Founder, Eyebetes Foundation.The collaboration highlighted the importance of developing datasets that represent Indian populations. Building Indian datasets and training AI models on relevant populations could play an important role in evaluating and refining the applicability of such technologies in the country.A broader role for AI in preventive healthcareThe Mumbai pilot reflects an evolution in healthcare, where artificial intelligence is being explored as a supporting tool for screening, risk identification and early intervention.For retinal healthcare, the possibilities extend beyond detecting eye conditions. The ability to examine retinal images for patterns associated with systemic health conditions could position the eye as an accessible entry point for preventive screening.However, responsible implementation remains central to this evolution. Clinical validation, representative datasets, appropriate referral pathways and clear communication about the limitations of AI-generated insights are critical to ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces established medical care.Bringing health awareness into everyday lifeThe collaboration between Forus Health and Eyebetes Foundation demonstrated an approach that combined technology, medical expertise and community engagement.By taking retinal screening to Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal during one of Mumbai’s largest cultural celebrations, the initiative created an opportunity to connect preventive healthcare with everyday community life.Its significance extended beyond the screening activity itself. It opened a conversation around whether emerging technologies such as AI-powered retinal analysis could help make preliminary health screening more accessible, encourage earlier awareness and create links between communities and formal healthcare systems.The screening programme was intended for awareness and preliminary risk assessment. AI-generated health insights should not be considered a substitute for conventional HbA1c testing, clinical diagnosis or consultation with a qualified healthcare professional.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Mint's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. Mint assumes no editorial responsibility for the content.The information does not constitute medical/health advice. Readers are strongly advised to consult a registered medical practitioner.

headline: Karnataka to frame migrant worker policy soon: Minister Santosh Lad
content: Bengaluru: Karnataka Labour Minister Santosh Lad has signalled plans to frame a dedicated policy for migrant workers, a first in the country, even as Bengaluru continues to see friction over migration and competition for jobs. Speaking at the 43rd national conference of All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in Bengaluru, Lad urged trade unions to help shape a structured policy framework for migrant labourers. .Plans afoot to introduce unified helpline for public grievances: Minister Santosh Lad.“India has 93% of its workforce in the unorganised sector. The issue of migrant workers is a challenge and whichever state they belong to, they should be our focus,” said Lad. The minister also highlighted Karnataka’s push on platform and gig worker protection through a legislation and a welfare board. Calling for stronger state and central support — such as subsidies, credit facilities, and district-level backing for small-scale industries to generate local jobs in rural areas and reduce migration pressure on major cities, Lad urged experts to examine how artificial intelligence, automation, and robotics impacts economy.

headline: College teachers’ body issues open letter on safeguarding education
content: Shillong, Nov 23:The teachers of deficit pattern from the institutes availing grant-in-aid facility, have issued an open letter highlighting various aspects of safeguarding education. Full text below MEGHALAYA COLLEGE TEACHERS’ ASSOCIATION (MCTA) OPEN LETTER TO THE PEOPLE OF MEGHALAYA AND ALL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS Date: 23rd November 2026 A Call to Safeguard Public Education in Meghalaya: Our Collective Responsibility to Future Generations To the People of Meghalaya, Civil Society Organisations, Parents, Students and All Concerned Citizens, the Meghalaya College Teachers’ Association (MCTA) addresses this open letter to the people of Meghalaya at a critical juncture in the history of public education in our State. We write with deep concern over the growing threats to the Deficit Grant-in-Aid System, the continued neglect of longstanding grievances affecting educators, and the larger implications these developments hold for the future of education and the generations who depend upon it. The ongoing indefinite strike by the Khasi Jaintia Deficit School Teachers’ Association (KJDSTA) must be understood within this larger context. The agitation is not merely about salaries or monetary entitlements. It concerns longstanding and unresolved issues, including the implementation of the Centralised Provident Fund Scheme 2023 and withdrawal of the Scheme 2026, CPF and NPS-related concerns, the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme (MACPS), the Structured Pay Framework and Composite Grant, non-advertisement of vacant deficit teaching posts, pending salaries and delays in the release of Dearness Allowance despite repeated assurances. These concerns relate fundamentally to the service security, dignity and welfare of those entrusted with educating our children. The MCTA recognises the anxiety and inconvenience that the ongoing agitation has caused students and parents, particularly with regard to the disruption of examinations and academic activities. We do not dismiss these concerns. However, when longstanding grievances remain unresolved despite repeated representations and appeals, disruptions to the educational calendar become an increasingly difficult consequence to avoid. The responsibility for ensuring uninterrupted education cannot rest solely upon teachers while the structural conditions necessary to sustain that education remain unaddressed. The greater danger lies not merely in the temporary disruption of examinations but in the gradual erosion of the public educational system itself. For decades, the Deficit Grant-in-Aid System has played a vital role in expanding educational opportunities in Meghalaya, particularly for communities and families who would otherwise struggle to access affordable education. These institutions, though administered by nongovernmental management, perform an essential public function through state-supported education. To characterise them merely as private institutions receiving government assistance risks overlooking their historical contributions and the public responsibilities they fulfil. The MCTA has consistently maintained that the Deficit Grant-in-Aid System must not only be preserved but also strengthened and improved. Our longstanding representations to the State Government have stressed the critical need to fill sanctioned vacant teaching posts, create additional faculty positions in response to the implementation of the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUP), resolve pending cases of UGC Scale implementation, placement and upgradation, and release outstanding Dearness Allowance revisions, and establish a fair and sustainable retirement security framework. The Association has also repeatedly advocated the proper implementation of UGC norms and regulations and the protection of the institutional framework that sustains accessible higher education in Meghalaya. These are not demands for preferential treatment. They concern the implementation of established policies, the fulfilment of institutional responsibilities and the conditions necessary for educational institutions to function effectively. The welfare of teachers and non-teaching employees cannot be separated from the welfare of students. Vacant posts, inadequate staffing, uncertainty over service conditions and weakened institutional support inevitably affect the quality and continuity of education. We must therefore ask ourselves what kind of educational future we envision for Meghalaya. Is education to remain a public responsibility, accessible to children and young people regardless of their economic or social circumstances? Or are we prepared to allow the gradual weakening of institutions that have historically made education possible for large sections of our society? The MCTA firmly believes in the principle of People's Education — an education that is publicly funded, accessible, equitable and directed towards the collective advancement of society. Public education must not become a privilege determined by the ability to pay. It is an essential means through which individuals and communities realise their aspirations, overcome disadvantage and contribute to the development of the State. The present struggle must therefore be understood as extending beyond the interests of any single association or category of employees. It concerns the future of our schools and colleges, the opportunities available to our children, and the responsibility we bear towards generations yet to come. If the foundations of public education are progressively weakened, the consequences will not be confined to the teaching fraternity. They will be borne by society as a whole. It is in this spirit that the MCTA appeals to parents, students, civil society organisations, community leaders, concerned citizens and all stakeholders to recognise the seriousness of the issues confronting public education in Meghalaya. We urge the public to engage with these concerns in their entirety and to recognise that the legitimate rights and welfare of educators are inseparable from the larger public interest. The Association further extends an open invitation to representatives of civil society and concerned citizens who wish to express their solidarity to join the Peaceful Silent Protest March scheduled for Wednesday, 25th November 2026, commencing at 10:30 AM. The route shall be from Don Bosco Square, Shillong, and proceed through Jacob’s Ladder, St. Anthony’s College, Raj Bhavan, the Deputy Commissioner’s Office, Central Secretariat, All Saints Church and Barik Point, before culminating at Malki Ground, subject to the necessary administrative arrangements. The march is intended as a peaceful and dignified expression of collective concern for the future of education in Meghalaya. Those who share these concerns are welcome to participate in solidarity with the teaching community and in defence of the principles of accessible and publicly funded education. The MCTA urges the State Government to address educators' grievances, uphold its policy commitments, and strengthen the public education system. Our struggle is not merely for the rights of teachers. It is for the preservation, improvement and future of public education in Meghalaya. The upliftment of everyone must remain our collective goal. Yours in solidarity, (Smti. L. W. Kharpuri) General Secretary Meghalaya College Teachers’ Association (MCTA)

headline: AAP to kick off 2027 poll campaign with Moga rally
content: The Amritsar leadership of Aam Aadmi Party strongly appealed to all Punjabis to participate in a large number in the grand rally being held in Moga on November 26.This appeal was made by the local AAP leaders, including both urban and rural district heads, MLAs and Halqa in-charges who took part in a preparatory meeting for the party’s upcoming rally at Moga.On this occasion, Amritsar district president (Urban) Sarabjot Singh Dhanjal, Amritsar district president (Rural) Gurpartap Singh Mianwind, Lok Sabha in-charge Jarnail Singh Dhot, MLA Dr Ajay Gupta, Dr Jasbir Singh Sandhu, Dalbir Singh Tong, Arvinder Singh Bhatti, Varun Rana, Satnam Singh Matharu, Nirmal Sokhi, Raghu Raj, Bhagwant Wazir were present.They said November 26 also coincides with the foundation day of Aam Aadmi Party and on this historic occasion, the party will also launch its election campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.The leaders added the Aam Aadmi Party government has taken decisions for the welfare of Punjab and Punjabis during its four and a half years in power, which the traditional parties could not even imagine during their long rule. As soon as the government was formed under the leadership of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, it was decided to provide 300 units of free electricity per month to every household, due to which the electricity bills of about 90 per cent of the households in Punjab are coming to zero. Similarly, people-friendly steps have been taken like providing cashless treatment facility of up to Rs 10 lakh to every family, arranging religious pilgrimage for the elderly through the Chief Minister’s Tirath Yatra Scheme and providing free health services to the people near their homes through Aam Aadmi Clinics.They mentioned their government launched the Chief Minister’s Mawan-Dhiyan Satkar Yojana for the respect and economic empowerment of women, under which financial assistance of Rs 1000 and Rs 1500 are being given to eligible women every month. A lot of work has also been done to provide canal water to farmers.They recalled that when CM Bhagwant Mann took over the government, at that time only 22 per cent of the agricultural area was using canal water, whereas today this figure has reached 88 per cent.

headline: Amritsar: 40,000 students, teachers take part in nagar kirtan
content: The holy city of Amritsar witnessed a magnificent spectacle of faith, devotion and Sikh heritage as nearly 40,000 students, teachers and staff members from 22 educational institutions participated in a mega nagar kirtan organised by the Khalsa College Governing Council (KCGC) to commemorate the 557th Parkash Purb of Guru Nanak Dev.The grand religious procession commenced from Khalsa College and proceeded towards Sri Harmandar Sahib (Golden Temple), transforming the city streets into a vibrant celebration of Gurbani, Sikh traditions and community spirit.Led by Guru Granth Sahib, placed in a beautifully decorated palanquin and accompanied by the Panj Pyaras, the nagar kirtan featured colourful presentations, devotional singing, Gatka performances, PT displays and rhythmic beating of drums. Students from Khalsa University, historic Khalsa College and other schools and colleges participated, chanting Gurbani hymns and singing ‘Nanak Aya, Jagat Jagaya’.The procession passed through GT Road, Putlighar, Sadar, Railway Station, Bhandari Bridge, Hall Gate and Town Hall before reaching the Golden Temple. The massive participation reflected the enthusiasm of young people in preserving Sikh religious traditions and cultural heritage.Addressing the gathering, Khalsa University Pro-Chancellor and Khalsa College Governing Council Secretary Rajinder Mohan Singh Chhina extended Gurpurb greetings and said Guru Nanak Dev’s message of peace, equality, universal brotherhood and welfare of humanity was particularly relevant in today’s strife-torn world.“We need to learn from the message of Guru Nanak for a peaceful and justice-driven world. Guru Nanak spoke against the divisions in society and called for the welfare of mankind,” he said.Vice-Chancellor Dr Mehal Singh and Khalsa College Principal Dr Atam Singh Randhawa urged people to follow Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings of peaceful co-existence and a society without discrimination.They said organising the mega nagar kirtan was part of the Khalsa College management’s longstanding tradition of celebrating Gurpurb and connecting younger generations with Sikh values and heritage.

headline: Nagar kirtan to mark Guru Nanak birth anniversary: Colours of devotion adorn Amritsar
content: A nagar kirtan was taken out from Akal Takht Sahib on Sunday to mark the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, with a large number of devotees participating in the religious procession organised by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) in collaboration with religious organisations and Sikh congregations.The procession was taken out under the canopy of Sri Guru Granth Sahib and led by the Panj Pyare. After prayers, the sacred saroop of Sri Guru Granth Sahib was placed in the palanquin by the Head Granthi of Sri Harmandar Sahib, Giani Amarjit Singh.Schoolchildren, band parties, Shabad Chowki jathas and gatka teams participated in the nagar kirtan, adding to the religious fervour. Devotees along the route welcomed the procession and served refreshments and langar.Meanwhile, SGPC president Harjinder Singh Dhami extended greetings to the Sikh community in India and abroad on the occasion of Guru Nanak Dev’s birth anniversary.Dhami said Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings of equality, universal brotherhood and welfare of humanity continued to hold relevance across the world. He said the Guru challenged caste-based discrimination, social inequalities, superstitions and divisions, and advocated a life based on love, mutual respect and compassion.He said the principles of Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhako offered guidance not only for spiritual life but also for fulfilling social responsibilities. Guru Nanak Dev, through his teachings and life, inspired people to uphold truth, humility, service, compassion and selflessness, he added.

headline: BSWML seeks 37 land parcels to expand Bengaluru's waste management infrastructure
content: Bengaluru: Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) has written to the Bengaluru Urban district administration seeking 37 land parcels to expand the city's waste management infrastructure. .Prominent among the properties are 207 acres in Anekal, 169 acres in Mandur, 100 acres in Mavallipura and 84 acres in Gollahalli. .According to documents accessed by DH, BSWML has sought the handover of 11 land parcels, mutation of revenue records (RTCs) of 17 properties in favour of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), and transfer of nine abandoned stone quarries on government gomala land to the GBA following joint inspections. .Bengaluru waste management set for overhaul.The proposal was also discussed at a recent meeting chaired by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. He reportedly directed GBA officials to convene another meeting with the Bengaluru Urban Deputy Commissioner. The meeting is yet to be scheduled. .Some of the land parcels sought by the GBA and BSWML were earlier held on lease by the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP). .For instance, the civic body had leased around 100 acres in Mavallipura at Rs 1,000 per acre a year. BSWML has now sought the land without the earlier lease conditions. Similar requests have been made for parcels in Chikkanagamangala, Bingipura, Mandur and Bidarahalli. .Some parcels have been sought to set up construction and demolition (C&D) waste processing plants at Doddabidarakallu and Marenahalli in Yelahanka. A waste transfer station is proposed at Chokkanahalli in Byatarayanapura. .BSWML Chief Executive Officer Karee Gowda said the land was required to meet future needs. ."We need land for creating waste management facilities such as dry waste collection centres, processing facilities, leaf composting units and coconut processing plants. We have held several meetings with the district administration on this issue," he told DH. .Nine stone quarries .BSWML has also sought joint inspections of nine abandoned stone quarries by the Revenue and Mines and Geology departments to assess their suitability for waste management facilities. .These include quarries at Marenahalli (32 acres) and Tarahunase (19 acres) in Yelahanka; Hulimangala (18 acres and 21 guntas) in Anekal; and Yarappanahalli (16 acres and 18 guntas) in Bengaluru East. The list also includes three quarries in the Thippagondanahalli Reservoir catchment area. .Recently, residents of Tarahunase protested against BSWML's plan to transport the city's waste to their village. They said the gram panchayat had been scientifically managing its waste and urged the agency to follow the same practice instead of transporting garbage to the city's outskirts.

headline: Deputy DEO inspects mid-day meal at schools in Sarhali
content: Deputy District Education Officer (Elementary) Rajinder Kaur on Monday paid a special visit to Government Primary School, Sarhali (Girls) and Government Senior Secondary School, Sarhali. She thoroughly inspected the arrangements for the mid-day meal.During the visit, Rajinder Kaur inspected the quality of mid-day meal, the process of food preparation and the cleanliness used while serving food. During her visit to the Government Primary School, Sarhali (Girls), she taught the children the tricks of writing Punjabi language and also showed special interest in the preparation of students going to appear for the Navodaya Vidyalaya entrance examination. On this occasion, Birinder Singh Lehri, Assistant Nodal In-charge (Secondary) and Prem Singh, Assistant District Nodal Incharge (Primary) were also present.

headline: Monsoon session not yet prorogued, Congress slams government
content: NEW DELHI: Congress expressed apprehension that something "truly sinister" is being planned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, as it lashed out at the absence of information on the upcoming Parliament session. It argued that dates of winter session or the special session should have been out by now.The winter session is due soon while monsoon session has not been prorogued yet after the passage of 100 days since it was adjourned, resulting in unending speculation about a special session for delimitation bill.AICC spokesman Jairam Ramesh said, "What games are being played by the PM-HM jodi, assuming that the jodi is still together?" He said the country should have known by now when the winter session will take place, or when the monsoon session will be reconvened (special session)."By now having seen (through) the desperate efforts of the jodi to cobble together a super-tainted two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha, the nation is entitled to know what the PM-HM formula for delimitation is, assuming that there is indeed one," he said.Ramesh said the suspense about Parliament and delimitation bill suggests the PM-HM jodi "is trapped by its own bluff and bluster" and "there is something truly sinister that is being planned."He said the "two GTA (Gyanesh Theft Arrangers) stars" stand brutally exposed but the "shenanigans of the diabolical duo" are diminishing the institution of Parliament.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Dutch transgender activist Jason Bhugwandass dies by euthanasia at 28 after years of physical and mental
content: Dutch transgender activist Jason Bhugwandass, who dedicated his life to exposing alleged abuses in youth care institutions, has died by euthanasia at the age of 28 following years of serious physical and mental health struggles. His death has prompted tributes from Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema, who remembered him for his courage and efforts to give vulnerable young people a voice.Jetten said he was deeply affected by the news, praising Bhugwandass for speaking up against mistreatment in youth care centres and standing up for people who had experienced similar treatment.“Deeply affected by the death of Jason Bhugwandass. The way he fought against abuses in youth care over the past few years deserves respect and appreciation,” the Prime Minister said. “He gave others who had been through the same things the voice he himself had so sorely missed.”He also offered his condolences to Bhugwandass' loved ones and everyone who had cared for him.Jason Bhugwandass' health struggles and final daysThe activist's death was announced through a statement shared on his Instagram account on Saturday. It said he had experienced symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) for years and had later developed a functional neurological disorder and Lance-Adams syndrome, a rare movement disorder.“The combination of these conditions reinforced each other and severely limited him in his daily life,” the statement said.It added that Bhugwandass could no longer live at home and required round-the-clock care. The statement described his death as the loss of a powerful voice who refused to stay silent in the face of injustice.Just two days before his death, the Stichting Ambulance Wens (Ambulance Wish Foundation), a Dutch non-profit that fulfils final wishes for seriously ill and immobile people, shared photographs of Bhugwandass enjoying a beach photoshoot with his carers and loved ones.“A fierce, but also very beautiful wish. Being this sick at 28 is unimaginable. Right then, photos together with the people you love are incredibly valuable,” the organisation wrote alongside the pictures.From painful experiences in youth care to becoming an activistBhugwandass' campaign for change was shaped by his own experiences growing up. He had spoken about a difficult childhood and the challenges he faced as a teenager, including gender dysphoria, depression and suicidal thoughts. He spent time in youth care institutions, where he later said he experienced isolation and a lack of emotional support.In a 2019 interview with local media, he described feeling as though he was “locked up” in the institutions.“You could be taken to an isolation room for the slightest thing,” he said, recalling how group leaders often felt more like security guards than people he could approach for help.“Not like people I could turn to with my problems. While what I really needed was someone who would stand by my side,” he added.Those experiences led Bhugwandass to campaign for better treatment of children and teenagers in the youth care system. He also carried out peer-led research, interviewing dozens of former residents who had experienced isolation in psychiatric wards.The research found that vulnerable children were kept in extreme isolation for an average of 20 to 21 hours a day. His activism helped bring the issue into the political spotlight, with the Dutch House of Representatives adopting a motion calling for the closure of strict isolation wards in youth care institutions.Named Amsterdammer of the Year in 2022Bhugwandass received wider recognition for his work in 2022 when he was named Amsterdammer of the Year by then-mayor Femke Halsema. He was also known for becoming a prominent face of transgender pride in the Netherlands, including appearing shirtless on billboards in a campaign that drew attention to his visible self-harm scars.Speaking after receiving the award, he said his connection with the city made the recognition particularly meaningful.“Because I am very attached to my city. It means a lot to me to know that it is mutual,” he said.Following his death, Halsema shared an emotional tribute, recalling the impression he had made on her from their first meeting.“Sometimes there are people who change your life. Gradually, not with a bang. From the very first moment I met Jason, I have loved him. Because of his giftedness, his courage, and his incredible perseverance,” she said.She also spoke of her sadness over the injustices he had experienced, saying she felt compassion for “the life stolen from him that prevented him from truly flourishing”.“How Jason deserved that. And how our society deserved that,” she added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

headline: Varsity unveils roadmap to mark 450th anniversary of Amritsar
content: Marking the 57th Foundation Day of Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU), to be celebrated from November 24 to 26, the university has planned a series of initiatives commemorating the 450th foundation year anniversary of Amritsar. The celebrations will focus not only on the city’s rich historical, spiritual and cultural heritage but also on envisioning its sustainable and progressive future.Vice-Chancellor Prof (Dr) Karamjeet Singh said the convergence of the two significant milestones provided an opportunity to initiate a broader dialogue on Amritsar’s development over the next 25 years. The university aims to move beyond ceremonial celebrations and encourage collective efforts towards shaping the city’s future.Amritsar 2052: A vision for the futureThe key initiative is the proposed ‘Amritsar 2052 Vision Document’, which seeks to outline a long-term roadmap for the city’s development. As part of a proposed 13-point action plan, the university will organise a two-day global conclave on November 25 and 26, release a documentary on Amritsar, launch the ‘450 Voices’ oral history project and present the proposed Amritsar Declaration.“The idea is to bring together historians, academicians, urban planners, environmental experts, economists, industrialists, citizens and members of the global Punjabi and Sikh diaspora to discuss Amritsar’s future. A city’s progress lies in the quality of life, environmental sustainability, intellectual growth, cultural preservation and opportunities available to its people,” said Prof Karamjeet Singh.450 voices and 450 young ambassadorsAmong the distinctive initiatives are the proposed ‘450 Voices’ Oral History Project and the association of 450 young people as Amritsar Ambassadors.The oral history project aims to document the memories and experiences of residents, preserving the city’s living heritage beyond monuments and official historical records. The initiative will provide a platform to capture personal narratives and experiences that have contributed to Amritsar’s social and cultural identity.The 450 young ambassadors, meanwhile, will explore and promote the city’s historic streets, prominent personalities, institutions, folk traditions and cultural landmarks to wider audiences.“It is important that citizens across generations become active participants in preserving and promoting Amritsar’s identity,” the Vice-Chancellor said.The two-day Global Conclave, scheduled for November 25 and 26, will bring together experts, policymakers, historians, environmentalists, economists, industry representatives and members of the diaspora to deliberate on the city’s future.Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu have also been invited to interact with students during the event.The proposed Amritsar Declaration will present a collective expression of ideas and commitments emerging from the deliberations, while the documentary will highlight the city’s historical and cultural significance.Prof Karamjeet Singh also emphasised the need for greater participation of the university’s academic departments, research scholars and subject experts in conducting scientific studies, developing innovative solutions and formulating policy recommendations.The proposed academic initiatives will address key challenges concerning environmental management, heritage conservation, urban planning and economic development, with the broader objective of positioning Amritsar as a sustainable, culturally vibrant and globally connected city.

headline: Over 4 kg heroin worth ₹20 crore recovered from Kalas village
content: The Sarai Amanat Khan Police and the BSF recovered 4 kilograms and 34 grams of heroin from Kalas village in the border area.Inspector Baljinder Singh, SHO of Sarai Amanat Khan, said that a packet was recovered during the search operation. Upon examination, it was found to contain 4.034 kilograms of heroin along with 42 grams of packing material. The international market value of the seized contraband is estimated to be more than Rs 20 crore.The police have registered a case under relevant sections of the NDPS Act, along with BVA Act, 2024.

headline: Sanitation contracts worth ₹167 crore under cloud; vigilance probe sought
content: BJP Punjab State Core Committee member and former IAS officer Dr Jagmohan Singh Raju on Monday demanded an independent vigilance probe into sanitation contracts worth approximately Rs167.03 crore awarded by the Municipal Corporation.He flagged possible irregularities in waste management, raising questions over overlapping contractual responsibilities, substantial price differences and bidding practices.Addressing the media in Amritsar, Raju, who had previously contested the Vidhan Sabha elections from Amritsar East, said he had submitted a detailed representation dated November 21 to the Central Vigilance Commissioner, the Chief Vigilance Officer of the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Director, Bureau of Investigation, Punjab, seeking an independent inquiry, a special financial and performance audit and a time-bound action-taken report. The contracts under scrutiny include approximately Rs 138 crore for integrated solid-waste management and a separate Rs 29.12-crore mechanised road-cleaning arrangement. Raju clarified that these figures represented the value of the contracts being questioned and not any established financial loss.The BJP leader’s demand comes amid continuing concerns over garbage accumulation, waste collection and sanitation in the city, making the issue significant for both civic governance and political accountability.According to documents cited in his complaint, two Letters of Award issued on October 6, 2025, assigned integrated solid-waste management across all 85 municipal wards to M/s 3R Management Limited, in consortium with M/s Suntan Life, for approximately Rs 98 crore.The contracts covered 41 wards for Rs 49.25 crore and 44 wards for Rs 48.75 crore. A concession agreement was subsequently executed on December 18, 2025.“An effective waste-processing facility had not been established despite the passage of several months, while complaints of missed door-to-door collection, accumulated garbage and inadequate transportation continued from different wards. Did the MC verify the payments against actual performance, including physical inspection of processing facilities, vehicle GPS records, weighbridge slips, daily collection logs and penalty records,” he asked.He also questioned the performance of mechanised road-cleaning agencies M/s Ricchcon Engineering Company and M/s Lion Services Limited, seeking details of equipment deployment, work executed and payments released.‘Why another contract when all 85 wards were covered?’ he asked.Questions over additional contract, rates and biddingRaju said why the MC had awarded an additional Rs 39.91-crore sanitation contract for the “Balance Area” when the earlier contracts reportedly covered all 85 wards. He alleged that the boundaries of the new contract were unclear and sought to rule out duplication of work.The MC, last year, had clarified that the additional contract covered Amritsar Improvement Trust properties excluded from earlier agreements, generating an estimated 121.4 tonnes of waste daily. Raju said the explanation needed verification.He also questioned the allocation of 17 wards to the new agency, claiming these were already covered under the earlier contracts. The matter reached the Punjab and Haryana High Court after 3R Management challenged the allocation. The MC later withdrew its order, and the court disposed of the petition without deciding the corruption allegations.“There was nearly 85 per cent difference in rates, from around Rs 1,600 per tonne under earlier contracts to Rs 2,957 per tonne under the new arrangement,” he said.Raju said the vigilance probe was necessary to ensure transparent tendering, prevent unnecessary public expenditure and establish whether payments matched actual work.

headline: 'Coward government': CJP's Saurav Das says he was stopped from flying for lecture at University of Oxfor
content: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Saurav Das on Monday alleged that he was stopped by the Central government from boarding a flight to London at Delhi airport, where he was scheduled to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.In a post on X, Das claimed that he was invited by several universities, including Oxford, Cambridge, the London School of Economics (LSE) and the University of Edinburgh, to speak about the CJP movement. He alleged that the government prevented him from travelling because it was afraid of his views reaching international academic institutions."This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement. Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" Das wrote.In another post, the CJP also criticised the govt saying, "This cowardly government fears educated voices so much that it has stooped to stopping those who carry India's voice to the world," the organisation alleged.CJP activist Abhijit Dipke also reacted to the development, alleging that Das was prevented from travelling despite being invited to speak at Oxford."Saurav was invited to speak at a conference at the University of Oxford, but looks like some anpadh gawar in power, who himself loves travelling around the world, is jealous of Saurav getting an invitation from Oxford," Dipke wrote on X.In another post, he took a swipe at the government, saying, "Wish Saurav had looted a bank or committed financial fraud, then the government would definitely have allowed him to fly to London."The allegations come a day after CJP activists Abhijit Dipke, Saurabh Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde attended the launch of the 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign in Goa, where they raised concerns over land rights, employment opportunities and the preservation of the state's cultural identity.Addressing a gathering, Dipke praised people who had extended solidarity to the CJP movement despite having no prior association with the organisation. He described standing up against injustice, even for people one does not know, as the essence of being a 'cockroach'.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
