headline: How the Iran war drove India and China to record Russian oil imports in 2026, and why purchases may ease in 2027
content: India and China are set to import record volumes of Russian crude oil in 2026 as the Iran war disrupts supplies from the Middle East, pushing refiners to seek alternative sources, Reuters reported. Temporary US sanctions waivers have further eased access to Russian barrels, allowing the two countries to increase purchases at a time of heightened uncertainty in global energy markets, However, the surge may prove temporary. Traders and analysts expect Russian oil demand in both countries to moderate in 2027 as Middle Eastern supplies become more readily available and the economics of buying Russian crude change. Seaborne Russian oil shipments to India and China averaged around 3.4 million barrels per day (bpd) through mid-November, approximately 530,000 bpd higher than the corresponding period last year, according to tanker data and industry sources cited by Reuters. The increase has provided Moscow with a significant boost to oil revenues, even as Ukrainian drone strikes have disrupted Russian refining capacity and forced more crude into export markets. Brent crude prices have also climbed nearly a third since the Iran war began, adding to volatility in global oil trade.How the Iran war changed Russian oil flowsThe disruption to Middle Eastern oil supplies following the Iran war has reshaped crude-buying patterns across Asia. As Iranian oil flows declined and concerns mounted over the availability of supplies from the Gulf, India and China increased their reliance on Russian crude to secure adequate feedstock for their refineries.Temporary US sanctions waivers targeting Russian oil have also helped buyers access more shipments by widening the pool of available vessels and suppliers.India and China together accounted for more than 80% of Russia's crude exports, according to estimates cited by Reuters.Moscow is also expecting its overall oil exports to rise this year. Russia's Ministry of Economic Development has forecast a 6% increase to 244.7 million metric tonnes, equivalent to approximately 4.9 million bpd.The higher exports underline how geopolitical disruptions have benefited Russia's oil trade. With traditional supply routes under pressure, Russian crude has become an important alternative for the world's two largest oil importers.India emerges as the biggest buyer of Russian crude India's purchases of Russian oil have climbed to record levels, reinforcing its position as Moscow's largest seaborne crude buyer. Data from tanker tracker Kpler cited by Reuters showed that India's Russian crude imports averaged 1.99 million bpd through early November, around 250,000 bpd higher than a year earlier. The increase comes after Indian refiners had scaled back purchases earlier in the year amid concerns over the possibility of higher US tariffs. However, the disruption to Middle Eastern supplies changed the buying calculus, making Russian crude more important for refiners seeking to maintain supplies. Between January and October, India's Russian crude imports rose about 10% to 1.87 million bpd, accounting for approximately 38% of the country's total crude imports, according to trade sources cited by Reuters. Indian refiners expect the full-year average to reach around 1.9 million bpd. The rise reflects both the availability of Russian barrels and the need to diversify supply sources as the Iran war puts pressure on flows from the Gulf. Why China has also increased its Russian oil imports China has also stepped up purchases, although its overall crude imports have declined. Chinese customs data cited by Reuters showed that Russian oil shipments to the country rose 17% to 2.34 million bpd between January and October. The imports were valued at around $59.6 billion, with Russian crude accounting for roughly a quarter of China's total oil imports during the period. This increase came even as China's overall crude imports fell 15%, highlighting the growing importance of Russian supplies in its import mix.Lower shipping risks and greater reliability have been key factors behind the shift. Muyu Xu, an analyst at tanker tracker Kpler, told Reuters that these considerations had driven the increase in China's Russian crude imports since the war began.Why Russian oil purchases could ease in 2027The outlook for Russian crude will depend significantly on how quickly Middle Eastern oil supplies recover and whether Russian barrels remain competitively priced.If Gulf supplies return to normal in 2027, Indian refiners are likely to have more alternatives.Sources at Indian refiners told Reuters that purchases of Russian crude could move back towards pre-Iran war levels, with buying decisions increasingly determined by price.China could follow a similar path. Greater availability of Middle Eastern crude may reduce the need for Russian supplies, particularly if Russian grades continue to trade at premiums rather than discounts.For Moscow, that could mean a tougher export environment next year. India and China have absorbed record volumes in 2026 partly because the Iran war disrupted their traditional sources of supply and made Russian crude more accessible.If those disruptions ease, Russia will have to compete more directly with oil from the Gulf and other producers. Its ability to retain market share will therefore depend less on geopolitical circumstances and more on the price, availability and shipping costs of its crude.

headline: A different layoff saga: Job-cut emails to employees first, apology later. Why did this company do so? ‘Very sorry’
content: An email intended for internal administrative communication ended up revealing some unwelcome news to employees of Australia's National Australia Bank (NAB). Several workers learnt that their jobs could be at risk through an automated notification before their managers had a chance to speak to them.The bank has apologized after accidentally sending redundancy-related emails to employees before formally informing them about the outcome of their voluntary exit applications. The affected staff members were supposed to receive the decisions directly from their managers. However, an administrative or technical error caused the automated emails to reach them before those conversations could take place.According to Reuters, NAB acknowledged the mistake and said it understood that receiving such news unexpectedly could cause distress."We are very sorry this happened, and that receiving an automated email this way would be upsetting and unsettling to many," the bank said in a statement shared with Reuters.NAB said the notifications were not meant to be sent before employees were informed of the decisions through direct conversations. Following the incident, the bank said it would bring forward discussions with the affected workers.Why is NAB planning to cut 2,500 jobs?The email blunder comes as the Australian lender prepares for a major workforce restructuring. Last month, NAB announced plans to cut 2,500 jobs over the next 12 months, affecting approximately 6% of its total workforce.The bank said the restructuring is intended to simplify its operations and lower costs. As many as 1,500 roles, primarily across corporate functions, are expected to be affected by the end of this year.Which other Australian companies have announced job cuts?NAB's planned workforce reduction comes amid a wider wave of layoffs across Australia. Several companies, including Qantas, Canva, WiseTech and Atlassian, have also announced job cuts this year.For employees seeking voluntary redundancy, the process can already involve considerable uncertainty. Workers have to wait to find out whether their applications have been accepted, when their employment will end and what steps they need to take next.Receiving an unexpected automated email about an employment decision before a formal conversation with management can make an already stressful situation even more difficult.Businesses are increasingly turning to automated systems to handle routine employee communications, including recruitment updates, onboarding instructions, payroll notifications and internal announcements.While these tools help organisations save time and manage communication more efficiently, the NAB incident highlights the potential risks of using automation to deliver sensitive employment-related decisions that can directly affect people's livelihoods.(With inputs from Reuters)

headline: Bangalore cab driver reveals  ₹20k daily income from Uber, 10 rental cars; passenger stunned - how he does it
content: A conversation between a Bengaluru passenger and a cab driver has triggered a discussion on social media about daily earnings, multiple income streams and the business of operating taxis. What started as an ordinary cab ride to Majestic soon turned into an interesting exchange about the driver's earnings and his fleet of vehicles.Recounting the experience in a post on X, the passenger said he had booked a cab in Bengaluru the previous night. During the journey, he began chatting with the driver about his work and daily life. The conversation eventually shifted to the driver's daily income."Then we started talking about how much he earns in a day. He literally showed me his earnings for the day on Uber: ₹4,800, and that was until 10:30 PM. He was going to drive for another 2 hours," he wrote.However, driving a cab was reportedly not the driver's only source of income.The passenger said the driver also owned 10 Maruti Suzuki Ertiga cars in Mumbai, which he rented out at ₹1,500 per vehicle per day. This reportedly earned him ₹15,000 daily in rental income.When combined with his reported Uber earnings of ₹4,800, the driver's total daily income came to approximately ₹19,800, or nearly ₹20,000, according to the passenger's calculation.The passenger was impressed by the driver's approach to building multiple income sources and the hard work involved in running the business."That is an insane amount, and he is truly earning it through his hard work. This amount is even more than the package of a senior manager at a product company," he added.How did social media users react to the cab driver's earnings? The post has drawn considerable attention online, with users sharing different views on the driver's reported income. While some praised his ability to build a business alongside his cab-driving work, others questioned whether the figures reflected his actual profits. One user pointed out that the income might look impressive but needed to be assessed after accounting for expenses such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, rental costs and the long hours spent behind the wheel. Another user highlighted the benefits and challenges of running an independent business, arguing that being one's own boss offers a level of flexibility that may not always be possible in corporate jobs. A third person said, "10 Ertigas? That's actually impressive if true." What did users say about the costs of running a 10-car fleet? A fourth user questioned how much the driver would actually earn after meeting the costs of operating the fleet. “ ₹15,000 a day from renting 10 cars sounds impressive, but what about EMIs, maintenance, insurance, driver payments and days when the cars aren't running? Still, owning and managing a fleet of 10 vehicles is a serious business in itself. We often underestimate how much business happens outside the corporate world. Would be interesting to know how much he actually takes home after all expenses.”

headline: IIT Bombay's ceiling fan replacement drive: Why are hostel rooms getting wall-mounted fans?
content: Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay has begun replacing ceiling fans and fan rods in hostel rooms with wall-mounted fans as part of a campus-wide renovation and maintenance exercise. The move has drawn attention amid renewed concerns over student suicides at premier educational institutions.The replacement drive has been initiated after a student died by suicide in July, but gained renewed attention following the death of 22-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode in September.The institute is installing wall-mounted fans across its hostels and other utility areas on campus. Images of wall-mounted fans arriving at the Powai campus as part of the renovation work have also circulated widely on social media.While the timing has prompted questions about whether the move is intended to prevent student suicides, the institute has not officially defined the replacement exercise as a suicide-prevention measure.Why is IIT Bombay replacing ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans?The shift comes against the backdrop of repeated student suicide cases at premier educational institutions, including IIT Bombay. Ceiling fans and their supporting rods can potentially be used as ligature points in suicide attempts. Replacing them with wall-mounted alternatives is therefore being viewed as a possible physical-safety intervention in hostel rooms.The move could reduce access to certain potential hanging points in student accommodation. However, it is not clear whether the institute has formally adopted the measure as part of a broader suicide-prevention policy.What happened to IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode?Sahil Wakode, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found dead in his hostel room at IIT Bombay's Powai campus on September 18.He hailed from Maharashtra's Yavatmal district and was reportedly caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination hours before his death.His death triggered protests and renewed concerns about academic pressure, student welfare and mental health support at India's premier technical institutions.

headline: Gurugram bans smoking in parks, markets and public spaces: What prompted MCG's  ₹200 fine?
content: The Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) has declared all public places within its jurisdiction as no-smoking zones with immediate effect. Smoking tobacco products, spitting tobacco, and throwing cigarette or bidi butts in these areas are now prohibited. Anyone violating the order can be fined up to ₹200.The order was issued by Municipal Commissioner Pankaj on Monday to improve cleanliness and public health in the city, while reducing people's exposure to tobacco smoke in public spaces, an official told news agency PTI.What prompted MCG to declare public places no-smoking zones?According to the order, smoking and the disposal of tobacco waste in public places can create health risks, particularly for children, women and senior citizens. Such activities also contribute to unhygienic conditions in public areas.The civic body has issued the directive under Section 4 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, which bans smoking in public places.The order also refers to the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules. These rules require authorities responsible for public spaces to prevent smoking and the disposal of cigarette and bidi butts in public areas and parks.Which places come under Gurugram's no-smoking ban?The restrictions cover all public places falling within the MCG's jurisdiction. These include:- Markets, bus stops, bus stands and public transport facilities.- Parks, green belts, playgrounds and open gyms owned, maintained or managed by the civic body.- Sheds, gazebos and other covered structures in these locations.- MCG offices, community centres, libraries and dispensaries.- Parking lots and toilet complexes.What is the fine for smoking in public places in Gurugram? Anyone found smoking in areas covered by the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram's (MCG) order can be fined up to ₹200. The penalty is provided under Section 21 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, commonly known as COTPA. Section 4 of the Act bans smoking in public places. The Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, also make it mandatory for those responsible for public spaces to prevent smoking and the disposal of cigarette and bidi butts. The fine comes at a time when cigarette prices have increased significantly this year. In February 2026, following the introduction of a 40% GST rate and additional excise duty, cigarette prices rose by at least ₹22-25 for a pack of 10 sticks. Premium varieties saw price increases of ₹50-55. A 10-stick pack of Wills Navy Cut, which earlier cost ₹95, was expected to be priced at around ₹120. ITC also increased prices of select cigarette brands in September. The price of a 20-stick pack of Classic Connect rose from ₹390 to ₹428. Are cigarette butts and tobacco spitting also prohibited? Yes. The MCG order prohibits people from throwing cigarette and bidi butts or spitting tobacco in public places. The restrictions extend beyond smoking to include tobacco-related littering. According to the civic body, these activities contribute to unhygienic conditions and can affect public health. The order also points to the risks of passive smoking, particularly for children, women and senior citizens. Who will ensure compliance? The MCG has assigned responsibility for implementing the order to its joint commissioners, the chief medical officer and officials from the sanitation and horticulture departments. These officials have been instructed to monitor compliance in their respective zones and parks. They have also been directed to put up signboards declaring the designated areas as no-smoking zones within 15 days.

headline: What does  ₹1.25L monthly budget look like? ‘ ₹30,000 grocery,  ₹20,000 grooming’: Noida couple’s expenses go viral
content: Owning a home does not always mean that monthly expenses are low. A couple living in Noida has revealed that they spend around ₹1.25 lakh every month, even though they own their house and do not have to pay rent.The couple shared a video on Instagram explaining their monthly expenses. Their spending includes groceries, household help, gym memberships, grooming, food and travel.The expense breakdown has started a discussion on social media, with many people questioning how a couple can spend so much every month without paying rent.Groceries cost ₹30,000, grooming costs ₹20,000According to the couple, groceries are their biggest monthly expense at ₹30,000. They also spend around ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym memberships and Pilates classes cost another ₹15,000 every month. Supplements such as protein powder and multivitamins add ₹15,000 to their expenses.The couple said they spend around ₹30,000 on groceries every month and another ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym and Pilates sessions cost ₹15,000, while supplements add another ₹15,000 to their monthly expenses.They also pay ₹10,000 for household help and spend another ₹10,000 on eating out. Home maintenance costs them ₹8,000, while electricity bills come to around ₹5,000. Internet, mobile and OTT subscriptions together cost ₹6,000. Their monthly commute expenses are between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000.Together, these expenses add up to around ₹1.25 lakh every month.The couple also spends ₹10,000 on household help, which includes cooking and cleaning. Their electricity bill is around ₹5,000, while home maintenance costs them another ₹8,000.They spend ₹6,000 on internet, mobile bills and OTT subscriptions. Travelling to work costs them between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000 every month.Renting a home could push expenses to ₹1.75 lakhThe couple also explained how much more they would have to spend if they did not own their home.According to them, renting a similar 3BHK flat in their area would cost around ₹45,000 to ₹50,000 every month.This could take their total monthly expenses from ₹1.25 lakh to nearly ₹1.75 lakh.Their video has received mixed reactions online. Some people questioned the ₹30,000 grocery budget, while others were surprised by the ₹20,000 spent on grooming.Some users also pointed out that spending ₹15,000 on gym memberships and another ₹15,000 on supplements was a personal choice rather than a necessary monthly expense.Others said that the couple's spending showed how expensive certain lifestyles can become in a city like Noida.The couple's video has also started a wider discussion about monthly expenses in Indian cities. Even without rent or home loan payments, costs such as food, fitness, personal care and household help can take up a large part of a family's income.

headline: Uber, Ola, Mega Cabs fares at Bengaluru Kempegowda airport getting costlier? Here’s what passengers, cab drivers said
content: Passengers and cab drivers at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) have accused ride-hailing platforms of manipulating cab availability to push up fares, even as hundreds of taxis allegedly remain idle in airport parking areas, according to a report by Deccan Herald.The reported complaints come amid long passenger queues, failed bookings and extended waiting periods for drivers.Commuters have alleged that they are being pushed towards more expensive cab categories when their preferred rides are unavailable, while drivers say they often spend hours waiting for a single booking, as per the report.The situation has also been compounded by a reported decline in passenger traffic, particularly at the international terminal, which drivers have partly attributed to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to air travel.G Narayana Swamy, president of Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta, told Deccan Herald that hundreds of cabs could be seen parked in the airport's P7 parking zone even as passengers faced long queues at pickup points.He alleged that some authorised cab operators were deliberately restricting vehicle availability to drive up fares.Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates the airport, has nine authorised cab partners, including KSTDC, Mega Cabs, Uber, Uber Black, Ola, Quick Ride, OHM Electric Cabs and WTI, as per the report.Passengers report long waits and expensive cab optionsPassengers have reported waiting between 40 and 60 minutes to secure a ride. Some said their initial bookings did not materialise, leaving them with the option of booking more expensive vehicle categories.A passenger travelling from Goa told Deccan Herald that she found at least 60 people waiting at the Uber kiosk when she arrived at around 7 PM last week.Quick Ride had only one pre-booked SUV available, while drivers at the Namma Yatri kiosk reportedly said that only SUVs could be arranged.The passenger said that after waiting for around 45 minutes, the driver assigned to her booking refused the trip because her destination was not close enough to the airport. She was travelling to Marathahalli.She also alleged that another driver demanded an additional fare, raising concerns over the availability of airport taxis and the enforcement of fare rules.Why are cab drivers waiting for hours? Cab drivers have also raised concerns about declining passenger traffic and operational restrictions, saying these are affecting their earnings. According to the report, drivers said they sometimes wait between two and three hours for a single booking. They are required to remain in designated parking areas until their ride-hailing applications clear them to enter the passenger pickup zone. Drivers have particularly flagged weaker demand at the international terminal, which they partly attribute to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to flight operations. A premium cab operator at the airport said it deploys around 800 vehicles across both terminals, with the bulk of demand concentrated at Terminal 1. The operator told the daily that services generally run smoothly outside peak hours, but longer trip durations affect vehicle availability.

headline: Black jackets, grey wigs and Nvidia pitches: What happened at Vancouver’s Jensen Huang lookalike contest? Who won $200?
content: A contest to find the best lookalike of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang brought together more than 200 registered participants in Vancouver, Canada. The event had an unusual set of challenges, with contestants not only trying to look like the billionaire tech executive but also pitching Nvidia products and making funny pleas to get their jobs or wives back. Organised by Plug Vancouver, the contest was held at Mangos Kitchen and Bar on Howe Street on Sunday, 22 November. The contestants came dressed to look like Huang, wearing black leather jackets, glasses and sneakers. Some also wore grey wigs to copy his hairstyle. The winner was Walter Lim, a retired man from Seattle who drove around three hours to take part in the event. He won the top prize of US$200. The two runners-up received US$50 each. According to the organisers, the event was free for the public and received a much bigger response than expected. Three rounds tested the contestantsThe competition had three rounds, with judges and cheers from the audience helping decide the finalists.The first round was about looks. Contestants had to convince the judges and audience that they looked like Huang, who is known for his black leather jacket, glasses and grey hair.The second round required contestants to pitch Nvidia's latest product. They had to present their ideas while holding a bag of potato chips.One contestant made the crowd laugh by crushing the bag during his pitch and calling the crumbs inside it "microchips".The final round was even more unusual. Contestants had to make a funny plea to get either their wife or their job back. The challenge was a reference to the personal controversy surrounding Huang, which had recently made headlines.Lim eventually won the competition after the finalists faced the audience. He said his sister had told him about the event while he was travelling in Madrid. He then decided to drive from Seattle to Vancouver to take part.Lim said people had often told him that he looked like Huang. He also said that owning a similar leather jacket and wearing the same style of glasses helped him match the Nvidia chief's appearance. Why is Jensen Huang in the news? The contest took place during an unusual period for Nvidia and its chief executive. Huang had stepped down as Nvidia's CEO on November 12 following a controversy involving an alleged extramarital affair with Singapore-based businesswoman Alice Huang. Reports also raised questions about possible links to China and national security. The allegations involving espionage have not been established as fact. His departure led to discussions about the company's leadership and calls from supporters for him to return. However, Nvidia announced on 23 November that its board had reinstated Huang as president and CEO with immediate effect. The company said the board was satisfied with his explanations and ability to lead the business.The Vancouver contest also followed a separate lookalike event in New York linked to Alice Huang, adding to the unusual attention around the Nvidia controversy.Plug Vancouver has previously organised a similar lookalike competition when singer Bruno Mars visited the city.For now, Walter Lim has won the title of Vancouver's Jensen Huang lookalike, along with a US$200 prize.

headline: India may review wheat export policy amid concerns over lower acreage
content: New Delhi: India has initiated inter-ministerial deliberations on a possible review of its liberalized wheat export policy, just three months after allowing unrestricted overseas shipments of the grain, as it assesses domestic production for the current crop year through June 2027, said two people aware of the matter.

headline: After 27 years, Odisha restores 29 land plots in Puri to Lord Jagannath Temple, ending a major land dispute
content: The Odisha government has restored ownership records of 0.115 acres of land in Puri to Shree Jagannath Temple after discovering that the property had been incorrectly registered under the names of private individuals. The correction was carried out following the resolution of a revenue case that had remained pending for 29 years, according to a report by Times of India (TOI).The land is situated in Bada Deula Sahi mouza under Puri tehsil. The revision of revenue records covers 29 plots spread across 19 khatas (revenue accounts), which have now been registered in the name of Shree Jagannath Mahaprabhu, represented by the Shree Jagannath Temple Managing Committee.Revenue case pending since 1997 resolvedTimes of India citing officials said, proceedings in the abatement case had been pending since 1997. After the case was finally settled, the revenue department amended the Record of Rights (RoR), removing the names of private individuals and entering the deity's name as the rightful owner.Bada Deula Sahi is considered a distinctive mouza in Odisha's revenue administration as it is exclusively associated with the Shree Jagannath Temple.Odisha steps up efforts to reclaim temple landThe latest restoration is part of the Odisha government's wider drive to identify and safeguard land owned by Lord Jagannath. As part of these efforts, the revenue department has established a dedicated Shree Jagannath Mahaprabhu land cell to address matters concerning the temple's landholdings.Officials told TOI that the specialised cell is tasked with identifying temple-owned properties, clearing illegal encroachments and ensuring that revenue documents correctly reflect the deity's ownership. Similar measures have reportedly resulted in the removal of encroachments from temple properties at various locations and the correction of land records in the deity's name.Minister Suresh Pujari oversees the exerciseThe initiative is being carried out under the supervision of Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, with senior government officials also participating in the exercise.Shree Jagannath Temple chief administrator Arabinda Kumar Padhee appreciated the officers and employees who contributed to the efforts to safeguard the temple's land assets.Odisha celebrates 'Boita Bandana', Lord Jagannath adorns 'Suna Bhesa' on Kartik PurnimaMeanwhile, people of all ages, from children to the elderly, thronged water bodies across Odisha on the occasion of Kartik Purnima on Tuesday and floated miniature boats to commemorate the ancient maritime history of Kalinga, news agency PTI reported.People started assembling at ponds, tanks, rivers, lakes, and the sea from early in the morning on the full moon day of Kartik month of the Hindu calendar, and set small boats, traditionally made of banana stems or paper, afloat with lighted lamps (diyas), betel leaves, flowers, and offerings in them.Water bodies wore a colourful look as people observed the tradition of 'Boita Bandana' or worship of boats on the occasion.

headline: Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee: What is 2018 case filed by Vikas Sankrityayan?
content: A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a criminal defamation case filed by social media activist Vikas Sankrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey, over a video uploaded on Rathee's YouTube channel in 2018. Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant after Rathee failed to appear before the court, according to a PTI report. The matter has been listed for further proceedings on December 3. A detailed order is awaited. The development comes after the court issued bailable warrants against Rathee on October 31, as per a Bar and Bench report. Earlier, on October 17, it had issued a bailable warrant after a process server reported that Rathee's residence was locked while attempting to serve the notice. The court had subsequently directed that fresh summons be sent to Rathee at his Gurugram address in Haryana. During the proceedings, Rathee's counsel submitted that the YouTuber ordinarily resides in Austria and had travelled to India to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. The court also noted that Rathee had initially been summoned in July 2019. What is the Dhruv Rathee defamation case? The case dates back to May 2018, when Rathee uploaded a video alleging that the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) IT cell had attempted to bribe Sankrityayan to malign his reputation. Sankrityayan subsequently filed a criminal defamation complaint, arguing that the allegations made in the video were false and had harmed his reputation. The video was also shared by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then the chief minister of Delhi. Sankrityayan initiated defamation proceedings against both Rathee and Kejriwal. While the case has remained pending since 2018, proceedings against Kejriwal took a different turn after he tendered an apology before the Supreme Court for sharing the video. The proceedings against Rathee, who originally uploaded it, continued before the trial court.Why did the court issue fresh warrants against Rathee?The Saket court had issued a bailable warrant against Rathee on October 17 after he failed to appear for the hearing.However, the warrant could not be executed because it had reportedly been sent to an incorrect address in Austria, according to Bar and Bench.At the October 31 hearing, the court directed that a fresh warrant be issued at Rathee's Gurugram address after being informed about the error.The proceedings also saw the court question the urgency of issuing the warrant after being informed that Rathee had already left India."Ab itni jaldbazi ka koi logic hai?" the court observed, as reported by Bar and Bench.The court subsequently issued fresh bailable warrants before moving to a non-bailable warrant on Monday.Who is Vikas Sankrityayan, alias Vikas Pandey?Vikas Sankrityayan, popularly known as Vikas Pandey, is a social media activist associated with the 'I Support NaMo' online group, which supports Prime Minister Narendra Modi.According to his Facebook profile, Sankrityayan describes himself as a digital creator and writer from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. His stated areas of interest include social media misuse and fake news.His X profile identifies him as a software architect associated with IBM India Software Labs. He has also listed his involvement with online groups such as 'I Support NaMo' and 'Hindu IT Cell'.In a Facebook post, Sankrityayan described himself as one of the early targets of Rathee's videos and accused the YouTuber of making false claims about him."I was one of the first victims of fake news peddler Dhruv Rathee," he wrote.

headline: Bisleri under FSSAI scanner, but how many Indian households actually rely on bottled water? Just 1%, survey finds
content: The controversy surrounding Bisleri’s packaged drinking water after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) flagged a batch from its Goa facility has brought the spotlight back to drinking water safety in India.Interestingly, a LocalCircles survey found, as per multiple news reports, that just 1 per cent of respondents said they rely on bottled water for drinking and cooking instead of treating municipal water, highlighting the limited reliance on packaged water as a primary source for household consumption.84% use purifiers or RO systemsThe survey, covering 29,161 responses from urban households across 284 districts, found that 40 per cent use water purifiers, while 44 per cent rely on RO systems. Another 9 per cent said they boil water before consuming it, while 1 per cent use chlorination, alum or other mineral-based methods. A further 1 per cent reported using other methods to treat water.Trust in tap water declinesOnly 2 per cent of respondents said they consume piped water directly without purification. The proportion of households confident about the safety of untreated municipal water has also declined sharply, from 6 per cent in the 2025 survey to 2 per cent in the latest exercise.The findings come at a time when packaged drinking water brands are facing increased scrutiny following FSSAI's enforcement action against Bisleri International.FSSAI sanctions prosecution against BisleriOn November 1, FSSAI said it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International over unsafe packaged drinking water from its Goa manufacturing facility. The regulator also issued an order prohibiting the sale of a specific batch of the product after testing found a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.Bisleri says issue limited to one batchBisleri, however, maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption and said the issue was restricted to a single batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025. The company said five of the six samples collected from the plant on September 30, 2025, met the applicable standards, while one sample was found to have a marginally higher bromate level.The company has said it will cooperate with food safety authorities as FSSAI expands its enforcement drive across major packaged drinking water brands.

headline: Enhancing Livelihoods and Nutritional Security through Backyard Poultry in Zunheboto, Nagaland
content: Nagaland faces a significant gap between the demand and availability of animal-based protein, particularly meat and eggs. According to the Annual Administrative Report of the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Government of Nagaland (2022–23), the state’s annual meat requirement is 52.37 MT, while availability stands at 23.87 MT, resulting in a reported deficit of 38.50 MT. Similarly, against an annual requirement of 1,870 lakh eggs, availability is only 350.42 lakh, leaving a substantial shortfall. Per capita meat availability is reported at 40 grams per day against the recommended 70 grams, while annual egg availability is 22 eggs per person compared with the requirement of 182.5 eggs. This situation highlights the need to strengthen local poultry production to improve nutritional security and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Addressing this challenge, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Zunheboto, implemented a NABARD-sponsored programme titled “Promoting Sustainable Livelihood and Nutritional Security of Women SHGs through Low-Cost Egg Incubator and Backyard Poultry Production”. The initiative aimed to empower women farmers through scientific poultry management, improve household access to nutritious food and generate additional income through backyard poultry farming. Under the programme, selected women beneficiaries received quality day-old chicks of the improved Rainbow Rooster strain, feed for the first 20 days, vaccination and medication support, feeders, drinkers and low-cost egg incubators for on-farm chick production. KVK scientists provided regular training, technical guidance and field-level support to help beneficiaries adopt scientific bird management practices and strengthen disease prevention. The introduction of low-cost incubators was particularly significant, as it enabled farmers to begin producing chicks locally and reduce their dependence on external sources. The programme has delivered encouraging results in terms of household nutrition and income generation. During the reporting period, beneficiary households consumed 1,380 birds, contributing to improved access to animal protein, while another 2,135 birds were sold to generate income. Average meat availability increased by 66.7 kg per household, and the beneficiaries collectively generated an income of ₹30,80,360. The programme also recorded the production of 22,618 eggs, which were either consumed by the households or sold. Each beneficiary earned a reported net income of ₹32,592 to date, demonstrating the potential of backyard poultry as a supplementary livelihood activity for rural women. The low-cost incubators installed at farmers’ fields have also started producing chicks regularly. This development is expected to improve the local availability of chicks and meet the requirements of beneficiary villages and neighbouring areas in the coming years, while supporting the continuity and expansion of backyard poultry farming. The NABARD-sponsored initiative implemented by KVK, Zunheboto, demonstrates how scientific poultry management, affordable technologies and sustained technical support can create livelihood opportunities while addressing nutritional challenges. By enabling women Self-Help Group members to produce poultry and eggs for household consumption and sale, the programme has strengthened their economic participation and encouraged self-reliance. The initiative offers a promising model for promoting women-led rural entrepreneurship, improving access to animal protein and supporting inclusive agricultural development in Zunheboto district and other parts of Nagaland.

headline: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
content: NEW DELHI Hardly three days before the retirement of incumbent Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) proposed the transfer of Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru to the office. Who is Justice Surya Kant, the 53rd Chief Justice of India? storyline 1 Also read | Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jharkhand/hemant-soren-writes-to-cji-to-urgently-appoint-jharkhand-hc-chief-justice-successor/article71730713.ece The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote to the Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, who is superannuating on November 27. Hemant Soren | Weathering the political storm storyline 1 Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor storyline 1 Mr. Soren had highlighted that a Chief Justice to the State High Court should ideally have been recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium in advance, and cleared by the Union government as per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts. Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Chief Secretary Avinash Kumar and other senior officials were present on the occasion. Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court storyline 1 The Chief Minister, as the head of the State government, had expressed objections about any interim arrangement, making it clear that the State High Court must have a regular Chief Justice at the helm. Mr. Soren, in his letter to the CJI and the Collegium judges, had reportedly pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment. On Tuesday (November 24), the Supreme Court Collegium proposed that Justice Bakhru take over as the Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice. The ball is now with the government to clear the Collegium resolution and notify the appointment of Justice Bakhru by November 27. The Collegium has recommended Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court, to be transferred as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in the place of Justice Bakhru. In a separate resolution on November 24, the Collegium recommended the appointment of Himachal Pradesh High Court judge, Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court following the transfer of Justice Rao to the Karnataka High Court.

headline: International Shri Renuka Ji Fair concludes in HP, governor calls it symbol of India’s civilisation
content: Nahan (HP), Nov 24 (PTI) The six-day International Shri Renuka Ji Fair concluded on Tuesday in Himachal Pradesh’s Sirmour district, with Governor Kavinder Gupta describing the religious event as “a living symbol of India’s civilisational heritage and Sanatan traditions”. The conclusion was marked by the departure of the palanquin of Lord Parshuram and other deities. Governor Kavinder Gupta said the fair is not only a religious event but a living symbol of India’s civilisational heritage, Sanatan traditions, family values and social harmony. He called for preserving the rich cultural and spiritual legacy of Himachal Pradesh while promoting sustainable tourism and local livelihoods. The governor said the divine reunion of Goddess Renuka and Lord Parshuram symbolises love, sacrifice, devotion and duty. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vikas bhi-Virasat bhi’, he said India was advancing towards modernity while strengthening and showcasing its cultural and spiritual heritage, a statement issued here said.

headline: BJP announces 12-member core committee for Himachal
content: Shimla, Nov 24 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh BJP president Rajeev Bindal on Tuesday announced a 12-member state core committee which includes two special invitees. The announcement came in accordance with the directives of BJP national president Nitin Nabin. A notification has been issued in this regard, the party said in a statement. The state core committee includes former BJP national president and Union minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, the party’s state president Dr Rajeev Bindal, former chief minister and Leader of the Opposition Jairam Thakur, state general secretary (organisation) Siddharthan and Lok Sabha MP and former Union minister Anurag Thakur. The other members are former state president and Lok Sabha MP Suresh Kashyap, MLA and former state president Satpal Singh Satti, Lok Sabha MP Rajeev Bhardwaj, state vice president and MLA Vipin Singh Parmar, Rajya Sabha MP and state general secretary Dr Sikander Kumar and state general secretaries Payal Vaidya and Sanjeev Katwal. Additionally, BJP state in-charge Shrikant Sharma and state co-in-charge Darshana Singh have been appointed special invitees to the core committee. headline: High Court Takes Stern View of Order Defiance, Asks Hamirpur SP: Why Should Contempt Proceedings Not Be Initiated?
content: The Allahabad High Court has taken a strict stance against Hamirpur Superintendent of Police Mrigank Shekhar Pathak for failing to comply with an earlier judicial order. Finding a prima facie case of wilful disobedience of its directive, the court granted the officer a final opportunity of one month to ensure strict compliance. The bench warned that if the order is not implemented in letter and spirit by the next hearing, the Superintendent of Police must appear in person to explain why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against him. ​A single bench of Justice Piyush Agrawal passed the order while hearing a second civil contempt petition filed by Gayatri Devi. The dispute centers on the non-payment of family pension and other government dues following the disappearance of her husband, Head Muharrir Rajaram Shukla, who was posted in Hamirpur. The petitioner alleged that despite clear instructions from the High Court, the authorities failed to decide on her representation within the stipulated timeframe. ​Advocate Jaideep Tripathi, representing the petitioner, informed the court that on April 1, 2026, the High Court had directed the Hamirpur SP to decide on Gayatri Devi’s representation within six weeks. However, the directive remained unexecuted even after the deadline expired. Counsel further submitted that an earlier contempt petition had been disposed of with the liberty for the petitioner to approach the court again in case of unnecessary delay. With the order still pending compliance, she was compelled to file a second contempt petition. ​After perusing the case records, the High Court observed that a prima facie case of deliberate non-compliance with judicial orders was made out. Taking a serious view of the administrative inaction, Justice Piyush Agrawal remarked that while the conduct warranted strict scrutiny, the court was granting one last opportunity in the interest of justice. ​The court directed the Superintendent of Police to fully execute the earlier order within one month and file a compliance affidavit before the next date of hearing. Through the affidavit, the officer must demonstrate that the petitioner’s representation has been decided in accordance with the previous directive. The bench made it clear that any further lapse would invite personal appearance and formal contempt proceedings. ​The underlying matter stems from the disappearance of Head Muharrir Rajaram Shukla, who has been missing since August 10, 2023. Following his sudden disappearance, the local police initiated a search operation, and the investigation was subsequently handed over to a Special Investigation Team. When the SIT failed to trace him, the probe was transferred to the Crime Branch. Despite these efforts, his whereabouts remain unknown.

headline: 7,950 NDPS cases registered, assets worth Rs 92 crore seized in Himachal in four years
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh has registered 7,950 cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and arrested 12,302 accused persons over the past four years as part of its intensified campaign against drug trafficking.The state govt has also seized illegally acquired assets worth approximately Rs 92 crore during the period.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said on Tuesday the state govt was committed to making Himachal Pradesh drug-free and had directed all departments and central agencies to strengthen coordination and accountability in the anti-drug campaign. Since the implementation of the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (PIT-NDPS Act), a total of 225 drug traffickers have been detained, including 159 in 2026. Himachal ranks second nationally in preventive detention under the Act. The police have seized 1,384 kg of charas and 59 kg of chitta during the past four years. For the first time, property worth Rs 48 lakh acquired through drug trafficking has been transferred to the state govt. Besides, 86 properties involving encroachments and illegal constructions by NDPS accused persons have been identified, with demolition and eviction proceedings completed against 22. The state govt has identified 246 highly drug-affected panchayats for special monitoring. Around 12,000 individuals have been identified and categorised to connect those requiring help with treatment and rehabilitation services.The chief minister said action was being intensified against drug kingpins, their financial networks and inter-state connections rather than being confined to small-time peddlers. A police-operated de-addiction centre for women has been established at Mashobra in Shimla district, while steps are underway to strengthen rehabilitation facilities. The state govt has also registered cases against 168 employees allegedly involved in drug-related activities. Moreover, 30 state govt employees and 21 police personnel have been dismissed. Sukhu said awareness programmes were being strengthened in educational institutions, with 9,677 institutions declared tobacco-free.

headline: Insurer rejects claim over husband’s death, Himachal widow gets Rs 49 lakh payout
content: A Himachal Pradesh consumer commission has directed a private insurance company to pay Rs 49.18 lakh to a widow after the insurer rejected her husband's Rs 50 lakh death claim, alleging that he killed himself within 12 months of the policy's revival. Questioning the insurer's reliance on statements recorded by its investigator, the commission said there was no police report or post-mortem examination to establish its version and held that the rejection of the claim was not genuine. Kangra District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur were hearing a complaint filed by the man’s wife challenging the insurer's decision to reject the Rs 50 lakh death claim on the ground that he had allegedly killed himself. “Random statements obtained without disclosing consequences—and where it is not established what prompted the complainant to depose in such a manner—do not inspire confidence. Therefore, the statement that he committed suicide does not appear to be genuine…Hence, the rejection of the claim is not genuine,” the commission said on November 3. The dispute arose after the man died on April 9, 2024. His wife, the nominee under his life insurance policy, sought the Rs 50 lakh sum assured. However, the insurer transferred only Rs 81,954 to her bank account as a refund of premiums and refused to pay the remaining amount. Why insurer rejected death claim According to the complaint, the man had purchased the Rs 50 lakh life insurance policy on November 22, 2021, by paying an annual premium of Rs 31,943. His wife was named as the nominee. Following his death, she submitted a claim maintaining that he had died of a heart attack. The insurer disputed her version and relied on an investigation report prepared by an investigation agency hired by it, which claimed that the man had died after consuming a poisonous substance. According to a statement recorded during the investigation, he had been suffering from a cough and had mistakenly consumed poisonous medicine while attempting to take cough syrup. The insurer argued that the policy had lapsed on February 6, 2023, and was revived on October 31, 2023. Since the man died within 12 months of its revival, the company invoked the suicide exclusion clause, arguing that its liability was limited to refunding the premiums. The company rejected the claim through a communication dated April 10, 2025, after receiving a legal notice from the widow on March 25, 2025. No police report, post-mortem The insurer's explanation did not convince the commission. It noted that the policy was in force when Kumar died on April 9, 2024. A gram panchayat certificate stated that he had gone for a morning walk and died that morning. It found no police report or post-mortem examination establishing suicide. The insurer's investigation report described the man as hale and hearty, with no previous medical history. Statements by the village ASHA worker and gram pradhan also confirmed his death and the cremation in the village on the same day. Questioning the insurer's reliance on statements by the man’s wife and son, the commission said the investigator had not explained their legal consequences. It also rejected the explanation that the man had mistakenly consumed poisonous medicine instead of cough syrup, saying that the statement did not inspire confidence. It held that the suicide allegation was not substantiated and the claim rejection was not genuine. Allowing the complaint, the commission directed the insurer to pay the wife Rs 49.18 lakh, after deducting the Rs 81,954.90 already refunded, with 6.5 per cent annual interest from May 14, 2025, until realisation. It also ordered Rs 5,000 in compensation and Rs 7,500 towards litigation costs. Takeaway Insurance companies cannot reject death claims merely by relying on unverified statements recorded during an investigation. If an insurer alleges suicide to invoke a policy exclusion, it must have credible evidence to support that allegation. Policyholders and nominees should also seek copies of investigation reports and challenge claim repudiations that are not backed by convincing evidence. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states (Himachal Pradesh: 1800-180-8087) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. headline: China leveraging India's supply-chain dependence to curb its rise: US panel
content: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission has alleged that China is using economic pressure, supply-chain dependencies and its support for Pakistan to constrain India's rise. In its recent report titled China's Other Front: India and the Future of US Strategy in the Indo-Pacific, the commission said China had restricted exports of key inputs to India, recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow electronics manufacturing, reduced pharmaceutical input prices to undercut Indian producers, and imposed export controls on battery technology.China uses industrial dependence as leverageThe report said China was using India's dependence on Chinese industrial inputs to limit its ability to compete with Chinese manufacturers. "China uses economic coercion not simply to influence India's behaviour but also to constrain its emergence as a manufacturing and technological competitor," the commission said. In spring 2025, China restricted sales of specialised fertilisers and delayed exports of tunnel-boring machines for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project. Chinese authorities cited technical reasons for the delays, but the measures were seen as retaliation for India's restrictions imposed after the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes, the report said. China also delayed approvals for exports of rare-earth permanent magnets to Indian companies after introducing global export licensing requirements in April 2025. Shipments meant for Indian automakers were held at Chinese ports, while those bound for German and US automakers were approved. Beijing lifted the restrictions in August 2025. China also restricted the movement of specialised engineers and manufacturing equipment to Apple supplier Foxconn's Indian factories from January 2025, affecting iPhone production. By July, Foxconn had recalled hundreds of Chinese engineers from its Indian facilities and brought in workers from Taiwan to fill key vacancies, the report said. ALSO READ: How did US lawmakers react to Jensen Huang's return at Nvidia as CEO?Battery technology and pharmaceutical inputsChina's export controls on battery manufacturing technology and equipment have threatened India's plans to develop its clean energy manufacturing base, according to the report. In October 2025, China announced export controls on battery manufacturing equipment and technology as part of wider restrictions on rare-earth exports. Although the expanded controls were subsequently suspended, barriers to technology transfers continued to delay Indian production. Reliance Industries reportedly faced difficulties securing access to Chinese technology required for its battery gigafactory in Gujarat. Alternative suppliers in countries such as South Korea would significantly increase costs, the report said. The pharmaceutical sector is another area where the commission identified China's pricing as a source of pressure on Indian manufacturers. In 2025, Chinese producers cut prices of 41 active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and key starting materials (KSMs) by 40-50 per cent. Indian media reports cited by the commission said the reductions were timed to undercut new Indian API plants that had started production in November 2024 with support from the government's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. The price cuts affected two major Indian factories supported under the PLI programme, one in Himachal Pradesh and the other in Telangana. India has sought to reduce its dependence on Chinese pharmaceutical inputs through domestic manufacturing incentives. As of September 2025, the PLI scheme had supported production capacity for 38 critical APIs and 26 KSMs and drug intermediates. The government had also approved 48 greenfield projects, backed by $455.8 million in committed investment. However, the commission said achieving the scale needed across all pharmaceutical inputs remained a challenge. ALSO READ: Jensen Huang to Steve Jobs: CEOs who made dramatic corporate comebacksChinese restrictions extend to US supply chainsThe commission described China's end-user verification certificate requirements as "the most novel and strategically significant coercive tool China has employed", with direct implications for US-India supply-chain integration. In October 2025, China reportedly delayed exports of heavy rare-earth magnets to India for several months, seeking assurances that the materials would be used for domestic production and would not be re-exported to the US or used for military purposes. Following the Trump-Xi trade détente that month, Beijing approved shipments to several Indian companies that provided the required certifications. The commission said extending such requirements to pharmaceuticals or other sectors where India supplies the US could undermine Washington's efforts to reduce its dependence on Chinese-controlled inputs.India's dependence on Chinese imports continuesIndia has restricted Chinese investment and expanded domestic manufacturing, but its industrial dependence on China has continued to grow, the report said. Following the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes, India tightened investment restrictions on Chinese companies, banned Chinese applications and introduced additional screening requirements for Chinese firms seeking government-funded projects. However, Indian manufacturers continue to depend on Chinese machinery, components and technical expertise. The report cited India's railway manufacturing sector as an example. A shortage of axles halted domestic production of railway wheels in early 2025, prompting the government to allow imports of Chinese parts to meet the requirements of the national railway company. The commission said India's PLI scheme had expanded manufacturing capacity but had not substantially reduced dependence on Chinese imports. By the end of 2025, the programme had an announced public funding outlay of more than $20 billion across 14 sectors. Government figures cited in the report showed that it had generated $214.8 billion in production and $87.4 billion in exports. However, many companies had focused on final assembly rather than developing domestic suppliers for components and industrial inputs. The report said building domestic supplier networks would require "substantial capital, technology, and time".China's support for Pakistan adds to India's security concernsThe commission said China's military and strategic support for Pakistan had increased India's concerns about a possible two-front conflict. China supplied 81 per cent of Pakistan's arms imports between 2020 and 2024, according to figures cited in the report. During the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, which followed the Pahalgam terror attack and India's launch of Operation Sindoor, Pakistan reportedly used advanced weapons procured from China. The report also referred to allegations that Beijing provided Pakistan with intelligence support during the conflict. Indian military officials had said Pakistan may have received real-time satellite imagery or other intelligence from China. Beijing did not confirm or explicitly deny these claims. In May 2026, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV aired an interview with Zhang Heng, an engineer from the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC). Zhang confirmed that he and other AVIC personnel had provided on-site technical support in Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict. The commission said China's evolving military partnership with Pakistan had made a two-front contingency an increasingly important concern for India.US-India cooperation faces challengesThe report said India was strengthening domestic manufacturing, modernising its military and expanding cooperation with the US and other partners to respond to China's growing influence. However, India's commitment to strategic autonomy would continue to shape its relationship with Washington, it said. The commission said New Delhi's rivalry with Beijing was driven by its own territorial disputes and security concerns, rather than an alignment with US foreign policy objectives. The two countries have established a broader framework for cooperation through a 10-year defence framework, trade negotiations, technology initiatives covering semiconductors and biomanufacturing, and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad). However, differences in export control rules, procurement requirements, financing arrangements and bureaucratic processes could limit the implementation of these initiatives, the report said.

headline: Himachal’s fiscal health far weaker than National average: PRS finds
content: State spends over 90% of expenditure on revenue items; committed liabilities consume 88% of receipts against 52% national average Himachal Pradesh’s fiscal problems appear more pronounced when its financial indicators are compared with the National average, with the state lagging on revenue mobilisation, carrying a substantially higher debt burden and spending a disproportionate share of its income on recurring obligations, according to the latest report of PRS Legislative Research. The State of State Finances 2026–27 report presents a revealing comparison of the state’s financial position with the consolidated finances of States across the country, showcasing the limited revenue flexibility available to Himachal for undertaking developmental expenditure. One of the most striking findings relates to the composition of government expenditure. Himachal Pradesh is among the states estimated to spend 90% or more of its total expenditure on revenue items during 2026–27, compared with the all-state average of 82%. This leaves a relatively smaller proportion for capital investment and the creation of durable public assets such as roads, bridges, hospitals and other infrastructure. The difference becomes even more pronounced when committed expenditure is examined. Himachal has budgeted Rs 35,641 crore towards salaries, pensions and interest payments in 2026–27, equivalent to 88% of its estimated revenue receipts. In comparison, states collectively have budgeted around 52% of their revenue receipts towards these commitments. The state’s own revenue-generating capacity also remains below the National average. Himachal’s own-tax revenue is estimated at 5.5% of its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), against an all-state average of 7%. States such as Maharashtra (7.7%), Punjab (7.2%) and Karnataka (6.7%) have higher own-tax revenue relative to their respective GSDPs.

headline: Dog menace on rise in Hamirpur, close to 6,000 people bitten in 2026
content: Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh A total of 5,876 people were bitten by dogs in Himachal Pradesh’s Hamirpur district over 10 months this year, averaging 19 bite cases daily. The Health Department data shines a light on the canine crisis, which is not limited to stray dogs. Between January and October this year, stray dogs accounted for 3,863 bite cases, while pet dogs were involved in 2,013. The number of reported cases this year has already exceeded the total for the entire previous year by 1,551. On average, nearly 19 people have been targeted by dogs every day. "Dog bite cases must be taken seriously. People should not be negligent if bitten or scratched by a dog and should immediately visit the nearest healthcare facility for treatment. It is essential to complete the full course of the anti-rabies vaccine as per medical advice," Hamirpur chief medical officer Dr Satish Kumar said on Monday (November 23, 2026). Allowing pet dogs to roam freely in public spaces, failing to maintain proper control and negligence in their care are posing a risk to public safety too, he said. In Hamirpur town, the worst-hit areas are the Hirangar forest region and Anu zone, as stray dogs are found in great numbers on the Hamirpur-Sujanpur main road and near the Ano chowk. Students exercising here are targeted by the dogs, with residents alleging that the local municipal corporation is silent on this issue. The number of people bitten by stray dogs in 2026 was 445 in January, 420 in February, 382 in March, 396 in April, 425 in May, 444 in June, 294 in July, 428 in August, 321 in September, and 308 in October. Meanwhile, regarding pet dogs, the number of people injured by them was 164 in January, 212 in February, 234 in March, 188 in April, 224 in May, 208 in June, 192 in July, 191 in August, 220 in September, and 180 in October. Treating a dog bite as a minor injury can prove costly. Rabies is a serious and life-threatening disease, but it can be prevented through timely treatment and vaccination. If bitten or scratched by a dog, immediately wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, health officials said. “Regardless of whether the wound is small or large, consult a doctor without delay. Complete the full course of the rabies vaccine as advised by the physician. Do not apply turmeric, chilli, soil, oil, or any other substances to the wound,” they added.

headline: VERY VERY IMPORTANT NEWS RECEIVED FROM DIRECTOR PUBLIC RELATIONS SHIMLA FOCUSING CM THAKUR SUKHVINDER SINGH AND HIS ASSOCIATES
content: Cooperation of all sections of society essential in fight against drug abuse :CM The present state government, under the leadership of Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu is working with firm commitment to completely eradicate all forms of drugs, including chitta, from the state. All concerned departments and central agencies have been directed to make the anti-drug campaign more effective through mutual coordination and accountability. The fight against drugs in the state is not being limited to police action alone; rather, it is being transformed into a mass movement involving the public. Walkathons are being organized in various districts, with enthusiastic participation from students, teachers, Mahila Mandals, Yuvak Mandals and citizens. The police and Special Task Force have been directed to ensure that action is not restricted to small-scale drug peddlers. Instead, strict action must be taken against major kingpins, their associates, supply networks, financial sources and inter-state connections. Over the past four years, 7,950 cases under the NDPS Act have been registered in the state and 12,302 accused persons have been arrested. During this period, large quantities of narcotic substances were seized, including 1,384 kilograms of charas and 59 kilograms of chitta. Since the implementation of the PIT-NDPS Act in 2023, a total of 225 drug traffickers have been detained, including 159 in 2026 alone. Himachal Pradesh ranks second in the country in terms of preventive detention under this Act.

headline: Concerned Over Rapid Decline In Kasauli's Green Cover, Himachal Pradesh High Court Restricts Land...
content: Expressing concern over the rapid depletion of green cover in Kasauli due to commercial construction, the Himachal Pradesh High Court has directed the State not to grant any permission under Section 118 of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972 in Solan district without obtaining the Court's approval by furnishing justifiable reasons. Section 118 restricts the transfer of land to non-agriculturists.A Division Bench of Chief Justice G.S. Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin C. Negi passed the order in a suo motu PIL concerning large-scale excavation and construction activities near Lower Mall in Kasauli.The Bench observed that rampant grant of permissions under Section 118 had led to large-scale commercial construction in Solan district and that the State Government had failed to bring the situation under control.While the State strongly opposed the passing of any interim order, the Bench remarked,“...since we have been constantly dealing with these issues in Public Interest Litigations, we are of the considered opinion that until any extreme orders are passed, the State will not remedy itself, as these permissions have been unabatedly given over the last decades by successive Governments, thus diluting the strict provisions of Section 118 of the Act.”Taking note of the gross violation of hill-cutting norms, the Court also directed strict enforcement of stop-work notices issued to three builders in Kasauli. In case of non-compliance by the builders, the jurisdictional Station House Officer (SHO) was directed to ensure enforcement of the notices.The Court further directed the Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), Kasauli, to ensure inspection of all major construction projects, primarily commercial in nature, considering the rapid reduction of green cover in the Kasauli range.SDM's Inspection ReportThe Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), Kasauli, appeared in person and filed a status and inspection report. In October 2026, a joint inspection was carried out with officials of the following, the Cantonment Board, the Tehsil, the Town and Country Planning Department; and the Forest Department.The inspection found excavation going on at a property called “Woodvilla” in Ferozi Village. The roots of existing trees were exposed. The project's representative was directed to stop work, restore the exposed roots and protect the trees.The developers responded that some branches had been lopped only because high-voltage wires ran close to them, and denied that any trees had been uprooted or cut. The Forest Department counted 35 existing trees and found no felled trees. The report also recorded that the Gram Panchayat had issued no NOC for the property.Three LLPs, One ProjectThe Court noted that three builders were carrying out “massive construction and excavation” at the site M/s Reviera Luxury Project Five LLP, M/s Sretan Luxury Project Four LLP; and M/s Jambavati Project Reality Three LLP.According to the record, the first two firms, both based at the same Mumbai address, received Section 118 permissions in December 2023 and June 2024 to set up housing colonies.It then bought adjoining parcels from the same family for ₹7.60 crore and ₹1.90 crore. The Director of Town and Country Planning gave the third firm in-principle approval in August 2026 for a plotted development, after relaxing norms. These included reducing the required access road width from 7.5 metres to 5.48 metres.The Bench said, “The harsh steps are being initiated against the said builders/newly impleaded respondents, as even the Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), who is present, has admitted that the site in question has been developed to the extent that the greenery and the damage caused to the hill side just below the Radio Tower, can be seen from Shimla at Kasauli, which is at least at a distance of 25 kms by “Crow's flight”. Therefore, the extent of damage to the hill side is but apparent and if one is to lift the “Corporate Veil” the three developers have got necessary permission by setting up different Partnerships for the same project, which the State has conveniently given making Section 118 of the Act a dead letter.”'Gross Violation' Of Hill-Cutting NormsAfter going through the photographs, the Court found a “major deviation” from the Policy Guidelines for Cutting, Conservation and Preservation of Hill, 2025. These guidelines were issued following directions in the pending PIL Kusum Bali v. State of Himachal Pradesh (CWPIL No. 13 of 2021).The Court noted that under Regulation 4 of the guidelines, no hill cutting is allowed without prior intimation to the competent authority, the maximum permissible slope for construction is 45 degrees, cutting at any one level cannot exceed 3.5 metres, and must be done in steps, slope stabilisation measures must be technically vetted by an institute such as IIT, CBRI or NIT; and vertical hill cutting is not permitted.It held, “We are of the considered opinion that from these photographs it is apparent that there...

headline: Nearly 5,900 People bitten by dogs in Hamirpur in ten Mlmonths; stray and pet dogs pose growing threat
content: Nearly 5,900 people have been bitten by dogs in Himachal Pradesh’s Hamirpur district during the first ten months of 2026, highlighting a growing public safety concern as attacks by both stray and pet dogs continue to rise. The alarming figures indicate that an average of 19 people are being bitten by dogs every day in the district. According to Health Department data, as many as 5,876 dog-bite cases were reported between January and October this year, against 4,325 cases during the entire year of 2025 and 4,269 cases in 2024. The number of victims recorded in just ten months of the current year has thus exceeded the previous year’s total by 1,551. Of the total cases reported this year, 3,863 involved stray dogs, while 2,013 people were bitten by pet dogs, indicating that the threat is not confined to street animals alone. The growing number of incidents involving domesticated dogs has also raised questions about the responsibility of pet owners and enforcement of regulations governing the movement and control of animals in public places. The situation is particularly worrying in Hamirpur town, where residents have reported a considerable presence of stray dogs in the Hiranagar forest area, Anu zone and along the Hamirpur-Sujanpur main road, particularly near Anu Chowk.

headline: IHG Signs Holiday Inn Mandi in Himachal Pradesh
content: IHG Hotels & Resorts has signed a management agreement with Mac View Infrabiz Private Limited for the development of Holiday Inn Mandi, a 100-key hotel that will expand the company’s presence in Himachal Pradesh and support its growth strategy across North India. Located on the Chandigarh–Manali corridor, the hotel is positioned to serve a mix of business, leisure and transit travellers. The location provides convenient access between the National Capital Region and some of Himachal Pradesh’s key tourism destinations, while also benefiting from Mandi’s role as an administrative and commercial centre. Holiday Inn Mandi will feature 100 guestrooms and suites, three food-and-beverage outlets, and event facilities, including a ballroom designed to host meetings, conferences, and social gatherings. Holiday Inn remains one of IHG’s established hotel brands, serving a broad range of travellers across business and leisure segments. In India, the brand currently operates 17 hotels and has 34 additional properties in the development pipeline. Commenting on the signing, Sudeep Jain, Managing Director, South West Asia, IHG Hotels & Resorts, said the company continues to identify opportunities in emerging destinations supported by infrastructure development and growing travel demand. He noted that the addition of Holiday Inn Mandi will further strengthen IHG’s presence in Himachal Pradesh while bringing an internationally recognised hospitality brand to an important transit and commercial market.
