headline: UnaStella secures 5 billion won to develop 5‑ton rocket engine under Global TIPS
content: Korean startup plans electric motor‑pump cycle and clustering engines for UNA EXPRESS series over four years Korean space launch vehicle developer UnaStella will receive 5 billion won in government funding over four years to develop a 5‑ton electric motor‑pump engine for small launch vehicles. The company will also seek demonstration partnerships with overseas customers that need microgravity experiments or in‑orbit testing of space components. UnaStella announced on the 24th that it has been finally selected for the general research and development project of the “2026 Global TIPS” program overseen by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and the Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs. Global TIPS is a program that links private investment with government R&D support to back technology development and global growth of promising small and venture companies. While companies carry out core technology development and performance verification, an operator consortium supports their growth through investment, commercialization consulting, and overseas network connections. Founded in 2022, UnaStella has continued its technology development through R&D support programs from the Ministry of SMEs and Startups since its establishment. Through “TIPS,” the company began engine design and manufacturing, and under “Scale-up TIPS” it carried out development and verification of the electric motor‑pump system. UnaStella succeeded in launching UNA EXPRESS-I in May 2025 and is currently developing follow-up launch vehicles and an “electric motor‑pump–based engine.” With its selection for Global TIPS, the company plans to extend its accumulated development achievements into further R&D and overseas commercialization.

headline: Over 2k Himachal-made drug samples failed quality tests over 3 years, assembly told
content: Kullu: A total of 2,216 medicine samples manufactured in Himachal Pradesh failed quality tests over the past three years, with 47 pharmaceutical companies recording 10 or more failures, according to data tabled in the state assembly.The figures were disclosed by the health and family welfare department in a written reply to a question by Bharmour MLA Dr Janak Raj during the recently concluded winter session in Dharamshala. The samples were tested in different laboratories during 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 up to Nov 1.Of the 2,216 failures, 844 were recorded in 2024-25, 963 in 2025-26 and 409 in the current financial year. The manufacturing units were located in Solan, Sirmaur, Una and Kangra districts.Several companies disputed the test findings, with some challenging the analysis reports.Of the 47 companies with repeated failures, 43 were jointly inspected by the state drug control administration and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The state drug controller also conducted separate inspections.The department said manufacturing licences of three companies had been cancelled, while production at 19 companies was fully or partially stopped until they complied with the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945.In all, 1,608 product licences were suspended and 59 cancelled over the three years. Warnings were issued in four cases. The action affected 1,667 products, and the govt directed the recall of medicines corresponding to all samples declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). Legal action was initiated in 17 cases.The reply also flagged suspected spurious or counterfeit medicines carrying the names of established pharmaceutical companies. These included cough syrups and medicines for high blood pressure and bacterial infections. The companies denied manufacturing the products and described them as spurious or counterfeit.The department said drug inspectors had been directed to inspect every pharmaceutical manufacturing unit at least once a year. Units with repeated quality failures were being inspected independently by the state department and jointly with CDSCO.

headline: Missed flight after 4-hour train delay, Jammu couple gets Rs 63,000 from Indian Railways
content: A couple travelling from Jammu to Delhi missed their connecting flight to Guwahati after their train arrived nearly four hours late, forcing them to book fresh air tickets and pay for a hotel stay. Holding the Railways responsible for failing to provide evidence explaining the delay, the Jammu District Consumer Commission has directed it to pay Rs 63,199. The Jammu District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Pawan Dev Kotwal and member Neelam Bala Bhardwaj were hearing a complaint by Mohit Singh Bhau and his wife Damini Billoria against Northern Railways and the Union of India, alleging that a nearly four-hour train delay made them miss their connecting flight to Guwahati. They sought Rs 60,000 for financial losses, Rs 50,000 for mental agony and inconvenience, and Rs 30,000 in litigation expenses. “Every passenger's time is precious, and they might have booked the tickets for further journey,” the commission said on November 4, referring to a Supreme Court verdict, holding that the Railways could not escape responsibility without producing evidence to explain the delay. “Since the complaint faced inconvenience and discomfort and mental agony due to deficiency in service on the part of OPs (Railways and its officials), they are also entitled to receive compensation for the same,” it added. Couple forced to book fresh flight, pay for hotel The couple had booked tickets on the Jammu-Delhi DEE Duronto Express for December 19, 2022. The train was scheduled to reach Delhi at 3.55 am on December 20, while their flight to Guwahati was scheduled to depart at 7.15 am. However, the train was delayed by three hours and 55 minutes, leaving them unable to catch their flight. According to the complaint, the couple had to book fresh air tickets to Guwahati and arrange hotel accommodation after missing their flight. They spent Rs 35,699 on fresh flight tickets and Rs 2,500 on hotel accommodation, bringing their additional expenditure to Rs 38,199. The couple approached the consumer commission on February 13, 2023, alleging deficiency in service by the Railways. However, the Railways opposed the complaint, arguing that it could not be held liable for delayed train arrivals under Rule 115 of the Indian Railway Conference Association Coaching Tariff. During the proceedings, the Railways' counsel argued that the train had been delayed because of fog and that the administration was protected from liability under the applicable railway rules. The commission, however, noted that the Railways had failed to produce evidence establishing that fog had caused the delay. It also recorded that the couple had disputed this explanation, stating that there was no fog on the day of their journey. The commission further noted that the Railways had not filed its written version within the statutory period and that its subsequent reply could not be taken on record. Although its counsel participated in the proceedings and cross-examined the complainants, the Railways did not lead any evidence explaining the delay. It observed that the couple had established a prima facie case of deficiency in service, while the Railways had failed to substantiate its defence. The commission also referred to an earlier Supreme Court ruling involving a passenger who missed a connecting flight because of a delayed train. Finding the circumstances similar, the Jammu commission said the Supreme Court's reasoning applied to the couple's complaint as well. “Citizen/passenger cannot be at the mercy of the authorities Somebody has to accept the responsibility,” the commission observed. Allowing the complaint, the commission directed the Railways to reimburse Rs 38,199 towards fresh flight tickets and hotel accommodation, with simple interest at 7.5 per cent per annum from February 13, 2023, until realisation. It also awarded Rs 20,000 as compensation for inconvenience, discomfort and mental agony, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses. The total award comes to Rs 63,199, besides interest on Rs 38,199. The commission directed the Railways to deposit the amount within six weeks of receiving a copy of the order. Takeaway Preserve your train and flight tickets, hotel bills and other receipts if a train delay makes you miss a connecting flight. The Railways may be held liable if it fails to provide evidence explaining the delay and establish that it was beyond its control. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories (Himachal Pradesh: 1800-180-8087) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. headline: Bank holiday today Tuesday, 24 November: Branches closed in these 21 cities across India — Check RBI list and reasons
content: Banks in several parts of India will remain closed today, Tuesday, 24 November, on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti. However, the holiday is not applicable across the country.According to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) holiday calendar, branches in 21 cities will remain closed today under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Banks in other cities will continue to operate as usual.Meanwhile, stock market trading will also remain closed today, with both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) observing a trading holiday.Which cities are observing a bank holiday today?According to the RBI's November 2026 holiday calendar, bank branches in the following cities/ states will remain closed on 24 November:Aizawl (Mizoram)Belapur (Maharashtra)Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)Bhubaneswar (Odisha)ChandigarhDehradun (Uttarakhand)Hyderabad (Telangana)Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh)Jaipur (Rajasthan)Jammu (Jammu and Kashmir)Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh)Kohima (Nagaland)Kolkata (West Bengal)Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh)Mumbai (Maharashtra)Nagpur (Maharashtra)New DelhiRaipur (Chhattisgarh)Ranchi (Jharkhand)Shimla (Himachal Pradesh)Srinagar (Jammu and Kashmir)This means that branches of all public and private sector banks, including State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, will remain closed in these 21 cities. However, the bank holiday will not affect most routine digital banking services. Customers can continue to access their accounts through mobile banking and internet banking, transfer money using UPI, NEFT and IMPS, check account balances, download statements and make bill payments.Why are banks closed today?The RBI has listed the 24 November holiday as Guru Nanak Jayanti/Karthika Purnima/Rahas Purnima. Guru Nanak Jayanti: It marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism and the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.Karthika Purnima: It marks the full moon day of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik. The occasion is considered auspicious in Hinduism and Jainism.Rahas Purnima: Also known as Raas Purnima, it celebrates Lord Krishna's divine Raas Leela with Radha and the Gopis.Where will banks remain open today?Bank branches in cities not covered by the 24 November holiday will continue to operate as usual, with regular banking services available to customers. These include Agartala, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gangtok, Guwahati, Imphal, Kochi, Panaji, Patna, Shillong, Thiruvananthapuram and Vijayawada.Customers should check with their respective bank branches for any local operational changes.Disclaimer: This information is based on the RBI's regional bank holiday calendar and is provided for informational purposes only.

headline: Jai Ram demands rollback of hotel fee hike in HP
content: Shimla: Leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur on Monday demanded the immediate rollback of a 2.5-fold hike in consent-to-operate fees imposed on Himachal Pradesh’s hotel industry by the State Pollution Control Board, accusing the Congress government of burdening tourism operators with excessive charges.The former chief minister said hoteliers were being forced to pay five years’ fees upfront, despite most properties in the state being leased out on an annual basis.Questioning the rationale behind the move, Thakur pointed out that owners of small green-category hotels with 10 to 13 rooms would now have to pay Rs 1.8 lakh for five years, up from Rs 72,000 earlier.With the annual fee raised from Rs 14,400 to Rs 36,000, small hotel operators face an additional financial burden of Rs 1.08 lakh over five years, he added.Thakur alleged that instead of framing effective policies to strengthen the state’s economy, the government was focused on extracting revenue from citizens, warning that the decision would discourage entrepreneurs and hurt a sector vital to Himachal’s economy.Contrasting the move with successive governments’ efforts to promote tourism, he criticised the current dispensation for demanding five years’ advance fees and recalled its earlier attempts to tax homestays.Accusing the govt of repeatedly hiking levies across sectors, Thakur also cited increased taxes on tourist vehicles, higher educational fees, and raised charges for medical and revenue-related services.

headline: Himachal Pradesh eyes 1,000 more e-buses to cut HRTC costs
content: The state government will add 1,000 e-buses to make Himachal Pradesh clean and green and to make the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) a self-reliant corporation, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said today. He was inaugurating a new bus route at Majhyar in the Nadaun Assembly constituency of Hamirpur district.The route will connect villages around Sera with Hamirpur, meeting a long-pending demand of residents of Nadaun, Sera and several adjoining villages. The Chief Minister said it would significantly improve public transport connectivity in the area and particularly benefit patients and their attendants visiting Dr Radhakrishnan Government Medical College at Jol Sappad, besides students, employees and other daily commuters.The HRTC, he said, bears substantial financial liabilities on account of pensions, salaries and other expenses, so it was essential to reduce its operating costs. Electric buses were cheaper to run than diesel buses, which would improve the corporation’s financial health. The government was giving priority to promoting electric buses and more would be added in the coming years to move the HRTC gradually towards electric mobility.Himachal’s geographical conditions were different from those of other states, the Chief Minister said. Diesel buses would continue to run in remote, inaccessible and difficult mountain terrain to ensure uninterrupted services and would remain important in areas where electric buses faced technical or geographical challenges.The government was committed to providing the best health, transport and education facilities to people, he said, and had started many welfare schemes for the poor and needy. It was making concerted efforts to modernise public transport and make it more economical and environment-friendly. In its very first budget, he said, the government had envisioned making Himachal a green energy state and had accordingly prioritised electric mobility.Meanwhile, the Chief Minister attended the wedding ceremony of his niece, Nikita, at his ancestral village of Bhavdan in the Nadaun constituency last night. He congratulated the newlyweds and wished them a happy and prosperous married life.

headline: Educational exposure visit to DIET-Solan, PM Shri schools
content: A delegation of officials of the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs), Block Resource Centres (BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs) from New Delhi undertook an educational exposure to DIET-Solan, PM SHRI School, Baddi, and PM SHRI School, Nalagarh, recently and interacted with faculty.The visiting team observed the teaching-learning environment, infrastructure, instructional resources and student activities and held detailed discussions with the faculty members and students in these institutes.The interactions focused on teacher education, classroom practices, school leadership, mentoring, student engagement, learning outcomes, inclusive education and the implementation of the PM SHRI initiatives which are aimed at strengthening teacher capacity and institutional leadership through structured professional development supported by DIETs.The faculty members and coordinators from both New Delhi and Himachal Pradesh shared good practices being implemented in their respective institutions and school systems. The discussions covered effective teacher-training strategies, academic support mechanisms, use of teaching-learning materials, community participation, monitoring of classroom processes and innovative approaches to improving student learning.The participants also discussed challenges and issues commonly faced by schools and teacher-education institutions. These included teacher workload, diverse learning needs, resource constraints, ensuring quality in classroom transactions and sustaining educational innovations. Practical solutions and successful strategies adopted by both sides were also shared during the deliberations.Deputy Director, School Education (Quality), Himachal Pradesh, Rajinder Verma, apprised the visiting delegation of new practices and initiatives in the state to improve the quality of school education and strengthen teacher capacity.Principal, DIET-Solan, Mamta Gupta, and coordinator Babita Thakur shared the details of the institute’s academic, training and outreach activities. Coordinators Amit and Anamika from New Delhi spoke about the good practices of their institution while also participating in the discussions.

headline: AI lab, auditorium planned for Bilaspur engineering college
content: The state government is providing financial assistance to encourage research and innovation and to help youth in their pursuits, Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani said on Sunday. He was addressing ‘Emerge-2026’, a technical and cultural festival, at the Government Hydro Engineering College, Bandla, in Bilaspur district.He announced an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) lab at the college to give students access to modern technical facilities and a modern auditorium to provide better infrastructure for academic, technical and cultural activities.Dharmani said the government was committed to fostering the creative thinking and innovative spirit of youth. Through the State Innovation Policy 2026 and a State Innovation Fund of Rs 2 crore, efforts were under way to help students turn ideas into prototypes, provide seed funding for startups, strengthen incubation centres and promote training and capacity building. Research and development projects were also being encouraged through the Department of Science, Technology and Environment and HIMCOSTE, he added.Earlier in the day, the minister distributed prizes to students at the Government Senior Secondary School, Kapahra, in the Ghumarwin Assembly constituency. He said the school would be developed as a ‘Centre of Excellence’ to improve the quality of education in government institutions and prepare students for a competitive era. The school, he said, is affiliated with the CBSE and has 14 teachers from the CBSE cadre.Dharmani said the government was prioritising road connectivity in Kapahra and neighbouring panchayats. Nearly Rs 20 crore was being spent on the construction, repair and paving of roads in the area and about Rs 16 crore on the upgradation of the road from Barthin to Chhat and Junala, on which work worth Rs 4 crore to Rs 5 crore had already been completed.

headline: Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhu visits ailing Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania at IGMC
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu today visited Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC), Shimla, to enquire about the health of Himachal Pradesh Vidhan Sabha Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania, who is undergoing treatment at the hospital. The Chief Minister wished him a speedy recovery. Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri also visited the hospital to enquire about the Speaker’s health.Pathania was admitted to IGMC today on the advice of doctors after experiencing repeated bouts of fever and general weakness. According to Vidhan Sabha sources, he had been feeling slightly unwell during the winter session of the Assembly, held in Dharamsala from November 16 to 21.Doctors suspect typhoid, although confirmatory blood test reports are awaited. A doctor said that the Speaker had no apparent health issues apart from recurring fever. His ultrasound and X-ray reports were normal and he had been put on antibiotics. His condition is stable, the doctor added.During his visit, Chief Minister Sukhu also enquired about the health of Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur’s sister, who is undergoing treatment at IGMC. He wished her a speedy recovery.
